tools.name: voicestudio
tools.description: Desktop app for voice cloning, dubbing, dictation and audiobooks
strengths: Covers cloning, voice design, dubbing, dictation and audiobooks in one app
Runs on NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon (MPS) or CPU only
Local API and MCP server for agent integration
weaknesses: Model weights and voices carry licence terms separate from the AGPL-3.0 app
CPU-only use is slower; the CPU PyTorch build needs about 5 GB disk

tools.name: career-ops
tools.description: Job-search agent that scores listings, tailors CVs and drafts applications
strengths: Drafts only: no auto-submit, and no mail transport in the code
No telemetry or backend; CV goes only to the AI provider you choose
Covers evaluation, tailored PDF CV, cover letter, contact drafts, tracker and interview prep
weaknesses: Needs a separate AI CLI and provider; it does not run models itself
README says early runs are rough until it learns your profile

tools.name: ppt-master
tools.description: Agent skill that turns documents into natively editable PowerPoint decks
strengths: Exports native PowerPoint objects: shapes, charts, tables and slide masters stay editable
Runs locally; only model, search, image and speech calls leave the machine
Works with any agent-capable tool and models like Claude, GPT, Gemini and Kimi
weaknesses: Output quality depends on the driving model; cheaper models need more manual polish
Needs a separate agent tool and model access; it is not a standalone app

tools.name: ai-job-search
tools.description: Claude Code workflow that searches job boards and drafts tailored CVs and cover letters
strengths: Drafter-reviewer pipeline compiles CV and cover letter PDFs with page-count and ATS checks
Postings pass a deterministic integrity gate for hidden text and injected instructions
Tracks applications end to end: /outcome, /gmail-sync, /notion-sync, /html-report, /interview
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code with a paid subscription or API credits; other agent tools only partly supported
Most portal skills target Denmark; other markets rely on LinkedIn, freehire.me or a custom portal

tools.name: hindsight
tools.description: Agent memory server with retain, recall and reflect operations
strengths: Four parallel retrieval strategies (semantic, BM25, graph, temporal) with cross-encoder reranking
Works with 25+ LLM providers, including local ones: ollama, lmstudio, llamacpp
Python, Node.js and Go clients, CLI, REST API and a built-in MCP endpoint per bank
weaknesses: Retain depends on an LLM call for fact extraction, adding provider cost and latency
Dashboard, backups and uptime SLA are described only for the hosted Hindsight Cloud

tools.name: AutoGPT
tools.description: Role-based AI agents coordinated by one lead agent, plus a visual workflow builder
strengths: Single-container Docker image for self-hosting, plus an installer for Linux, macOS and Windows
Visual builder with branching logic and a marketplace of reusable workflows
Per-Expert account access and spending controls
weaknesses: Platform code is Polyform Shield, not OSI open source; only classic/ is MIT
Hosted Platform is paid; built-in model access is not included when self-hosting

tools.name: transformers
tools.description: Model-definition library for pretrained text, vision, audio and multimodal models
strengths: Pipeline API covers text, audio, vision and multimodal tasks in a few lines
Model definitions are reused by vLLM, SGLang, TGI, Axolotl, Unsloth and DeepSpeed
Loads from 1M+ Hub checkpoints across hundreds of architectures
weaknesses: Not a modular toolbox for neural nets; model files avoid shared abstractions on purpose
Training API targets its own PyTorch models; generic loops need Accelerate

tools.name: OmniRoute
tools.description: LLM gateway routing one OpenAI-compatible endpoint across 372 providers
strengths: Single /v1 endpoint covers 372 providers with automatic fallback to healthy targets
Dashboard tracks free-tier pools and quota use at /dashboard/free-tiers
Works with coding CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex, Cline and Cursor via one config
weaknesses: Free-token headline is an estimate; provider limits and terms change and can lower it
Providers flagged tos: avoid are excluded from automatic routing by default

tools.name: daily_stock_analysis
tools.description: LLM-driven daily analysis of watchlist stocks across six markets, pushed to chat apps
strengths: Runs free on GitHub Actions with a fork and secrets; no server needed
Works with Gemini, Claude, OpenAI-compatible APIs, DeepSeek, Qwen or local Ollama
Free data sources (AkShare, Baostock, YFinance) allow zero-config start
weaknesses: Free market data sources are rate-limited and stability is not guaranteed
Report quality depends on separately configured news search API keys

tools.name: ultralytics
tools.description: Python library and CLI for training and running YOLO vision models
strengths: One API and CLI covers train, val, predict, track and export across seven vision tasks
Pretrained YOLO26 n/s/m/l/x weights with published COCO mAP and CPU/T4 latency tables
Installs via pip, Conda or Docker; reproduction commands given for benchmark numbers
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0; commercial use requires a separate Enterprise License
Vision only; no LLM or language model support

tools.name: openhuman
tools.description: Rust agent harness with desktop app, built-in memory and embeddable library
strengths: Usable as a typed Rust library, with no sidecar or daemon to run
Ships memory, voice, browser/desktop control, workflows and 14 channels in one app
Supports local models (Ollama, LM Studio, MLX) and BYOK for 26 providers
weaknesses: Marked early beta; README warns of rough edges
GPL-3.0 license may constrain embedding in proprietary products

tools.name: pytorch-image-models
tools.description: PyTorch library of image models, pretrained weights and training scripts
strengths: Broad model zoo with pretrained weights for nearly every listed architecture family
Includes train.py, validate.py, inference.py and sweep.py for reproducible ImageNet-style runs
forward_intermediates and prune_intermediate_layers supported across all models
weaknesses: Image models only; no text or LLM support
Some model variants ship without pretrained weights

tools.name: llama.cpp
tools.description: C/C++ inference engine for GGUF LLMs and VLMs with an OpenAI-compatible server
strengths: Many backends: CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, CANN, MUSA, OpenCL, RPC, WebGPU
1.5-bit to 8-bit integer quantization reduces memory use
CPU+GPU hybrid inference for models larger than VRAM
weaknesses: OpenVINO backend is marked in progress
Building from source needs backend-specific toolchains such as CUDA or Vulkan SDKs

tools.name: ruview
tools.description: WiFi CSI sensing on ESP32 for presence, breathing, heart rate and pose
strengths: Runs on roughly $9 ESP32 nodes; the pretrained encoder fits in 8 KB at 4-bit
Publishes 21 Home Assistant MQTT entities per node, plus Matter and Apple Home bridges
Pretrained weights on Hugging Face, plus a phase-variance presence fallback needing no model
weaknesses: Live sensing needs ESP32-S3/C6 CSI firmware; the Docker image runs simulated data
Committed on-device pose model scores PCK@20 of 3.0% and its runtime path is a stub

tools.name: servers
tools.description: Reference MCP servers for files, git, fetch, memory and time
strengths: Maintained by the MCP steering group, so it tracks the spec and official SDKs
Seven small servers covering files, git, web fetch, knowledge-graph memory and time
Starts with one command: npx for TypeScript servers, uvx or pip for Python ones
weaknesses: README says these are reference implementations, not production-ready
Only Everything supports Streamable HTTP; the other servers are stdio only

tools.name: deer-flow
tools.description: Agent harness running sub-agents, memory and sandboxes with pluggable skills
strengths: Interactive `make setup` wizard and `make doctor` health check for configuration
Many search and fetch backends: Tavily, Brave, DuckDuckGo, SearXNG, Jina, InfoQuest
Optional tracing through LangSmith, Langfuse and Monocle
weaknesses: 2.0 shares no code with v1; the original research framework lives on the 1.x branch
README is dense with option-level detail, which buries the core setup steps

tools.name: Lightpanda
tools.description: Headless browser written in Zig for agents and scraping, with CDP and MCP
strengths: README benchmark: 123MB peak vs 2GB for headless Chrome over 100 pages
Speaks CDP, WebDriver BiDi and MCP, so Puppeteer and Playwright clients can connect
Agent mode supports many LLM providers and local Ollama or llama.cpp, or runs with --no-llm
weaknesses: No graphical rendering; web platform coverage is partial (see WPT results)
No native Windows binary; needs WSL2, and Linux binaries need glibc

tools.name: frigate
tools.description: Local NVR with realtime object detection for IP cameras
strengths: Runs detection only where motion is found, which limits CPU use
Retention rules based on detected objects, plus 24/7 recording
RTSP re-streaming, plus WebRTC and MSE for low-latency live view
weaknesses: README strongly recommends a GPU or AI accelerator for detection
Tightly oriented to Home Assistant; other setups rely on MQTT

tools.name: gbrain
tools.description: Memory store with sources and a knowledge graph for coding agents
strengths: Keyless start: embedded PGLite and keyword search, no server or API keys needed
MCP access via local stdio, Tailscale tailnet exposure, or remote URL with token
`gbrain think` answers carry citations and note stale or missing knowledge
weaknesses: Not on npm; install from GitHub with Bun 1.4.4 or newer
Semantic search, synthesis and enrichment need separately configured, paid model providers

tools.name: open-design
tools.description: Design workspace that drives your coding agent to build prototypes, decks and video
strengths: Works with 26 coding-agent CLIs, with MCP setup via `od mcp install <agent>`
Ships 151 design systems, 15 deck templates and 93 image prompt templates
BYOK proxy covers OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Gemini, Ollama, LM Studio and vLLM, with SSRF checks
weaknesses: Ships no agent of its own; needs a separate agent CLI or API key
No prebuilt Linux desktop release; Linux requires running from source

tools.name: pytorch
tools.description: Python tensor library with GPU support and tape-based autograd
strengths: Dynamic graphs run line by line, so stack traces point at user code
GPU backends for NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm (Linux only) and Intel GPUs
Custom layers can be written in Python or C++ via an extension API
weaknesses: Source build needs a C++20 compiler, 10 GB disk and 30-60 minutes first time
ROCm is Linux only; Windows distributed support is a prototype

tools.name: keygraphhq/shannon
tools.description: Autonomous pentester that exploits web apps and APIs using source analysis
strengths: Reports only exploits with a reproducible proof of concept, which cuts speculative findings
Outputs PDF, Markdown, JSON and SARIF 2.1.0, with GitHub and GitLab CI integrations
Bring your own key: Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Bedrock, gateways, or local Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio
weaknesses: Needs the target's source code; black-box testing is only in paid editions
Actively executes exploits, so it must not be run against production

tools.name: airi
tools.description: AI VTuber companion with VRM and Live2D avatars, voice, and game-playing
strengths: Runs as browser PWA, desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux) and iOS app
Supports 25+ LLM providers via xsai, including Ollama, vLLM and SGLang
VRM and Live2D avatars with auto blink, look-at and idle eye movement
weaknesses: README describes development as early stage; plugin system is WIP
Memory system (Memory Alaya) and in-browser WebGPU inference are unfinished on the roadmap

tools.name: supervision
tools.description: Python toolkit for annotating detections, tracking and managing vision datasets
strengths: Model-agnostic: sv.Detections connectors for Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection and Inference
Converts datasets between YOLO, Pascal VOC and COCO, with split and merge helpers
Configurable annotators for drawing detections on images and video frames
weaknesses: Does not include detection models; you supply and run your own
Inference connector example needs a Roboflow API key

tools.name: Open Notebook
tools.description: Self-hosted NotebookLM alternative for research notebooks, chat, and podcasts
strengths: 20+ providers plus Ollama and OpenAI-compatible servers, configured in the UI
Podcast generation with 1-4 speakers and custom episode profiles
Full REST API on port 5055 and MCP integration docs
weaknesses: No password by default; UI and API bind to all interfaces
Multi-user support is only a direction under consideration, not shipped

tools.name: LightRAG
tools.description: Graph-based RAG framework with a REST server and WebUI
strengths: Runs with local file storage by default; no database required
Pluggable backends: PostgreSQL, Neo4j, MongoDB, OpenSearch, any OpenAI-compatible LLM
Optional reranker, citations, document deletion with KG regeneration, RAGAS and Langfuse
weaknesses: Entity extraction makes one LLM call per chunk, raising indexing time and cost
Server binds 0.0.0.0 with authentication off by default

tools.name: handy
tools.description: Offline push-to-talk dictation app that pastes transcripts into any text field
strengths: Runs fully offline on Windows, macOS and Linux with Whisper or Parakeet models
Hold-to-talk or toggle shortcuts, plus CLI flags and signals for remote control
Accepts custom Whisper GGML models and manually downloaded GGUF files
weaknesses: Linux Wayland support is limited and needs wtype, dotool or ydotool for text input
Clipboard paste can insert stale clipboard content; Reliable Paste is still experimental

tools.name: copilotkit
tools.description: React and Angular SDK for adding agent chat and generative UI to apps
strengths: Works with many agent backends: LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, Google ADK, PydanticAI, Strands, LlamaIndex
Covers React, Angular, Vue, React Native, plus Slack and Teams channels
Three generative UI modes: registered components, A2UI specs, sandboxed MCP Apps
weaknesses: Memory, persistent threads and Continual Learning sit in Intelligence, not the MIT SDK
Slack and Teams are GA only on cloud-hosted Intelligence

tools.name: opendataloader-pdf
tools.description: PDF parser that outputs Markdown, JSON with bounding boxes, and Tagged PDF
strengths: Bounding boxes and element types for every extracted item, usable for source citations
Local mode needs no GPU; README reports 0.015 s/page
Hybrid mode adds OCR, LaTeX formulas and chart descriptions; OCR engine is selectable
weaknesses: Requires Java 11+ on the host, even when using the Python package
Each convert() call spawns a JVM, so calls must be batched

tools.name: mastra
tools.description: TypeScript framework for building AI agents, workflows and MCP servers
strengths: Graph workflow engine with .then(), .branch() and .parallel() control flow
Suspend and resume agents or workflows, with execution state kept in storage
Built-in evals, observability, memory and RAG alongside agents
weaknesses: TypeScript only; no other language SDKs mentioned
Code in ee/ directories needs an enterprise license for production use

tools.name: resume-matcher
tools.description: Resume builder that tailors a master resume to each job description
strengths: Runs locally on SQLite with no account; Ollama keeps the resume on your machine
ATS score and PDF parse check are deterministic code with documented weightings
Tailoring prompts forbid adding skills, employers or metrics absent from the master resume
weaknesses: Non-Docker setup needs Python 3.14+, Node 24.22.1 and uv
Claude CLI provider is not available inside the Docker images

tools.name: screenpipe
tools.description: Local screen and audio recorder with search, MCP server and workflow discovery
strengths: Event-driven capture pairs screenshots with accessibility text, using OCR only as fallback
Local REST API on port 3030, MCP server, JS SDK and raw SQLite access
Pipes are markdown files with per-pipe app, window and endpoint permissions
weaknesses: Source-available commercial license; commercial use requires a paid license
Free, Basic and Business plans gate some desktop app features

tools.name: OpenClaw
tools.description: Personal AI assistant reachable through Discord, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp and more
strengths: Connects to 20+ messaging channels plus native apps on five desktop and mobile platforms
Model providers and agent harnesses are plugins, with hosted and local models supported
No paid tier or hosted service; only a daily version check phones home, and it can be disabled
weaknesses: Tools run on the host for the main session unless sandboxing is configured
Prompts still go to whichever model provider and chat platforms you configure

tools.name: headroom
tools.description: Compresses tool outputs, logs and history before they reach the LLM
strengths: Seeded, offline benchmark: 21–57% fewer input tokens across four agent scenarios
One-command `headroom wrap` for many coding agents, reversible with `headroom unwrap`
Compression runs locally; reported 0.21 ms p50 on a 10K-token JSON result
weaknesses: Little savings on prose or already-dense output; gains depend on repetitive payloads
Cursor and ZCode need manual base-URL setup; Cortex Code is library-only

tools.name: ai-engineering-from-scratch
tools.description: Free curriculum of 542 coding lessons on building AI systems from scratch
strengths: Lessons ship runnable code; some start dependency-free, e.g. a vectors.py linear algebra lesson
Three staged projects with starters, reference solutions and local graders (project_test.py)
Covers math through agents, MCP and production infrastructure across 20 phases
weaknesses: 542 lessons is a large scope; the README tells readers to pick one goal path
Projects need different toolchains: Python 3.10+, Node.js 22.18+ and Rust

tools.name: docling
tools.description: Python library that converts PDFs, Office files and more into structured text
strengths: Handles a wide format list: PDF, Office, ODF, EPUB, email, calendar, audio and video
PDF layout, table structure, formula and reading-order extraction with OCR for scans
Runs locally, usable in air-gapped setups; MIT licensed
weaknesses: Model weights carry their own licenses, separate from the MIT code
Metadata extraction and chemistry understanding are listed as not yet available

tools.name: cherry-studio
tools.description: Desktop client for chatting with many LLM providers, with agents and knowledge bases
strengths: Supports many cloud providers plus Ollama and LM Studio in one app
Agents can use files, commands, browser automation, Skills and MCP servers
Local knowledge bases from files, folders and web pages, with OCR options
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0; a commercial license is needed to avoid AGPL terms
Centralized management and access controls are in the separate Enterprise Edition

tools.name: anywhere-labs/dsh-desktop
tools.description: Native Windows and macOS desktop client for DeepSeek Harness, built on plugins
strengths: Installers for Windows x64 and macOS Universal; the app starts and manages the local Harness service
Runs a pinned, unmodified upstream version, with desktop features added as plugins
Built-in plugin market and iOS/Android remote control from 2.0.9
weaknesses: No Linux build listed
Optional LAN access has no authentication; anyone on the network can operate the machine

tools.name: openai-agents-python
tools.description: Python SDK for multi-agent workflows with handoffs, guardrails and tracing
strengths: Small API: Agent and Runner cover a text agent in a few lines
Tools can be Python functions, MCP servers or hosted tools
Built-in tracing, guardrails, sessions and human-in-the-loop support
weaknesses: Examples assume OPENAI_API_KEY; non-OpenAI models go through optional LiteLLM or any-llm
Pull requests limited to repository collaborators

tools.name: FastGPT
tools.description: Visual workflow builder for knowledge-base agents and RAG apps
strengths: Knowledge base supports hybrid retrieval, reranking, QA splitting and editable chunks
Call-chain logs, citation editing and app evaluation help debug RAG answers
Two-way MCP plus hot-updatable system tools via the separate fastgpt-plugin
weaknesses: Custom license, not OSI: commercial use allowed but offering it as SaaS is not
Fuller features and support sit in a paid commercial edition

tools.name: MLflow
tools.description: Tracing, evaluation and prompt registry for LLM apps, plus ML tracking
strengths: One-line autologging for more than 60 agent frameworks and model providers
Covers both LLM tracing and evaluation and classic ML tracking and model registry
Native OpenTelemetry support; works from Python, TypeScript/JavaScript and Java
weaknesses: Broad scope across LLM and classic ML makes the surface area large to learn
Setup wizard assumes Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode is installed

tools.name: MaxKB
tools.description: Enterprise knowledge-base agent platform with RAG, workflows and MCP tools
strengths: Single docker run with all data under one mounted volume
Workflow engine with function library and MCP tool calling
Crawls online documents into the knowledge base automatically
weaknesses: GPL-3.0 limits bundling into proprietary products
Ships with default admin password MaxKB@123..

tools.name: ha-mcp
tools.description: MCP server that lets AI assistants configure and control Home Assistant
strengths: 87 tools covering automations, dashboards, helpers, areas, backups, traces and device registry
In-process integration works on OS, Supervised, Container and Core installs
Read Only Mode, per-tool enable/disable and automatic backups before edits
weaknesses: Integration requires Home Assistant 2026.8.0 or newer
Acts with an administrator token; a leaked token or secret URL grants broad access

tools.name: Ollama
tools.description: Runs open models locally through a CLI and REST API
strengths: Installs via shell script, manual download on macOS/Windows, or the ollama/ollama Docker image
REST API with a chat endpoint plus official ollama-python and ollama-js libraries
`ollama launch` connects it to coding agents and the OpenClaw assistant
weaknesses: Only llama.cpp is listed as a supported backend
Models come from the ollama.com library; custom ones need import via Modelfile

tools.name: mineru
tools.description: Parses PDFs, images and Office files into Markdown and structured JSON
strengths: Handles PDF, images, DOC/DOCX, PPT/PPTX, XLS/XLSX, EPUB, OFD, HTML and CSV inputs
Four parsing tiers trade speed against layout and OCR quality
Runs on CPU, with automatic ONNX acceleration on Intel, AMD, NVIDIA and Apple GPUs
weaknesses: 4.1 replaced the /v1/uploads and /v1/parse/jobs APIs, a breaking change for existing clients
Requires Python 3.11 to 3.14; older interpreters are unsupported

tools.name: whisper.cpp
tools.description: C/C++ speech-to-text engine running OpenAI Whisper models locally
strengths: No runtime dependencies; CPU-only inference works, with zero memory allocations at runtime
Broad backend coverage: Metal, Core ML, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, OpenVINO, CANN, MUSA, Ryzen AI NPU
Runs on macOS, iOS, Android, Linux, Windows, WebAssembly and Raspberry Pi
weaknesses: whisper-cli accepts only 16-bit WAV unless built with the FFmpeg option
Core ML, OpenVINO and ANEForge need Python-side model conversion before use

tools.name: new-api
tools.description: Gateway that unifies LLM providers behind OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs
strengths: Converts between OpenAI, Anthropic Messages and Gemini request formats via RelayKit
Channel priorities, weights, retries and multiple upstream keys per channel
Per-user quotas, subscriptions, usage logs and expression-based pricing
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 with extra terms requiring attribution and a visible project link in modified UIs
Protocol conversion is not exact; tools and fields may not map across protocols

tools.name: LocalAI
tools.description: Self-hosted model server with OpenAI, Anthropic and ElevenLabs-compatible APIs
strengths: Covers text, vision, speech, image and video models behind one API
Backends install on demand as OCI images, so unused engines are not pulled
Runs on CPU, NVIDIA CUDA 12/13, AMD ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Vulkan, Apple Silicon
weaknesses: Distributed mode requires running PostgreSQL and NATS alongside the server
Broad scope: 60+ backends and frequent releases to keep up with

tools.name: Milvus
tools.description: Distributed vector database with dense, sparse and hybrid search at scale
strengths: Index types HNSW, IVF, FLAT, SCANN, DiskANN plus GPU CAGRA
Dense, sparse (BM25, SPLADE, BGE-M3) and hybrid search in one collection
Multi-tenancy at database, collection, partition or partition-key level
weaknesses: Distributed mode is Kubernetes-native with several microservices to operate
No port, RAM or Docker command in the README; install lives in docs

tools.name: Supermemory
tools.description: Memory and context engine for AI agents, with user profiles and hybrid search
strengths: Hybrid search returns RAG documents and user memories in a single query
Handles knowledge updates and contradictions, and auto-forgets expired facts
Local server keeps data in ~/.supermemory and can use Ollama with local embeddings
weaknesses: Benchmark #1 claims are self-reported in the README, with details on a separate research page
Hosted MCP server and plugins point at supermemory.ai cloud by default

tools.name: genesis-world
tools.description: Python multi-physics simulator and renderer for robotics and physical AI research
strengths: Rigid, FEM, MPM, SPH, PBD and IPC solvers share one scene and state
Compiler backends cover CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan and CPU (x86, ARM64)
Many runnable examples: sensors (IMU, lidar, tactile), controllers, domain randomization, drones
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.12 to 3.14 and a separate PyTorch install
IPC solver (pyuipc) limited to Linux/Windows x86 with an NVIDIA GPU

tools.name: Sim
tools.description: Visual workspace for building and running AI agents and workflows
strengths: 270+ integrations with 5,400+ actions and 520+ triggers
Tables, files and knowledge bases live in the same workspace as workflows
Setup wizard with start, update, status, logs and doctor commands
weaknesses: Chat is a Sim-managed service and needs a Chat API key from sim.ai
Setup prompt in the README says the Docker stack needs 12GB+ RAM

tools.name: haystack
tools.description: Python framework for building RAG pipelines and agents from modular components
strengths: Pipelines support loops, branches and conditional routing, so context flow is explicit and traceable
Agent hooks (before_llm, before_tool, on_exit) plus step_count and token_usage tracking
Model-agnostic: many hosted providers and local models, swappable without rewriting pipelines
weaknesses: Collects anonymous component-usage telemetry by default; opt-out is documented separately
Serving as REST or MCP needs the separate Hayhooks project

tools.name: OpenShell
tools.description: Policy-enforced sandbox runtime for autonomous AI agents
strengths: Kernel-level enforcement of file, syscall and network policy per agent sandbox
Credentials are added only to requests bound for approved endpoints
Formal verification flags risky policy changes for human review
weaknesses: Native Windows support is limited; WSL 2 is marked experimental
Default sandbox image has no agent installed; you set up the agent yourself

tools.name: peft
tools.description: Python library for LoRA and other parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods
strengths: Adapter checkpoints are a few MB instead of GBs, per the T0_3B and Stable Diffusion examples
LoRA trains bigscience/mt0-xxl (12B) in 56GB GPU where full fine-tuning runs out of memory
Integrates with Transformers, Diffusers, Accelerate and TRL; installs with pip
weaknesses: Library only: no training UI, you write the loop or use Trainer or TRL
Transformers integration lacks some PEFT features, such as merging adapters into the base model

tools.name: apify-mcp-server
tools.description: Official MCP server exposing Apify Store Actors as tools for web scraping
strengths: One connection reaches thousands of Store Actors instead of a separate MCP server per site
Tool categories selectable via `tools` URL parameter, `--tools` flag or `TOOLS` env var
Hosted OAuth endpoint plus local stdio mode and an .mcpb bundle for supported clients
weaknesses: Requires an Apify account; Actors run and store results on Apify's platform, not locally
Actor runs are paid per Actor pricing; cost depends on each Actor

tools.name: SurfSense
tools.description: Desktop NotebookLM-style agent that researches and edits local documents
strengths: Index stays on your disk; no account required
Edits PDF, Word and Excel files as copies, never altering originals
Transcribes audio locally and reads scanned pages via OCR
weaknesses: Built-in plugins (Google Search, Web Crawl, etc.) need a SurfSense license; trial is 30 days
Word and PowerPoint to PDF needs LibreOffice, not included in the installer

tools.name: kornia
tools.description: Differentiable computer vision and geometry operators for PyTorch
strengths: Batched, differentiable ops that run on GPU tensors inside PyTorch training pipelines
Covers filters, augmentation, feature matching, cameras, epipolar geometry and Lie groups in one library
Publishes CPU and CUDA test pass rates and known half-precision failures per module
weaknesses: Half precision is incomplete: about 95% pass in float16 and bfloat16 on CPU
Epipolar solvers raise NotImplementedError in half precision on CPU

tools.name: browser-use
tools.description: Python library that lets an LLM agent control a web browser
strengths: Works with several LLM providers, plus local models through Ollama
Custom actions can be registered with the Tools decorator
Can reuse a local Chrome profile for authenticated sessions
weaknesses: Stealth, CAPTCHA solving and residential proxies require paid Browser Use Cloud
BU2 model needs a Browser Use API key and is not local

tools.name: RAGFlow
tools.description: RAG engine with document parsing, agentic retrieval and citations
strengths: Template-based chunking with visualization so humans can inspect and edit chunks
Citations trace answers back to source chunks
Agentic retrieval with four thinking modes for multi-step questions
weaknesses: Many services to run: MySQL, MinIO, NATS, Kvrocks and a document engine
Recommended start is 4 cores, 16 GB RAM and 50 GB disk

tools.name: MemPalace
tools.description: Local verbatim memory store for AI agents with semantic search and MCP
strengths: Stores original text verbatim; raw mode needs no LLM or API key
Pluggable backends: Chroma, SQLite exact, Rust exact, Milvus, Qdrant, pgvector
Benchmarks reproducible from the repo with committed per-question results
weaknesses: Native Termux install unsupported; Android needs a Debian PRoot container
Claude Code sessions expire in 30 days unless auto-save hooks are wired

tools.name: Multica
tools.description: Issue board where coding agent CLIs are assigned work like teammates
strengths: Drives 26 existing agent CLIs, so switching providers is a dropdown change
Code runs on your own daemon machine, not on the Multica server
Per-run execution log, cost analytics, review gates, retries and timeouts
weaknesses: Ships no model; needs at least one agent CLI installed and signed in
Custom Multica License: Apache 2.0 plus conditions on hosting, embedding, branding

tools.name: agent-browser
tools.description: Native Rust CLI that lets AI agents drive a browser via accessibility snapshots
strengths: Compact ref-based accessibility snapshots keep each agent step to one short shell call
Clicks fail explicitly when the target is hidden, disabled, or covered by a banner
Attaches to running Chrome, Lightpanda, Obscura, iOS Simulator, or cloud providers like Browserbase
weaknesses: Refs go stale after navigation or DOM changes, so agents must re-snapshot
Default setup downloads Chrome for Testing; Linux needs extra system libraries

tools.name: openmaic
tools.description: Generates interactive AI-taught classrooms from a topic or document
strengths: Per-slot model config in openmaic.yml, with fallbacks and options to lock user overrides
Exports classrooms to PPTX, a single offline HTML file, or ZIP
Generation runs server-side and continues after the browser tab closes
weaknesses: Requires PostgreSQL and a long-running Node process; Vercel and serverless unsupported since 1.2.0
Docker Compose runs single-user mode and binds to 127.0.0.1 by default

tools.name: gradio
tools.description: Python library for building web UIs around ML models and functions
strengths: Few lines of Python give a working UI; no JavaScript or CSS needed
share=True creates a public gradio.live link while compute stays local
Python and JavaScript clients can call any Gradio app programmatically
weaknesses: Blocks layouts are limited to Gradio's component set unless you write custom components
Not a hosted chat product; no user accounts or chat history described

tools.name: Onyx
tools.description: Team knowledge search and chat that indexes 50+ connected apps with permissions
strengths: Indexes 50+ connectors with source permissions, so answers respect existing access controls
Hybrid vector and keyword index plus a retrieval-tuned agent for search
Works with Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM and major hosted LLM providers
weaknesses: Standard mode needs a multi-service stack: index, workers, Redis, MinIO and model inference servers
SSO, SCIM, RBAC and analytics are in the Enterprise Edition

tools.name: nanoclaw
tools.description: Personal assistant that runs Claude agents in per-agent Linux containers behind chat apps
strengths: Agents run in Docker containers and see only explicitly mounted directories
Credential gateway injects keys at request time, with per-agent policies and rate limits
Small codebase: one host process and two SQLite files per session
weaknesses: Customization and setup recovery depend on Claude Code, not config files
Default path is built around Anthropic credentials and the Claude Agent SDK

tools.name: trl
tools.description: Python library for post-training LLMs with SFT, DPO, GRPO and KTO
strengths: Covers SFT, DPO, KTO, GRPO and reward model training behind one trainer API
Scales from one GPU to multi-node via Accelerate, DDP, DeepSpeed ZeRO and FSDP
PEFT integration allows LoRA/QLoRA training of large models on modest hardware
weaknesses: AsyncGRPOTrainer needs a separate vLLM server on a different GPU than the trainer
Features under trl.experimental may change or be removed in any release

tools.name: autoclip
tools.description: Turns a video link into short clips with covers and captions
strengths: Editing and rendering run locally; cloud is used only for chosen analysis, transcription or image steps
Same pipeline from desktop, CLI and MCP server, so agents can drive it
Works with Ollama and LM Studio for local analysis, plus OpenAI-compatible APIs
weaknesses: Desktop installers only for macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64; Intel Mac and Linux need Docker or CLI
Tuned for interviews, podcasts and talking-head video; screen recordings need vision models and manual checks

tools.name: bisheng
tools.description: Enterprise LLM app platform with visual workflows, knowledge spaces and a task agent
strengths: Workflow editor supports loops, parallel branches and batch runs in one flow with chat
RBAC plus ReBAC permissions down to single files, with department and user-group grants
Includes SSO/LDAP, approvals, audit logs and an open API with service accounts
weaknesses: Heavy install: Elasticsearch, Milvus and Onlyoffice by default; 16 GB RAM minimum
Dashboards and DSH Desktop enterprise access are commercial edition only

tools.name: Open WebUI
tools.description: Self-hosted web UI for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible models with users and RAG
strengths: Works with Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so local and cloud models mix in one UI
RBAC, user groups, LDAP, OAuth/SSO and SCIM 2.0 provisioning for multi-user deployments
RAG with hybrid BM25 plus vector search and 9 vector databases, including ChromaDB, PGVector and Qdrant
weaknesses: Custom license requires preserving Open WebUI branding; not a standard OSS license
Per-user isolated terminals are in the Enterprise edition only

tools.name: tradingagents
tools.description: Multi-agent LLM framework that simulates a trading firm's analysis process
strengths: Many providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen, Bedrock, Azure, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible
Past-dated runs read SEC EDGAR statements as filed, which avoids look-ahead in backtests
Separate provider and model for quick-think and deep-think tiers
weaknesses: Approved orders go only to a simulated exchange; no live broker execution is described
Research use only; results vary with model, temperature and data quality

tools.name: deeptutor
tools.description: Tutoring workspace with knowledge bases, guided learning, memory and quizzes
strengths: Multiple retrieval backends (LightRAG, PageIndex, GraphRAG, FAISS) and several document parsing engines
Learning features beyond chat: mastery paths, question bank, quizzes, Anki and calendar export
Multi-user accounts with per-user isolation; Docker Compose and desktop installers available
weaknesses: Very large feature surface; many settings to configure before it is useful
Fast release cadence, including a breaking front/back-end refactor in v1.6.3

tools.name: strata
tools.description: Desktop and terminal app that runs GGUF models locally with OpenAI-compatible APIs
strengths: Covers NVIDIA RTX 20-50, AMD Radeon, Intel Arc (Linux), Apple Silicon, Strix Halo and DGX Spark
Exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs for Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode and others
Desktop app plus terminal monitor showing speed, memory and recent requests
weaknesses: Documented models are limited to Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
Intel Arc support is Linux only; AMD RX 6000 support is marked experimental

tools.name: agno
tools.description: Python SDK and runtime for building and serving agents and workflows
strengths: Serves agents over REST API and MCP, with Slack and other chat interfaces
Built-in durable execution, scheduling, human approval and resume/replay
Deployment templates for Docker, AWS, GCP, Azure, Railway, Fly.io, Render, Modal, Helm
weaknesses: Management UI is the hosted os.agno.com, not a bundled self-hosted frontend
Sends a telemetry event per agent unless AGNO_TELEMETRY=false is set

tools.name: laya
tools.description: Single-pass multilingual classifier returning typed decisions with calibrated odds
strengths: Answers carry conformal prediction sets, abstain and out-of-distribution flags, and a route field
Reports 33 ms per decision on a T4 with the English checkpoint
Covers 100+ languages; vegaml mode takes images, audio, video and 73,728-token documents
weaknesses: Returns typed decisions only; it does not generate free text
In the 40-row fit example, all 20 held-out rows routed to review

tools.name: ZeroClaw
tools.description: Single-binary Rust agent runtime that answers across 30+ chat channels
strengths: Single Rust binary with one TOML config at ~/.zeroclaw/config.toml
30+ channel adapters feed the same agent loop
Default supervised autonomy, with Landlock, Bubblewrap, Seatbelt or Docker sandboxes
weaknesses: Config needs provider, agent and risk-profile sections plus schema_version = 4
YOLO mode disables safety gates, so misconfiguration risk sits with the user

tools.name: openai-python
tools.description: Official Python client for the OpenAI REST API, sync and async
strengths: Type definitions for all request params; responses are Pydantic models
Sync and async clients with identical interfaces, plus optional aiohttp transport
Workload identity auth for Kubernetes, Azure, GCP and X.509 mTLS instead of static keys
weaknesses: Client for OpenAI's hosted API; it does not run or serve models locally
Requires an OpenAI API key or workload identity credentials

tools.name: modular
tools.description: Mojo language and MAX inference framework with an OpenAI-compatible server
strengths: Includes an OpenAI-compatible inference server under max/python/max/serve
Open Mojo compute kernels and GPU programming abstractions, source available since May 2025
Models can be authored in Python on the MAX framework, with ready-made pipelines
weaknesses: Mixed licensing: parts of MAX source and binaries fall under a separate MAX license
Only some components are open source; more are being released over time

tools.name: vercel/ai
tools.description: Provider-agnostic TypeScript toolkit for text, structured output, agents and chat UIs
strengths: Single generateText API across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other providers
Typed structured output via Output.object with Zod schemas
UI hooks for React, Svelte, Vue and Angular, with Next.js route helpers
weaknesses: TypeScript and JavaScript only; requires Node.js 22+
Default model-string path goes through the Vercel AI Gateway, a hosted service

tools.name: toonflow-app
tools.description: Infinite-canvas tool for AI short drama and comic video production
strengths: Covers script, storyboard, asset and video-clip steps on a single canvas
Models are configurable: third-party APIs, local ComfyUI workflows or local LLMs
MIT license with no commercial restrictions; extensible via MCP, A2A and plugins
weaknesses: No login or auth on the web UI or API; needs a firewall or authenticated proxy
Port 3000 is fixed and not configurable

tools.name: onnx
tools.description: Open model format and operator spec for exchanging ML models between frameworks
strengths: Vendor-neutral spec with documented IR, operator set and versioning rules
Installs from PyPI; abi3 wheels work across Python 3.12 and later
Includes shape and type inference and opset version conversion utilities
weaknesses: Not a runtime; running models needs a separate inference engine
Scope is inference; training is not a focus

tools.name: pydantic-ai
tools.description: Typed Python SDK for building LLM agents across many model providers
strengths: Structured outputs, tools and dependency injection are typed and validated before your code runs
Switch providers with a model string, with fallback models when a provider fails
Durable execution integrations for Temporal, DBOS, Prefect, Restate and others
weaknesses: Python only
Memory, guardrails, sub-agents and the coding agent live in the separate Harness package

tools.name: suna
tools.description: Cloud harness that runs custom pi agents on per-session computers
strengths: Agents, skills and connectors are files in one git repo, with approval-gated change requests
Each session gets an isolated cloud computer that sleeps when idle and keeps state
Triggers include schedules, signed webhooks, connector events, Slack, Teams and email
weaknesses: License detected as NOASSERTION; free white-label use requires Platinum as exclusive compute provider
Self-host pulls images from Docker Hub and defaults to Platinum for agent sandboxes

tools.name: langbot
tools.description: Platform for running LLM agents as bots on Slack, Discord, Telegram and WeChat
strengths: Covers about a dozen chat platforms, including QQ, WeCom, DingTalk and Lark, from one deployment
Web panel for configuring and monitoring bots, so no YAML editing is needed
Connects to Dify, n8n, Coze and Langflow, and to Ollama and LM Studio for local models
weaknesses: Many supported platforms and providers are China-focused, which may matter for Western teams
Some integrations need an external service or account, such as Dify, n8n or Lark

tools.name: opensandbox
tools.description: Sandbox API for running AI agent code, commands and browsers in isolation
strengths: SDKs in five languages plus osb CLI and MCP server
Same lifecycle API for local Docker and Kubernetes deployments
Per-sandbox egress policies and a credential vault keep real secrets out of workloads
weaknesses: Docker required for local use; Kubernetes setup needed for the fast runtime
No hosted demo or playground listed in the README

tools.name: burn
tools.description: Rust tensor library and deep learning framework for training and inference
strengths: Same code trains and runs inference; no export step to ONNX or other runtimes
Backends for CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU, CPU, Wasm and no_std
Swap backends at runtime via Device; autodiff and fusion work as decorators
weaknesses: Rust only; smaller ecosystem and model zoo than PyTorch
ONNX import supports only a limited set of operators

tools.name: fathah/hermes-desktop
tools.description: Desktop GUI for installing and chatting with Hermes Agent
strengths: Guided first-run install resolves Git, uv and Python 3.11+ for the Hermes backend
Local or remote Hermes backend, with presets for Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and llama.cpp
16 messaging gateways and cron scheduling with delivery targets configurable in the UI
weaknesses: Depends on upstream Hermes Agent for all agent behavior and tool execution
Windows installer is unsigned; Fedora RPM is not GPG-signed and has no auto-update

tools.name: langchain
tools.description: Python framework for building LLM agents and apps from interoperable components
strengths: Common interface across model providers, embeddings and vector stores
Large integrations library covering tools, retrievers and vector stores
Companions: LangGraph for orchestration, Deep Agents for planning and subagents
weaknesses: Observability, evals and managed deployment sit in LangSmith, a separate product
Controllable stateful agent workflows need LangGraph, not core LangChain

tools.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
tools.description: Generates short videos from a topic, with script, footage, voiceover and subtitles
strengths: Covers the full pipeline: script, footage, voiceover, subtitles, music and render
Many LLM providers, including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and local Ollama
Edge TTS voiceover needs no API key; GPU is not required
weaknesses: Stock footage sources and AI video generators need their own API keys
Main README is Chinese-first and carries many sponsor promotions

tools.name: agent-reach
tools.description: CLI that gives coding agents read access to login-gated and Chinese web platforms
strengths: Covers Chinese platforms (Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, V2EX, Xueqiu) that generic agent search handles poorly
Per-action ordered tool list with automatic fallback when an upstream tool breaks
Read-only by design: no posting, commenting, liking or messaging
weaknesses: Twitter, Facebook and Instagram channels are labeled experimental and may break at any time
Login-gated channels copy your Chrome session, usually the main account; README advises a spare account

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: Inference engine serving LLMs with PagedAttention and an OpenAI-compatible API
strengths: Continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix caching and speculative decoding (n-gram, EAGLE and others)
Tensor, pipeline, data, expert and context parallelism for multi-GPU serving
Many quantization formats: FP8, NVFP4, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF and more
weaknesses: Aimed at server-scale deployments; distributed features need tuning knowledge
TPU, Gaudi, Ascend and other hardware run through separate plugins

tools.name: unsloth
tools.description: Desktop and web app to run and fine-tune local models
strengths: Covers both running and fine-tuning models, with export to GGUF, NVFP4 and FP8
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel GPUs, CPU and Vulkan on Windows, Linux, WSL and macOS
Free Colab and Kaggle notebooks for many models, including GRPO and TTS
weaknesses: Speed and VRAM figures (2x, 70% less) are the project's own claims
Server-side tools are on by default; exposing it needs a password or --disable-tools

tools.name: Mem0
tools.description: Long-term memory layer that stores and retrieves user facts for LLM agents
strengths: Python (pip) and npm SDKs plus a CLI, so it embeds in existing agents
Hybrid retrieval: semantic, BM25 keyword and entity linking fused in one search
Evaluation framework is open-sourced so benchmark numbers can be reproduced
weaknesses: Benchmarks reflect the managed platform; OSS results may differ
Needs an LLM; default is OpenAI gpt-5-mini and text-embedding-3-small

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: OpenAI-format gateway and Python SDK for calling 100+ LLM providers
strengths: Covers chat, responses, embeddings, images, audio, batches and rerank endpoints across many providers
Works as an in-process Python SDK or a standalone proxy server
Proxy includes virtual keys, spend tracking, guardrails and load balancing
weaknesses: Endpoint support varies per provider; the README table shows many gaps
License is detected as NOASSERTION; check the repo's license files before use

tools.name: ai-agent-book
tools.description: Open-source book on AI agent design with 109 runnable experiments
strengths: 109 experiments organized by chapter, with uv.lock for reproducible per-chapter environments
PDF and EPUB downloads plus an online reader, in 15 languages
Covers context, memory, tools, evaluation, post-training and multi-agent topics in one text
weaknesses: Chinese original is canonical; community translations may lag behind it
README says experiment code is generated by coding agents, not read line by line

tools.name: freellmapi
tools.description: OpenAI-compatible gateway pooling free-tier LLM providers with automatic failover
strengths: Per-key rate counters keep routing under each provider's free-tier caps
Covers chat, embeddings, images, video and speech, plus Anthropic and Gemini wire formats
One-command setup for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Aider and other agents
weaknesses: Free installs get new models 30 days late; same-day catalog needs $19/yr premium
Catalog updates depend on a signed feed from freellmapi.co

tools.name: nanobot
tools.description: Self-hosted personal AI agent reachable from browser, terminal and chat apps
strengths: Many channels: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, Email, Mattermost, Linear, Feishu, Teams
Built-in MCP, cron automations, long-running goals and PDF/Office file tools
Also usable as a Python SDK and OpenAI-compatible HTTP API
weaknesses: Supplies no model; needs a provider account or local model server
Background gateway does not restart after reboot or crash without an OS service

tools.name: AstrBot
tools.description: Agent chatbot platform connecting LLMs to QQ, Telegram, Slack and other chat apps
strengths: Official adapters for 15 messaging platforms, including QQ, Telegram, Slack, Discord, LINE and Feishu
Works with OpenAI-compatible APIs, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and LM Studio, plus Dify, Coze and Bailian
Speech-to-text and text-to-speech integrations such as Whisper, SenseVoice, Edge TTS and FishAudio
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license carries copyleft obligations for network-hosted modifications
Platform list leans toward Chinese services such as QQ and WeChat

tools.name: deepspeed
tools.description: PyTorch library for distributed training of very large models with ZeRO
strengths: Used to train models such as BLOOM 176B and Megatron-Turing NLG 530B
Integrates with Hugging Face Transformers and Accelerate, Lightning, Composer and Determined
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel Gaudi and XPU, Huawei Ascend NPU and CPU accelerators
weaknesses: PyTorch must be installed first, and a CUDA or ROCm compiler is needed for JIT ops
Windows lacks async IO and GDS support

tools.name: llmfit
tools.description: Terminal tool that checks which LLMs and quantizations fit your hardware
strengths: Detects NVIDIA, AMD, Apple Silicon and Intel accelerators, including multi-GPU and unified memory
Handles MoE models and GGUF, AWQ, GPTQ and EXL2 quantizations in estimates
JSON CLI output and REST endpoints (/api/v1/system, /api/v1/models) suit scripts and pipelines
weaknesses: Speed and memory figures are estimates unless you benchmark on your own hardware
Cluster mode for Ray is a preview, tested only against a mock dashboard

tools.name: Obscura
tools.description: Headless browser engine in Rust with V8 and a Chrome DevTools Protocol server
strengths: Puppeteer and Playwright connect over CDP, so existing scripts need little change
README reports ~30 MB memory and ~70 MiB binary, versus 200+ MB for headless Chrome
Renders CSS layout, screenshots and PDFs without Chromium
weaknesses: Independent rendering engine; long-tail CSS, some Web APIs and media playback differ from Chromium
Stealth transport needs a separate build or archive plus CMake and Clang to compile

tools.name: diffusers
tools.description: PyTorch library of diffusion pipelines and schedulers for image generation
strengths: Loads any of 30,000+ Hub checkpoints with a few lines via from_pretrained
Schedulers, models and pipelines are separate, so custom sampling loops are possible
Docs include training and memory/speed optimization guides
weaknesses: Library only: no web UI or HTTP server included
README documents PyTorch installs only

tools.name: Cognee
tools.description: Long-term memory engine that builds a knowledge graph from documents, code and sessions
strengths: Keyless local mode: GLiNER extraction and local embeddings, no LLM API key required
Four-call API (remember, recall, improve, forget) in Python, CLI, REST, TypeScript and Rust
Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw, plus an MCP server
weaknesses: Postgres-only graph store is labelled a demo; production version is a licensed product
Bundled GLiNER extractor is a demo; the more accurate version requires contacting the vendor

tools.name: Graphiti
tools.description: Python framework for building temporal knowledge graphs for agent memory
strengths: Facts carry validity windows; old facts are invalidated, not deleted, enabling point-in-time queries
Incremental ingestion with no full graph recompute; every fact traces to its source episode
Custom entity and edge types defined as Pydantic models, or learned from data
weaknesses: Needs a separately run graph database; no built-in storage
Defaults to OpenAI; needs structured-output LLMs, and smaller models can fail ingestion

tools.name: meetily
tools.description: Desktop app that records, transcribes and summarizes meetings locally
strengths: Local Whisper or Parakeet transcription; audio never leaves the machine
Summary providers include Ollama, Claude, Groq, OpenRouter, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Records microphone and system audio together, with ducking and clipping prevention
weaknesses: Speaker identification, custom templates, and PDF/DOCX export are only in paid PRO
Prebuilt installers cover Windows and Apple Silicon macOS only; Linux needs a source build

tools.name: deepagents
tools.description: Python agent harness on LangGraph with sub-agents, filesystem and context management
strengths: Sub-agents run with isolated context windows; any LangGraph CompiledStateGraph can be a sub-agent
Works with any tool-calling LangChain chat model, including Ollama, vLLM and llama.cpp
Filesystem and memory backends are pluggable: local, sandboxed or remote
weaknesses: Follows a trust-the-LLM model; boundaries must be enforced in tools or sandbox
Tracing, evaluation and deployment integrations point to LangSmith, a separate product

tools.name: mlx
tools.description: NumPy-style array framework for machine learning on Apple silicon
strengths: Python API follows NumPy; mlx.nn and mlx.optimizers follow PyTorch
Unified memory: CPU and GPU ops share arrays without transfers
Composable transforms for autodiff, vectorization and graph optimization
weaknesses: Designed for Apple silicon; Linux CUDA and CPU backends are add-on installs
Example models live in a separate mlx-examples repo

tools.name: InvokeAI
tools.description: Web UI for diffusion image generation with inpainting canvas and node workflows
strengths: Unified Canvas with in/out-painting and brush tools for iterative editing
Node-based workflow editor for building and sharing generation pipelines
Broad model list: SD 1.5 through Flux.2, Qwen Image, Z-Image, SAM/SAM2 segmentation
weaknesses: README gives no RAM, VRAM or GPU requirements
Nano Banana, GPT Image and Wan are API-only, not local

tools.name: flash-attention
tools.description: Fused GPU kernels for exact attention in PyTorch, FlashAttention 2 through 4
strengths: Official reference implementation with papers for FA1, FA2 and FA3
Covers NVIDIA (Ampere, Ada, Hopper, Blackwell via FA4) and AMD ROCm (CK and Triton backends)
Decoding-oriented API: in-place KV cache update, rotary, paged cache, GQA/MQA
weaknesses: Source build is slow without ninja: about 2h versus 3-5 minutes on 64 cores
FA3 is a beta, requires H100/H800 and CUDA 12.3 or newer

tools.name: eliza
tools.description: Specification workspace for Eliza v4, an on-device agent OS built on Vibestack
strengths: Formal specs with Quint models and Dafny proofs of safety obligations
Generated contracts and replay checks run through pnpm check and pnpm verify
MIT licensed, with recent commits and a release in November 2026
weaknesses: README covers specification and contributor workflow, not installing or running an assistant
Requires Node 26, pnpm 10.24.0 and Dafny 4.11, a narrow toolchain

tools.name: experiential
tools.description: OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway with per-user budgets and traffic-trained routers
strengths: Install with pip and start with `exp`; local gateway listens on 127.0.0.1:8000
Per-identity model access and budgets (setup wizard defaults to a $50.00 budget)
Builds a router from OTLP traces and can fine-tune a model from them
weaknesses: Traffic capture is experimental, macOS only, needs Python 3.13+, and has reliability issues
Model fine-tuning depends on the external Tinker service

tools.name: megatron-lm
tools.description: NVIDIA's library for training large transformer models across many GPUs
strengths: Supports TP, PP, DP, EP and CP parallelism in one library
Mixed precision from FP16 and BF16 down to FP8 and FP4
Distributed checkpointing with resharding, plus MoE and hybrid model support
weaknesses: Aimed at multi-GPU clusters; no small-scale or CPU workflow described
Source builds can run out of memory and need MAX_JOBS tuning

tools.name: pipecat
tools.description: Python framework for real-time voice and multimodal agent pipelines
strengths: Many pluggable services: 23 STT, 25 LLM and 30+ TTS providers listed, including local Whisper and Ollama
Official client SDKs for JS, React, React Native, Swift, Kotlin, C++ and ESP32
Structured conversation flows (Pipecat Flows) built in, plus Whisker debugger and Tail dashboard
weaknesses: Library, not a ready app: you write Python pipeline code to get a working bot
Most listed STT, LLM and TTS services are hosted APIs needing separate keys

tools.name: xiaohongshu-mcp
tools.description: MCP server that lets AI clients post, search and comment on Xiaohongshu
strengths: Covers publishing, search, comments, likes, favorites and profiles as MCP tools
Prebuilt binaries for macOS arm64, Windows x64 and Linux x64, plus Docker images
Optional Bearer token auth via AUTH_TOKEN and optional proxy via XHS_PROXY
weaknesses: Automates the web UI, so site changes or risk controls can break posting
One account cannot stay logged in on other web clients without kicking the MCP session

tools.name: nanobrowser
tools.description: Browser agent in a Chrome/Edge side panel that clicks and types for you
strengths: Per-site Allow/Ask/Block rules; Ask mode confirms submit, send, delete and upload
Supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral, Ollama and LM Studio
Several tasks run in parallel, each in its own tab group
weaknesses: Only Chrome and Edge are supported; other browsers are untested
Models must support tool calling; local models suit only simple tasks

tools.name: llm-gateway
tools.description: OpenAI-compatible gateway routing requests across providers, subscriptions, local models
strengths: Supports 35 provider connections plus any custom /v1/chat/completions or /v1/messages endpoint
Can route through 18 subscription flows (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot), not only API keys
Connects local runtimes: Ollama, LM Studio (port 1234), llama.cpp (port 8080)
weaknesses: Self-hosting is Docker-only; the npm-based path is no longer supported
Volume-backed templates are single-instance; scaling out needs S3-compatible storage

tools.name: Hermes Agent
tools.description: Self-hosted agent with skill learning, memory and Telegram/Discord/Slack gateway
strengths: One gateway process serves Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and email with shared history
Seven terminal backends, including Docker, SSH, Modal, Daytona and Vercel Sandbox
Built-in cron scheduler, FTS5 session search and agent-created skills compatible with agentskills.io
weaknesses: Windows installer may trigger antivirus false positives on the bundled uv.exe
Installs via a curl-piped shell script rather than a pinned package on desktop

tools.name: markitdown
tools.description: Python library and CLI that converts office files, PDFs and audio to Markdown
strengths: Covers many formats (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, EPub, ZIP, YouTube) through one convert call
Built-in converters run offline; install only needed formats via extras like [pdf,docx,pptx]
Plugin system, plus a markitdown-ocr plugin that uses an LLM vision client for embedded images
weaknesses: Not meant for high-fidelity conversion for human reading, per the README
Runs with the calling process's privileges; untrusted input must be sanitized by the caller

tools.name: LobeHub
tools.description: Multi-agent chat workspace connected to team IM apps and 40+ model providers
strengths: Compose stack bundles Postgres, Redis, file storage and SearXNG search
Setup guides for 40+ model providers, including local models
Channels connect agents to Discord, Slack, Telegram, LINE, QQ, WeChat, Feishu, Lark
weaknesses: Self-hosting needs several services; Vercel deploy needs Postgres and S3-compatible storage
README says the project is under active development

tools.name: cowagent
tools.description: Agent assistant you chat with via web console, Telegram, Slack and more
strengths: Many channels in one instance, including Telegram, Slack, Discord and Chinese IM platforms
Native MCP support via mcp.json (stdio, SSE) plus a skill marketplace
Three-tier memory with hybrid keyword and vector retrieval and a Markdown knowledge base
weaknesses: README warns agent mode uses substantially more tokens than regular chat
Local models only through a generic Custom provider, chat only

tools.name: ifixai
tools.description: Audits AI agents for policy violations in a simulated business environment
strengths: Every finding shows the request and what the agent did, so results are checkable
Judge is chosen from a different provider than the agent under test
Mock provider lets you try the full flow without any API key
weaknesses: Probes are real requests, so it must be pointed at a staging copy of the agent
Grading depends on an external LLM judge, which adds API cost and judge variance

tools.name: langgraph
tools.description: Python framework for building long-running, stateful agents as graphs
strengths: Durable execution resumes agents from where they stopped after a failure
Interrupts allow inspecting and modifying agent state mid-run
Built-in short-term and long-term memory across sessions
weaknesses: Low-level API; higher-level agent building is pushed to the separate Deep Agents package
Tracing UI and managed deployment rely on LangSmith, a commercial LangChain product

tools.name: artcraft
tools.description: Desktop app for staging 2D and 3D scenes before generating images and video
strengths: 3D scene staging, character posing and camera placement before generation
Large catalog: 62 ArtCraft-listed models across image, video, audio, 3D and worlds
Canvas tools for masks, inpainting, background removal and layer compositing
weaknesses: Generation uses hosted providers; no local model inference is described
Some catalog models are disabled or restricted in the desktop app

tools.name: marker
tools.description: Converts PDFs, Office files and images to markdown, JSON, HTML or chunks
strengths: Outputs markdown, JSON with block polygons, HTML or chunks from one pipeline
Fast mode and --disable_ocr allow CPU-only, text-layer extraction
Extensible processors, converters and block API for custom logic
weaknesses: Model weights use a modified OpenRAIL-M license with revenue limits for commercial use
Needs Docker with NVIDIA Container Toolkit, or llama.cpp, for the VLM server

tools.name: quivr
tools.description: Headless engine that stores, searches and alerts on incoming documents
strengths: Keeps every document version; withdrawn documents leave search at once and alerts are told
Results cite the exact passage, document and version
Formats, sources, embeddings, ranking and alerts are HTTP plugins in any language
weaknesses: No user interface; the web demo is a separate app on the public API
Local setup needs Docker Compose v2, Go, Python 3.12, jq and about 1 GB download

tools.name: vibe-trading
tools.description: Finance research agent for backtests, paper trading and broker-linked execution
strengths: 28 market-data sources with per-market fallback chains (Tencent, Yahoo, OKX, Binance)
Backtest engines model A-share price limits, crypto funding and futures margin
Alpha Zoo benchmarks Qlib, Alpha101 and GTJA factors with walk-forward checks
weaknesses: Many recent fixes are on main only, not in the latest pip release
Gildata financial features are opt-in and need a separate token

tools.name: mediapipe
tools.description: On-device ML task APIs and a C++ pipeline framework for mobile, web and desktop
strengths: Prebuilt Tasks for vision, audio, text, retrieval and LLM inference, with ready-to-run models
Targets Android, iOS, web, Python and C++ from one project
Input data stays on device; no images, video or text sent to Google servers
weaknesses: Tasks APIs send performance and usage metrics to Google; app developers must obtain user consent
Framework layer requires learning packets, graphs and calculators, and a C++ build setup

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: LLM tracing, evaluation, prompt management and cost tracking for agent apps
strengths: Built on OpenTelemetry, so any OTLP-instrumented app or collector can send traces
Python and JS/TS SDKs plus integrations for LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, LiteLLM and others
Covers tracing, prompt versioning, evals, datasets and dashboards in one platform
weaknesses: Docker Compose suits a single machine or VM; Helm is the preferred production path
AI Gateway and Skill Management are marked beta

tools.name: block/buzz
tools.description: Self-hosted team workspace where humans and agents share channels on a Nostr relay
strengths: Agents are scoped by their own keypair, channel membership and audit trail, like human members
Production Compose bundle with Postgres, Redis, MinIO and optional Caddy TLS for a single-node relay
buzz-cli is JSON in, JSON out; ACP harness supports Goose, Codex and Claude Code
weaknesses: Mobile clients, workflow approval gates and huddle lifecycle events are still being wired up
Push notifications and cross-relay reputation are not implemented yet

tools.name: netron
tools.description: Viewer for neural network and machine learning model graphs
strengths: Covers many formats: ONNX, TFLite, PyTorch, Core ML, OpenVINO, Keras, Safetensors and more
Hosted browser version at netron.app can open a model from a URL
Also ships as macOS, Linux and Windows installers and a pip package
weaknesses: GGUF, MLIR, JAX, ncnn, MNN, PaddlePaddle and scikit-learn support is experimental
Viewer only: does not edit, convert or run models

tools.name: dsh-go
tools.description: Android client for DeepSeek Harness, local or remote
strengths: Runs the DSH engine on-device via a bundled Ubuntu runtime, no root or Termux
Can switch to DSH on a PC or server over SSH or DSHarness Remote
Phone control reads the screen and taps, with three confirmation levels
weaknesses: Android 8+ only; iOS and HarmonyOS are not yet supported
Model requests still go to a configured provider; local run is not offline

tools.name: GPT Researcher
tools.description: Research agent that writes cited reports from web and local documents
strengths: Works on web sources and local PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, PowerPoint and Markdown files
Usable as a web app, a pip package, or a Claude skill
Recursive deep research mode with configurable depth and breadth, about $0.4 per run
weaknesses: Needs an LLM API key and a search key such as Tavily; no offline setup documented
Default context filter (Jev) is a hosted service requiring TYPESAFE_API_KEY

tools.name: page-agent
tools.description: In-page JavaScript agent that operates a web page from natural language
strengths: Runs as in-page JavaScript; no Python, headless browser or extension required
Text-based DOM control, so no screenshots or vision-capable model needed
Bring your own LLM via baseURL and apiKey, including local models
weaknesses: Single-page scope by default; multi-page tasks need the Chrome extension
Designed for client-side page enhancement, not server-side automation

tools.name: budibase
tools.description: Low-code platform for internal apps, automations and AI agents
strengths: Agents, internal apps and automations are built in one platform
Self-host via Docker (ARM image), Compose, Kubernetes, DigitalOcean or Portainer
Public API with interactive docs lets it act as a backend
weaknesses: Mixed licensing: GPL v3 core, MPL client, paid features under Business Source License
Agent features are described in general terms, with no concrete capability list

tools.name: openwork
tools.description: Desktop app where OpenCode-based agents work on your local files
strengths: Runs on macOS, Windows and Linux; files stay local, cloud is optional
Works with 50+ providers, own API keys, Ollama or OpenAI-compatible servers
OpenWork MCP exposes four tools to Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and other clients
weaknesses: Den control plane (ee/) is source-available; production use above 5 users needs a subscription
Shared MCP endpoint is hosted at api.openworklabs.com and needs browser sign-in

tools.name: omlx
tools.description: MLX-based LLM server for Apple Silicon with tiered KV cache and menu bar app
strengths: Hot RAM and cold SSD KV cache persists across requests and server restarts
OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible endpoints, plus embeddings, rerank and audio transcription
Per-model pinning, TTL, LRU eviction and a memory limit (default system RAM minus 8GB)
weaknesses: Apple Silicon and macOS 15+ only; no Linux or Windows server
Native custom kernels need full Xcode; GLM-5.2, MiniMax M3, Qwen3.5 are much slower without them

tools.name: deepface
tools.description: Python library for face verification, search and age/gender/emotion analysis
strengths: Single-call API for verify, find, analyze, represent and extract_faces
Wraps 10 recognition models and many detectors, switchable by argument
ONNX Runtime default keeps the install to a few hundred MB
weaknesses: Race and gender prediction raise bias and ethics concerns in production use
Defaults are VGG-Face and the OpenCV detector, not the most accurate options

tools.name: Skyvern
tools.description: Browser automation agent using vision LLMs, with a Playwright-compatible SDK
strengths: Playwright-compatible SDK; selector, AI, or selector-with-AI-fallback modes per action
Python and TypeScript SDKs plus a visual workflow builder
Can attach to your own Chrome via CDP, keeping existing logins and cookies
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license restricts closed-source network use
Web UI not in the pip package; needs Docker Compose or a source checkout

tools.name: Opik
tools.description: LLM tracing, evaluation and prompt management platform for agents and LLM apps
strengths: Full platform, backend included, is Apache-2.0 and self-hostable without a commercial license
Accepts traces via Python/TypeScript SDKs, OpenTelemetry, and many framework integrations
Evaluation built in: datasets, experiments, LLM-judge metrics, PyTest integration for CI
weaknesses: Local self-host runs several containers (databases, backend, UI), heavier than a single binary
Docker Compose path is described for local development and testing, not production

tools.name: adk-python
tools.description: Code-first Python framework for building and deploying multi-agent apps
strengths: Graph Workflow runtime with fan-out/fan-in, loops, retry, nested workflows and human-in-the-loop
CLI covers running, web UI testing, eval sets and deployment
Tools from plain functions, OpenAPI specs and MCP, plus a tool confirmation flow
weaknesses: Documented deploy paths and defaults lean toward Gemini and Google Cloud
Requires Python 3.11 or newer

tools.name: parlant
tools.description: Python framework for customer-facing agents that follow policies
strengths: Plain-language policies; only the relevant ones are put in front of the model each turn
Optional validation of replies and of tool calls such as refunds before they run
Supports OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, LiteLLM and custom providers, no inference markup
weaknesses: Agent behavior must be written in Python; other stacks reach it only over HTTP
Hosting, testing and analytics Dashboard is a flat monthly fee beyond development use

tools.name: cvat
tools.description: Self-hosted annotation tool for image, video, audio and 3D point cloud datasets
strengths: Covers image, video, audio and 3D point cloud annotation in one tool
Exports and imports 20+ formats including COCO, YOLO, Pascal VOC and KITTI
Python SDK, CLI and REST API for scripting task creation and exports
weaknesses: Auto-annotation needs a separate Nuclio serverless stack and manual nuctl function deployment
Built-in SAM 2/SAM 3 labeling, SSO and quality control UI are paid-only

tools.name: livekit/agents
tools.description: Python framework for realtime voice and multimodal agents on LiveKit WebRTC
strengths: Mix STT, LLM, TTS or realtime APIs via plugins (OpenAI, Deepgram, Cartesia, Google)
Built-in job dispatch and AgentServer for scheduling sessions across processes
Telephony via LiveKit SIP for inbound and outbound calls
weaknesses: Needs a LiveKit server (Cloud or self-hosted) and credentials beyond console mode
README examples default to LiveKit Inference, a LiveKit Cloud service

tools.name: copilotkit/openbot
tools.description: Self-hosted team assistant where each bot gets its own browser and audited actions
strengths: Per-Bot container with own browser profile and workspace volume, optional gVisor (runsc) runtime
Single gateway applies CEL deny/allow policy and logs every action; refusals name the rule
Works with any AG-UI endpoint: LangGraph, Mastra, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, Google ADK or custom
weaknesses: Marked alpha; README warns of rough edges and changing behavior
Requires a CopilotKit Intelligence project and license for threads and memory

tools.name: inbox-zero
tools.description: AI assistant that sorts Gmail and Outlook, drafts replies, and files attachments
strengths: Supports both Gmail and Outlook, with rules written in plain English
Chat control from Slack or Telegram
Local dev mode needs no OAuth credentials or AI API keys
weaknesses: License is detected as NOASSERTION, so terms need manual checking
Real use needs your own Google or Microsoft OAuth setup

tools.name: axolotl
tools.description: YAML-driven fine-tuning framework for LLMs with LoRA, QLoRA, RL and multi-GPU
strengths: One YAML config reused across preprocessing, training, evaluation, quantization and inference
Broad methods: full FT, LoRA/QLoRA, QAT, DPO/KTO/ORPO, GRPO, reward models
Multi-GPU and multi-node via FSDP2, DeepSpeed, Torchrun and Ray, plus context and expert parallelism
weaknesses: Requires NVIDIA (Ampere or newer for bf16) or AMD GPU; no CPU path stated
Needs Python 3.12+ and PyTorch 2.13+, a narrow environment

tools.name: cocoindex
tools.description: Incremental Python pipelines that keep vector indexes and agent context fresh
strengths: Memoization keyed on input and code hash re-embeds only changed files
Pipelines are plain Python functions, not a DAG or YAML config
Per-row lineage traces target vectors back to source content
weaknesses: Library only: no UI, you write and run the pipeline code yourself
Python 3.10-3.13 supported; other languages are not mentioned

tools.name: rf-detr
tools.description: Real-time transformer models for object detection, segmentation and keypoints
strengths: Detection, segmentation and keypoints share one Python API across Nano to 2XLarge sizes
Apache 2.0 for the package and N/S/M/L detection and all segmentation models
README benchmarks on COCO and RF100-VL, with T4 TensorRT FP16 latency per size
weaknesses: Atto, Femto, Pico, XL and 2XL detection models use PML 1.0, not Apache 2.0
Keypoint detection is labeled preview

tools.name: Xinference
tools.description: Serves LLM, embedding, speech and image models behind an OpenAI-compatible API
strengths: Covers LLM, embedding, audio, image and multimodal models in one server
OpenAI-compatible REST API with function calling, plus CLI, RPC and web UI
Distributed multi-node deployment; Docker image and Helm chart for Kubernetes
weaknesses: README gives no RAM or VRAM requirements; sizing depends on the chosen model
Docker instructions target Nvidia GPUs; other accelerators are not described in the README

tools.name: Morphic
tools.description: AI answer engine with cited search results and generative UI components
strengths: Docker Compose bundles SearXNG, so no search API key is required
Many model providers, including local Ollama and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Four search backends: Tavily, SearXNG, Brave, Exa
weaknesses: Compose stack needs PostgreSQL, Redis and SearXNG alongside the app
Needs at least one model provider API key or a local Ollama setup

tools.name: davinci-resolve-mcp
tools.description: MCP server that lets AI assistants drive DaVinci Resolve via its scripting API
strengths: Compound mode groups operations into 37 tools; full mode exposes 390, one per API method
Optional Node server edits .drp, .drt and .drx files offline, without Resolve running
Tool results include an _operation block with status, readback verification and change deltas
weaknesses: External scripting needs Resolve Studio; the free edition relies on an in-app bridge
Free-edition bridge is a 21.0.x path; on 21.1 Python scripts no longer list

tools.name: ComfyUI
tools.description: Node-graph editor for running diffusion image, video, audio and 3D workflows
strengths: Native support for many models: SDXL, Flux, Wan 2.x, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo, ACE-Step
README claims large models run on 4GB VRAM with 8GB RAM via weight streaming
Desktop app, Windows portable builds, comfy-cli and manual install; NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple GPUs
weaknesses: Node graph has a learning curve compared with form-based generation UIs
Commits between stable tags may be unstable and break many custom nodes

tools.name: Paperclip
tools.description: Task manager and org chart for coordinating teams of AI coding agents
strengths: Works with many agent runtimes via adapters, plus custom processes and HTTP endpoints
Budgets per company, agent and project with warning thresholds and hard stops
Atomic task checkout with execution locks prevents two runs claiming one task
weaknesses: Does not run models itself; needs separately configured agents and provider access
