Budget stops rely on reported spend, so in-flight work can overrun limits

tools.name: Crawl4AI
tools.description: Async Python web crawler that outputs LLM-ready Markdown and structured JSON
strengths: Schema-based CSS/XPath extraction works without any LLM call
Fit Markdown filters (pruning, BM25, LLM) strip menus and boilerplate
Deep crawl with BFS, DFS and score-ordered strategies, resumable after crashes
weaknesses: Search, SERP and answer endpoints exist only in the hosted cloud
Self-hosted bot-wall handling relies on your own proxies and settings

tools.name: colibri
tools.description: C inference engine that streams MoE experts from disk to run huge models
strengths: Runs models up to 2.8T parameters on CPU only, with disk streaming of experts
One-step setup script picks a model that fits RAM and disk, and resumes downloads
Exposes OpenAI and Anthropic base URLs, plus an MCP server for setup
weaknesses: Large models are slow: GLM-5.2 0.05-0.1 tok/s cold on a 25 GB laptop
Downloads are big: 23 GB for the smallest chat model, 1.56 TB for Kimi K3

tools.name: ray
tools.description: Distributed Python runtime with libraries for data, training, tuning, RL and serving
strengths: One runtime covers data loading, training, tuning, RL and serving in Python
Core primitives are small: tasks, actors and objects, for scaling arbitrary Python code
Runs on a laptop, any cluster, cloud providers and Kubernetes
weaknesses: Python-centric; the README offers no path for non-Python applications
Several libraries to learn (Core, Data, Train, Tune, RLlib, Serve) before productive use

tools.name: prompt-optimizer
tools.description: Prompt optimization and testing workspace with model comparison and an MCP server
strengths: Arena compares one prompt across multiple models side by side
Ships as web, desktop, Chrome extension, Docker and MCP server
App data stays in the browser or locally; model calls go to your provider
weaknesses: Browser builds hit CORS limits with many providers; desktop app or proxy needed
VITE_* API keys are exposed in browser assets on public deployments

tools.name: Qdrant
tools.description: Rust vector database with payload filtering, REST and gRPC
strengths: Dense, sparse and multivector (ColBERT) search with RRF and DBSF fusion
Quantization cuts RAM up to 97 percent; on-disk storage and io_uring
REST with OpenAPI 3.0 spec plus gRPC; six official clients
weaknesses: Default docker run has no auth and binds all interfaces
GPU acceleration covers indexing only; search runs on CPU

tools.name: aionui
tools.description: Desktop and WebUI app that runs a built-in agent plus external CLI agents
strengths: Auto-detects installed CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code and others) in one interface
Built-in agent works after pasting an API key, with no separate CLI install
Scheduled tasks support cron with timezone, fixed intervals and one-time triggers
weaknesses: Local models are reached through a custom API endpoint, not a bundled runtime
Slack, Discord and WeCom channels are listed as coming soon

tools.name: promptfoo
tools.description: CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps
strengths: Evals run locally, so prompts stay on your machine
Installs via npm, brew or pip; npx runs it without installing
Covers both quality evals and red-team scans in one tool
weaknesses: Most providers need an API key from the vendor
Project is now part of OpenAI, though README says it stays MIT

tools.name: ag-ui
tools.description: Event-based protocol connecting agent backends to user-facing apps
strengths: Transport-agnostic: SSE, WebSockets or webhooks, with loose event format matching
Many framework integrations: LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno
Community SDKs for Kotlin, Go, Dart, Java, Rust, Ruby, C++ and .NET
weaknesses: A protocol, not an agent runtime; you still need an agent framework and a UI client
OpenAI Agents SDK, AWS Bedrock Agents, Nim, Flowise and Langflow integrations are still in progress

tools.name: trigger.dev
tools.description: TypeScript platform for durable background tasks and AI agent workflows
strengths: Tasks have no timeouts, with checkpointing and automatic retries for long AI jobs
Waitpoints pause a run until a human approves, rejects or gives feedback
Realtime API and React hooks stream run state and LLM output to the frontend
weaknesses: Code-first and TypeScript/JavaScript only; no visual workflow builder
Managed cloud is the primary path; self-hosting needs extra setup and services

tools.name: tensorrt-llm
tools.description: NVIDIA inference engine for LLMs and diffusion models with custom CUDA kernels
strengths: Kernel and parallelism work for Blackwell, NVL72 and NVLink-based expert parallelism
Documents speculative decoding, disaggregated serving, guided decoding and KV cache reuse
Day-0 support for models such as GPT-OSS and EXAONE 4.0 is documented
weaknesses: Tied to NVIDIA GPUs, CUDA 13.4.1 and PyTorch 2.14.0
Current version shown is a release candidate (1.4.0rc1)

tools.name: instructor
tools.description: Python library that returns validated Pydantic objects from LLM calls
strengths: Same from_provider call works across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq and Ollama
Automatic retries feed Pydantic validation errors back to the model via max_retries
Streams partial objects with Partial[Model], including nested models
weaknesses: Scoped to structured extraction; no agent runtime, README points to PydanticAI for that
Retries add extra LLM calls, so cost and latency rise on failed validations

tools.name: assistant-ui
tools.description: React library of chat UI primitives for building AI chat interfaces
strengths: Unstyled primitives let you build custom chat layouts instead of one fixed component
Runtime adapters for AI SDK, LangGraph, AG-UI, A2A, Google ADK and custom backends
Renders tool calls as React components with inline human approval
weaknesses: Frontend only: you supply the model backend and API routes yourself
React and TypeScript only; no other UI framework is listed

tools.name: lmcache
tools.description: KV cache offloading and reuse layer for LLM serving engines
strengths: Runs as a separate daemon, so KV cache survives inference engine crashes
Backends include CPU RAM, disk, Redis/Valkey, Mooncake, S3-compatible, NIXL and GDS
Non-prefix KV reuse at any prompt position through CacheBlend
weaknesses: Not a standalone server; it needs a supported serving engine in front
README gives no hardware requirements or supported-engine version list

tools.name: arize-ai/phoenix
tools.description: LLM tracing, evaluation and prompt management built on OpenTelemetry
strengths: Auto-instrumentation via OpenInference for OpenAI, Anthropic, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, DSPy and others
Starts with pip install arize-phoenix and phoenix serve, or uvx arize-phoenix serve
Covers tracing, evals, datasets, experiments and prompt versioning in one server
weaknesses: License is reported as NOASSERTION, so terms need checking before commercial use
Managed production workflows are offered through the separate Arize AX product

tools.name: anarlog
tools.description: Local-first meeting notetaker that records device audio without a bot joining
strengths: No meeting bot; audio is captured on the device
Transcription and LLM providers can be swapped independently
Notes and transcripts in local SQLite; Markdown export
weaknesses: On-device transcription is described only for supported Macs
Building from source needs Node 22, pnpm, Rust 1.94, process-compose, Tauri deps

tools.name: rakazo
tools.description: Self-hosted AI assistant with persistent bots on sandboxed computers
strengths: Bots can delegate to peer bots or short-lived subagents
Installer script sets up the Docker Compose stack with random secrets, no clone needed
Web, Electron, iOS and Android clients share one API
weaknesses: Marked beta by the project
Needs Docker with Compose and PostgreSQL; heavier than a single binary

tools.name: xiaobei
tools.description: Self-media marketing agent team on openclaw, controlled through WeChat
strengths: Drafts and publishes across WeChat, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, TikTok, X and Weibo
Crews such as content-producer and it-engineer delegate to each other without user prompts
Smart-search covers 18 source types with no API key required
weaknesses: License is NOASSERTION with a custom LICENSE file, so reuse terms need checking
Defaults to Alibaba Bailian cloud models; README describes no local model setup

tools.name: isaaclab
tools.description: Robot learning framework for RL and imitation learning in GPU simulation
strengths: More than 30 ready-to-train environments and 16+ robot models, from manipulators to humanoids
Works with RSL RL, SKRL, RL Games and Stable Baselines, and supports multi-agent RL
Sensor simulation covers RTX cameras, LIDAR, IMU, contact sensors and ray casters
weaknesses: Isaac Sim workflows need a matching Isaac Sim version (6.2 for main) and carry proprietary license terms
The isaaclab_mimic extension is Apache 2.0 and requires cuRobo, which is proprietary

tools.name: ai-infra-guard
tools.description: Red-teaming platform for AI infra CVEs, MCP servers, agent skills and jailbreaks
strengths: Fingerprints 100+ AI components (Ollama, vLLM, ComfyUI, n8n, Triton) against 2000+ CVE rules
Covers infra CVEs, MCP and skill scanning, and jailbreak evaluation in one web UI
Separate CLIs such as pip-installable aig-skill-scan fit into CI/CD pipelines
weaknesses: No authentication; README says not to deploy on public networks
Skill scanning needs an external LLM API key

tools.name: arcreel
tools.description: Self-hosted workbench that turns novels or scripts into short videos
strengths: Reuses asset reference images across storyboards to keep characters consistent
Stages can be confirmed, single assets regenerated, and versions rolled back
Shows estimated and actual cost per generation
weaknesses: Generation depends on external provider APIs that you configure and pay for
Jianying export targets the mainland China version; CapCut compatibility not verified

tools.name: decepticon
tools.description: Autonomous red-team agents that run multi-stage attack chains from an approved plan
strengths: Reports 102/104 (98.08%) on XBOW validation benchmarks, with per-challenge results published
Persistent tmux sessions let interactive tools like msfconsole and evil-winrm work
Kali sandbox runs on its own network, separate from the management plane
weaknesses: Needs Docker Compose with several services: LiteLLM, PostgreSQL, Neo4j, LangGraph, sandbox
LangGraph drives the sandbox through the Docker socket, which widens host exposure

tools.name: excel-mcp-server
tools.description: MCP server that lets AI clients create and edit Excel files without Excel
strengths: No Microsoft Excel needed; runs on Windows, macOS and Linux via uvx
Built-in calculator with 479 functions returns formula values for files never opened in Excel
Safety options: --allow-dir confinement, --read-only, formula safety checks, atomic saves
weaknesses: Legacy .xls files are not supported; only CSV import as a workaround
Formulas the calculator cannot reproduce return null and are listed as uncalculated

tools.name: tensorflow
tools.description: Tensor and neural network framework with Python and C++ APIs
strengths: Stable Python and C++ APIs
CUDA GPU support via pip on Ubuntu and Windows; separate tensorflow-cpu package
Device plugins for DirectX and macOS Metal
weaknesses: APIs for languages other than Python and C++ have no backward compatibility guarantee
Built-in GPU support is CUDA only; other devices need separate plugins

tools.name: Strix
tools.description: Autonomous multi-agent pentesting CLI that validates vulnerabilities with working PoCs
strengths: Findings come with working PoCs, which cuts false positives versus static scanners
Accepts source dirs, GitHub URLs, live apps, OpenAPI and Postman targets
Headless mode exits non-zero on findings; GitHub Actions example scopes PR scans to changed files
weaknesses: Needs a running Docker daemon; sandbox image is pulled on first run
Needs an LLM; recommended models are hosted, and some require provider access programs

tools.name: Meilisearch
tools.description: Rust search engine with typo tolerance, filtering and hybrid semantic search
strengths: Single binary or Docker image; quick start is one command on port 7700
Typo tolerance, facets, filters, sorting, synonyms and geosearch built in
Hybrid full-text plus semantic search through one REST API
weaknesses: Sharding and other advanced features need the Enterprise Edition and a commercial agreement
README recommends Meilisearch Cloud over self-hosting

tools.name: LibreChat
tools.description: Self-hosted multi-provider chat UI with agents, MCP tools and multi-user auth
strengths: Many providers in one UI, plus custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints without a proxy
Multi-user auth via OAuth2, LDAP and email, with admin panel and token spend tools
Agents with MCP servers, Skills, subagents, file search and code execution
weaknesses: Large feature surface; the README lists many components to configure and operate
Some features, such as attached code workspaces, are marked highly experimental

tools.name: SGLang
tools.description: Inference engine for LLM, vision-language and diffusion models on many hardware types
strengths: Supports NVIDIA, AMD, TPU, Intel, Apple Silicon, Ascend and Moore Threads hardware
Built-in diffusion engine for image and video generation in the same package
Integrates with RL training stacks such as verl and slime for rollouts
weaknesses: README gives no RAM or VRAM requirements; sizing depends on model and hardware
Several hardware integrations (Trainium, Cambricon, Qualcomm) are still in progress

tools.name: agentmemory
tools.description: Shared persistent memory server for coding agents, exposed via MCP, hooks and REST
strengths: Keyless BM25 recall works with no API key; README reports 84.7% recall-all@5 on LongMemEval-S
One memory store shared across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI and others via hooks, MCP or REST
No external database required; data stays local, with Redis backend migration documented
weaknesses: Keyless mode has no vector embeddings, so purely semantic queries can return nothing
Hook-based capture depth varies by agent; several are MCP-only with no automatic capture

tools.name: lerobot
tools.description: PyTorch library for robot control, datasets and policy training
strengths: Covers the full loop: record, train (lerobot-train), evaluate (lerobot-eval), deploy (lerobot-rollout)
Many policies in pure PyTorch: ACT, Diffusion, Pi0, SmolVLA, GR00T N1.7, HIL-SERL
Native SO101, Koch, LeKiwi, Unitree G1, Reachy2 support, plus auto-discovered third-party plugins
weaknesses: Useful results need a physical robot or simulation benchmarks such as LIBERO or MetaWorld
Install depends on optional extras (dataset, training, feetech) that vary by robot and policy

tools.name: openmausbot
tools.description: Chat app where each bot is a Claude, Codex or Grok CLI agent
strengths: Reuses your existing claude, codex and grok CLI logins, with no proxy in between
Approval cards for shell commands and file edits, for cloud and local computers
Transcripts, keys and events stay in ~/.openmausbot on your machine
weaknesses: Needs the claude, codex or grok CLI installed; local open-weight models are not described
Cloud computers rely on boat.dev and app connectors on Composio, both hosted

tools.name: rag-anything
tools.description: Python library for RAG over PDFs, Office files, images, tables and equations
strengths: Indexes images, tables and LaTeX equations as graph entities, not just text chunks
Parses PDF, DOC/DOCX, PPT/PPTX, XLS/XLSX and images; accepts pre-parsed content lists
Hybrid retrieval combines vector similarity with knowledge graph traversal
weaknesses: Default MinerU parser needs MinerU 3.x and Python 3.10-3.13; MinerU 4.x is unsupported
Office documents require a separate LibreOffice installation

tools.name: NemoClaw
tools.description: Reference stack for running AI agents inside OpenShell sandboxes
strengths: Runs three agents (OpenClaw, Hermes, Deep Agents Code) under one CLI and sandbox model
Network policy with baseline rules, operator approval flow and presets for egress control
Guided installer with express presets for supported DGX and WSL hosts
weaknesses: Alpha project; no guaranteed response times on issues, discussions or pull requests
README says new development focuses on Agent Configs, not this main-branch experience

tools.name: onnxruntime
tools.description: Cross-platform inference engine for ONNX models with hardware accelerator support
strengths: Accepts models from PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras, scikit-learn, LightGBM and XGBoost via ONNX
Runs on multiple hardware targets and operating systems with graph optimizations
MIT license, with docs, roadmap and companion example repositories
weaknesses: Library, not a server: README describes no built-in HTTP API
Models must be converted to ONNX format first

tools.name: ebook2audiobook
tools.description: Converts ebooks to chaptered audiobooks with local TTS and voice cloning
strengths: Supports 1158 languages via Fairseq/MMS models, plus optional voice cloning from a voice file
Gradio GUI and headless CLI with batch directory mode and per-book voice map
Runs on CPU, CUDA, ROCm, Apple MPS, Intel XPU and Jetson
weaknesses: README says modern TTS engines are very slow on CPU; lower-quality engines are advised
EPUB has no standard chapter structure, so unwanted text must be removed manually

tools.name: wrenai
tools.description: Semantic layer and context engine that lets agents write governed SQL
strengths: Business definitions are YAML and Markdown in Git, reviewable as pull-request diffs
Dry-plan validation, row limits and structured errors constrain agent-written SQL
Connects 22+ sources, including BigQuery, Snowflake, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse and DuckDB
weaknesses: GenBI UI, dashboards, row/column security and user groups are commercial only
Docker chat BI app moved to legacy/v1 with no new features or security fixes

tools.name: rowboat
tools.description: Desktop assistant that builds a Markdown knowledge graph from email and meetings
strengths: Data stored as plain Markdown on your machine, editable and inspectable
Works with Ollama, LM Studio or hosted models via your own API key
Connects external tools through MCP servers or Composio
weaknesses: Voice, web search and Composio each need separate third-party API keys
Google services require manual setup steps

tools.name: freetoken
tools.description: MoE inference engine that runs large open models on consumer NVIDIA GPUs
strengths: Bandwidth-adaptive CPU-GPU co-execution targets MoE models larger than VRAM
Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible APIs work with Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
Re-allocates VRAM between expert cache and KV memory without engine restart
weaknesses: Focused on MoE models; dense model support is not stated in the README
Native support listed only for NVIDIA RTX 30, 40 and 50 series

tools.name: labelme
tools.description: Desktop image annotation tool with polygon labeling and SAM-assisted masks
strengths: Supports polygon, rectangle, circle, line, point shapes plus image-level flags
Exports VOC and COCO datasets for segmentation and detection
Built-in SAM, EfficientSAM, YOLO-world and SAM3 assisted labeling
weaknesses: v7 requires Python 3.12+ and PySide6; Qt5 users must pin labelme<7
No stable Python API; internal modules were made private in v7

tools.name: everos
tools.description: Local-first agent memory runtime that stores memories as Markdown files
strengths: Canonical Markdown files are editable and Git-versionable; a watcher re-syncs indexes after edits
No MongoDB, Elasticsearch or Redis needed; storage is Markdown, SQLite and LanceDB
Search can be scoped by user_id, agent_id, app_id, project_id and session_id
weaknesses: Needs an LLM provider (OpenRouter in the quick start); no fully offline setup is described
Hybrid search, reflection and skill extraction require a separate embedding provider

tools.name: liteparse
tools.description: Local PDF and Office document parser with bounding boxes and Markdown output
strengths: No ML model or GPU required; ~2-5 ms per page text extraction via PDFium
Bindings for Rust, Node.js, Python and browser WASM, with one `lit` CLI
Pluggable OCR: bundled Tesseract or any server following its OCR HTTP API spec
weaknesses: Markdown is heuristic and rule-based; complex layouts may render imperfectly
Charts score near zero in its own ParseBench results

tools.name: camofox-browser
tools.description: REST API server that gives AI agents an anti-detection Camoufox browser
strengths: Accessibility snapshots with stable element refs, stated as about 90% smaller than raw HTML
Per-user session isolation with persisted cookies and localStorage under ~/.camofox/profiles
Proxy support including backconnect sticky sessions, with GeoIP-derived locale and timezone
weaknesses: First run downloads the Camoufox binary, about 300MB
Docker build needs make or build.ps1; plain docker build is explicitly unsupported

tools.name: skypilot
tools.description: Run and scale AI jobs across Kubernetes, Slurm and 20+ clouds
strengths: One task spec runs on Kubernetes, Slurm, or 20+ listed clouds without code changes
Auto-failover on capacity errors and cheapest-available placement across infra
Autostop of idle clusters and binpacking on shared clusters reduce idle GPU spend
weaknesses: Infra orchestrator, not a model library or trainer; you bring your own training code
Needs cloud credentials and GPU quota set up per provider before use

tools.name: sandcastle
tools.description: TypeScript library that runs coding agents in isolated sandboxes on git branches
strengths: Native OS sandboxes (Bubblewrap, Seatbelt) need no container runtime
Many providers: Docker, Podman, Daytona, E2B, Fly.io Sprites, Modal, Vercel
Branch strategies and merge-back suit parallel agents and review pipelines
weaknesses: Library only: no UI, you write TypeScript to orchestrate runs
Cloud providers require accounts with third-party services

tools.name: openresearch
tools.description: Desktop app and CLI that runs research agents with experiment tracking
strengths: Works with several coding agents, plus local models via OpenCode with LM Studio, oMLX or Ollama
Many compute backends: local, SSH, Slurm, Kubernetes, Modal, Ray, Hugging Face Jobs
Experiment logs, code and artifacts stay in a local SQL database on your machine
weaknesses: Official builds send opt-out analytics and agent feedback; disable in Settings or `orx telemetry off`
Windows build is beta and requires Git for Windows

tools.name: obsidian-copilot
tools.description: Obsidian plugin that runs OpenCode, Claude Code and Codex agents on your vault
strengths: Works with Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode using your existing logins, no Copilot plan required
BYOK supports cloud, local and OpenAI-compatible providers; keys go in the Obsidian Keychain, not data.json
Skills, Commands and Projects are shared across the installed agents
weaknesses: Agent mode is desktop-only because backends run as local processes
Multi-agent requests and hosted models need a paid Plus license

tools.name: deep-live-cam
tools.description: Real-time webcam face swap and video deepfake from a single source image
strengths: Live webcam mode needs only one source image; output can be streamed via OBS
Mouth Mask and face mapping handle multiple subjects with different faces
Execution providers for CUDA, CoreML, DirectML, OpenVINO and CPU
weaknesses: Manual install is technical: Python, ffmpeg, CUDA 12.8 and cuDNN 8.9.7 for NVIDIA
CPU-only runs are slower; live preview takes 10-30 seconds to appear

tools.name: heretic
tools.description: Modifies LLM behavior, such as refusals, without training, via ablation
strengths: One command to process a model: pip install heretic-llm, then heretic <model>
Custom scorer plugins load from a file path without modifying the package
Optional 4-bit bitsandbytes quantization lowers VRAM needed to process a model
weaknesses: Runs are slow: about 30-40 minutes for a 4B model on an RTX 3090
Heretic 1.x config files are incompatible with 2.x and need migration

tools.name: OpenViking
tools.description: Filesystem-style context database for agent memory, resources and skills
strengths: Stored memories are plain Markdown under viking:// paths that you can inspect and edit
Semantic search can be scoped to a directory subtree instead of a flat vector pool
Plugin installer covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, TRAE, OpenCode and more
weaknesses: Needs a model provider with both an embedding model and a VLM
AGPL-3.0 license restricts use in closed-source network services

tools.name: pageindex
tools.description: Vectorless RAG that builds a tree index of a document and searches it with an LLM
strengths: No vector DB or chunking; retrieval is traceable to tree nodes and page references
Local indexing costs about $0.001 per page; 9 to 1,098 pages took 13 seconds to 4.5 minutes
Reports 98.7% on FinanceBench; the repo documents a separate OSS benchmark with a runner
weaknesses: Local mode handles text-based PDFs only; OCR and image understanding require the paid Cloud
Metadata, folders, MCP server and File System for large corpora are Cloud-only

tools.name: WeKnora
tools.description: Knowledge base framework with RAG Q&A, tool-using agents and auto-generated wikis
strengths: Many data source connectors: Feishu, Confluence, Notion, GitLab, Yuque, DingTalk, Seafile, RSS
Multi-workspace RBAC with four roles, audit log and scoped API keys
Swappable LLMs, vector databases and storage; 29 built-in model vendors including Ollama
weaknesses: License reported as NOASSERTION by detection, while the README badge says MIT
Full feature set needs several services (Neo4j, MinIO, Langfuse via profiles)

tools.name: agentscope
tools.description: Python framework for building tool-using agents, with a FastAPI service and web UI
strengths: Many model providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Volcengine, xAI, Ollama
Sandbox backends include Docker, Bubblewrap, E2B, Daytona, K8s and Apple Container
Agent service adds multi-tenancy, SQL/NoSQL persistence, scheduling and Feishu/Discord channels
weaknesses: Realtime voice and SOP features are marked experimental
Web UI needs a separate pnpm dev server; service is run from the examples folder

tools.name: jax
tools.description: Python library for autodiff, JIT compilation and vectorization of NumPy-style code
strengths: grad, jit and vmap compose arbitrarily, including higher-order derivatives and per-example gradients
Three sharding modes: compiler-automatic, explicit in types, and manual per-device with collectives
Compiles through XLA to CPU, NVIDIA, AMD and Google TPU targets
weaknesses: README calls it a research project, not an official Google product, and warns of sharp edges
jit restricts Python control flow, so some code needs rewriting

tools.name: xiaozhi-esp32
tools.description: ESP32 firmware for a voice chatbot with MCP device and cloud tool control
strengths: Supports 138 board directories and 171 release variants across ESP32, C3, C5, C6, S3 and P4
Documented WebSocket and MQTT+UDP protocols let third-party servers and clients interoperate
Offline wake-word detection with customizable wake words; Wi-Fi, Ethernet and Cat.1 4G networking
weaknesses: Models do not run on the device; a server is needed for ASR, LLM and TTS
Default setup depends on the hosted xiaozhi.me service and an account

tools.name: rag_techniques
tools.description: Collection of 42 runnable notebooks implementing RAG techniques
strengths: 42 notebooks grouped by category: foundational, query enhancement, context enrichment, and more
Colab badge on listed notebooks, so no local setup is needed to run them
Covers chunking, query transformation, reliability and evaluation, with video explainers for some
weaknesses: Notebooks, not an installable package or service; code must be adapted for production
License reported as NOASSERTION, so reuse terms are unclear

tools.name: cs249r_book
tools.description: Open textbook series on ML systems, with TinyTorch, labs and hardware kits
strengths: Textbook paired with runnable parts: TinyTorch, browser Marimo labs, simulator, hardware kits
Instructor hub with syllabi and Beamer slides for every chapter
Hardware kits target Arduino, Seeed, Grove and Raspberry Pi devices
weaknesses: Volumes III and IV are open drafts; author asks readers not to cite or teach from them
Volume II is still in active revision

tools.name: ego-lite
tools.description: Desktop browser that AI agents drive through isolated per-agent Spaces
strengths: Per-agent Spaces let several agents run in parallel without taking over your tabs
Agent writes one JavaScript snippet per multi-step task, not a command-by-command loop
Optional Chrome data migration gives agents your existing logins, cookies and extensions
weaknesses: Runs on macOS and Windows only; Linux is just on the roadmap
Browser binary is a separate download, not built from this MIT repository

tools.name: agents-towards-production
tools.description: Runnable tutorials for taking LLM agents from prototype to production
strengths: 28 tutorials, each in its own folder, spanning memory, search, RAG, security and deployment
Covers concrete stack pieces: LangGraph, Redis, Mem0, FastAPI, Docker, RunPod, Inngest
Actively maintained: last commit 2026-11-15, last release 2026-10-26
weaknesses: Many tutorials are sponsor-contributed and tied to specific commercial services
Several tutorials need third-party accounts or API keys (Tavily, Bright Data, RunPod)

tools.name: dataelement/dsh-desktop
tools.description: Desktop agent app for macOS and Windows with Office document templates
strengths: Generates editable DOCX, XLSX and PPTX from templates; PPT ships 16 templates, 192 layouts
Bundles Python and Office processing dependencies, so no separate runtime install
Safe mode (--safe-mode) disables third-party plugins while keeping sessions and model config
weaknesses: No Linux or Windows ARM64 builds
Built on DeepSeek Harness; depends on its runtime and upstream licenses

tools.name: triton
tools.description: Python-based language and compiler for writing custom GPU kernels for deep learning
strengths: Supports NVIDIA (compute capability 8.0+) and AMD (ROCm 6.2+) GPUs
TRITON_INTERPRET=1 runs kernels without a GPU, so Python breakpoints work
Extensive debug knobs: per-pass MLIR dumps, reproducers, kernel IR override
weaknesses: Linux only; CPU backend is still under development
Source builds depend on LLVM, which has no stable API and builds slowly

tools.name: rocketride-server
tools.description: Visual AI pipeline builder in VS Code with a C++ runtime
strengths: Pipelines are plain JSON .pipe files, diffable and version-controllable
100+ nodes, including 15+ LLM providers and 9 vector databases; nodes are Python-extensible
Built-in tracing of token usage, LLM calls, latency and call trees
weaknesses: Visual builder is delivered as an IDE extension (VS Code or Open VSX editors)
SDK falls back to RocketRide Cloud when run outside the extension's folder

tools.name: pyvideotrans
tools.description: Video translation and AI dubbing pipeline with ASR, subtitle translation and TTS
strengths: Full pipeline in one tool: ASR, translation, TTS and video merge
Mixes local engines (Faster-Whisper, Ollama) with many commercial APIs
Pause and edit between recognition, translation and dubbing stages
weaknesses: GPU acceleration is NVIDIA only; AMD needs the Whisper.NET route
Windows GPU use requires manually installing CUDA 12.8 and cuDNN 9.11

tools.name: docsgpt
tools.description: Document-grounded AI agents and visual workflows with cited answers
strengths: Answers cite source documents; connectors keep Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, GitHub and S3 in sync
Embeds via script-tag widget, React package, OpenAI-compatible /v1 API or MCP server
SSO (OIDC, SCIM), roles, audit log and usage quotas are included under MIT
weaknesses: Full stack needs API, worker, Postgres and Redis, heavier than a single-binary tool
One-command installer pipes a script from curl to bash and requires Docker

tools.name: claude-obsidian
tools.description: Claude Code plugin that builds a linked Markdown wiki in an Obsidian vault
strengths: Writes are transactional, with hash conflict detection and journal rollback after interrupted writes
Output is plain Markdown that works in Obsidian or any editor, with originals kept untouched
Same skills run in Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, ZCode, Cursor and Windsurf via a setup script
weaknesses: No built-in text extraction for PDF and EPUB; only metadata, hash and size
Web pages and YouTube need a separate runner; OCR needs an external tool

tools.name: transformers.js
tools.description: Runs Hugging Face models in browser or Node via ONNX Runtime
strengths: Pipeline API closely matches Python transformers, easing code translation
Runs in the browser with no server; models load from the Hugging Face Hub
Optional WebGPU and q4/q8/fp16 dtypes to cut download size and speed up inference
weaknesses: Models must be in ONNX format; others need conversion with Optimum
README calls WebGPU experimental in many browsers

tools.name: sherpa-onnx
tools.description: Offline speech recognition, TTS, diarization and VAD runtime built on ONNX Runtime
strengths: Covers ASR, TTS, diarization, VAD, keyword spotting and enhancement in one library
Bindings for 12 languages, plus Flutter and Tauri demo apps
Runs on x64, x86, arm32, arm64 and riscv64, including Android, iOS and WebAssembly
weaknesses: Library and SDK, not an end-user app; you integrate it in code
Models are downloaded separately, and you choose among many ASR and TTS variants

tools.name: ms-swift
tools.description: Fine-tuning, RL, quantization and serving toolkit for 600+ text and 400+ multimodal LLMs
strengths: Covers SFT, DPO/KTO/RM, GRPO variants, embedding and reranker training in one CLI
Megatron TP/PP/CP/EP support for full-parameter and LoRA training of MoE models
Runs on NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Ascend NPU, Apple MPS and CPU
weaknesses: Large dependency matrix (torch, transformers, peft, trl, deepspeed, vllm) with version pins
No Docker image or compose file in the README

tools.name: banana-slides
tools.description: AI slide deck generator that exports PPTX, PDF and narrated video
strengths: Several providers: Gemini, OpenAI-format, Volcengine, Vertex AI and LazyLLM vendors like Qwen and DeepSeek
Exports PPTX, PDF, editable PPTX (beta) and narrated MP4 with subtitles
Edit pages by natural-language prompt or box selection; per-page templates supported
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license restricts use in closed-source hosted services
Needs paid external image-generation API; README warns Nano Banana Pro calls are costly

tools.name: qm
tools.description: Team agent harness for Slack and web with per-scope sandboxes
strengths: Per-person and per-room scopes isolate memory, files, keychain view and sandbox
Org-wide security postures (Strict, Auto, Dangerous) plus audit log and command policy rules
Runs crons, watches and inbound webhooks while users are away
weaknesses: Requires Postgres and cloud infrastructure; deployment is multi-step via the qm CLI
Upstream accepts contributions only as written proposals in adrs/, not code

tools.name: Speech-to-Speech
tools.description: Local voice agent pipeline with an OpenAI Realtime-compatible server
strengths: Core OpenAI Realtime events over WebSocket and WebRTC; CI tests the OpenAI Agents SDK
Many swappable backends: Whisper variants, Parakeet, Kokoro, Pocket TTS, OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Works offline after first model download; no API key needed for default pipeline
weaknesses: Realtime support is a tested core subset, not full OpenAI Realtime API parity
Default Linux Qwen3-TTS wheel targets CUDA 12.8 and Ubuntu 24.04; others need manual wheels

tools.name: cubesandbox
tools.description: MicroVM sandbox service for AI agents with an E2B-compatible API
strengths: Each sandbox gets a dedicated kernel in its own KVM MicroVM, not shared-kernel containers
E2B SDK compatible; README says switching needs one environment variable change
Snapshot, clone and rollback, plus auto pause/resume of idle sandboxes
weaknesses: Requires x86_64 Linux with KVM for the quick start path
Multi-component stack (API, master, cubelet, eBPF switch, proxy), heavier than a single binary

tools.name: IronClaw
tools.description: Rust assistant that sandboxes every untrusted tool in WebAssembly
strengths: WASM sandbox with per-tool rate, memory, CPU and time limits
Secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM, never exposed to tool code; full audit log
Describe a tool in chat and IronClaw builds it as a WASM module
weaknesses: Requires PostgreSQL for persistence; SQLite is not an option
Installer needs a release tag chosen by hand; no latest channel

tools.name: MemOS
tools.description: Graph-structured long-term memory API and local plugins for LLM agents
strengths: Self-host REST API plus local SQLite plugins with no cloud dependency
Memory cubes isolate or share knowledge bases across users, projects and agents
Plugins use hybrid retrieval (FTS5 + vector) and include a local Memory Viewer
weaknesses: Self-hosted server needs Neo4j and Qdrant running alongside the API
Cloud API and Cloud plugins send data to MemOS Cloud and need an API key

tools.name: whisperlivekit
tools.description: Real-time streaming speech-to-text server with diarization and translation
strengths: Serves OpenAI-style /v1/audio/transcriptions, Deepgram-style WebSocket and native /asr WebSocket
Many backends: Whisper, MLX Whisper, Voxtral, Qwen3-ASR, Canary, SenseVoiceSmall
Optional Sortformer speaker diarization and translation to and from 200 languages
weaknesses: Heavy extras (voxtral-hf, vLLM stacks) conflict and need separate environments
Qwen3 causal mode is English-only; vLLM causal and Metal paths are experimental

tools.name: autogluon
tools.description: AutoML library for tabular, time series and multimodal data in Python
strengths: Three task APIs (tabular, time series, multimodal) share a fit/predict pattern
Combines classic ML models and foundation models in one ensemble
Installs with pip or conda on Linux, macOS and Windows
weaknesses: README gives no RAM, VRAM or training-time figures
Not an LLM app; no chat UI, model server or agent runtime

tools.name: soup
tools.description: CLI for fine-tuning and post-training LLMs from a single YAML config
strengths: Many tasks in one config: SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO, KTO, ORPO, SimPO, IPO, vision, audio
Layer streaming trains Llama-3.1-8B NF4 in 3.32 GB peak on a 4 GB laptop GPU
Same tool merges adapters, exports GGUF, serves an OpenAI-compatible API, has a web UI
weaknesses: Python 3.10-3.12 only; 3.13+ is unsupported
Layer streaming is opt-in and still beta; a correctness repair changed its benchmark numbers

tools.name: Local Deep Research
tools.description: Agentic research tool that searches web, papers and your files, writes cited reports
strengths: Per-user AES-256 SQLCipher databases, including per-user LLM API keys
Egress scopes (Adaptive, Public only, Private only, Strict) restrict search and model traffic
README reports ~95% SimpleQA (n=500) with Qwen3.6-27B on one RTX 3090
weaknesses: Needs a separate LLM backend and SearXNG; pip install does not include them
Egress guard is a partial safeguard, not an air gap; relays to hosted models go undetected

tools.name: adk-go
tools.description: Code-first Go toolkit for building and orchestrating multi-agent applications
strengths: Agents, tools and orchestration are plain Go, so they can be tested and versioned like other code
Composes multiple specialized agents into larger systems
Sibling ADKs exist for Python, Java, Kotlin and TypeScript
weaknesses: README names no model providers besides Gemini optimization
Requires a very recent Go toolchain (1.26.10 or later)

tools.name: stable-diffusion.cpp
tools.description: C/C++ inference for Stable Diffusion, Flux, Qwen-Image and Wan video models
strengths: Backends: CPU (AVX/AVX2/AVX512), CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, OpenCL and SYCL
Covers SD1.x to SDXL, SD3, FLUX, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, plus Wan and LTX video
Reads .ckpt, .safetensors and .gguf; convert mode writes .gguf or .safetensors
weaknesses: README warns API and command-line options may change frequently
ControlNet support is stated only for SD 1.5

tools.name: vllm-omni
tools.description: Serving engine for omni-modality, diffusion, TTS and robot-policy models, built on vLLM
strengths: Covers omni, TTS, diffusion (image/video/audio) and robot-policy models in one runtime
Reuses vLLM KV cache management; supports tensor, pipeline, data and expert parallelism
OpenAI-compatible server with streaming outputs and full-duplex realtime audio API
weaknesses: Version and model support tied to specific vLLM releases; needs matching upstream vLLM
README gives no RAM or VRAM requirements; check per-model recipes

tools.name: aisoc
tools.description: Self-hosted SOC that detects threats and investigates alerts with auditable AI agents
strengths: Every agent prompt, tool call and citation is logged and exports as a signed evidence bundle
Ships a local model, so triage works with no API key or hosted provider
Response actions and playbooks default to preview and need a separate approver
weaknesses: Heavy stack: 16 services and about 8 GB RAM for core, about 12 GB for full
No hosted LLM provider has been tested; bundled 3B model is not frontier-class

tools.name: feast
tools.description: Feature store that serves consistent ML features for training and online inference
strengths: Point-in-time correct joins for training sets, avoiding future-value leakage
Wide backend list: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Redis, DynamoDB, Postgres, Cassandra and more
Python, Java and Go feature servers plus a Kubernetes operator
weaknesses: Many components are alpha or beta: Java/Go servers, operator, streaming transformations, web UI
Many backends are contrib or community plugins with varying support

tools.name: apfel
tools.description: CLI and local OpenAI-compatible server for Apple's on-device Mac language model
strengths: Drop-in OpenAI-style /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses endpoints with streaming and tool calling
Schema-guaranteed JSON output via FoundationModels guided generation
Installs with brew install apfel; no API keys, inference stays on-device
weaknesses: Requires macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon with Apple Intelligence enabled
Single fixed ~3B model; context window is only 4096 tokens (8192 on some macOS 27 Macs)

tools.name: open-connector
tools.description: Connector gateway exposing 1,000+ SaaS providers to agents via MCP, HTTP and SDK
strengths: Large catalog: 1,000+ providers and 10,000+ Actions with inspectable request/response schemas and scopes
Built-in OAuth 2.1 server with PKCE S256 and revocable, policy-scoped tokens for remote MCP clients
Many deployment targets: Docker, Node.js, Helm, Cloudflare Workers, SQLite or PostgreSQL 15+
weaknesses: Modified Apache-2.0 license: offering it to third parties as a hosted service needs a commercial license
Self-hosting requires registering your own OAuth apps per provider; managed OAuth is only on OOMOL hosted

tools.name: mcp-atlassian
tools.description: MCP server exposing Jira and Confluence tools to AI assistants
strengths: Covers both Jira and Confluence in one server, with 98 tools
Supports Cloud and Server/Data Center with API token, PAT or OAuth 2.0
Starts with a single uvx command; Docker, pip and source installs also documented
weaknesses: Not an official Atlassian product
98 tools may crowd an assistant's tool list or context

tools.name: generative-ai-for-beginners
tools.description: 21-lesson course on building generative AI apps in Python and TypeScript
strengths: Covers 21 lessons from LLM basics to RAG, agents and fine-tuning
Build lessons include code in both Python and TypeScript
Foundry Local option runs models offline without a cloud subscription
weaknesses: Most samples target Azure OpenAI or OpenAI API, which need accounts and keys
Several lessons still list video as coming soon

tools.name: openmontage
tools.description: Agent-driven video production pipelines run from your AI coding assistant
strengths: Works with zero API keys: Piper TTS, free archival footage, Remotion and FFmpeg rendering
Many optional providers: fal.ai, Kling, Runway, ElevenLabs, Suno, Google, OpenAI, Pexels
Backlot local board adds scene-level approval gates and per-asset cost tracking
weaknesses: Needs an external AI coding assistant to drive it; no standalone prompting UI
Local setup requires Python 3.10+, Node.js 18+ and FFmpeg

tools.name: langextract
tools.description: Python library that extracts grounded structured data from text using LLMs
strengths: Each extraction carries a char_interval into the source; ungrounded results get None
Long-document handling via chunking, max_workers and extraction_passes for recall
Supports Gemini, OpenAI (with Batch API), Vertex AI batch and local Ollama models
weaknesses: Needs few-shot examples; misaligned examples trigger prompt alignment warnings
Ollama provider does not support output_schema

tools.name: QwenPaw
tools.description: Self-hosted personal AI assistant with memory, skills, and many chat channels
strengths: One instance serves DingTalk, Lark, WeChat, Discord, Telegram, iMessage and QQ
Runs with built-in local runtime, Ollama, LM Studio or 14+ cloud providers
Includes Tool Guard, File Guard, Skill Scanner and a kernel-level sandbox
weaknesses: Desktop app is Beta and the macOS build is not notarized
Requires Python >= 3.11 and < 3.14 for pip install

tools.name: xgboost
tools.description: Gradient boosted decision tree library for tabular machine learning
strengths: Same code runs on Kubernetes, Hadoop, SGE, Dask, Spark and PySpark
Packaged on PyPI, CRAN and conda-forge
Backed by a KDD 2016 paper; Apache-2.0 licensed
weaknesses: Tree boosting only; not a general deep learning framework
README has no install or quick-start example; relies on external docs

tools.name: stagehand
tools.description: Playwright-style SDK that drives browsers with act, observe and extract calls
strengths: Same browser driver API in TypeScript, Python and Go
observe() returns selectors, so login credentials stay out of model prompts
extract() validates output against Zod, Pydantic or Go types
weaknesses: Caching, model gateway, proxies and session recordings need the Browserbase service
Local runs need Chrome installed and an LLM provider API key

tools.name: moli
tools.description: Headless browser in Rust for AI agents, with CDP and WebDriver support
strengths: Single binary serves CDP, WebDriver Classic and BiDi; no ChromeDriver or Chrome install needed
Reported median RSS of 73 MiB on a 192-URL crawl, versus 773 MiB for Chrome Headless
CLI dumps Markdown, semantic tree text, PNG screenshots and PDF directly
weaknesses: Lexbench pass rate is 81.9% against Chrome's 99.8%, so some sites will fail
No GUI, GPU compositor, or high-fidelity Canvas, WebGL or media playback

tools.name: verl
tools.description: RL post-training library for LLMs with PPO, GRPO, FSDP and Megatron
strengths: FSDP, FSDP2 and Megatron-LM training with vLLM, SGLang or HF rollout
Covers PPO, GRPO, RLOO, ReMax and REINFORCE++, plus multi-turn tool-calling RL
README states scaling to 671B models via expert parallelism, with LoRA RL to save memory
weaknesses: Realistic runs need multiple GPUs; not a single-machine tool
Fully async and one-step-off trainers moved to verl-recipe, pinned to v0.9.1

tools.name: surya
tools.description: Document OCR, layout and table recognition VLM with a lightweight Python client
strengths: One VLM handles OCR, layout, reading order, tables and inline math (KaTeX LaTeX)
Backends: vllm on NVIDIA, llama.cpp on CPU, mlx_vlm on Apple Silicon
Reports 85.9 on OmniParseBench and 4.5 pages/s on one H100 at 192 DPI
weaknesses: Model weights are not Apache: free only for research, personal use, and startups under $5M
NVIDIA GPU path needs Docker or Podman plus the NVIDIA Container Toolkit

tools.name: Agent Zero
tools.description: General-purpose AI agent with its own Linux desktop, browser and terminal
strengths: Real Linux desktop and browser in the UI, with user takeover and page annotation
Projects isolate files, memory, secrets and model presets per job
Extensible via plugins, MCP, A2A and skills; prompts and tools are readable files
weaknesses: Needs a provider API key, AI account or local model server before first reply
Host file access means granting the agent permission to edit files and run commands

tools.name: sentence-transformers
tools.description: Python library for text embeddings, rerankers, and sparse and ColBERT-style models
strengths: Four model types behind one API: dense, cross-encoder, sparse and multi-vector
Loads 15,000+ pretrained models from the Hugging Face Hub, including MTEB leaderboard entries
Built-in training with 20+ embedding loss functions and evaluation during training
weaknesses: Library only: no server, vector store or retrieval pipeline included
Requires Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.2+ and transformers v5.0+

tools.name: weclone
tools.description: Builds a life portrait from chat history and fine-tunes a personal chat clone
strengths: Every portrait fact traces to its source and carries a privacy level
Per-domain and per-level access control for assistants reading the portrait over MCP
Encrypted local storage by default; training data filtered with Microsoft Presidio
weaknesses: Only Telegram is supported as a data source; WhatsApp, Discord and Slack are pending
Portrait and extraction prompts are in Chinese; English chats untested

tools.name: mnn
tools.description: On-device inference and training engine for phones, embedded and PC
strengths: Small footprint: about 800KB core .so on Android, about 12MB iOS static library with all options
Backends for ARM/x86 CPU, Metal, OpenCL, Vulkan, CUDA, CoreML, NNAPI and Hexagon
Converter covers TensorFlow, Caffe, ONNX and TorchScript, with FP16/Int8 quantization
weaknesses: Community discussion is on DingTalk groups, predominantly in Chinese
QNN is rated B or C in the README support table

tools.name: ragas
tools.description: Python library for scoring LLM and RAG application outputs with metrics
strengths: Installs with pip; quickstart command scaffolds a RAG evaluation project
Custom metrics defined by a prompt and allowed values, scored asynchronously
Generates test datasets when none are available
weaknesses: LLM-based metrics need an external model, such as an OpenAI key in the example
Only the rag_eval quickstart template exists; other templates are listed as coming soon

tools.name: openmotion
tools.description: Agent-driven studio that recreates reference videos as editable HTML projects
strengths: Works with 22 local agents including Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, using your own keys
Same project is edited on a Studio timeline and rendered to MP4
Imports HyperFrames project ZIPs and ships a template library of reference remakes
weaknesses: Needs a separate local agent and API keys; no built-in model
Source install asks for Node.js 26.11.1 while the badge says 22.18+

tools.name: google/ax
tools.description: Kubectl-style orchestrator that runs sandboxed agent tasks from YAML manifests
strengths: kubectl-shaped CLI: apply, get, describe, watch, delete, plus suspend/resume and ssh
Declarative Workspace manifests pre-wire Git repos, MCP servers and skill packages
Checkpoint and resume of idle agent tasks via ax suspend and ax resume
weaknesses: README warns of heavy development and major breaking changes before a stable release
Requires a Kubernetes cluster with Agent Substrate installed first

tools.name: octop
tools.description: Multi-user, multi-agent assistant for web, CLI and chat apps like Telegram
strengths: Single process serves dashboard, CLI, IM channels and cron; state lives under ~/.octop/
Channels: Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeChat, Telegram, Discord and WeCom
JWT multi-user isolation, tool approval and shell command guardrails
weaknesses: AgentTeams is marked Beta; mobile client is closed beta
Install one-liner pipes a script hosted on Tencent COS into bash

tools.name: fiftyone
tools.description: Dataset visualization, curation and model evaluation tool for computer vision
strengths: Installs with pip install fiftyone; supports Python 3.10 to 3.13
Built-in dataset zoo and model zoo for quick starts
Embeddings panel and evaluation tools to locate failure modes and label errors
weaknesses: Team collaboration and cloud-native workloads are in the separate commercial Voxel51 product
Focused on computer vision; not aimed at text or LLM workflows

tools.name: art
tools.description: Python RL framework that trains LLM agents with GRPO from rollout rewards
strengths: Client/server split: run the client on a laptop, train on a remote or local GPU
OpenAI-compatible client drops into existing agent code, with a LangGraph integration
RULER automatic reward generation and notebooks for 2048, email search, MCP and SFT
weaknesses: Inference is blocked while each training step runs
Gemma 3 does not appear to be supported

tools.name: infinite-canvas
tools.description: Browser-based infinite canvas for AI image and video generation
strengths: Browser calls the API directly; keys, canvases and assets stay in local browser storage
Custom scripts adapt image and video calls to non-standard OpenAI-compatible relays
Remote node plugins installable by URL, with a TypeScript SDK
weaknesses: Generates nothing itself; needs an external OpenAI-compatible image or video API
README warns of development stage; local storage formats may change without compatibility

tools.name: read-frog
tools.description: Browser extension that translates pages and subtitles for language learners
strengths: Works with 20+ providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek and local Ollama
Free translation backends available: Google Translate, Microsoft Translate, DeepLX
Request batching claims up to 70% lower API cost, with retry and per-request fallback
weaknesses: Dual-licensed GPLv3 and commercial; closed-source use needs a separate license
AI transcription for YouTube videos without captions is limited to Pro and Ultra plans

tools.name: runanywhere-sdks
tools.description: On-device LLM, speech, vision and RAG SDKs for mobile, web and desktop
strengths: One API across Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, Web, Electron and Python
Engine routing per device: Hexagon NPU, MLX, llama.cpp (Metal, CUDA opt-in, WebGPU)
Covers LLM, VLM, STT, TTS, VAD, embeddings, RAG, structured output and tool calling
weaknesses: Maturity varies: Flutter, React Native and Web are beta, Electron preview, Python alpha
Python SDK has stubs for voice agent, image generation and LoRA

tools.name: harness-sdk
tools.description: Python and TypeScript SDK for building agents, with a prebuilt harness
strengths: Same agent model in Python and TypeScript, with a CLI and an MCP docs server
Providers include Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and Ollama, plus custom ones
Hooks can intercept any step of the loop; tracing is on by default
weaknesses: TypeScript Agent defaults to Amazon Bedrock, so AWS credentials are needed unless you set a model
Several packages (harness, SDK, tools, CLI) to choose between; the split takes time to learn

tools.name: dynamo
tools.description: Multi-node orchestration layer for vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM inference
strengths: Adds disaggregated prefill/decode and KV-aware routing on top of vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM
KV block manager offloads cache across GPU, CPU, SSD and remote storage such as S3 or Azure blob
SLA-based planner autoscaler and Kubernetes operator with gang scheduling (Grove)
weaknesses: Not useful for a single model on a single GPU; the README says the engine alone suffices
Production path assumes Kubernetes and multi-GPU clusters; heavy for small setups

tools.name: magnitude
tools.description: Local inference engine that tunes kernels per model on your hardware
strengths: Per-model kernel tuning at download time; README reports ~2.2x faster decode than Ollama on Mac and NVIDIA
Runs on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD or CPU across macOS, Windows and Linux
One-click connection to eight named agents; OpenAI-compatible API for the rest
weaknesses: Optimized kernels cover popular open-weight families only; full model list is on the website
Benchmarks are the project's own and compare mainly against Ollama

tools.name: open-codesign
tools.description: Desktop app that turns prompts into prototypes and slide decks
strengths: Bring your own key: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama or OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Exports HTML, PDF, PPTX, ZIP and Markdown rather than only a hosted preview
One-click import of existing Claude Code or Codex provider configs
weaknesses: Installers are not notarized or signed; macOS needs an xattr workaround
Output is interactive prototypes with simulated data, not production backends or auth

tools.name: clawrouter
tools.description: Local LLM router that picks the cheapest capable model per request
strengths: Routing runs locally in under 1 ms, with no external calls for the decision
OpenAI-compatible proxy works with Cursor, continue.dev and the OpenAI SDK
Seven free models usable without signup, key or wallet
weaknesses: Paid models go through BlockRun's hosted gateway, not directly to each provider
Savings figures come from the vendor's own published workload mix

tools.name: remove-ai-watermarks
tools.description: CLI that strips visible AI marks, metadata and invisible watermarks from images and video
strengths: Visible and metadata removal run on CPU with OpenCV, MI-GAN or LaMa fill backends
Handles images, video (MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV) and text provenance from one CLI
Video path scans all frames for a stable mark and copies audio without re-encoding
weaknesses: Invisible image removal is CUDA-only, with no CPU or MPS fallback
No local SynthID pixel detector; detection relies on signed provenance

tools.name: deepchat
tools.description: Electron desktop client for cloud and Ollama models with MCP, Skills and ACP
strengths: Supports MCP Resources, Prompts and Tools over StreamableHTTP, SSE and Stdio, with one-click DeepLink install
Skills can be imported and exported with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar tools
Session Tape and Trace preview show request sequences, provider metadata and token budgets
weaknesses: Desktop-only Electron app; no web or server deployment described in the README
Encryption and obfuscation are described as reserved interfaces, not enabled features

tools.name: lobsterai
tools.description: Electron desktop agent that edits files, drives a browser, and takes tasks from chat apps
strengths: Permission prompts gate file, shell and network actions; sessions stored locally in SQLite
Built-in Word, Excel and PowerPoint editing and previews for HTML, PDF, images and video
Eleven IM channels incl. WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, Telegram, Discord; bots can route to different agents
weaknesses: Desktop only: macOS and Windows, no Linux build listed
Built-in models require sign-in; the README does not say what account is needed

tools.name: scikit-learn
tools.description: Python library of classical machine learning algorithms built on NumPy and SciPy
strengths: Installs with one pip or conda command; six required dependencies, all listed with minimum versions
BSD-3-Clause license; test suite runs with pytest sklearn
Volunteer community with institutional support; benchmarked with asv
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.12 or newer, which excludes older environments
Plotting needs Matplotlib, installed separately

tools.name: airllm
tools.description: Python library that runs huge LLMs on small GPUs by streaming layers
strengths: Runs 70B models in about 4GB VRAM without quantization, per the README
One AutoModel call covers Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Gemma, Phi and others
Optional 4bit/8bit block-wise compression of loaded weights for up to 3x speedup
weaknesses: Layer-by-layer disk loading makes generation slow; no tokens/s figures given
Splitting needs large disk space, e.g. ~360GB for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

tools.name: chatbox
tools.description: Electron desktop client for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and Ollama models
strengths: Installers for Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Linux AppImage; no server to deploy
Supports OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, ChatGLM-6B and Ollama local models
Chat data stored locally on the device
weaknesses: Community Edition is synced with a separate pro repo, so features may differ
README documents no built-in local inference; local models require Ollama

tools.name: faiss
tools.description: C++ library for similarity search and clustering of dense vectors
strengths: Many index types trading off speed, accuracy, memory per vector and training time
Compressed and binary indexes handle sets that do not fit in RAM uncompressed
GPU indexes (CUDA, ROCm) replace CPU ones, single or multi-GPU
weaknesses: Library only: no server, REST API, auth or built-in persistence service
Vectors are identified by integers; metadata filtering must be built separately

tools.name: dspy
tools.description: Python framework for building LM programs and optimizing their prompts and weights
strengths: Optimizers tune prompts and weights from code and metrics, replacing manual prompt editing
Compositional Python modules for classifiers, RAG pipelines and agent loops
Backed by published papers, including GEPA and MIPRO
weaknesses: README defers nearly all usage detail to the external docs site
LM layer moved off LiteLLM to lm15, with breaking changes to provider options

tools.name: semantic-kernel
tools.description: Model-agnostic SDK for building agents and plugins in C#, Python and Java
strengths: Same agent and plugin model across Python, .NET and Java
Connectors for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, NVIDIA, Ollama, LMStudio and ONNX
Plugins from native code, prompt templates, OpenAPI specs or MCP
weaknesses: README says Microsoft Agent Framework is the successor, so new work points elsewhere
Java support lives in a separate repository with its own build steps

tools.name: agent-desktop
tools.description: Desktop app control for AI agents via the OS accessibility tree
strengths: Uses accessibility tree refs instead of screenshots or pixel matching
Runs on macOS 13+, Windows 10 1809+, and Ubuntu 24.04+
Ref actions are headless by default, without moving the pointer or taking focus
weaknesses: No model or agent loop included; you must supply and drive the agent
Refs go stale when the UI changes, so snapshots must be retaken

tools.name: shap
tools.description: Python library that explains ML model predictions with Shapley values
strengths: Exact, fast Tree SHAP in C++ for XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, scikit-learn, pyspark
KernelExplainer works on any model that exposes a prediction function
Built-in plots: waterfall, force, beeswarm, scatter, bar, text, image
weaknesses: KernelExplainer is slower than the model-specific explainers
DeepExplainer supports TensorFlow/Keras; PyTorch support is described as preliminary

tools.name: langchainjs
tools.description: TypeScript framework for building LLM apps and agents with swappable model integrations
strengths: Runs on Node.js (ESM and CommonJS), Deno, Bun, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase Edge and browsers
Common interface across models, embeddings, vector stores and retrievers makes providers swappable
Large integration library covering model providers, tools and vector stores
weaknesses: Monitoring and evaluation depend on LangSmith, a separate hosted product
Abstraction layers add indirection over direct provider SDK calls

tools.name: eigent
tools.description: Desktop app running single agents or parallel multi-agent teams on your machine
strengths: Single-agent mode and multi-agent workforce mode in one desktop workspace
Built-in browser, terminal and document toolkits, with MCP and skill integration
Local backend supports vLLM, Ollama and LM Studio, with no cloud account required
weaknesses: Quick start connects to Eigent cloud services and requires account registration
Local deployment is a separate server setup documented in another README

tools.name: chatterbot
tools.description: Python library for retrieval-based chatbots trained on example conversations
strengths: Installs with pip; a basic bot takes a few lines of Python
Bundled corpus training data for over a dozen languages
Language-independent design, trainable on custom conversation data
weaknesses: Replies come from matching past statements, not an LLM; no generative output
Untrained bot has no knowledge; quality depends on training data volume

tools.name: leann
tools.description: Vector index that recomputes embeddings on demand to cut storage
strengths: Graph-based selective recomputation avoids storing embeddings; README claims 97% less storage
HNSW and DiskANN backends, selectable with --backend-name
Works with Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
weaknesses: Recomputing embeddings at query time adds latency compared with stored vectors
DiskANN needs a native toolchain (Boost, protobuf, MKL) when built from source

tools.name: txtai
tools.description: Python embeddings database with pipelines, workflows and agents for search and RAG
strengths: Embeddings database combines vector indexes, graph analysis and SQL queries in one library
Pipelines for transcription, translation, summarization and labeling, not only LLM prompts
Web API from a YAML config via uvicorn; bindings for JavaScript, Java, Rust and Go
weaknesses: Code-first library with no built-in chat UI or visual workflow builder
No Docker or compose files detected in the repo; container docs are linked separately

tools.name: openwhispr
tools.description: Cross-platform voice dictation and meeting transcription app with local or cloud models
strengths: Offline transcription with Whisper and Parakeet; audio stays on the device
GPU-accelerated local Whisper on Metal, CUDA and Vulkan
Local speaker diarization and voice fingerprinting across meetings
weaknesses: Intel Macs lack live speaker identification and semantic notes search
Cloud sync, sharing and team spaces depend on OpenWhispr Cloud

tools.name: speechbrain
tools.description: PyTorch toolkit for training and running speech and text models
strengths: Over 200 recipes on 40+ datasets, with a consistent layout across tasks
Over 100 pretrained models on HuggingFace; ASR inference in three lines of Python
Single and multi-GPU training, dynamic batching and mixed precision built in
weaknesses: Library and research toolkit, not a ready-to-run server or app
No Docker image or HTTP API provided

tools.name: rerun
tools.description: Multimodal data logging, viewer and query engine for robotics
strengths: SDKs for Python, Rust and C++; pip install rerun-sdk bundles the viewer
Ingests MCAP, rrd and LeRobot alongside direct SDK logging
Time-aware viewer with scrubbing; in-memory buffer size is configurable
weaknesses: API still evolving; README warns to expect breaking changes
Viewer slows down with too many entities

tools.name: hive
tools.description: Runtime where a queen agent spawns parallel worker agents sharing a SQLite tracker
strengths: One agent-loop primitive; workers are clones, so no workflow graph to design
Shared SQLite tracker lets runs be queried, audited and resumed from where they stopped
Any LiteLLM provider, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or local Ollama model; workers can use a different model
weaknesses: No dollar spending limits yet; only turn, tool-call and concurrency caps
Repo is a uv workspace; pip install -e . does not work, quickstart script required

tools.name: nightly-labs/openbot
tools.description: Desktop workspace that runs coding-agent CLIs as persistent teammates
strengths: Supports about a dozen agent CLIs, plus custom ACP agents and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Per-agent workspaces, crash-safe FIFO queues and automatic context compaction
Can run headless via a server install script or Docker image (amd64 and arm64)
weaknesses: PolyForm Noncommercial license; not free software and restricted for commercial use
Agents run with danger-full-access and no per-action approval after first-launch consent

tools.name: failproofai
tools.description: Policy enforcement and run tracing for coding agent CLIs and gateways
strengths: Pre-execution blocking of tool calls verified on all 12 supported harnesses
Custom policies are JS files in .failproofai/policies/, committed and shared with the team
Local dashboard and audit read existing history with no account or upload
weaknesses: License is MIT with Commons Clause, not OSI open source; resale needs a separate agreement
Setup selects no policies; only block-failproofai-commands is active until a pack is added

tools.name: pysyft
tools.description: Python library for running data-owner-approved jobs on private data
strengths: Private data stays on the owner's machine; scientists work on mock data until a job is approved
Needs no new server; syncs over Google Drive, with Microsoft 365 and WebRTC also named
Each collaborator and each job requires explicit data owner approval
weaknesses: README describes only Google Drive as a working transport; others are called extensible
Local or Jupyter use needs a Google Cloud OAuth token, about 15 minutes to set up

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: Go AI gateway with web UI, fallbacks, budgets and semantic caching
strengths: Single Go binary via npx or Docker with zero-config web UI on 8080
Drop-in base URLs for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google GenAI SDKs
Virtual keys, team budgets, OIDC provisioning and Prometheus metrics
weaknesses: Guardrails, clustering, adaptive load balancing and MCP gateway are enterprise-only
Benchmarks are self-reported on t3 instances

tools.name: accelerate
tools.description: Thin PyTorch wrapper that runs your training loop on CPU, GPU, TPU or multi-node
strengths: Whole API is one Accelerator class; the rest of the training loop stays unchanged
Same script runs on CPU, single or multi-GPU, multi-node and TPU
Optional CLI wraps torchrun, MPI and DeepSpeed launch config; plain python also works
weaknesses: No built-in trainer; you must write and maintain your own training loop
DeepSpeed, FSDP and Megatron-LM support are labeled experimental in the README

tools.name: pocketpal-ai
tools.description: Phone app that runs GGUF language models offline on iOS and Android
strengths: Chat, TTS and tool calls run on-device with no account or internet after model download
Searches and downloads GGUF models from Hugging Face, including gated ones with a token
CPU, Metal, OpenCL (Adreno) and Qualcomm Hexagon NPU paths with graceful fallback
weaknesses: Only three built-in tools: calculate, datetime and render_html
Mobile only; no desktop or server build is described

tools.name: praisonai
tools.description: Python SDK and CLI for building multi-agent workflows with tools and MCP
strengths: Workflows can be written in Python or in YAML with no code
Tools can run in Docker, E2B, Modal, Daytona, Fly.io, SSH or subprocess
Explicit loop controls: iteration cap, budget ceiling, doom-loop detection on by default
weaknesses: Large surface (SDK, CLI, Claw, Flow, UI) split across several pip extras
Quick start assumes an OpenAI API key; local model setup is left to provider examples

tools.name: tabpfn
tools.description: Pretrained transformer for tabular classification and regression, no per-dataset training
strengths: Drop-in fit/predict estimators for classification and regression, installed with pip
Data stays local; works offline once weights are downloaded
Several checkpoints selectable, including smaller TabPFN-3.5-Fast and older V2, V3
weaknesses: TabPFN-2.5 to 3.5 weights are non-commercial; commercial use needs a license
First use requires browser login and license acceptance, or a TABPFN_TOKEN

tools.name: osaurus
tools.description: Native macOS agent harness with memory, sandbox and tools over local or cloud models
strengths: Native Swift app with MLX inference; works fully offline with local models
Agent code runs in an isolated Linux VM (macOS 26+) or a Seatbelt fallback
On-device privacy filter scrubs PII before cloud sends and blocks the send if anything leaks
weaknesses: macOS 15.5+ on Apple Silicon only; no Linux or Windows build
Linux VM sandbox needs macOS 26; older systems get weaker Seatbelt confinement

tools.name: reef
tools.description: Serves agent traffic, collects feedback, and publishes versioned weight or harness updates
strengths: Harness-evolving recipes (Reefine) need only a model endpoint, no training GPUs
Serves /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses and /v1/messages while updates roll in live
Versioned artifact history with candidate evaluation; rejected candidates leave the current release serving
weaknesses: Weight training needs a supported GPU stack; exact GPU requirements are only in linked docs
Requires Python 3.12+ and git-lfs; no Docker or compose files provided

tools.name: openpencil
tools.description: Vector design editor that generates UI on canvas from prompts
strengths: `.op` files are plain JSON, so designs diff and version cleanly in Git
Built-in MCP server over stdio or local HTTP, no Node.js required
Code export to React, Vue, Svelte, Flutter, SwiftUI, Compose and React Native
weaknesses: Web host and Docker image support only built-in API-key agents, not CLI agents
Building from source needs three git submodules (jian, casement, agent)

tools.name: bla
tools.description: Hardens release artifacts against AI reverse-engineering agents
strengths: Format shields are pure TypeScript/Node, with no Ghidra, IDA or packer dependency
One setup command registers MCP tools with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others
Empirical table names the exact REA limit tripped per format, reproducible via npm run redteam:rea
weaknesses: Token and USD amplification figures are internal estimates, not measured against live agents
Ghidra, Frida, LLDB, JADX and firmware paths are not empirically tested

tools.name: smile
tools.description: JVM machine learning library with classic ML, deep learning and LLM inference
strengths: Broad classic ML coverage: SVM, random forest, GBDT, t-SNE, UMAP, HMM, CRF, FP-growth
Serve module exposes SMILE, ONNX and OpenAI-compatible chat endpoints with a bundled web UI
Idiomatic Scala and Kotlin APIs plus a Spark integration module
weaknesses: Multi-product license with commercial terms; not a single standard open-source license
v5+ requires Java 25, which limits use on older JVM stacks

tools.name: raven
tools.description: Host agent that orchestrates built-in and third-party agents in shared workflows
strengths: Presets for 13 third-party agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes and others)
Four built-in agents: research, coding, visual design, unattended long-running workflows
Trajectory view shows every agent, turn and step of a run on one timeline
weaknesses: Curator self-improvement is experimental and ships with the repo, not the package
Benchmark claims are self-reported and shown only as images

tools.name: HelixDB
tools.description: Graph database with built-in vector and BM25 search, written in Rust
strengths: Graph, vector and BM25 queries in one transactional engine
SDKs for Rust, TypeScript, Python and Go emit the same JSON request
No build or deploy step for queries; embedded mode runs in-process
weaknesses: Local dev needs Docker or Podman; data is in memory unless started with --disk
Cypher support is only in source builds

tools.name: axonhub
tools.description: LLM gateway that translates between OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs
strengths: Cross-format translation: call Claude with the OpenAI SDK or GPT with the Anthropic SDK
Per-request cost breakdown for input, output and cached tokens, plus thread-level tracing
Covers text, image generation, embedding and rerank APIs across about a dozen providers
weaknesses: Realtime API is listed as Todo; AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud channels are still in testing
Mixed licensing: Apache-2.0 plus LGPL-3.0 for the llm directory

tools.name: ai-for-beginners
tools.description: 24-lesson AI curriculum with notebooks in PyTorch and TensorFlow
strengths: Most lessons have notebooks in both PyTorch and TensorFlow
Covers symbolic AI, genetic algorithms and multi-agent systems alongside deep learning
Many lessons include labs; Binder badge allows running without local setup
weaknesses: Excludes generative AI services, chatbots and deep math; points to other courses
README says neural architecture coverage may lag the state of the art

tools.name: Voicebox
tools.description: Local voice studio for cloning, TTS, dictation and agent speech
strengths: Eight switchable TTS engines; Chatterbox Multilingual covers 23 languages
REST API plus HTTP and stdio MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf
Runs on MLX, CUDA, ROCm, DirectML, Intel Arc or CPU
weaknesses: No prebuilt Linux binaries; build from source or use Docker
Only Chatterbox Turbo honors tags like [laugh]; other engines read them aloud

tools.name: timesfm
tools.description: Pretrained time-series foundation model for zero-shot forecasting from Google Research
strengths: Zero-shot forecasting of univariate and multivariate series with past-only and future covariates
Returns point forecast plus 9 quantiles (0.1 to 0.9) per step
MLX backend runs 3.0 on Apple silicon without PyTorch, numerically matched to PyTorch
weaknesses: TimesFM 3.0 weights are non-commercial and non-production; commercial use only via Google Cloud services
Not an officially supported Google product

tools.name: chidiwilliams/buzz
tools.description: Offline desktop app for transcribing and translating audio with Whisper
strengths: Runs offline; transcription and translation stay on the local machine
Several Whisper backends: Whisper.cpp with Vulkan, CUDA, Apple Silicon, Hugging Face models
Speaker identification and speech separation for noisy audio
weaknesses: Current releases require Apple silicon; last Intel Mac version is 1.4.5
Windows installer is unsigned and triggers a security warning

tools.name: Hermes WebUI
tools.description: Browser UI for Hermes Agent with sessions, workspace file browser and profiles
strengths: No build step or bundler: Python backend plus vanilla JS frontend
Reuses existing Hermes agent config, models and CLI sessions, which appear in the sidebar
Workspace file browser with preview, editing, rename and git branch badge
weaknesses: Only a front-end for Hermes Agent; it does not work standalone with other agents
Native Windows is unsupported by bootstrap; WSL2 or a community guide is needed

tools.name: web-llm
tools.description: Runs LLMs inside the browser on WebGPU with an OpenAI-style JS API
strengths: No server needed: inference and model caching happen client-side, so prompts stay in the browser
OpenAI-style chat API with streaming, JSON mode, and seed for reproducible output
Web Worker, Service Worker and Chrome extension support, with examples in the repo
weaknesses: Requires a WebGPU-capable browser; the README gives no browser or GPU requirements
First run downloads full model weights, which can take a long time

tools.name: optuna
tools.description: Python hyperparameter optimization library with define-by-run search spaces and pruning
strengths: Search spaces are plain Python, so conditionals and loops work inside the objective
