Pruning of unpromising trials, multi-objective and constrained optimization are supported
Installs from pip or conda with few requirements; MIT license
weaknesses: Web dashboard is a separate package (optuna-dashboard), not part of core
Requires Python 3.10 or newer

tools.name: semantica
tools.description: Python library for building context graphs with decision provenance and reasoning
strengths: Graph construction, reasoning and provenance are deterministic; no LLM required
Swappable storage: Oxigraph, Blazegraph, Jena, RDF4J, Neo4j, FalkorDB, AGE, Neptune
Decisions stored as graph nodes with causal tracing, precedent search and PROV-O export
weaknesses: Broad scope (ontology, reasoning, ingestion, analytics) means a large surface to learn
Explains context and decisions outside the LLM only, not the model's internal reasoning

tools.name: nltk
tools.description: Python library of classic NLP modules, corpora and tutorials
strengths: Backed by a published book and tutorials, suited to teaching NLP
Ships with corpora and datasets alongside the code
Apache 2.0 source license; last release 2026-10-21
weaknesses: Corpora are redistributable for non-commercial use only, per each corpus README
Documentation license is non-commercial and no-derivatives

tools.name: opencreator
tools.description: Creator workspace for video translation, image and video generation, built on Codex CLI
strengths: Video translation covers 14 source and 101 target languages, with bilingual subtitles and dubbing
Reuses Codex agent loop, Skills and MCP config instead of a second engine
Local transcription via faster-whisper, WhisperKit or whisper.cpp where available
weaknesses: Depends on Codex CLI and a configured model provider or ChatGPT sign-in
Image, video and voice generation need external services set under AI Services

tools.name: open_clip
tools.description: PyTorch library for training and running CLIP-style image-text models
strengths: Large zoo of pretrained checkpoints with ImageNet zero-shot results, up to 85.4% in the README table
Loads OpenAI, SigLIP, SigLIP2, DFN and PE-Core weights through one API
Training supports DDP, FSDP2, torch.compile strategies and SigLIP loss chunking
weaknesses: Main branch breaks the training API; older scripts need the v3 branch or a 3.x release
Horovod, torchscript and trace support were removed on main

tools.name: yue
tools.description: Lyrics-to-song model that writes an editable melody and chord score first
strengths: Editable ABC score between prompt and audio lets you inspect and change melody and chords
Staged Python API: plan, generate_semantic, synthesize, decode; artifacts saved per run
Zero-shot covers via SheetSage2 transcription with the same checkpoint, no cover fine-tuning
weaknesses: Needs Linux, Python 3.12 and an NVIDIA BF16 GPU with 24 GB VRAM
Weights are CC BY-NC 4.0; commercial company use requires a separate license

tools.name: edge0
tools.description: Streaming MoE inference that serves 35B models from SSD on Apple Silicon
strengths: Reported 2.9 GiB peak MLX allocator memory for the 35B tier on a Mac mini M4 Pro
Ships trained LoRA and prerouter adapters with the checkpoints, ready to serve
Separate engines for macOS (Rust), iOS (Swift), Android (Kotlin) and Windows (C++/Vulkan)
weaknesses: Python framework supports only macOS on Apple Silicon; CUDA backend is roadmap only
Decode speed is 14.9-17.7 tok/s for the 35B tier, 23.9-25.3 for the 8B

tools.name: presenton
tools.description: Generates editable PPTX and PDF slide decks from prompts or documents
strengths: Exports fully editable PPTX as well as PDF
Many text LLM providers, including local Ollama and LM Studio, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Includes a generation API, a built-in MCP server and multi-user workspaces with an admin panel
weaknesses: SSO, SCIM, audit logs and Helm charts are only in the Enterprise edition
Community template gallery calls a cloud service by default; air-gapped setups must disable it

tools.name: lancedb
tools.description: Embedded vector database built on the Lance columnar format
strengths: Runs embedded and locally, with no separate server required per the README
Combines vector search, full-text search and SQL in one store
Automatic data versioning and zero-copy access without extra infrastructure
weaknesses: README gives no benchmarks or hardware figures to back the billion-vector claims
Managed Cloud and Enterprise tiers exist; feature split with open source is not detailed

tools.name: metaflow
tools.description: Python framework for building, scaling and deploying ML and AI workflows
strengths: Same flow code runs on a laptop, in a notebook, on cloud compute and in production
Built-in experiment tracking, artifact versioning and a client API for inspecting past runs
Supports foreach parallelism and gang-scheduled distributed jobs on CPUs and GPUs
weaknesses: Cloud scaling and production orchestration need separate infrastructure setup beyond pip install
Not LLM-specific; README describes no model serving or agent features

tools.name: rig
tools.description: Rust library for building LLM agents, plus a Bevy-based terminal coding agent
strengths: 20+ model providers and 10+ vector stores behind one interface
Covers completion, embeddings, transcription, audio and image generation
Core and agent runtime target browser WASM (wasm32-unknown-unknown)
weaknesses: Pre-1.0; each release contains breaking changes, so migration notes must be read
Rust only; the coding agent needs Rust 1.97.1 or newer

tools.name: treg
tools.description: Tool registry proxy giving agents one token for a priced API catalog
strengths: Credentials are injected server-side; callers and agents never see provider keys
Own key takes precedence over treg's and is never metered
Per-call pricing shown in catalog; 402 response carries balance and top-up URL
weaknesses: Catalog access relies on treg's provider accounts via hosted treg.to, not self-hosting alone
License is NOASSERTION, so reuse terms are unclear

tools.name: vowpal_wabbit
tools.description: Online machine learning library with contextual bandits and hashed features
strengths: Memory footprint is bounded; training data is not loaded into RAM
Hashing trick bounds feature set size independent of data volume
Several contextual bandit algorithms for reinforcement learning
weaknesses: Not an LLM or deep learning tool; no neural model serving described
README gives no hardware requirements or benchmark numbers

tools.name: Engram
tools.description: Persistent memory store for AI coding agents, exposed over MCP
strengths: Single Go binary with one SQLite file; no Node, Python or Docker required
One-command setup for 14 agents, plus manual MCP config for any other client
Memory is project-aware, resolved from explicit project, env var or cwd
weaknesses: Search is SQLite FTS5 full-text; README mentions no embedding or vector retrieval
Aimed at coding agents; not a general-purpose memory layer for other apps

tools.name: yuxi
tools.description: Multi-tenant agent platform with Milvus RAG, Neo4j graphs and LangGraph agents
strengths: Per-user, department and tenant permissions over knowledge bases, agents, Skills and models
Built-in RAG evaluation and retrieval testing with embedding and rerank scores
Supports MCP, Skills, SubAgents and sandboxed file output with in-browser preview
weaknesses: Heavy stack: Milvus, Neo4j, PostgreSQL, MinerU and PaddleOCR all run in Compose
README is mainly Chinese; English version is a separate file

tools.name: nvidia-nemo/guardrails
tools.description: Programmable input, output and dialog guardrails for LLM applications
strengths: Five rail types: input, dialog, retrieval, execution and output
Built-in rails for jailbreak, PII masking, fact-checking and hallucination checks
Python API plus CLI server with OpenAI-style chat completions endpoint
weaknesses: Dialog rails require learning Colang, a separate modeling language
Sends anonymous telemetry to NVIDIA by default; opt-out needed

tools.name: dramaclaw
tools.description: Node-canvas and pipeline for producing AI short dramas from script to final cut
strengths: Covers the whole chain: ingest, episode planning, storyboards, voice-over, subtitles and video export
Canvas with 18 node types plus an agent that builds and runs graphs after confirmation
Light local footprint: 2 vCPU / 4 GB recommended, GPU only for the optional world extra
weaknesses: Elastic License 2.0 with a Powered by DramaClaw notice; hosted SaaS use not permitted
Previz 3D stage and interactive stories are closed beta, not in the main branch

tools.name: mooncake
tools.description: KV cache transfer engine and distributed cache store for LLM inference clusters
strengths: Transfer Engine reports up to 190 GB/s on 8x400 Gbps RoCE, about 4.6x faster than TCP
Integrated upstream in SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, LMDeploy, NIXL and vLLM-Ascend
Mooncake Store pools KV cache across DRAM and SSD/NVMe with replication and eviction
weaknesses: Infrastructure component, not a standalone server; needs a serving engine such as vLLM or SGLang
Reported bandwidth figures assume RDMA NICs and multi-node GPU clusters

tools.name: open-multi-agent
tools.description: TypeScript runtime for multi-agent teams with approval gates and offline run review
strengths: Three modes: runAgent, runTasks for explicit pipelines, runTeam for goal-planned task graphs
Approval gates before plans, tasks or tool calls; persistent storage lets restarts resume
Offline Run Viewer and run journal; no telemetry or hosted control plane
weaknesses: TypeScript and Node.js only; Node 20 is upstream-EOL and slated for removal
Approval UI and notifications must be built by the application

tools.name: pytorch-metric-learning
tools.description: PyTorch library of metric learning losses, miners, and distances for embedding models
strengths: Losses, miners, distances and reducers are separate components that can be combined
Fits into a plain PyTorch loop; core needs only PyTorch and NumPy
Each component's docs page states its signature, defaults, tensor contract, and paper
weaknesses: Version 3 requires Python 3.12+, PyTorch 2.14.0+ and NumPy 2.5.3+
Upgrading from version 2 requires a migration guide because names changed

tools.name: anymodelbot
tools.description: Multi-bot desktop assistant with memory, file access and chat-app channels
strengths: Per-bot memory, persona and workspace, three permission levels, approval cards for outside writes
Connects to WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, Slack and Discord with shared account setup
Background tasks and scheduled rules with per-task budgets, quiet hours and daily message caps
weaknesses: Default model route goes through hosted Modelflare, which keeps request logs
Image and video generation only work through Modelflare, not direct API keys

tools.name: Agenta
tools.description: Shared team workspace for building and running chat-built agents
strengths: Multi-user by design: roles, shared agents and chat sessions, per-agent tool permissions
Each session runs in its own sandbox; model credentials are not exposed to the agent
Every run is traced and costs are tracked per agent, with versions visible
weaknesses: Supports only Claude Code, Pi and Codex harnesses today; more are on the roadmap
Not a visual workflow builder; agents decide steps, so execution is less predictable

tools.name: basic-memory
tools.description: MCP server that stores AI memory as Markdown notes with a knowledge graph
strengths: Notes are plain Markdown files, editable in Obsidian or any editor, with two-way sync
Hybrid full-text and vector search via FastEmbed, with optional cross-encoder reranking
MCP tools carry read-only/destructive/idempotent hints; works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, VS Code
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license may be a problem for embedding in proprietary products
Install needs uv and the --prerelease=allow flag due to a FastMCP 4 pre-release dependency

tools.name: rapid-mlx
tools.description: MLX-based LLM inference server for Apple Silicon with coding-agent tool calling
strengths: OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible endpoints, so most local-endpoint clients work without an adapter
`rapid-mlx launch <agent>` sets up a private profile without editing existing agent settings
27 tool-call parser modules with auto-detect fallback, aimed at coding agents
weaknesses: Apple Silicon only; Windows and Linux desktop builds are not available
Speed comparisons are the project's own, single run per engine

tools.name: Firecrawl
tools.description: Web API that turns sites and searches into markdown or JSON for LLMs
strengths: Endpoints for search, scrape, crawl, map, batch scrape and document parsing
Official SDKs for seven languages, plus a CLI and MCP server
Outputs markdown, HTML, screenshots or schema-based structured JSON
weaknesses: README examples target the hosted API and require an API key
AGPL-3.0 license restricts use in closed-source network services

tools.name: ai-agents-for-beginners
tools.description: 18-lesson course on building AI agents with Microsoft Agent Framework
strengths: Covers design patterns, RAG, memory, protocols, deployment and security across 18 lessons
Each lesson pairs a README with Python samples; most also have a video
Translated into 50+ languages via Co-op Translator
weaknesses: Samples depend on Microsoft Foundry, which requires an Azure account
Code centers on Microsoft Agent Framework, not other agent libraries

tools.name: ai-hedge-fund
tools.description: Terminal app that paper-trades and backtests LLM-driven investor agents on stocks
strengths: Installs with pipx, uv or pip; API keys are prompted for and saved to ~/.hedge-fund/.env
Paper-trading sessions go into a hash-chained ledger, so NAV is an auditable record
Approval step shows the exact decision before a paper trade executes; kill switch included
weaknesses: Does not execute real trades; no broker integration
Requires a Financial Datasets API key for prices, fundamentals and earnings

tools.name: llama_index
tools.description: Python framework for RAG and agent apps over your own data
strengths: Over 300 integration packages for LLM, embedding and vector store providers
Small core package plus a starter bundle; install only the integrations needed
High-level API indexes and queries a directory in a few lines
weaknesses: README says company focus has shifted to the paid LlamaParse platform
README is noted as less up to date than the documentation

tools.name: SillyTavern
tools.description: Local chat front end for role-play across many LLM backends
strengths: Runs on anything that can run Node.js 20; no GPU needed for the UI itself
Backends: KoboldCpp, Horde, NovelAI, oobabooga, TabbyAPI, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Claude, Mistral
WorldInfo lorebooks and deep prompt controls for long-form character chat
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license
Single-user local tool; no accounts or team features

tools.name: pentagi
tools.description: Multi-agent system that runs autonomous pentests with nmap, Metasploit and sqlmap
strengths: Runs 20+ tools such as nmap, Metasploit and sqlmap in an isolated Docker sandbox
Supports 10+ LLM providers, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and local Ollama or vLLM
Persistent memory in PostgreSQL with pgvector, plus optional Neo4j knowledge graph
weaknesses: Full stack spans many containers (Postgres, Neo4j, Langfuse, ClickHouse, Grafana), a heavy footprint
Not a breach-and-attack-simulation tool; no predefined campaigns or attack plans

tools.name: scrapegraph-ai
tools.description: Python library that builds LLM-driven scraping pipelines from a prompt and a URL
strengths: Prompt plus URL returns a JSON dict; no per-site selectors to write
Runs against local Ollama models or hosted APIs by changing the llm config
Several pipelines: single page, multi-page, search results, Python script generation
weaknesses: Proxies, anti-bot handling and scaling are left to the user in the open-source version
Needs a separate `playwright install` step to fetch page content

tools.name: gallery
tools.description: Mobile app for running open LLMs offline on Android and iOS
strengths: Inference runs on-device via LiteRT, so prompts and media stay offline
Chat, image Q&A, audio transcription, prompt lab and media search in one app
Built-in benchmarks show how each model performs on your own hardware
weaknesses: README calls it an experimental Beta release
Requires Android 12+ or iOS 17+; the macOS build is versioned 0.1.0

tools.name: paddle
tools.description: Deep learning framework with dynamic/static graphs and automatic parallel training
strengths: Automatic parallelism from minimal tensor partition annotations on single-card code
Same framework handles both large-model training and inference
High-order autodiff, complex numbers and Fourier transforms for scientific computing
weaknesses: README gives no hardware requirements or supported Python versions
README refers to both 3.2 and 3.3, so the current feature set is unclear

tools.name: machine-learning-for-trading
tools.description: Code for the book on ML trading strategies, with nine case studies
strengths: 27 chapter guides map book sections to notebooks and list the data each needs
Nine case studies apply one pipeline across ETFs, crypto, options, FX and futures
Covers overfitting controls: walk-forward CV, Deflated Sharpe Ratio, White's Reality Check
weaknesses: Written to accompany a paid book; the book carries no code listings
Some case studies need real compute or licensed data, per the README

tools.name: funasr
tools.description: Speech recognition toolkit with VAD, punctuation, speaker labeling and streaming
strengths: Composable pipeline: ASR, FSMN-VAD, ct-punc and CAM++ speaker clustering in one AutoModel call
Streaming Paraformer with chunked input and per-session cache
GGUF llama.cpp binaries run SenseVoice on CPU with no Python at runtime
weaknesses: Language coverage differs per checkpoint; Fun-ASR-Nano is only zh/en/ja plus Chinese dialects
Speaker labels are anonymous per recording, not known-speaker identification

tools.name: KTransformers
tools.description: CPU-GPU hybrid inference and MoE fine-tuning for large models on limited VRAM
strengths: Runs large MoE models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM with experts split across CPU and GPU
Fine-tuning via LLaMA-Factory: LoRA and BF16 full-parameter, claimed 6-12x faster than ZeRO-Offload
CPU kernels cover AMX, AVX512 and AVX2-only machines
weaknesses: Needs large host RAM for big models; one earlier DeepSeek-R1 setup cited 382GB DRAM
README is mostly a changelog; setup lives in scattered sub-docs

tools.name: carla
tools.description: Autonomous driving simulator built on Unreal Engine 5.5 with a Python API
strengths: Open assets (maps, vehicles, buildings) included, code MIT and assets CC-BY
Configurable sensor suites and environmental conditions, driven through a Python API
Ecosystem repos for ROS bridge, Scenario_Runner, Autoware bridge and a driving leaderboard
weaknesses: Heavy hardware: 32 GB+ RAM and an RTX 3070-class GPU with 16 GB+ VRAM recommended
Build needs GitHub-linked Epic Games access to the Unreal Engine 5.5 fork

tools.name: dlib
tools.description: C++ machine learning toolkit with Python bindings
strengths: Boost Software License permits use in closed-source commercial software
Installs via CMake, vcpkg, or pip for the Python API
Ships a unit test suite (dtest) and many example programs
weaknesses: Requires a C++17 compiler and CMake to build from source
pip install from source needs a local compiler toolchain

tools.name: browseros
tools.description: Secondary Chromium browser that AI coding agents drive over MCP with your logins
strengths: Imports Chrome logins, bookmarks and extensions in one click, so agents use real accounts
Works with any MCP client; one-click connect for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and others
Sessions saved locally as scrubbable video with step-by-step action timeline
weaknesses: Linux builds are x64 only
Sends anonymous usage events by default; opt-out via a Settings toggle

tools.name: tvm
tools.description: Python-first machine learning compiler for optimizing and deploying models
strengths: Cross-level design: TensorIR for tensor programs and Relax for graphs, optimized jointly
Most compiler transformations can be customized in Python
Apache-2.0 license under the Apache committer governance model
weaknesses: README lists no supported hardware targets or model formats
README gives no install steps, version requirements or benchmarks

tools.name: llm
tools.description: CLI and Python library for prompting local and hosted LLMs, logging to SQLite
strengths: Plugin system adds remote providers, local models, tools, fragments and embedding models
Stores prompts and responses in SQLite for later querying
Works as both a shell command (pipes, stdin, system prompts) and a Python library
weaknesses: Command-line only; no built-in web UI or user accounts
Anthropic, Gemini and Ollama access each need a separate plugin install

tools.name: tokenizers
tools.description: Rust tokenizer library with Python and Node.js bindings
strengths: Every kernel has a portable scalar path; SIMD (NEON, AVX-512, SSE, wasm SIMD128) is optional
Sub-crates let serving builds omit training and legacy conversion code
Bindings for Rust, Python and Node.js; loads from file or Hugging Face Hub
weaknesses: v1.0.0 is a release candidate; Python install needs pip --pre
Python training, save, offsets, pair input and decode_stream are not back yet

tools.name: tambo
tools.description: React toolkit where an agent picks and renders your components
strengths: Zod-schema components become LLM tool definitions; props stream to the UI
Supports MCP tools, prompts, elicitations and sampling
Browser-side local tools can touch the DOM or React state
weaknesses: Hosted Tambo Cloud closes October 31, 2026; user data is deleted November 30
New signups are closed, and the team has moved on to a different product

tools.name: Pocket TTS
tools.description: CPU-only text-to-speech model with voice cloning and streaming output
strengths: Runs on CPU with 2 cores; about 6x real time on a MacBook Air M4
Voice cloning from a wav file, with export to fast-loading safetensors
Standalone Rust binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows need no Python or PyTorch
weaknesses: GPU is not officially supported; serve and the Docker image always run on CPU
No way to insert silence or pauses in the input text

tools.name: kev
tools.description: Small decision models answering yes/no, choice and score questions over text
strengths: Calibrated probabilities: each checkpoint ships with a fitted temperature
Works with the TypeSafe Python SDK unchanged via the /v1/systemone endpoint
Four sizes; 0.8B runs on a 4 GB GPU, 27B scores within a point of Jev on new sources
weaknesses: Not on PyPI; install from source with uv, Python 3.12 or 3.13 only
Kev-27B is 51 GB of full weights and needs an 80 GB-class GPU

tools.name: Higress
tools.description: Istio and Envoy API gateway with LLM proxying and MCP server hosting
strengths: Wasm plugins in Go/Rust/JS with hot updates, no connection drops on config change
Streams request and response bodies, including SSE, for LLM traffic
Hosts MCP servers with auth, rate limiting and audit logs; OpenAPI-to-MCP conversion
weaknesses: Heavier to operate than a lightweight LLM proxy; Istio/Envoy concepts apply
Default images are pulled from Alibaba Cloud registries; mirrors needed in some regions

tools.name: cog
tools.description: Packages Python ML models into Docker images with a generated HTTP API
strengths: Inputs and outputs are declared in Python types; OpenAPI schema is generated and validated
Resolves CUDA, cuDNN, PyTorch, TensorFlow and Python version combinations automatically
Same cog.yaml drives local runs (cog run, cog serve) and production builds (cog build)
weaknesses: Requires Docker, plus Buildx if using Docker Engine instead of Docker Desktop
No native Windows support; Windows 11 needs WSL 2

tools.name: openfilm
tools.description: Video editor and CLI that lets coding agents write films as HTML pages
strengths: Deterministic frame(t) contract; look renders frames twice in shuffled order and flags any that differ
Studio edits are saved to the film files, so the agent sees and keeps them
Exports MP4, GIF, stems, subtitles, transparent video and NLE timelines for Premiere, Resolve and FCP
weaknesses: Studio should be used in a Chromium browser so the preview matches the export
Generated voice, music, images and video need third-party service keys or an OpenFilm sign-in

tools.name: flowgram.ai
tools.description: TypeScript toolkit for embedding visual workflow editors in your own product
strengths: Two canvas modes: free layout and fixed layout with branch and loop nodes
Form engine covers validation, linkage and side effects for node config
Variable engine provides scope chains and type inference across nodes
weaknesses: Front-end toolkit, not a hosted workflow server; you build the platform around it
Desktop app is a preview; installers are unsigned and macOS builds not notarized

tools.name: mlx-lm
tools.description: Python package and CLI for running and fine-tuning LLMs on Apple silicon with MLX
strengths: Pulls MLX-compatible models from Hugging Face, with thousands in the MLX Community org
Converts, quantizes (e.g. 4-bit) and uploads models with one command
LoRA and full fine-tuning, including on quantized models
weaknesses: Targets Apple silicon only, per the README
Wiring memory for large models needs macOS 15 or higher

tools.name: harbor-framework/harbor
tools.description: Evaluation harness for running agents and models against container-based benchmarks
strengths: Official harness for Terminal-Bench 2.0; SWE-Bench and Aider Polyglot also listed
Same `harbor run` command works on local Docker or cloud providers via `--env`
Parallel runs across sandbox providers including Daytona, Modal, LangSmith and Blaxel
weaknesses: Needs model provider API keys and, for scale-out, a sandbox provider account
Local runs depend on Docker; no image or compose file in the repo

tools.name: open-duet
tools.description: Workspace for named AI agents with teams, memory, and scheduled routines
strengths: Per-agent approval modes: Ask first, Accept edits, Plan only, with reviewable tool activity
Works with CLI engines, OpenRouter and OpenAI-compatible local servers like Ollama and LM Studio
Routines trigger by schedule, webhook or manual run; none approve actions automatically
weaknesses: Team lead agents currently must use Claude
Server mode is experimental and single-owner, not multi-user

tools.name: flashinfer
tools.description: CUDA kernel library for LLM attention, GEMM, MoE and sampling
strengths: Covers attention, GEMM, MoE, sampling, RoPE and norm kernels behind one Python API
Supports SM 7.5 to SM 12.1, including FP8 and NVFP4/MXFP4 on Blackwell
Compatible with CUDAGraph and torch.compile for low-latency serving
weaknesses: Not a server or end-user tool; needs an inference engine or custom PyTorch code
NVIDIA GPUs only; not all features work on all compute capabilities

tools.name: koharu
tools.description: Desktop manga translator with local detection, OCR, inpainting and LLM translation
strengths: Full pipeline in one app: detection, OCR, inpainting, translation, typesetting and layered PSD export
Runs vision models and GGUF LLMs locally; hosted LLM and MT providers are optional
GPU backends: CUDA, ROCm/HIP, Metal and Vulkan; no full CUDA SDK install needed
weaknesses: CPU inference is documented as substantially slower than GPU
Editor canvas needs WebGPU and a current graphics driver even with CPU inference

tools.name: paperspine
tools.description: Agent skill that drafts research papers with analysis, figures and review
strengths: Five stage Skills can be called separately, e.g. followwriting to revise one section
Example papers ship with public data, analysis code and editable source ZIPs
Install manager checks SHA-256 and supports update, rollback and uninstall
weaknesses: Current release is a V6 beta (6.0.0-beta.2)
Web workbench is Windows x64 only and requires the Codex CLI

tools.name: llama-swap
tools.description: Go proxy that starts and swaps local model servers per request
strengths: One binary and one YAML file; no external dependencies
Covers chat, embeddings, rerank, audio, image and Anthropic messages endpoints
Per-model ttl auto-unload, API keys, Prometheus /metrics and log streaming endpoints
weaknesses: Does not run inference itself; needs separate upstream servers like llama-server
Python servers like vllm are recommended to run in Docker or Podman for clean shutdown

tools.name: zotero-mcp
tools.description: MCP server and CLI that lets AI assistants search and annotate Zotero
strengths: Local mode reads straight from zotero.sqlite; no web API key needed for reads
Agent skill uses 98 tokens of context versus 7,939 for the default 38-tool MCP profile
Semantic search supports local, OpenAI, Gemini or Ollama embeddings
weaknesses: As an MCP server, tool schemas cost about 8k to 11k tokens on every request
Local writes need Zotero 10+ and a one-time authorize step, or a web API key

tools.name: torchtitan
tools.description: PyTorch-native training stack for pretraining, fine-tuning and RL of large models
strengths: Stacks FSDP2, TP, PP, CP and EP into N-D layouts without rewriting the model
Config is a Python recipe function, so runs are readable and copyable
TitanRL shares model definitions and kernels with vLLM, with a bitwise-parity mode
weaknesses: Needs a recent PyTorch nightly; stable releases pin nightly torch and torchao
Verified recipes exist for only some models; others have CI debug configs only

tools.name: openagent
tools.description: Self-hosted AI assistant with RAG, browser-use agents and MCP tools
strengths: Ships as a single binary; native Windows support without WSL or Docker
30+ model providers including Ollama, switchable per conversation
Agent tool calls show arguments and return values step by step
weaknesses: Shell and browser tools run from the agent loop; sandboxing is not described
Broad scope (RAG, workflows, admin, media) makes it heavier than a focused assistant

tools.name: obsidian-second-brain
tools.description: Claude Code plugin that saves chats into a linked Obsidian vault and recalls them
strengths: Notes stay as local Markdown files; core commands need no API keys
Ingest rewrites existing pages rather than only appending new notes
Runs in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Grok Bot
weaknesses: Large surface of about 48 commands; README suggests starting with three
Research commands depend on external services such as Perplexity, Grok and Gemini

tools.name: esp32-iphone-agent
tools.description: AI agent that taps, swipes and types on an iPhone via an ESP32 board
strengths: Needs no computer at run time: only the phone, a ~$7 board and a model endpoint
Works with any OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint, including vLLM, llama.cpp and Ollama
Every run is stored on the phone with step-by-step replay and trace export
weaknesses: Requires specific hardware: an ESP32-S3 with native USB and PSRAM
Mirrors at 480x1040, up to 5 fps; each step takes a few seconds

tools.name: executorch
tools.description: PyTorch runtime for running exported models on phones, browsers and microcontrollers
strengths: Starts from torch.export, so existing PyTorch models need no separate framework
Backends span XNNPACK, Core ML, Vulkan, Qualcomm, MediaTek, OpenVINO, Arm Ethos-U, Cadence
Selective build links only the operators, kernels and delegates a deployment needs
weaknesses: Each hardware target needs its own backend-specific .pte export
Deployment depends on torch.export capture and operator coverage; some models need decompositions

tools.name: ruby_llm
tools.description: Ruby library for chat, tools, agents and evals across 23 LLM providers
strengths: One API covers 23 providers, including Ollama and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Rails generators give Active Record chat persistence and a working chat UI
Built-in evaluations, cost tracking and OpenTelemetry tracing
weaknesses: Ruby only; no bindings for other languages
OCR, video and reranking need API keys from specific providers

tools.name: openscience
tools.description: Research agent that reads papers, runs code and experiments, and logs every step
strengths: Full trace of searches, code runs and file writes for each turn
Hundreds of bundled science skills plus connectors to PubMed, arXiv, ChEMBL, UniProt
Remote compute on Modal, SSH, Slurm or PBS, approved before jobs run
weaknesses: First-run setup asks you to sign in to an OpenScience account
Skills are mostly third-party; a skill does not guarantee its tools are installed

tools.name: transformerlens
tools.description: Python library for inspecting and editing activations in language models
strengths: Caches and hooks any internal activation, enabling ablation and activation patching
Covers 15,000+ models across 140+ architecture families via TransformerBridge
Default bridge output matches raw HuggingFace logits and activations
weaknesses: 4.0 removed HookedTransformer.from_pretrained, so older code needs migration
HookedSAETransformer was removed in 2.0; SAE work moved to SAELens

tools.name: huggingface_hub
tools.description: Official hf CLI and Python client for the Hugging Face Hub
strengths: One package provides both the `hf` CLI and a Python API for downloads, uploads and repos
Local cache for downloaded files; Xet chunk-deduplicated storage on the Hub handles large files
`hf skills add` installs a command reference for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others
weaknesses: Tied to the Hugging Face Hub; it is a client, not a self-hostable server
Inference and Jobs run on Hugging Face infrastructure, not locally

tools.name: awesome-llm-apps
tools.description: Collection of 100+ runnable LLM agent, RAG and voice app examples in Python
strengths: Broad coverage: starter agents, multi-agent teams, voice, MCP and about 20 RAG variants
Each example is a separate folder, so one can be run without the rest
Apache-2.0 license allows reuse in commercial projects
weaknesses: Not a library or product: no shared package, versioning or releases
Many examples need paid API keys (OpenAI, Gemini, Firecrawl and others)

tools.name: llms-from-scratch
tools.description: Book code for building, pretraining and finetuning a GPT-style LLM in PyTorch
strengths: Chapter notebooks with exercise solutions, plus a 17-hour companion video course
Implements everything in plain PyTorch without external LLM libraries
Main chapter code runs on a laptop and uses a GPU automatically if present
weaknesses: Tied to a print book; extensions to main chapter code are not accepted
Trains small educational models, not production-scale ones

tools.name: tesseract
tools.description: OCR engine and command-line tool with LSTM recognition for 100+ languages
strengths: Recognizes more than 100 languages with UTF-8 support using downloadable traineddata files
Outputs plain text, hOCR, PDF, invisible-text PDF, TSV, ALTO and PAGE
C and C++ APIs plus a CLI; wrappers for other languages are listed in the docs
weaknesses: No GUI included; third-party front-ends are needed
Accuracy depends on input image quality; preprocessing is often required

tools.name: huggingface/datasets
tools.description: Python library for loading, streaming and preprocessing ML datasets on Apache Arrow
strengths: Memory-mapped Arrow storage lets datasets exceed available RAM
Streaming mode with `streaming=True` avoids downloading full datasets
Converts to NumPy, Pandas, Polars, PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX and Spark
weaknesses: Tied to the Hugging Face Hub for the one-line public dataset loading
Audio, vision, PDF and NIfTI support need optional extras installed

tools.name: DB-GPT
tools.description: Agentic data assistant that writes SQL and code over your databases
strengths: NL-to-SQL plus Python analysis with sandboxed execution
Outputs charts, dashboards and HTML reports, not only answers
Skills importable from GitHub for repeatable analysis workflows
weaknesses: Recommended install pipes a remote script into bash
Docs and community largely on dbgpt.cn; Docker and GPU setup only there

tools.name: openworker
tools.description: Desktop AI coworker with approval gates, plus an SDK for agent apps
strengths: Tiered approvals with hard floors and per-tool-call audit records showing approval provenance
Sandboxing via OpenShell, built-in macOS sandbox, or a restricted Windows account
Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, or local Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM
weaknesses: Desktop app is in open beta; Windows builds are not code-signed yet
Prebuilt downloads only for macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64; no Linux build listed

tools.name: agent-lightning
tools.description: Reinforcement learning framework for training agents through a model proxy
strengths: Agents run unmodified; the gateway captures training data from model calls
Runs rollouts as Kubernetes Jobs without an external sandbox service
Ships a full coding-agent pipeline: data cleaning, reward-hacking prevention, training scripts
weaknesses: Requires a verl and vLLM GPU stack; setup example targets CUDA 13.0
v1.0 was a full refactor; earlier releases live on a separate v0.x branch

tools.name: Weaviate
tools.description: Go vector database with built-in vectorizers, hybrid search and RAG
strengths: Vectorizes at import with OpenAI, Cohere, HuggingFace, Google or a local model2vec container
Hybrid BM25 plus vector, image search, filtering, RAG and reranking in one query
Multi-tenancy, replication, RBAC, horizontal scaling and vector compression
weaknesses: Enterprise features in wl/ need a commercial license key; one image mixes both
Vectorization needs a module container or external API keys

tools.name: unstructured
tools.description: Python library that parses PDFs, Office files and HTML into typed elements
strengths: One `partition` call auto-detects file type and dispatches to format-specific parsers
Per-format pip extras (docx, pptx, pdf) keep installs smaller for narrow use cases
Apache-2.0 licensed; multi-platform Docker images for x86_64 and Apple silicon
weaknesses: README's own benchmark lists table cell content accuracy of 0.426 versus 0.866 for the paid API
PDF, image and Office parsing needs system packages: poppler, tesseract, libreoffice

tools.name: skill_seekers
tools.description: CLI that turns docs, repos, PDFs and videos into AI skills and RAG data
strengths: Handles 18 source types and exports to 22 targets from one scrape
AI enhancement runs via API providers or local agents such as Claude Code, no API cost
Ships an MCP server (40 tools) with stdio and HTTP transports
weaknesses: Quality of SKILL.md depends on an external LLM agent or API for enhancement
Video visual extraction needs extra installs, including GPU-specific PyTorch and easyocr

tools.name: openvino
tools.description: Inference toolkit for converting and running models on Intel CPUs, GPUs and NPUs
strengths: Converts models from several frameworks, so the original framework is not needed at deploy time
One API targets x86 and ARM CPUs, Intel GPUs and Intel NPUs
APIs in C++, Python, C and NodeJS; installs with pip install openvino
weaknesses: GPU and NPU support is limited to Intel hardware
Core library is not an HTTP server; serving needs OpenVINO Model Server

tools.name: crm
tools.description: Single-tenant CRM where a background agent researches and fills in contact records
strengths: Agent runs on its own queue (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED leases) and keeps working with the browser closed
Works with no external API keys by reading your own mail threads, meetings and signatures
Agent sandbox has deny-all egress and is never given DATABASE_URL
weaknesses: Three deployments plus Postgres; production path assumes Vercel, AI Gateway, Sandbox and Blob
Single tenant by design; no organizations or multi-workspace support

tools.name: aihot
tools.description: Self-hosted site that scores, clusters and summarizes news feeds into daily digests
strengths: Selection and writing prompts and admission thresholds are published and editable without code changes
Event clustering with per-source heat scoring, so repeated coverage from one outlet counts once
Exposes RSS, public API, MCP, llms.txt and an /agent page for agent consumers
weaknesses: Synced from the live site, not a polished generic framework; upstream sync not guaranteed
Needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM API key, so token costs recur

tools.name: brigade
tools.description: Self-hosted crew of AI agents with shared memory, reachable from chat apps
strengths: Supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, switchable mid-chat
Org-chart agent hierarchy with A2A policy, sub-agent fan-out and depth/child caps
Default filesystem storage under ~/.brigade/, no database needed; Convex is optional
weaknesses: Install is a curl-pipe-to-shell script; no Docker or compose files detected
App connectors depend on a Composio platform key (ak_)

tools.name: ten-framework
tools.description: Framework for building real-time voice and multimodal conversational agents
strengths: Many working voice examples: SIP calls, diarization, Live2D avatars, ESP32-S3 hardware
Companion projects for VAD and turn detection, plus a memory extension example
TMAN Designer lets you set STT, LLM and TTS keys in a graph UI
weaknesses: License is Apache 2.0 with additional restrictions, not plain Apache 2.0
Quick start needs Agora credentials plus OpenAI, Deepgram and ElevenLabs keys

tools.name: x-anylabeling
tools.description: Desktop app for AI-assisted annotation of images, video, text and point clouds
strengths: Wide model library: YOLO family, SAM 1/2/3, Grounding DINO, RF-DETR, PP-OCR, Qwen3-VL
Exports COCO, VOC, YOLO, DOTA, MOT, PPOCR, ShareGPT and other formats
Covers many tasks in one tool: boxes, polygons, rotated boxes, tracking, OCR, VQA, 3D point clouds
weaknesses: GPL-3.0 license imposes copyleft terms on derived or redistributed code
Requires Python 3.11+ for source or PyPI install

tools.name: copilot-sdk
tools.description: SDKs that embed the GitHub Copilot CLI agent runtime in your own apps
strengths: Six official language SDKs: Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Java, Rust
Node.js, .NET and Rust bundle the CLI; Python downloads it on first use
BYOK mode supports OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry and Anthropic keys without GitHub auth
weaknesses: Standard use needs a GitHub Copilot subscription; usage counts against Copilot allowance
Go and Java do not bundle the CLI; it must be embedded or installed manually

tools.name: realtimestt
tools.description: Python speech-to-text library with VAD, wake words and realtime transcription
strengths: Many selectable engines: faster-whisper, sherpa-onnx, Kroko-ONNX, Moonshine, whisper.cpp, Parakeet NeMo
Documented CPU INT8 streaming profile: Nemotron for live text, Parakeet for the final transcript
Optional wake words via Porcupine or OpenWakeWord, plus callbacks for VAD and recording events
weaknesses: CI covers only Python 3.11 and 3.12; 3.13 and newer are not release targets
Uses multiprocessing, so scripts need a __main__ guard, especially on Windows

tools.name: niubigeo
tools.description: Self-hosted tool for tracking how AI models mention your brand and competitors
strengths: Stores original answers and citations behind each observation, with no opaque score
Mixes OpenRouter, direct provider and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints in one test
Per-model web search setting; results record the actual execution conditions
weaknesses: Keyword monitoring is labeled BETA in v0.3
No separate competitor detection dashboard in v0.3

tools.name: garak
tools.description: Command-line scanner that probes LLMs for jailbreaks, leakage and injection
strengths: Broad built-in probe set: promptinject, dan, encoding, glitch, leakreplay, malwaregen, xss and more
Many generator backends, plus a configurable REST generator for arbitrary endpoints
Plugin layout (probes, detectors, generators, harnesses) with base classes for custom additions
weaknesses: Command-line only; the README describes no web UI
Default run uses all probes with 10 generations per prompt, which is slow and costly on paid APIs

tools.name: espnet
tools.description: PyTorch toolkit for speech recognition, synthesis, translation and enhancement
strengths: One recipe structure and trainer across ASR, TTS, ST, enhancement, SLU and more
200+ corpus recipes with run.sh from data prep to scoring
Hundreds of pretrained models on Hugging Face, including OWSM v4 multilingual ASR
weaknesses: Full recipe and training setup needs Kaldi-style tooling beyond pip install
Recipe workflow assumes research familiarity with stages, corpora and configs

tools.name: oumi
tools.description: CLI and Python toolkit for fine-tuning, evaluating and deploying foundation models
strengths: Ready-made YAML recipes for many model families (Qwen, Gemma, Llama, gpt-oss, Phi)
Supports SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, KTO and GRPO, with FSDP, DeepSpeed and DDP
`oumi launch` runs jobs on AWS, Azure, GCP, Lambda and Slurm
weaknesses: README says beta; some advanced features may change
Broad scope means many dependencies (Transformers, TRL, vLLM, verl) to keep aligned

tools.name: modelscope
tools.description: Python library for running and fine-tuning ModelScope Hub models
strengths: Inference in a few lines via `pipeline`; fine-tuning via `build_trainer` and `trainer.train()`
Covers NLP, CV, audio, multi-modal and AI-for-science tasks under one API
Built-in Model-Hub and Dataset-Hub access with version control and cache management
weaknesses: README examples and Docker tags reference old stacks (Python 3.7/3.8, TF 1.15, torch 1.11/2.0.1)
Some audio models only support Python 3.7 and TensorFlow 1.15.4 on Linux

tools.name: monty
tools.description: Embedded Python interpreter in Rust for running LLM-generated code
strengths: No filesystem, env vars or network inside; host access only via passed-in functions and mounts
Reported under 1ms sandbox start from a pool, versus about 1500ms for a sandbox service
Packages for Python (pydantic-monty), npm (@pydantic/monty) and Rust (monty crate)
weaknesses: Runs only a subset of Python, so some model-written code will not execute
Server mode (Full Monty, WebSocket service) is a separate commercial product

tools.name: ds-bot
tools.description: Desktop app and DeepSeek Harness plugin for bots that collaborate in group chats
strengths: Group chats with admin bot, @ handoffs, per-group memory and staged goals
Links bots to Telegram, WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, QQ, Discord, Slack with no open port
Data stays in the local DSH home folder; connector credentials never reach a bot
weaknesses: Windows installer is unsigned and can be blocked by SmartScreen or Smart App Control
Labeled v0.3 preview

tools.name: monai
tools.description: PyTorch framework for deep learning on medical imaging data
strengths: Domain-specific networks, losses and metrics for medical imaging, not generic vision only
Supports multi-GPU and multi-node data parallel training
Installs with pip, conda-forge or a Docker image; Apache-2.0 licensed
weaknesses: Tied to PyTorch; supports the current release plus three previous minor versions
Scope is healthcare imaging; not a general-purpose ML or LLM library

tools.name: geniex
tools.description: LLM and VLM inference runtime for Qualcomm Snapdragon NPU, GPU and CPU
strengths: Runs GGUF models from Hugging Face, ModelScope or Docker Hub on Hexagon NPU, Adreno GPU or CPU
Pre-compiled AI Hub bundles use the qairt runtime for NPU-only execution
One C SDK with CLI, Python, Android, Docker and OpenAI-compatible server wrappers
weaknesses: Runs only on Qualcomm Snapdragon; no x86 or Apple hardware support
Marked developer preview; interfaces may change between releases

tools.name: mistral.rs
tools.description: Rust inference engine with OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs
strengths: Serves both OpenAI /v1 and Anthropic /v1/messages APIs from one process
Quantization options: ISQ, UQFF, GGUF 2-8 bit, GPTQ, AWQ, HQQ, FP8, BNB
Python and Rust SDKs allow in-process inference without running a server
weaknesses: README's BF16 benchmarks show much lower Gemma 4 26B-A4B prefill than vLLM
v0.9.5 changed memory and device-mapping options, so upgrades need migration

tools.name: clawx
tools.description: Electron desktop app for running and managing OpenClaw agents without a terminal
strengths: Embeds the OpenClaw runtime, so no separate install is needed
Setup wizard and settings UI replace config files and CLI use
Channels support multiple accounts, per-account agent binding and cron delivery
weaknesses: Depends on OpenClaw upstream, which the README describes as iterating rapidly
OpenClaw's general web_search tool is disabled in ClawX

tools.name: openllmetry
tools.description: OpenTelemetry instrumentations and SDK for tracing LLM calls and vector DBs
strengths: Emits standard OpenTelemetry data, so it works with an existing observability stack
Instruments many providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Ollama and Mistral
Covers vector DBs (Chroma, Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate) and frameworks like LangChain and CrewAI
weaknesses: Python only in this repo; JS/TS lives in the separate OpenLLMetry-JS repo
No bundled UI or storage; you need a separate backend to view traces

tools.name: trafilatura
tools.description: Python library and CLI that extracts main text and metadata from web pages
strengths: Reports top results in ScrapingHub and Bevendorff et al. 2023 extraction benchmarks
Handles discovery too: sitemaps (TXT, XML), feeds (ATOM, JSON, RSS), URL filtering and deduplication
Outputs TXT, Markdown, CSV, JSON, HTML, XML and XML-TEI, with metadata fields
weaknesses: Rule-based extraction with fallbacks; no LLM or JavaScript rendering mentioned
Versions before v1.8.0 are GPLv3+, which matters when pinning old releases

tools.name: trueforge
tools.description: Agent runtime with chat UI, HTTP API and TypeScript SDK
strengths: Two run modes: single process with SQLite, or Postgres + Redis via Compose, Helm or Railway
Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Remote MCP servers supported with header auth or OAuth, including in-chat authorization
weaknesses: Only Daytona is supported as a sandbox provider today; others are planned
Local mode has no login by default and is not meant for exposure beyond localhost

tools.name: agentscope-java
tools.description: Java framework for building multi-tenant agents with sandboxes and tool approvals
strengths: Three-state tool permission engine with human approval built into the event stream
Session state in Redis, MySQL or PostgreSQL allows cross-replica recovery
Sandbox options: local subprocess, Docker, Kubernetes and E2B, with snapshot and resume
weaknesses: Library only: requires JDK 17+ and Maven, no standalone app or UI
Quickstart uses DashScope and the docs link Aliyun pages, leaning on that ecosystem

tools.name: kun
tools.description: Desktop AI workbench for coding, documents and multi-agent chats
strengths: Installers for macOS (Apple Silicon/Intel), Windows x64 and Linux x64 (.AppImage/.deb)
Works with OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs, Ollama and presets such as DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen
Tool, directory and workbench actions require approval by default
weaknesses: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0: commercial use or hosting needs separate written permission
External contributions require signing a CLA

tools.name: kserve
tools.description: Kubernetes inference platform for generative and predictive models via InferenceService
strengths: Covers both LLM serving (vLLM, llm-d) and predictive frameworks in one platform
OpenAI-compatible inference protocol for generative models
Scale-to-zero, canary rollouts and InferenceGraph pipelines for predictive workloads
weaknesses: Requires a Kubernetes cluster; not a single-process local server
Standard Kubernetes install lacks canary and scale-to-zero autoscaling; those need Knative

tools.name: GPUStack
tools.description: GPU cluster manager that schedules vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM deployments
strengths: Pluggable engines: vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or a custom engine
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Ascend, Hygon, MThreads, Iluvatar, MetaX, Cambricon and T-Head accelerators
Built-in auth, API keys, token metering and Grafana/Prometheus dashboards
weaknesses: Worker nodes are Linux only; macOS is not supported as a worker
Needs Docker on every node, plus NVIDIA Container Toolkit for NVIDIA workers

tools.name: Kokoro-FastAPI
tools.description: OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech server for the Kokoro-82M model
strengths: Drop-in for OpenAI speech clients: set base_url to localhost:8880/v1
Weighted voice mixing, aliases and inline [voice:] tags for multi-speaker audio
Streams audio; README cites ~300ms first-token latency on GPU
weaknesses: ROCm image is experimental and amd64 only
Apple Silicon GPU (MPS) works only via uv scripts, not Docker

tools.name: model-optimizer
tools.description: Python library for quantizing, pruning and distilling models for NVIDIA inference
strengths: Covers PTQ, QAT/QAD, pruning, NAS, distillation, speculative decoding and sparsity in one library
Exports to TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT, vLLM and SGLang; unified HF export covers transformers and diffusers
Publishes pre-quantized checkpoints on Hugging Face, including NVFP4 and FP8 variants
weaknesses: Pre-1.0 API; deprecated features are removed after about one release
Tuned for the NVIDIA stack; NVFP4 and TensorRT paths target NVIDIA GPUs

tools.name: aipoch/open-science
tools.description: Local-first research workbench with provenance tracking and portable .science exports
strengths: Exports sessions as .science packages; imports are read-only and run no code or credentials
Provenance view shows inputs, code and execution history per figure or table version
Installers for macOS, Windows, Linux (x64/ARM64), plus Homebrew, npm and standalone CLI
weaknesses: Benchmark scores are AIPOCH's own local runs, not official leaderboard submissions
Rerunning an imported result needs a complete recipe, inputs and an available runtime

tools.name: LangWatch
tools.description: Tracing, evals, prompt management and an LLM gateway for AI apps and coding agents
strengths: Covers tracing, evals, simulation tests, prompt management and a gateway in one platform
Gateway exposes OpenAI and Anthropic compatible endpoint with virtual keys and budgets
Works with OpenTelemetry, LangChain, LangGraph, Vercel AI SDK, CrewAI, DSPy and no-code tools
weaknesses: Open-core: modules under enterprise/ need a commercial license in production
Self-host quick start needs Node.js 24+; macOS or glibc Linux only

tools.name: ContextForge MCP Gateway
tools.description: Registry and proxy federating MCP servers, A2A agents and REST/gRPC APIs
strengths: Wraps REST and gRPC (via reflection) services as virtual MCP servers
Exports OpenTelemetry traces to Phoenix, Jaeger, Zipkin and other OTLP backends
Installs from PyPI or GHCR image; Helm chart and Redis-backed federation available
weaknesses: Gateway refuses to start without JWT_SECRET_KEY and AUTH_ENCRYPTION_SECRET set
arm64 containers not supported in production; Apple Silicon needs Rosetta or PyPI

tools.name: coopanion
tools.description: Desktop pet that chats, listens, and can operate your computer with an LLM
strengths: Local speech recognition by default: FunASR (about 230 MB) or Whisper (about 360 MB)
Supports 14 listed providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, plus ChatGPT sign-in
Computer use is off by default, asks first, and pauses when you touch mouse or keyboard
weaknesses: Installers are unsigned and not notarized; Windows and macOS warn on first launch
Only DeepSeek, Anthropic and StepFun Step Plan tested with real keys

tools.name: figma-console-mcp
tools.description: MCP server that reads and writes Figma files, variables and components
strengths: Writes to Figma: creates components, frames, variables and FigJam boards, not just read access
Bidirectional token sync with DTCG JSON export plus 9 other formats
Deterministic checks: 14 WCAG design checks, design-code parity, scored health audit
weaknesses: Writing requires Figma Desktop with a manually imported Desktop Bridge plugin
Tool count varies by mode: 130 local, 105 cloud, read-only subset on remote SSE

tools.name: korean-law-mcp
tools.description: MCP server and CLI for Korean statutes, case law and citation checking
strengths: verify_citations checks cited articles and cases against the official DB, with the valid article range
Hosted endpoint needs no install; local npm install and CLI are also supported
42 APIs folded into 10 tools, keeping the tool list small in client context
weaknesses: Korean law only; README and tool output are mostly in Korean
Keyless use of the public server shares one rate limit across all users

tools.name: letsfg
tools.description: Flight and hotel search and booking for AI agents via MCP, CLI and API
strengths: Remote MCP endpoint works in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Windsurf without a local install
Free search; booking holds the fare and captures only after a real airline PNR
Covers hotels as well as flights, with cabin class filter and CLI search
weaknesses: Search and booking engine runs on LetsFG servers and is not self-hostable
Needs a hosted account token; booking requires a payment method via Revolut

tools.name: spacy
tools.description: Python and Cython NLP library with pretrained pipelines for 70+ languages
strengths: Pretrained pipelines install as ordinary Python packages via `python -m spacy download`
Tokenization and training support for 70+ languages
Built-in training system, model packaging, and syntax and NER visualizers
weaknesses: README lists Python >=3.7, <3.13 only, 64-bit
Models may need re-downloading or retraining after spaCy upgrades

tools.name: tencentdb-agent-memory
tools.description: Team memory layer for coding agents: chat memory, skills, wiki, code graph
strengths: Proxy integration: most agents only need a changed base URL and user key
Retrieval combines BM25, vectors and RRF, capped by item count, characters and timeout
Per-asset owner, version and private/team/restricted ACLs, with per-agent binding
weaknesses: Three services to run, plus two separate sets of LLM parameters to configure
MongoDB storage backend is experimental and off by default

tools.name: label-studio
tools.description: Multi-user data labeling tool for audio, text, images, video and time series
strengths: Handles images, audio, text, HTML, video and time series in one instance
Installs via pip, Docker, or a Compose stack with Nginx and PostgreSQL
ML backend SDK supports pre-labeling, online learning and active learning
weaknesses: Default install stores data in SQLite; PostgreSQL needs the Compose setup
Some features are tied to paid editions; README links a comparison page

tools.name: fastai
tools.description: High-level deep learning library on PyTorch for vision, text, tabular and recommenders
strengths: Layered API: 5-line high-level training down to low-level building blocks
Two-way callbacks can modify data, model or optimizer at any point in training
Docs are runnable notebooks, with a free course and a book
weaknesses: Jupyter on Windows forces num_workers to 0, making vision training much slower
Covers classic deep learning domains; README does not mention LLM or diffusion workflows

tools.name: ggml
tools.description: C/C++ tensor library for ML inference with quantization and many backends
strengths: Plain C/C++ with no dependencies; builds with CMake
Targets x86, ARM, RISC-V, LoongArch, PowerPC, s390x and WebAssembly
2- to 8-bit integer quantization, plus MXFP4 and NVFP4 formats
weaknesses: Low-level library, not a ready-to-use model server or app
Core changes are submitted via llama.cpp, not this repo

tools.name: rea-video
tools.description: Agent skill and CLI that breaks a video into shots and judges how each was made
strengths: Offline tools-only mode needs no paid model; README reports 98–99% accuracy on original files
Judges each shot separately as live, AI, 3D or code, then reassembles on the original timeline
Exports captions to SRT/ASS and reports BPM, cuts and sound effect placement
weaknesses: Accuracy on re-encoded platform videos drops to 88.6% without a vision model or agent review
Does not render video; automatic regeneration needs the separate capsule-cinema project

tools.name: gymnasium
tools.description: Python API and environment set for reinforcement learning research
strengths: Small, uniform env API with terminated and truncated flags
Environment families install separately via extras like gymnasium[atari] or gymnasium[all]
Strict -vN environment versioning to keep learning results reproducible
weaknesses: Provides environments and an interface only; no RL algorithms included
Older Gym-based third-party environments may need apply_env_compatibility

tools.name: kimi-k3-in-c
tools.description: Kimi K3 inference engine in portable C99 that streams weights from disk
strengths: Runs a 2.78T-parameter model in 8.24 GB peak RSS, measured
Small C99 codebase: needs only a compiler, libm and OpenMP
make test checks the engine against PyTorch fixtures without a checkpoint
weaknesses: Needs about 1.7 TB free disk for checkpoint and packed trunk
26.5 s per token at 8 GB and 5.6 s at 128 GB+; too slow for interactive use

tools.name: learnharness
tools.description: Desktop tutoring app that plans lessons from a model of what you understand
strengths: Persistent knowledge graph links claims to source sessions and can import notes
Works with provider keys, Claude Code CLI, or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints including local servers
Chats, graph and settings stored locally as inspectable plain files; system prompts editable
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license restricts use in proprietary or hosted derivatives
Web research and dictation need separate external service keys

tools.name: voltagent
tools.description: TypeScript framework for building multi-agent apps with workflows and memory
strengths: Workflow engine with suspend/resume for human-in-the-loop steps
Supervisor and sub-agent orchestration, Zod-typed tools and MCP client built in
Durable memory adapters, e.g. LibSQL with a local file database
weaknesses: TypeScript/Node only; no Python SDK mentioned in the README
Tracing, deployment and managed knowledge base tie into the VoltOps Console

tools.name: ltx-2
tools.description: Text and image to video model with synchronized audio, plus pipelines and trainer
strengths: Generates audio and video together in one model, including speech
Many pipelines: distilled, DFR, keyframe, audio-to-video, retake, HDR/EXR, dubbing
Includes a trainer for LoRA, full fine-tuning and IC-LoRA
weaknesses: Quick-start weights are about 66 GiB and gated behind Hugging Face terms
License is not identified by tooling (NOASSERTION); check the repo terms

tools.name: openrlhf
tools.description: Ray and vLLM based RLHF training framework for LLMs and VLMs
strengths: Several RL algorithms (PPO, REINFORCE++, GRPO, RLOO) selectable via one estimator flag
Hybrid engine lets models and vLLM share GPUs; README cites 70B+ scale
Multi-turn agent mode with reset/step environments, async training and VLM support
weaknesses: Needs NVIDIA GPUs and a Ray, vLLM and DeepSpeed stack; setup is involved
README recommends a specific NVIDIA PyTorch container and removing conflicting pip packages

tools.name: mobilerun
tools.description: LLM agent framework that taps, swipes and types on Android and iOS devices
strengths: Combines accessibility tree with screenshots; --vision-only covers apps without a11y data
Many providers supported, including local Ollama models
Custom tools, structured output and app cards extend agent behavior in Python
weaknesses: Requires ADB, USB debugging and installing the Portal app on the device
iOS setup is a separate flow and is documented only briefly

tools.name: mika
tools.description: Android assistant that operates phone apps and the web from one sentence
strengths: Drives any app by reading the screen, with no per-app integration or app APIs
Runs on a hidden background screen while you keep using the phone
Many provider presets plus a Custom endpoint, including Ollama and LM Studio
weaknesses: Android only; phone control needs Android 12+, 14+ recommended
Phone control needs wireless debugging pairing, which can switch off on Wi-Fi change or reboot

tools.name: darts
tools.description: Python library for time series forecasting and anomaly detection
strengths: One fit()/predict() interface across statistical, ML and deep learning forecasting models
Built-in backtesting, probabilistic and conformal forecasts, and past, future and static covariates
Anomaly detection module with scorers, detectors, PyOD and forecast-model wrappers
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.11 or newer
Deep learning models depend on PyTorch Lightning, which adds a heavy install

tools.name: microsandbox
tools.description: Embeddable microVM sandboxes for running untrusted code and AI agents
strengths: Embeds in-process via SDKs; no setup server or long-running daemon
Fork live sandboxes and snapshot/restore running state
Runs standard OCI images with network allowlists and host-scoped secrets
weaknesses: README marks it beta: expect breaking changes and missing features
Needs KVM on Linux, WHP on Windows, or Apple Silicon on macOS

tools.name: cyberstrikeai
tools.description: AI agent platform for authorized penetration testing
strengths: 100+ curated tool recipes covering recon, exploitation, forensics and post-exploitation in one workspace
RBAC, approval workflows, audit logs and regex-based call blocking for governed execution
Attack-chain modeling with cross-session facts, risk scoring and step-by-step replay
weaknesses: Includes high-risk capabilities (WebShell, built-in C2) that require careful hardening before use
No Docker/Compose support listed; deployment relies on local Go/Python setup via run.sh

tools.name: astron-agent
tools.description: Agentic workflow platform with model management, MCP tools and RPA nodes
strengths: Apache-2.0 with no stated commercial restrictions
RPA integration (AstronRPA) lets agents act on other systems
Published workflows callable over HTTP/SSE from existing projects
weaknesses: Helm chart is not released; Kubernetes deployment is marked as under development
Many ready-made tools come from the iFLYTEK Open Platform

tools.name: flue
tools.description: TypeScript framework for building autonomous agents with sandboxes, skills and tools
strengths: Agent defined as a single function composing model, sandbox, skills and tools
Deploys to Node.js, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Daytona and Render
Durable recovery of accepted work after failures and restarts
weaknesses: TypeScript only; no other language runtimes mentioned
No Docker image or compose file in the repository

tools.name: utopia
tools.description: Bitemporal knowledge graph with ontology, review queue and MCP access
strengths: Bitemporal facts: corrections close old versions instead of overwriting, so past beliefs stay queryable
Only a Rust binary and Postgres with pgvector; full-text search is embedded
Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, DeepSeek, Qwen) works, so it can run air-gapped
weaknesses: Version 0.1: schema changes between versions, migrations only roll forward
Chat and embedding models must be configured before extraction works

tools.name: ai-infra-book
tools.description: A quantitative book on AI infrastructure design, with calculation tools
strengths: Companion CLI lets readers recompute every quantitative example with their own model and hardware
Static calculations need only Python 3.10+ stdlib, no GPU or model weights
Covers the full inference/training stack: accelerators, networks, superpods, scheduling, edge-cloud
weaknesses: Manuscript is explicitly a draft still under revision
Experiments directory needs GPUs and large Git LFS downloads (~20GB) for full reproduction

tools.name: Honcho
tools.description: Memory service that builds per-peer representations from stored agent conversations
strengths: Peer model covers humans and agents, with optional modeling of what one peer knows about another
Hybrid BM25 plus vector search; context output formats for OpenAI and Anthropic messages
First-party plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo Code and OpenClaw share one config file
weaknesses: Background reasoning is asynchronous, so new messages may not appear in chat responses right away
Self-hosting needs an LLM provider key and Postgres with pgvector

tools.name: mochidiffusion
tools.description: Native macOS app for generating images offline with Stable Diffusion and FLUX.2 Klein
strengths: Runs fully offline; README states no data or telemetry is collected
Uses Neural Engine via Core ML for low memory use on Apple Silicon
Supports FLUX.2 Klein 4B and 9B without model conversion, with up to 4 input images
weaknesses: macOS only: requires Apple Silicon and macOS 15.6 or later
Core ML Stable Diffusion models have a fixed image size set at conversion

tools.name: openalice
tools.description: Local workspace that connects coding agents to market data and brokers
strengths: Reuses existing agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi) instead of a custom agent loop
Workspaces are plain directories and Git repos you can inspect and back up
Scheduled Issues rerun research using the Workspace's agent and context
weaknesses: Trading execution is marked beta; README advises simulator or paper accounts first
Source installs require a host agent CLI plus model credentials or login

tools.name: lance
tools.description: Columnar table format for multimodal AI data with vector and full-text search
strengths: Vector, BM25 full-text and SQL queries run on the same dataset with secondary indices
Reads and writes S3, Azure, GCS, Hugging Face Hub and other stores by URI scheme
Adds columns with backfilled values without rewriting the whole table
weaknesses: Library and format, not a server; the README shows no network query API
Only stable data_storage_version values carry a compatibility guarantee; next is unstable

tools.name: sellbird
tools.description: Cold outreach pipeline that finds prospects, verifies emails, drafts and sends
strengths: Uses Claude Pro/Max or ChatGPT plan via CLI; no API key or per-token billing
Default approval gate plus a no-model pre-send check for merge tags, links and bad addresses
Can stop after verification and export a CSV for another sequencer
weaknesses: Needs your own mailbox and warmup; README recommends a separate sending domain
Depends on a signed-in Claude Code or Codex CLI; subscription limits apply

tools.name: smolvm
tools.description: MicroVM runtime with live checkpoints and branching for agent sandboxes
strengths: Per-workload VM with own kernel; network off by default, egress limited to named hosts
Live checkpoint and copy-on-write branching of running machines, including RAM and CPU state
SDKs for Node, Python, Rust and Go run in-process with no daemon
weaknesses: No published macOS Intel build; that platform is untested
GPU acceleration is unavailable on Windows

tools.name: big-AGI
tools.description: Multi-model chat web app that sends one prompt to several LLMs
strengths: Beam and Merge compares several models on one prompt and combines the outputs
Supports 20+ providers plus local backends such as Ollama, LM Studio and LocalAI
API keys can be set in the UI or on the backend; no usage charges from the app
weaknesses: Cross-device Sync is only in the paid Pro tier on big-agi.com
SSO and shared prompts for teams are not in the open edition

tools.name: dograh
tools.description: Visual builder for voice agents with telephony, a Vapi and Retell alternative
strengths: Built-in telephony: Twilio, Vonage, Telnyx, Plivo, Vobiz, Cloudonix, Asterisk ARI
Bring your own LLM, TTS, STT, or use the bundled stack with no keys
MCP server lets coding agents create and edit workflows
weaknesses: Quickstart opens a public trycloudflare.com tunnel by default
Anonymous telemetry is on by default; opt out via ENABLE_TELEMETRY=false

tools.name: autorag
tools.description: Librarian agent that searches local files, mail and chats in place
strengths: Searches data in place across files, mail and chat apps, keeping source-native identities
Local embeddings (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B via MinSync); no remote embedder unless configured
Surfaces: CLI, Pi-based TUI, MCP server, TypeScript API, Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp
weaknesses: Desktop app is a separate repo under Fair Source FSL-1.1-MIT, not Apache-2.0
Needs a configured model provider or hosted plan; no bundled LLM

tools.name: vercel/eve
tools.description: TypeScript framework for durable agents defined as files in an agent/ directory
strengths: Agent layout is plain files: instructions.md, tools/, skills/, channels/, schedules/
Tools are typed functions defined with defineTool and Zod input schemas
Built-in channels for HTTP, Slack and Discord, plus cron schedules
weaknesses: Models are selected by AI Gateway model ID, tying setup to that gateway
Web Chat sign-in and deploy flow are built around Vercel projects

tools.name: zenml
tools.description: Python MLOps framework that runs ML and agent pipelines on any backend
strengths: Wraps existing code in a @step; no rewrite of scikit-learn, PyTorch or LangGraph code
Same pipeline runs across stacks like Kubernetes, Kubeflow, SageMaker and Vertex
Integrates with MLflow, Weights & Biases and Langfuse instead of replacing them
weaknesses: Production use needs a separate server plus stack setup
Replay-based agent evals live in the separate Kitaru project

tools.name: flux.jl
tools.description: Pure-Julia machine learning library with layers, losses and pluggable autodiff
strengths: Models are plain Julia: any parameterised callable, such as a closure, works as a model
Selectable AD engine: Zygote default, Enzyme or Mooncake as alternatives
GPU support for NVIDIA, AMD and Apple through CUDA, AMDGPU or Metal packages
weaknesses: Requires Julia, so Python-based model code and tooling do not carry over
License is reported as NOASSERTION, so terms need manual checking

tools.name: marin
tools.description: Python platform for training LLMs from data curation through evaluation
strengths: Experiments are declared as dependent steps in Python, executed in topological order
Scales from a CPU tutorial run to GPU or TPU pods, including multislice TPUs
Publishes checkpoints, training scripts, mixture pipelines and retrospectives, including failed runs
weaknesses: Research codebase tied to the project's own experiments; not a general fine-tuning tool
Large-scale runs need TPU or GPU clusters; no small-GPU recipe is given

tools.name: PipesHub
tools.description: Permission-aware search and cited answers across Slack, Drive, GitHub and 50+ systems
strengths: Answers carry block-level citations to the original documents
Access checks follow source-system permissions per user, resolved at query time
50+ connectors with real-time and scheduled indexing
weaknesses: Stack needs Neo4j or ArangoDB, Qdrant, MongoDB and Redis, plus Kafka at larger scale
Audio and video can be stored but are not indexed yet

tools.name: microsoft/mcp
tools.description: Monorepo for Microsoft's Azure and Fabric MCP servers, written in C#
strengths: Azure MCP Server bundles all Azure tools into one local server
Install paths for VS Code, Visual Studio, IntelliJ, Eclipse and Claude Code
Shared libraries and test tooling reduce duplication across Microsoft MCP servers
weaknesses: Tools target Azure and Fabric, so they are of little use outside Microsoft's cloud
Many listed servers live in other repos or are remote-only hosted endpoints

tools.name: av/harbor
tools.description: CLI that starts a pre-wired local LLM stack with one command
strengths: Many backends (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, TGI, mistral.rs) behind one CLI
Services come pre-connected, e.g. SearXNG web search and Speaches voice in Open WebUI
`harbor eject` exports chosen services as a standalone docker-compose file
weaknesses: Relies on Docker Compose; host-native inference is limited to a few macOS options
Very large service catalog means a broad surface to configure and troubleshoot

tools.name: kordoc
tools.description: Parses HWP, HWPX, PDF and Office files into Markdown, as library, CLI and MCP server
strengths: Reads HWP/HWPX without Hancom Office; 10,342/10,342 tables matched on 2,424 HWPX files
Local OCR on CPU with no API key; KORDOC_OFFLINE=1 blocks all external network calls
Emits RAG chunks with heading paths, plus Python and Java SDKs
weaknesses: README is written in Korean; an English version is linked separately
OCR table structure matched only 33 of 65 tables in its own benchmark

tools.name: supergateway
tools.description: Bridges MCP servers between stdio, SSE, WebSocket and Streamable HTTP
strengths: Converts between stdio, SSE, WS and Streamable HTTP with one command
Reads the Claude Desktop mcpServers config format, serving each server at /<name>
Built-in API key auth, tool allowlist and prefix, health checks, JSON logs
weaknesses: Each SSE or WS connection spawns its own server process
Listens on every interface by default; no auth unless --apiKey is set

tools.name: openai-cookbook
tools.description: Runnable notebooks and guides for common tasks with the OpenAI API
strengths: Maintained by OpenAI, so examples track the official API
Examples are runnable notebooks, mostly Python, with a searchable website
MIT license permits reuse of the code
weaknesses: Requires a paid-capable OpenAI account and API key to run examples
Tied to OpenAI's API; local models are not the focus

tools.name: PrivateGPT
tools.description: Anthropic-style messages API with RAG, tools and MCP over local models
strengths: Follows the Anthropic API spec, so Claude-compatible clients can point at local models
Works with any server exposing /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models
Built-in retrieval with citations, database and CSV querying, web search, and MCP connectors
weaknesses: Runs no models itself; a separate inference server and embedding endpoint are required
No prompt caching and no OAuth or organizations support

tools.name: exo-explore/exo
tools.description: Pools Macs and other devices into one cluster to run large models
strengths: Automatic device discovery, no manual cluster configuration
Tensor parallelism: up to 1.8x on 2 devices, 3.2x on 4 devices
Serves OpenAI, Claude Messages, Responses and Ollama-style APIs from one endpoint
weaknesses: On Linux it currently runs on CPU only; GPU support is under development
All devices must run the same exo version and build, or they do not join

tools.name: pytorch-lightning
tools.description: PyTorch training framework that automates multi-GPU, precision and logging boilerplate
strengths: Scales from CPU to multi-node GPU or TPU by changing Trainer arguments, not model code
Fabric keeps a custom training loop with few changes to plain PyTorch
Built-in loggers for TensorBoard, Weights & Biases, Comet and MLflow
weaknesses: Requires restructuring code into LightningModule and Trainer conventions
README states about 300 ms per epoch overhead versus plain PyTorch

tools.name: genai_agents
tools.description: Notebook tutorials for building GenAI agents, mostly with LangGraph
strengths: Core-pattern notebooks are mostly plain Python plus one SDK, so they depend less on framework churn
Covers routing, agent loop, skills, context engineering, trace-based evals and human approval
