Notebooks updated to import on LangChain 1.x and LangGraph 1.x, with retired model IDs replaced
weaknesses: Many use-case notebooks date from late 2024 and were not all run against live services
Every notebook needs its own API keys; no local-model setup is described

tools.name: deepeval
tools.description: Pytest-style framework for evaluating LLM apps, agents and RAG pipelines
strengths: Metrics cover RAG, agent trajectories, multi-turn, MCP, voice and multimodal use cases
Pytest-style assert_test and deepeval test run fit into existing CI pipelines
Integrates with LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI
weaknesses: Quickstart expects an OPENAI_API_KEY for the LLM-as-a-judge metrics
README pushes login to the hosted Confident AI platform, a separate commercial product

tools.name: speech
tools.description: PyTorch toolkit for training and running ASR, TTS and speech LLM models
strengths: Covers ASR, TTS and speech LLMs in one codebase with pretrained checkpoints
Streaming ASR with controllable latency, 80ms to 1s in Nemotron-3.5-ASR-Streaming
Installs over an existing PyTorch 2.7+ build via pip without replacing it
weaknesses: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA is required for training and recommended for inference
Requires Python 3.12 or newer

tools.name: leon
tools.description: Self-hosted personal assistant with tools, layered memory and agent-style execution
strengths: Three execution modes: smart, controlled (deterministic skills), and agent (step-by-step planning)
Layered memory for durable preferences, daily context and recent discussion
Supports both local and remote AI providers
weaknesses: 2.0 is a Developer Preview; new documentation is not ready
Public docs site mostly describes the legacy architecture

tools.name: zvec
tools.description: In-process vector database library with hybrid and full-text search
strengths: Runs in-process: pip or npm install, no server or config to operate
Dense and sparse vectors, full-text search and filters in a single hybrid query
WAL-based durability; multiple processes can read the same collection concurrently
weaknesses: Writes are single-process exclusive, limiting multi-writer setups
No standalone server mode or HTTP API described in the README

tools.name: langchain4j
tools.description: Java library for building LLM apps with unified provider and vector store APIs
strengths: Unified API across 20+ LLM providers and 30+ embedding stores
Integrates with Quarkus, Spring Boot, Helidon and Micronaut
Covers prompt templates, chat memory, tool calling, RAG and agents
weaknesses: JVM only; no Python or JavaScript support
README says some features are still being worked on

tools.name: sentencepiece
tools.description: Unsupervised BPE and unigram subword tokenizer trained from raw text
strengths: Lossless, reversible tokenization with no language-specific pre-tokenizer, incl. Chinese, Japanese, Thai
Supports subword regularization (unigram) and BPE-Dropout via enable_sampling, alpha and nbest_size
Single .model file holds normalization, vocabulary and segmentation; same results in C++ and Python
weaknesses: Tokenizer only; no model training or inference beyond tokenization
README states it is not an official Google product

tools.name: ekko-studio
tools.description: Desktop and web workspace for chatting with Hermes, Ekko and coding agents
strengths: One UI for Hermes, Ekko and 14 coding-agent CLIs, shared by chat, group chat and workflows
Visual workflows support conditions, loops, approval gates, run budgets and execution history
Ships as desktop app (Windows/macOS/Linux), npm CLI and Docker image
weaknesses: License is reported as NOASSERTION, so terms need manual checking
Coding agents must be installed on the backend host; some need manual installation

tools.name: xiaozhi-esp32-server
tools.description: Backend server for xiaozhi-esp32 voice devices with ASR, LLM and TTS pipeline
strengths: Many swappable providers for ASR, TTS, LLM and VLLM, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Streaming ASR/TTS configuration; README claims about 2.5 s faster responses since 0.5.2
Minimal install stores config in files and needs no database
weaknesses: Needs ESP32 hardware running xiaozhi-esp32 firmware to be useful
README says features are incomplete and not security-tested; not for production

tools.name: Triton Inference Server
tools.description: Multi-framework inference server with dynamic batching and HTTP/gRPC APIs
strengths: Backends for TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX, OpenVINO, Python and RAPIDS FIL in one server
Dynamic batching, sequence batching and concurrent model execution built in
HTTP/REST and gRPC based on the KServe v2 protocol, plus in-process C and Java APIs
weaknesses: Backend support varies by platform; a support matrix must be checked
Needs model repository layout and per-model configuration, more setup than simple LLM servers

tools.name: pandawiki
tools.description: Knowledge base and docs site builder with AI writing, Q&A and search
strengths: Imports from web URL, sitemap, RSS and offline files
Exports to Word, PDF and Markdown; editor accepts Markdown and HTML
Creates a separate wiki site for each knowledge base
weaknesses: AI writing, Q&A and search do not work until a model is configured
Install is a curl-piped root shell script; no compose file is documented

tools.name: sktime
tools.description: Python library with one scikit-learn-style API for time series tasks
strengths: Covers forecasting, classification, regression, clustering, and detection under one API
Composition tools: pipelines, ensembles, tuning, and reduction to scikit-learn regressors
Interfaces to statsmodels, tsfresh, PyOD, and Prophet behind the same API
weaknesses: Detection, clustering, and distances modules are maturing; alignment is experimental
Task extras install only a curated subset of soft dependencies

tools.name: pyod
tools.description: Python library of 61 anomaly detectors with fit/predict API and agent skill
strengths: 61 detectors across six modalities behind one fit/predict interface
Classic API unchanged in v3, so existing code keeps working
Optional MCP server and Claude Code/Codex skill for agent-driven detection
weaknesses: MCP investigate and iterate tools are stateful and deferred, not yet available
Full multi-turn agentic flow needs Claude Code or Codex via the skill

tools.name: spring-ai
tools.description: Spring-style Java API for chat models, embeddings, vector stores and tool calling
strengths: Portable ChatClient API across many providers, with sync and streaming modes
Boot starters and auto-configuration for models and vector stores
About 20 vector stores behind one SQL-like metadata filter API
weaknesses: Java and Spring Boot only; no support for other languages or frameworks
2.x requires Spring Boot 4; Boot 3.5 users must stay on 1.1.x

tools.name: stabilitymatrix
tools.description: Desktop package manager and built-in inference UI for Stable Diffusion tools
strengths: One-click install and update for many SD front-ends, including ComfyUI, Forge, SD.Next and InvokeAI
Embedded Git and Python, so neither needs a global install
Shared checkpoint directory across packages, with CivitAI and HuggingFace model browser
weaknesses: Binaries are under a separate EULA, while source is AGPL-3.0
Plugin and extension management covers only A1111, ComfyUI, SD Web UI-UX and SD.Next

tools.name: umap
tools.description: Python UMAP dimension reduction with a scikit-learn API
strengths: Drop-in sklearn fit/transform API, works inside pipelines
Embeds 70000x784 MNIST in about 42 seconds on a 3.1 GHz i7, per README
Many metrics incl. cosine and correlation; custom numba-JITed functions; sparse input
weaknesses: Runs on CPU only; GPU use requires the separate torchdr package
Numba JIT warmup adds delay on first run

tools.name: mlx-audio
tools.description: Python library for TTS, STT and speech models on Apple Silicon via MLX
strengths: Covers TTS, STT, diarization, enhancement and music generation in one library
Quantized models (3-bit to 8-bit) for Apple Silicon, with many mlx-community weights
CLI, Python API, OpenAI-compatible REST server and Swift package
weaknesses: Apple Silicon only, since it is built on MLX
Some listed models are large (e.g. 35B MoE, 8B), so memory needs vary widely

tools.name: substrate
tools.description: Kubernetes runtime that sandboxes agents and suspends idle ones to snapshots
strengths: Snapshots RAM and filesystem state, so actors resume intact on any worker in the pool
Egress gateway injects credentials, so sandboxed code never holds them
Per-actor SPIFFE certificates and default-deny networking; plain containers are not allowed
weaknesses: Requires a Kubernetes cluster; no standalone or single-host mode
Several components to operate: API server, atelet, controller, networking and router

tools.name: vibe
tools.description: Desktop app that transcribes audio and video offline with Whisper models
strengths: Runs transcription fully offline; no audio leaves the device
GPU acceleration via Vulkan or CoreML on Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Apple
Exports seven formats including SRT, VTT, DOCX and PDF
weaknesses: Pull requests are limited to a few collaborators
Cloud summaries need the Claude API; local ones need a separate Ollama install

tools.name: turbo-fieldfare
tools.description: Swift and Metal runtime that runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B in about 2 GB RAM
strengths: Runs a 26B MoE model in about 2 GB of weights plus 4K KV cache on 8 GB Macs
Measured 5.1-6.3 tok/s on an 8 GB M2 Air and 31-35 tok/s on a 24 GB M5 Pro
Includes Mac app, CLI and loopback server with Chat Completions, streaming and function tools
weaknesses: Supports only one pinned model, Gemma 4 26B-A4B instruction checkpoint
Requires macOS 26, Metal 4 and Swift 6.2; arm64 only

tools.name: laya-mlx
tools.description: MLX port of Laya typed-decision models for Apple Silicon, no token decoding
strengths: Median 13.42 ms (421M) and 7.39 ms (322M multilingual) per short question on M3 Max
Matched upstream answers on 63/63 validation questions in FP32 and FP16
Pure MLX and Rust tokenizer; no PyTorch or Transformers needed at inference
weaknesses: Apple Silicon only, macOS 14+; CUDA, ONNX and training are not supported
Constrained choice, score and noul outputs only; it does not generate text

tools.name: liger-kernel
tools.description: Triton kernels that cut memory and raise throughput for LLM training
strengths: One-line patching of Hugging Face models; also usable as standalone modules
Works with FSDP, DeepSpeed and DDP, and integrates with Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory and TRL
Exact computation, checked by unit and convergence tests against runs without Liger
weaknesses: Benchmarks come from one setup: LLaMA 3-8B on 8 A100s with FSDP1
Model patching APIs need transformers >= 5.0.0, and per-model support varies

tools.name: everywhere
tools.description: Hotkey-invoked desktop AI assistant that reads on-screen context in Windows and macOS apps
strengths: Reads active-app context via accessibility APIs and UI automation, not only screenshots
Supports Ollama and custom API endpoints alongside OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and DeepSeek
Agent tools include browser, file system, terminal scripts, sub-agents and MCP
weaknesses: No Linux build yet; listed as in development
Memory system, voice interaction and mouse shortcuts are still work in progress

tools.name: Lemonade
tools.description: Local multi-modal AI server with OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama APIs
strengths: Covers text, speech, TTS and image generation behind one server
Backends for AMD XDNA2 NPU, ROCm, Vulkan, CUDA and Apple Metal
OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama API compatibility, so existing apps connect
weaknesses: Many backends are marked experimental or guest, mostly AMD Strix Halo on Linux
NPU paths need XDNA2 hardware; ryzenai-llm NPU backend is Windows only

tools.name: Paperless-AI
tools.description: AI metadata tagging and archive Q&A extension for Paperless-ngx
strengths: Runs as one Node.js process; README cites ~135 MB image and 80–150 MB idle RAM
Works fully local with Ollama and a built-in offline CPU embedding model
History with undo restores original values in Paperless; settings apply without restart
weaknesses: Only works with Paperless-ngx; not a general document search tool
Versions before 4.0 had an unauthenticated setup wizard that is being exploited

tools.name: giskard-oss
tools.description: Python library for evals and red-team scans of LLM agents
strengths: Wraps any sync or async callable, so LLMs, black-box agents and pipelines are all testable
Supports multi-turn scenarios and suites, not just single-prompt assertions
Scan generates adversarial tests across OWASP LLM Top-10 categories from a text description
weaknesses: LLM judges and scan generators need a provider extra and API key; default judge is openai/gpt-4o-mini
Requires Python 3.12+

tools.name: areal
tools.description: Asynchronous reinforcement learning system for training reasoning and agentic LLMs
strengths: Asynchronous RL; setting max_head_offpolicyness=0 gives the synchronous variant
Many algorithms with example configs: GRPO, GSPO, PPO, DAPO, RLOO, M2PO, DPO, SFT
Agentic RL for existing agents by swapping base_url; examples for SWE, search and tau2
weaknesses: Needs CUDA GPUs; install requires a matching flash-attn wheel
Model support varies by training backend; other Hugging Face LLMs only on FSDP

tools.name: tokscale
tools.description: CLI and dashboard that tallies token usage and cost across AI coding agents
strengths: Reads local session files from 50+ coding agents, so no proxy or code changes are needed
Terminal UI with overview, models, daily, hourly and session breakdowns
Covers local inference sources like LM Studio and Unsloth Studio, costed at $0
weaknesses: Some clients need a manual sync step first, such as Amp, Trae, Warp and Antigravity
Warp data is aggregate requests and spend only, with no token transcripts

tools.name: sahi
tools.description: Sliced inference library for detecting small objects in large images
strengths: Works with many detectors: Ultralytics, MMDetection, Hugging Face, TorchVision, RF-DETR, Detectron2
CLI covers prediction, COCO slicing, evaluation, error analysis and COCO-to-YOLO conversion
Installs with pip install sahi; detection frameworks are optional extras
weaknesses: Does not ship models; you install torch and a detection framework yourself
mmdet support requires torch 2.1.2, and YOLOv5 needs the pinned sahi 0.12.1

tools.name: skillhub
tools.description: Self-hosted registry for publishing and installing versioned agent skill packages
strengths: Namespaces with Owner/Admin/Member roles, review flow and audit-logged governance actions
Semantic versioning with custom tags and automatic latest tracking
CLI and REST API, plus a compatibility layer for ClawHub-style clients
weaknesses: Needs PostgreSQL and Redis alongside the Java backend and web frontend
Release template enables a default bootstrap admin password that must be changed

tools.name: Latitude
tools.description: Agent observability that groups failures and dispatches coding agents to fix them
strengths: Signals auto-group failing traces with status, size and trend
Agent Dispatch sends sample traces to Claude Code or Cursor via Linear or webhooks
Regression datasets replay fixes against the real failing traces
weaknesses: README quickstart targets the cloud; self-host steps are in external docs
Automatic fixing depends on third-party coding agents and their subscriptions

tools.name: logfire
tools.description: Python SDK for OpenTelemetry tracing, with a SQL-queryable hosted backend
strengths: Built on OpenTelemetry; supports traces, metrics and logs, with TypeScript and Rust SDKs
Query recorded data with standard SQL, usable from existing BI tools
One-line integrations like logfire.instrument_fastapi(app), plus Pydantic validation analytics
weaknesses: Server, UI and backend are closed source; this repo holds only the SDK and docs
Self-hosting the platform requires purchasing an enterprise license

tools.name: isaacsim
tools.description: NVIDIA robotics simulator on Omniverse with RTX sensors and GPU physics
strengths: Imports URDF, MJCF and CAD robot descriptions for simulation
Covers RL, synthetic data generation and ROS bridge in one platform
Runs on Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 and Windows; pip wheels for releases
weaknesses: Needs an RTX-class GPU; stated minimum is an RTX 4080 or A40
Linux build requires GCC/G++ 11; newer compilers are unsupported

tools.name: archestra
tools.description: Self-hosted LLM and MCP gateway with chat, agents, and guardrails
strengths: Covers LLM, MCP and A2A traffic with cost limits and virtual API keys
MCP tools run as the calling user via OAuth On-Behalf-Of, not a shared account
SSO (OIDC, SAML, Okta, Entra), RBAC with team sync, per-environment egress policies
weaknesses: Open core: AGPL-3.0 plus enterprise licensing, free only for teams under 30 users
Quickstart mounts the Docker socket, which grants broad host access

tools.name: optillm
tools.description: OpenAI-compatible proxy that applies inference-time reasoning techniques to any LLM
strengths: Technique chosen per request via model prefix, extra_body or prompt tag; chainable with & and |
Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and LiteLLM providers; clients only change base_url
Plugins for privacy, memory, MCP client, code execution, JSON output and provider failover
weaknesses: Techniques like MoA, MCTS and N-sample selection multiply API calls, raising latency and token cost
CoT decoding, entropy decoding and AutoThink are marked not available through the proxy

tools.name: cherry-studio-app
tools.description: Mobile AI chat and agent app for iOS and Android
strengths: Native iOS and Android app with system share sheet and light/dark themes
Agents with per-agent instructions, default models and tools, plus approval for tool actions
Supports plugins and MCP servers for extending agents
weaknesses: README marks status as in development
Needs a custom development client to build; not runnable in Expo Go

tools.name: obsidian-wiki
tools.description: Markdown skills that let coding agents compile notes into an Obsidian wiki
strengths: Knowledge is plain markdown on disk, readable, greppable and diffable; no vector store or API key
Manifest tracks ingested sources, so repeat runs process only changed files
Works across many agents from one skills directory, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI
weaknesses: Quality depends on the host agent and model; the project ships no model of its own
Audio and video are skipped, and Office file handling depends on the agent

tools.name: redamon
tools.description: Self-hosted AI pentest agent with Neo4j attack-surface graph and auto-fix PRs
strengths: Claims 101/104 on the XBOW web benchmark black-box, with raw agent sessions published
Recon results merge into a Neo4j graph the agent can query in natural language
Closes the loop: triage agent plus CodeFix agent that opens GitHub PRs
weaknesses: Heavy footprint: 9 containers, 7 GB RAM and 80 GB disk minimum without OpenVAS
OpenVAS option needs about 10 GB RAM and a ~30 minute first feed sync

tools.name: fluidaudio
tools.description: Swift SDK for on-device speech, TTS and diarization on Apple devices
strengths: Inference runs on the Neural Engine, avoiding GPU/MPS and keeping CPU use low
One SDK covers ASR, TTS, VAD, diarization, speaker embeddings and echo cancellation
Used by many shipping dictation and meeting apps, listed in a showcase table
weaknesses: Apple platforms only (macOS and iOS); no Linux, Windows or Android support
Requires Swift 6.0+; dropping the ITN engine needs Swift 6.2+

tools.name: simpletuner
tools.description: Fine-tuning toolkit for diffusion image, video and audio models, with a web UI
strengths: Covers about 40 model families across image, video and audio, with a quickstart per model
Memory options: int8/fp8/nf4 quantization, DeepSpeed, FSDP2; most models train on 24G
Multi-user mode with LDAP/OIDC SSO, RBAC, quotas and audit logging, all free
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license carries copyleft obligations for modified network-served versions
Many supported base models have non-commercial or restricted licenses, varying by checkpoint

tools.name: toolhive
tools.description: Runs MCP servers in isolated containers behind a gateway and registry
strengths: Each MCP server runs in its own container with a minimal permission file
Kubernetes operator with CRDs, OIDC/OAuth SSO, OpenTelemetry and Prometheus metrics
Same runtime across desktop UI, CLI and cluster deployments
weaknesses: Needs Docker, Podman or Kubernetes to run servers
Registry server and desktop UI live in separate repositories

tools.name: ml-for-beginners
tools.description: 12-week, 26-lesson classic machine learning course using Scikit-learn
strengths: Project-based lessons with solutions in /solution folders and quizzes before and after each lesson
Many lessons also ship R Markdown versions alongside Python
50+ translations maintained with Co-op Translator
weaknesses: Covers classic ML only; deep learning is in a separate AI for Beginners course
Full clone is large because of 50+ translations; sparse checkout needed to avoid it

tools.name: llamafactory
tools.description: Fine-tuning toolkit for 100+ LLMs with a CLI and Gradio web UI
strengths: Covers SFT, reward modeling, PPO, DPO, KTO and ORPO in one framework
Supports QLoRA via AQLM, AWQ, GPTQ, LLM.int8, HQQ and EETQ
Integrates FlashAttention-2, Unsloth, Liger Kernel, GaLore, BAdam, APOLLO and Muon
weaknesses: Official documentation is marked WIP in the README
Many features are toggled through YAML flags, so you need to know the options

tools.name: trendradar
tools.description: Aggregates trending news and RSS, filters it, pushes digests to chat apps
strengths: Nine push channels, with long messages split to each channel's byte limit
LiteLLM integration supports 100+ providers, with retries and fallback models
Timeline scheduling with presets, plus a browser-based visual config editor
weaknesses: Hot-list data depends on the third-party newsnow API unless self-hosted
Main README and docs are in Chinese; English README is separate

tools.name: yolov5
tools.description: PyTorch YOLOv5 object detection, segmentation and classification models with training code
strengths: Five model sizes, from 1.9M to 86.7M params, with published CPU and V100 latency
detect.py accepts webcam, video, screen, YouTube and RTSP/RTMP/HTTP sources
Export to ONNX, TensorRT, CoreML and TFLite, with a Jetson deployment guide
weaknesses: Last tagged release is v7.0 from 2022-11-22
AGPL-3.0 license; commercial use needs a paid Enterprise License

tools.name: open-generative-ai
tools.description: Image, video and lip-sync studio app that calls hosted models through MuAPI
strengths: Local inference in desktop app via bundled sd.cpp (Metal, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm) with no API key
Wan2GP integration for local video, including a remote MCP server so Macs can offload to a GPU box
Accepts up to 14 reference images on compatible edit models
weaknesses: Cloud generation depends on MuAPI, a paid third-party service, not self-hosted models
Local inference is desktop-only; the web version always uses cloud APIs

tools.name: tinygrad
tools.description: Small deep learning stack with tensors, autograd, and a readable compiler
strengths: Whole compiler and IR are visible and hackable, unlike PyTorch
Eager Tensor API and autograd close to PyTorch, so training loops look familiar
Backends for OpenCL, CPU, Metal, CUDA, AMD, NV, QCOM and WebGPU
weaknesses: Fewer functional transforms than JAX: no full vmap or pmap yet
README says the library is not 1.0 yet

tools.name: ncnn
tools.description: C++ neural network inference library for mobile, embedded and desktop devices
strengths: No third-party runtime dependencies; CPU and Vulkan GPU backends
Prebuilt packages for Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, macOS, Linux, Windows and WebAssembly
pnnx converts PyTorch and ONNX models; C++ and Python APIs
weaknesses: Library only: no HTTP server or OpenAI-compatible API included
Models must be converted to ncnn's own param/bin format first

tools.name: awesome-ai-apps
tools.description: Collection of 141 runnable LLM agent and RAG example apps
strengths: Each project is isolated with its own README, dependencies and .env.example
Covers many frameworks side by side, including Agno, LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra and Google ADK
Spans agents, voice (LiveKit, Pipecat), MCP, memory, RAG and fine-tuning in one repo
weaknesses: Not one application; each example must be set up and run separately
Many examples depend on hosted APIs such as Nebius, Exa or Firecrawl

tools.name: thesysdev/openui
tools.description: Generative UI framework that streams model-written UI via a compact language
strengths: Renderers for React, Vue, Svelte and Angular on a framework-agnostic core
System prompt is generated from the component library you allow
Benchmarked at 4800 tokens vs 10180 for Vercel JSON-Render across seven scenarios
weaknesses: Prebuilt chat UI and component libraries ship for React only
Requires adopting a new language that models must be prompted to emit

tools.name: edge-tts
tools.description: Python module and CLI for Microsoft Edge's online text-to-speech service
strengths: Installs with pip or pipx; the README mentions no API key
Writes audio and SRT subtitles in a single command
Many voices across languages, listed with --list-voices
weaknesses: Depends on Microsoft's online service; not offline or local
Custom SSML removed; service allows only one voice and prosody tag

tools.name: wandb
tools.description: Python SDK for tracking ML experiments and versioning datasets and models
strengths: Adds tracking with wandb.init() and run.log() in an existing training script
Integrates with popular ML frameworks and libraries for tracking and data versioning
Hosted multi-tenant, dedicated cloud, or self-managed server options
weaknesses: This repo is the client SDK; the server and dashboard are not included
Needs a W&B account and API key for the default hosted setup

tools.name: cutlass
tools.description: CUDA C++ templates and Python DSL for writing GEMM and tensor kernels
strengths: Supports FP64, FP32, TF32, FP16, BF16, FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4/6/8 and integer types
CuTe DSL lets kernels be written in Python without deep C++ template expertise
Covers Volta, Turing, Ampere, Ada, Hopper and Blackwell, with initial Rubin support
weaknesses: NVIDIA GPUs only; requires CUDA Toolkit 11.4 or newer and a C++17 compiler
CuTe DSL is in public beta, and the extension compiler is an opt-in preview

tools.name: baml
tools.description: Typed programming language for writing LLM functions and agents
strengths: Can be adopted incrementally by calling BAML functions from TS, Python, Go, C#, Java
Built-in test and eval framework plus a stdlib for agents
Typed, statically analyzed errors and no `any` type
weaknesses: Requires learning a new language and toolchain instead of a library in your existing one
Claims of faster compiles than Go are given without benchmarks

tools.name: modly
tools.description: Desktop app that generates 3D meshes from photos using local models
strengths: Model extensions install from a GitHub URL; official ones cover Hunyuan3D 2 Mini, TripoSG, Trellis2 GGUF
Runs on Windows, Linux and Apple Silicon macOS; AMD GPUs supported via ROCm
Node-based workflows are validated before run; meshes can be smoothed and decimated in-app
weaknesses: Focused on image-to-3D; no general image or video generation described
Hugging Face is the only supported model weight provider

tools.name: dataflow
tools.description: Operator-based Python pipelines for generating and cleaning LLM training data
strengths: Pipeline → Operator → Prompt structure, with custom operators packaged via GitHub or PyPI
Ready-made pipelines for text, reasoning, Text2SQL, knowledge-base cleaning and agentic RAG
Works with API LLMs or local vLLM inference (`open-dataflow[vllm]`)
weaknesses: Output quality depends on the LLM backend you configure; API use needs a DF_API_KEY
Local GPU inference needs the vllm extra and a CUDA Docker image (cu124)

tools.name: stickman-video-director
tools.description: Agent Skill that turns a topic or script into stickman explainer videos
strengths: Two workflows: prompt-only Director Mode and end-to-end Autopilot rendering for 10+ minute videos
Ten visual styles, each with animated example clips
Supports 9:16, 16:9 and 1:1 aspect ratios and a choice of narration language
weaknesses: Director Mode clips must be generated in third-party video tools, then edited by hand
Autopilot needs a coding agent with file and terminal access; results vary by agent

tools.name: agent-native
tools.description: TypeScript framework for agents that share actions and state with an app UI
strengths: One action definition serves agent tool, UI call, HTTP, MCP, A2A and CLI
Agent and UI share validation, permissions, data and current UI state
Includes auth, memory, automations and agent teams out of the box
weaknesses: Examples and hooks are React-oriented; other front-ends are not documented in the README
No Docker or compose setup shown in the README

tools.name: ipollowork
tools.description: Desktop workbench running OpenCode, Codex or DeepSeek Harness agents on shared projects
strengths: One UI over OpenCode, Codex and DeepSeek Harness via a shared engine protocol
Installers for macOS, Windows and Linux on both x64 and ARM64
Works locally without an account; the Cloud connection is optional
weaknesses: Source-available license, not OSI open source; three or more users need written authorization
Hosting, SaaS or customer-facing use requires prior written authorization

tools.name: atomic-agents
tools.description: Python framework for building agents from typed Pydantic input and output schemas
strengths: Schema-typed inputs and outputs make agents and tools swappable and chainable
Works with providers Instructor supports, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq and Ollama
Every agent and tool run is an OpenTelemetry span, usable with Phoenix, Langfuse or OTLP
weaknesses: Code-only: no visual builder or hosted runtime
Version 2.0 has breaking changes for v1.x users

tools.name: smartsub
tools.description: Desktop app for subtitle transcription, translation, dubbing and burn-in
strengths: Full local path: transcription, TTS, voice cloning and ffmpeg burn-in need no API key
Seven local transcription engines switchable per task, plus 9 optional cloud ASR providers
111 MCP tools and a smartsub CLI with headless daemon for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, CI
weaknesses: Intel Mac build is CPU only, no GPU acceleration
Free translation uses unofficial Youdao/Bing/Google endpoints; Edge TTS availability not guaranteed

tools.name: river
tools.description: Python library for online machine learning on streaming data
strengths: Models learn per sample without revisiting past data, suited to event-based streams
Broad algorithm set: trees, linear models, drift detection, clustering, bandits, forecasting
Core learn_one/predict_one interface has no pandas dependency
weaknesses: README states it favors clarity over performance
Requires Python 3.11 or newer

tools.name: youdub-webui
tools.description: Desktop app that transcribes, translates and voice-clones videos into dubbed versions
strengths: Per-sentence voice cloning uses the matching source audio clip as reference
Three output modes: burned-in subtitles, dubbing, or dubbed video with subtitles
Node workflows support branching, merging and manual correction; tasks can be retried from a given step
weaknesses: Language catalog covers only English, Chinese and Japanese, depending on provider
Requires a configured translation model provider and API key

tools.name: dali
tools.description: GPU-accelerated data loading and preprocessing library for deep learning pipelines
strengths: Decodes JPEG, JPEG 2000, H.264, VP9, HEVC and audio formats on the GPU
One pipeline definition retargets to PyTorch, TensorFlow, PaddlePaddle or JAX
Supports GPUDirect Storage and multi-GPU scaling
weaknesses: Requires an NVIDIA driver and CUDA Toolkit; README documents no AMD or Apple GPU path
Pipeline mode and dynamic mode are two separate APIs to learn

tools.name: go-sdk
tools.description: Official Go SDK for building MCP clients and servers
strengths: Official SDK; v1.7.0+ supports five MCP spec versions, 2024-11-05 through 2026-07-28
Typed tool handlers with input and output schemas taken from Go struct tags
Separate jsonrpc package lets you write custom transports
weaknesses: Client-side OAuth is marked experimental for the 2025-11-25 spec
Roots, sampling and logging are deprecated in spec 2026-07-28; kept only for a compatibility window

tools.name: nono
tools.description: Kernel-enforced sandbox and policy layer for running AI coding agents
strengths: Single binary, no root needed; runs on laptops, CI, Kubernetes pods and microVMs
Per-tool rules, e.g. aws may use a credential while curl cannot
Credentials stay outside the sandbox via proxy injection and phantom tokens
weaknesses: README says APIs are still stabilizing ahead of a 1.0 release
Windows support only through WSL2

tools.name: agent-sandbox
tools.description: Kubernetes CRD and controller for stateful, singleton sandbox pods for agents
strengths: Warm pools of pre-created sandboxes cut startup time for claims
Delegates isolation to gVisor or Kata via RuntimeClass, vendor-neutral
Go and Python SDKs plus an optional HTTP sandbox router
weaknesses: Requires an existing Kubernetes cluster, 1.25+ with CEL validation; 1.29+ recommended
Does not provide isolation itself; you must set up a sandbox runtime

tools.name: aurelio-labs/semantic-router
tools.description: Python library that routes queries to predefined routes by embedding similarity
strengths: Runs fully locally with FastEmbed, no API keys needed
Calibration via fit() turns scores into probabilities and allows a none-of-these result
Swappable encoders (OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face) and indexes (Pinecone, Qdrant, Postgres)
weaknesses: 1.x changes the API from 0.x; 0.x gets bug fixes only and needs migration
Routing quality depends on hand-written example utterances and labelled calibration data

tools.name: openai-agents-js
tools.description: TypeScript SDK for multi-agent workflows with handoffs, guardrails and tracing
strengths: Built-in tracing, guardrails, sessions and human-in-the-loop without extra libraries
Realtime agents connect browser microphone and audio output via WebRTC
Sandbox agents can use local Unix, Docker or hosted sandbox clients
weaknesses: Cloudflare Workers support is experimental and needs nodejs_compat
Pull requests accepted only from repository collaborators

tools.name: tracecat
tools.description: Security automation platform with workflows, case management and AI agents
strengths: Workflows run on Temporal, giving durable execution and resilience
Includes case management and tables alongside workflows and agents
SAML/OIDC and exportable audit logs are in the open-source edition
weaknesses: Multi-tenancy, RBAC/ABAC and human-in-the-loop approvals are Enterprise-only
Code in packages/tracecat-ee cannot be used in production without a license

tools.name: keras
tools.description: Multi-backend deep learning framework running on JAX, TensorFlow and PyTorch
strengths: Same model code runs on JAX, TensorFlow or PyTorch by changing one environment variable
Drop-in replacement for tf.keras on the TensorFlow backend using the .keras format
Keras models can be used inside PyTorch Modules, JAX functions or native training loops
weaknesses: Backend must be set before import and cannot be changed afterward
OpenVINO backend supports only model.predict(), no training

tools.name: graphrag
tools.description: Pipeline that builds knowledge graphs from text for LLM question answering
strengths: Backed by a published paper (arXiv 2404.16130) and a Microsoft Research blog post
Prompt tuning guide for adapting extraction to your own data
Installable from PyPI, with a CLI quickstart and hosted documentation
weaknesses: Maintenance mode: no new features and no new PRs accepted
Indexing can be expensive in LLM calls; README advises starting small

tools.name: llamafile
tools.description: Single-file executables that bundle llama.cpp with model weights
strengths: Single file, no installation, runs across OSes and CPU architectures
0.10 build system tracks upstream llama.cpp for recent model support
Can run external GGUF weights with the bare llamafile binary
weaknesses: Windows cannot run executables above 4 GB; larger models need external weights
0.10.x dropped some classic features; older releases remain for those

tools.name: vision
tools.description: PyTorch library of vision datasets, model architectures and image transforms
strengths: Maintained in the pytorch organization, with releases matched to each torch version
Supports torch tensor and PIL image backends, with optional Pillow-SIMD
Bundles datasets, model architectures and transforms in one package
weaknesses: Each release only works with its matching torch version
Requires PyTorch; not usable with other tensor frameworks

tools.name: libretranslate
tools.description: Self-hosted machine translation API built on Argos Translate
strengths: Translates locally through Argos Translate, with no proprietary translation API calls
Public hosted instance at libretranslate.com to try before installing
Separate API usage guide and community forum
weaknesses: README gives no hardware requirements, ports or language list
Setup and API details live only on the external docs site

tools.name: agent-framework
tools.description: Microsoft's Python and .NET framework for agents and multi-agent workflows
strengths: Same agent and workflow APIs in Python and .NET, with a separate Go SDK
Graph workflows with checkpointing, streaming, human-in-the-loop and time-travel
Built-in OpenTelemetry tracing and a middleware pipeline
weaknesses: Quickstarts target Microsoft Foundry and Azure credentials; other providers need extra setup
Durable Task and Azure Functions hosting live in a separate extension repo

tools.name: pyannote-audio
tools.description: Python toolkit for speaker diarization with pretrained PyTorch pipelines
strengths: Pretrained community-1 runs locally; README reports lower DER than 3.1 on 11 of 12 listed benchmarks
Pipelines and models can be fine-tuned, with multi-GPU training via pytorch-lightning
Python-first API with a progress hook and optional GPU placement via pipeline.to()
weaknesses: Needs a Hugging Face token and acceptance of user conditions to download community-1
precision-2, with lower reported DER than community-1, is premium and needs a pyannoteAI key

tools.name: chatgptbox
tools.description: Browser extension that adds an LLM chat panel and selection tools to any page
strengths: Installs on Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and Android
Site integrations for search engines, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, GitLab, StackOverflow, Zhihu and Bilibili
Custom Model mode works with OpenAI-compatible backends such as Ollama
weaknesses: Does not run models itself; needs an external API or local server
No user accounts or server-side chat history; it is a client-side extension

tools.name: llama-cpp-python
tools.description: Python bindings and OpenAI-compatible server for llama.cpp
strengths: Low-level ctypes access to the C API plus a high-level Llama class
OpenAI-compatible server with function calling, vision and multi-model config
JSON and JSON Schema constrained output via response_format
weaknesses: Default pip install compiles llama.cpp and needs a C compiler
Only GGUF models are supported

tools.name: stanza
tools.description: Python NLP toolkit for tokenizing, tagging and parsing text in 60+ languages
strengths: Models for 60+ languages, covering all Universal Dependencies v2.8 treebanks
Each neural module can be retrained on your own CoNLL-U or BIOES data
Official Python client for Java CoreNLP, including Semgrex and Ssurgeon
weaknesses: Training is not supported through the Pipeline interface; requires a source checkout
Per-sentence calls are slow; documents must be concatenated and batched manually

tools.name: flax
tools.description: Neural network library for JAX built around mutable Python objects
strengths: Flax NNX models are plain Python objects, so they can be inspected and debugged directly
Developed with the JAX team; runs on CPU, GPU and TPU through JAX
Includes common layers plus checkpointing, serialization, metrics and device prefetching
weaknesses: Two APIs exist, Linen and NNX, with separate docs sites and a migration guide
Requires JAX and its own accelerator setup, which Flax does not handle

tools.name: flower
tools.description: Python framework for federated learning across clients with any ML library
strengths: Framework-agnostic: documented quickstarts for PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, scikit-learn, MLX, XGBoost and more
Baselines reproduce papers such as FedProx, FedAvg, FedBN, MOON and FedNova
Examples cover Android (TFLite), iOS (CoreML), Raspberry Pi and Jetson clients
weaknesses: README gives no hardware requirements; RAM and GPU needs depend on the chosen ML framework
Privacy and security and scaling tutorials are listed as not yet written

tools.name: vllm-project/semantic-router
tools.description: Policy-driven router that selects or combines models behind one API endpoint
strengths: One endpoint (vllm-sr/auto) fronts many local, private and cloud backends
Policy can set quality, latency and cost priorities and location limits
Publishes its own routing models on Hugging Face and a hallucination detection endpoint
weaknesses: README gives no RAM, GPU or port requirements
Install is a curl-to-bash script; other methods documented only externally

tools.name: anomalib
tools.description: Library for training and benchmarking visual anomaly detection models
strengths: Many ready-made anomaly detection models and benchmark datasets behind one API and CLI
Most models export to OpenVINO for inference on Intel hardware
Install extras for CPU, CUDA 12.6/13.0, ROCm and Intel XPU
weaknesses: Focused on visual anomaly detection; not for tabular or time-series data
Anomalib Studio is pre-release and may be incomplete or unstable

tools.name: serving
tools.description: Inference server for TensorFlow SavedModels with gRPC and REST endpoints
strengths: Serves multiple models or versions at once; new versions need no client changes
Exposes both gRPC and REST predict endpoints
Batching scheduler groups requests for GPU with configurable latency controls
weaknesses: Built around TensorFlow SavedModel; other model types need a custom C++ servable
No LLM-specific features in the README, such as GGUF or an OpenAI-compatible API

tools.name: andee
tools.description: Agent that operates Android phones and Macs by reading the screen and tapping
strengths: Drives any Android app via Accessibility, no per-app integration, no root or custom ROM
Memory notebook stays on device; every entry can be read and deleted
Whole agent loop, including vault and confirmation rules, is in the repository
weaknesses: Custom Apache-2.0 plus conditions: no multi-tenant SaaS, white-labelling or embedding
Debug WebSocket server binds 0.0.0.0:9008 with no client authentication

tools.name: ag2
tools.description: Python framework for building single agents and multi-agent networks
strengths: Typed Network channels with a hub write-ahead log and audit trail for multi-agent runs
Opt-in knowledge store and summarizing history compaction, with disk-backed persistence
Human-in-the-loop via context.input() inside tools, with a pluggable hitl_hook
weaknesses: v1.0 is not a drop-in upgrade from the autogen-based classic API
Requires Python 3.11 or newer

tools.name: pyrit
tools.description: AI red teaming toolkit for scanning generative AI models and applications
strengths: Three interfaces: CLI scanner, CoPyRIT browser GUI, and extensible Python framework
Connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Ollama, Hugging Face and more
Can test whole applications via HTTP, WebSocket or Playwright browser targets
weaknesses: Extra providers beyond built-in ones need the optional LiteLLM adapter
Feature availability varies by target and model

tools.name: dimos
tools.description: Python runtime and SDK for controlling robots with agents and MCP skills
strengths: Replay and MuJoCo simulation modes run blueprints without robot hardware
Hardware list with stability tiers: Unitree Go2, xArm and Piper marked stable
Agent skills exposed over MCP and callable from the dimos CLI
weaknesses: Most hardware support is beta, alpha or experimental; only a few platforms are stable
Ubuntu is the CI-tested platform; macOS is alpha and Nix is not CI-tested

tools.name: nlpaug
tools.description: Python library for augmenting text, audio and spectrogram training data
strengths: Covers character, word and sentence text augmentation plus audio and spectrogram in one API
Sequential and Sometimes flows chain augmenters; change-log records what was modified
Optional extras (transformers, nltk, word-embs, audio, lambada) keep core install light
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.12+ in 2.x, excluding older environments
WordEmbsAug needs manual download of word2vec, GloVe or fasttext files

tools.name: langroid
tools.description: Python framework for multi-agent LLM apps with tools and RAG
strengths: Small Agent and Task abstractions; a 2-agent loop takes about 20 lines
Supports several vector stores: Qdrant, Milvus, pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate
MCP tool adapter converts server tools into ToolMessage instances
weaknesses: Pull requests accepted by invitation only, tied to real application use
OpenAIAssistant class removed in 0.68.0 after the Assistants API sunset

tools.name: cyberstrike
tools.description: Terminal agent that runs LLM-driven web penetration tests and writes reports
strengths: Works with Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, or local Ollama/LM Studio models
Findings confirmed by a 3-gate baseline/attack/response-diff check; speculative results discarded
Built-in intercepting browser and traffic engine feed requests straight to testing agents
weaknesses: Cloud, internal network and mobile agents are in the paid Pro edition
AGPL-3.0 license; commercial use needs a separate license

tools.name: switchyard
tools.description: Rust library that routes each agent request to an efficient or capable model
strengths: Routing can change mid-run using recent tool activity, not only the first prompt
You keep model clients and credentials; the library only returns the routing decision
Several algorithms: Auto, Task, Execution, Composite, escalation, advisor, sub-agent, random
weaknesses: Pre-1.0: libsy is Beta and its API will change before v1.0
Standalone server is demo-only, not a supported production path

tools.name: compozy
tools.description: Local daemon that runs Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions with approvals and loops
strengths: Wraps agent CLIs you already use; no model access resold, your keys stay yours
Loops have iteration caps, human approval gates and seven defined end states
Single Go binary with local SQLite state; remote access is off by default
weaknesses: README calls current use technical: terminal, local daemon and config.toml
No Loops ship by default; you write or install them

tools.name: openenv
tools.description: Gymnasium-style API for building and serving RL environments for agents
strengths: One reset/step/state API across all environments, with sync and async clients
40+ prebuilt environments including coding sandbox, BrowserGym, OpenSpiel and TextArena
Documented integrations with TRL, Unsloth, SkyRL, ART, Oumi, torchforge and Miles
weaknesses: README says early development; APIs may still change
Not a trainer: you still need a separate RL framework and GPUs

tools.name: claude-code-video-toolkit
tools.description: Claude Code skills and templates that script, voice, score and render videos
strengths: Covers the full pipeline: script, voiceover, music, image and video clips, Remotion render
Open models run on your own Modal or RunPod account; README quotes about $0.01 per voiceover
Hello-world example renders an MP4 locally with no API keys
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code; it is the driver, not a standalone tool
AI generation needs a cloud GPU account (Modal or RunPod) set up via /setup

tools.name: mcpjam/inspector
tools.description: Inspector and eval runner for testing MCP servers across clients and models
strengths: Guided OAuth debugger covers spec versions 2025-03-26 to the 2026-07-28 draft, with DCR and CIMD
Evals run expected-tool-call test cases across LLMs and track accuracy over time
CLI, SDK and CI/CD support let checks run on every PR
weaknesses: Hosted app supports only HTTPS servers: no STDIO, tunneling, skills or tasks
Hosted skills are only available on accounts where the feature is enabled

tools.name: learn-claude-code
tools.description: 17-chapter Python course on building a Claude Code-style agent harness
strengths: Each chapter isolates one mechanism with a runnable code.py
Covers permissions, hooks, memory, context compaction, MCP and agent teams in order
Includes a legacy-to-current chapter mapping for older links
weaknesses: Teaching code, not an installable library or product
Legacy and current tracks use different chapter numbers

tools.name: claude-cookbooks
tools.description: Jupyter notebooks and code recipes for building with the Claude API
strengths: Covers tool use, vision, prompt caching, evals and JSON mode with runnable notebooks
Maintained by Anthropic, with recent commits
MIT licensed, so snippets can be copied into your own projects
weaknesses: Requires a Claude API key; examples target Claude models only
Examples are mainly Python; other languages must be adapted by hand

tools.name: agenticseek
tools.description: Local autonomous agent that browses the web, writes code and plans tasks
strengths: Runs against Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp servers, so no cloud key is required
Supports many API providers: OpenAI, Google, Deepseek, Together, OpenRouter, Hugging Face, MiniMax
Web UI plus CLI mode, with bundled SearXNG for private web search
weaknesses: README calls it an early prototype; agent routing may pick the wrong agent
Voice is marked in progress; speech-to-text works only in CLI and is experimental

tools.name: anydoc
tools.description: Rust library converting Office, EPUB, CSV and PDF files to Markdown
strengths: Covers 14 formats through one Markdown serializer, so tables and footnotes render consistently
Pure Rust with no ML models; README reports 4.4 ms median conversion per document
Detects format from file content, so mislabeled extensions still convert
weaknesses: No local OCR; scanned PDFs fail with NeedsOcr unless sent to hosted Firecrawl Parse
Hosted OCR uploads the whole document, since Parse has no page selection

tools.name: fingpt
tools.description: LoRA fine-tuned financial LLMs, datasets and notebooks for sentiment and forecasting
strengths: Published LoRA adapters and datasets on Hugging Face for several base models
Notebooks fine-tune on a single RTX 3090 in 8-bit or int4 QLoRA
Benchmark table reports weighted F1 on FPB, FiQA-SA, TFNS and NWGI with cost per run
weaknesses: Forecaster is trained on US DOW 30 data only; other markets need your own data and fine-tuning
Most releases date from 2023 and use older bases such as Llama2 and ChatGLM2

tools.name: prophet
tools.description: Additive time series forecasting library for Python and R
strengths: Python (PyPI, conda-forge) and R packages with matching APIs
Handles missing data, trend shifts and holiday effects
Built-in cross-validation, performance metrics and custom metrics
weaknesses: Maintenance mode since v1.4.0: bug fixes only, no new features planned
CRAN release is outdated; latest R version installs from GitHub

tools.name: ace-step-1.5
tools.description: Text-to-music model with LM planner, DiT decoder, Gradio UI and REST API
strengths: Runs locally with under 4GB VRAM using the DiT-only turbo model; README claims under 10s per song on RTX 3090
Covers text-to-music, cover, repaint, stem separation, and vocal-to-BGM in one model family
LoRA training from a few songs: 8 songs in about 1 hour on a 12GB 3090, from the Gradio UI
weaknesses: XL 4B models need at least 12GB VRAM with offload and quantization, 20GB for comfortable use
Low-VRAM setups (6GB or less) run without the LM, losing planning and query rewriting

tools.name: cactus
tools.description: On-device LLM, vision and speech inference engine for phones and wearables
strengths: Published benchmarks per device, e.g. Gemma-4-E2B-CQ4 decodes 37 tok/s on iPhone 17 Pro
Bindings for Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, Python and Rust for mobile apps
Quantization accuracy tables across bit widths (CQ4 close to F16 on most listed tasks)
weaknesses: License is reported as NOASSERTION; terms need checking before commercial use
Converting arbitrary HuggingFace models is labelled experimental

tools.name: train-llm-from-scratch
tools.description: Hand-written PyTorch pipeline from raw text to a pretrained, aligned LLM
strengths: Pretraining and post-training (SFT, reward, PPO, DPO/ORPO/KTO, GRPO) all hand-written in PyTorch
Tiny preset trains on a laptop CPU in about five minutes
Typed JSON configs per stage, smoke configs that finish in seconds, and pytest coverage
weaknesses: Educational scale: the sample output from the 13M model is largely incoherent
Billion-parameter training needs a 24 GB+ GPU; larger configs are marked TBD on RTX 5090

tools.name: cosmos
tools.description: Open world foundation models for robotics and driving: video, reasoning, policies
strengths: Three sizes: 64B Super, 16B Nano, 4B Edge for Jetson and RTX Pro 6000
Runs on Diffusers, Transformers, vLLM, vLLM-Omni, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM and NIM
Post-trained checkpoints for driving simulation, multi-view transfer and DROID robot policy
weaknesses: Target hardware is H100, H200, B200, Jetson or RTX Pro 6000 class GPUs
Quickstart needs gated access to the Cosmos-1.0-Guardrail repo on Hugging Face

tools.name: pixelrag
tools.description: Visual RAG that renders pages and PDFs to screenshots and searches the images
strengths: Retrieves over screenshots, so tables, charts and layout survive indexing
Hosted API over 8.28M Wikipedia pages, no setup or API key
Stages run standalone: pixelshot, chunk, embed, build-index, serve
weaknesses: Pre-built base Wikipedia index is about 217G to download
Docker image is not built in CI and runs Chrome without its sandbox

tools.name: orkas
tools.description: Desktop app where a Commander agent delegates to specialist and CLI agents
strengths: Orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent under one plan
Projects keep memory and files; to-dos, auto-advance and scheduled automations
Data stays on disk; model calls go direct to your provider or local endpoint
weaknesses: Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing only in the packaged app
Scheduled automations need the computer awake; missed runs catch up within 12 hours

tools.name: jev-chat-jarvis
tools.description: Chat reply assistant that judges intent and risk before drafting replies
strengths: Never sends messages itself; it only fills the input box
Requests go only to your configured provider with your own key; no vendor server
Covers Android, Windows, macOS and iOS, MIT-licensed
weaknesses: Use inside WhatsApp, QQ, Feishu or X may breach their terms and risk bans
Chinese Android edition needs an ARM64 phone; macOS build is Apple Silicon only

tools.name: LMDeploy
tools.description: LLM and VLM inference server with quantization, TurboMind and PyTorch engines
strengths: Two engines: TurboMind for throughput, pure-Python PyTorch engine for easier extension
Supports 4-bit AWQ, weight-only and int8/int4 KV cache quantization, usable together with prefix caching
Proxy server distributes requests across multiple models, machines and GPUs
weaknesses: Supported models and data types differ per engine; must check a table to pick one
Throughput claims (1.8x vLLM) come from older benchmarks and are not re-verified here

tools.name: flyte
tools.description: Python-native orchestrator for ML pipelines, model serving and agents
strengths: Workflows are plain Python with asyncio.gather fan-out, no DSL or YAML
Same code runs via python script or the flyte CLI
Local Devbox, Codespaces and an optional TUI for development
weaknesses: Open-source Flyte 2 backend is listed as coming soon
Production-grade backend currently comes from Union.ai, a commercial service

tools.name: Plano
tools.description: Envoy-based data plane that routes, traces and guards agent traffic
strengths: Declarative multi-agent orchestration; agents are plain OpenAI-compatible HTTP servers
Zero-code OpenTelemetry traces and agentic signals for every request
Filter chains add moderation, jailbreak checks and memory out of process
weaknesses: Agent routing depends on Plano's own orchestrator model; hosted by default
Install prerequisites live in external docs; README shows only YAML and curl

tools.name: agentgateway
tools.description: One proxy for LLM, MCP and A2A traffic with auth and RBAC
strengths: One proxy for LLM, MCP and A2A traffic with an OpenAI-compatible API
MCP federation over stdio, HTTP, SSE and Streamable HTTP plus OpenAPI tools
JWT, API key and OAuth auth with CEL-based RBAC and rate limits
weaknesses: README has no install command, ports or resource needs; quickstart is external
Inference routing assumes Kubernetes Inference Gateway extensions

tools.name: openmed
tools.description: Clinical NER and PII de-identification SDK that runs locally on CPU, GPU, Apple, mobile
strengths: Same extract_pii and deidentify API across PyTorch, MLX, ONNX, Swift, Kotlin and Transformers.js
Runs offline from a local model directory without contacting the Hugging Face Hub
PII support for 42 language codes, 35 of them model-backed
weaknesses: Only the SDK source is Apache-2.0; model and dataset licenses vary
SDK use alone does not establish HIPAA compliance; expert review is required

tools.name: client
tools.description: PHP client library for the OpenAI API, with typed responses and streaming
strengths: Covers Responses, Conversations, Containers, Skills, Agents, Vaults, Batches and Realtime ephemeral keys
Streaming supported via createStreamed and retrieveStreamed methods
Factory accepts custom base URI, headers, query params and any PSR-18 HTTP client
weaknesses: Targets the OpenAI API; other providers only via a custom base URI or the Azure service
Requires PHP 8.2+ and a PSR-18 HTTP client such as Guzzle

tools.name: ultrarag
tools.description: MCP-based RAG framework with YAML pipelines and a visual pipeline builder
strengths: Loops and conditional branches in RAG pipelines are defined in YAML, not Python
Each component is an MCP server, so new tools register at function level
Built-in evaluation workflows and public benchmark datasets for reproducible RAG experiments
weaknesses: Aimed at research and prototyping; production hardening is not documented in the README
Full install pins Linux GPU dependencies to CUDA 12.9 with vLLM

tools.name: rlinf
tools.description: Distributed RL training framework for robot VLA policies and LLM agents
strengths: Covers simulated and real-robot RL, including teleoperation, SFT and deployment pipeline
Wide model support: π₀/π₀.₅, GR00T, OpenVLA-OFT, Cosmos3, Wan2.2, Moonlight-16B
Eight accelerator backends, including AMD ROCm, Ascend CANN, Moore Threads and MetaX
weaknesses: Each model and simulator integration has its own setup; the feature set is large
No Docker or compose files detected in the repository

tools.name: youtube-automation-agent
tools.description: Agent that researches, produces and schedules YouTube videos after your approval
strengths: Nothing uploads without approval; simulated or placeholder media cannot be approved
Eight text providers or OpenRouter, five AI video providers, plus free local slideshow rendering
Each generation stage is checkpointed, so a crash resumes instead of restarting
weaknesses: Requires Google Cloud OAuth setup; Testing-mode sign-in expires every 7 days
No Docker or compose files; setup is git clone, npm install and Playwright Chromium

tools.name: h2o-llmstudio
tools.description: No-code GUI and CLI for fine-tuning LLMs with LoRA and DPO
strengths: GUI covers dataset import, experiment tracking, comparison, chat and Hugging Face export
Supports LoRA, 8-bit training, DPO/IPO/KTO, plus causal classification and regression
Multi-GPU via DDP or DeepSpeed; YAML-configured CLI for scripted runs
weaknesses: Requires an NVIDIA GPU with drivers >= 580; no CPU or non-NVIDIA path documented
Backwards compatibility not guaranteed; README advises pinning versions

tools.name: artex-global
tools.description: Autonomous penetration-testing system using LLM planner and worker agents
strengths: Single Go binary with embedded Next.js UI; PostgreSQL is the only datastore
Supports Anthropic, OpenAI and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint via ARTEX_LLM_BASE_URL
Tool-approval gate, traffic-recording proxy and human chat let you steer and audit runs
weaknesses: Offensive tool that can carry out intrusion; only legal against authorized targets
Output language relies on a prompt directive; smaller models drift back to Chinese

tools.name: infiniflow/infinity
tools.description: Database for hybrid dense, sparse, tensor and full-text search
strengths: One query combines dense, sparse, tensor and full-text search with filters
Ships RRF, weighted-sum and ColBERT rerankers
Single binary with no external dependencies; also embeddable as a Python module
weaknesses: Requires an x86_64 CPU with AVX2; no ARM support listed
Quickstart uses the nightly Docker tag rather than a pinned release

tools.name: agency-swarm
tools.description: Python multi-agent framework built on the OpenAI Agents SDK
strengths: Explicit directional communication_flows control which agents can message each other
Tools can be written with @function_tool, BaseTool or generated from OpenAPI schemas
Non-OpenAI models (Claude, Gemini, Grok, OpenRouter) reachable through LiteLLM
weaknesses: Tied to the OpenAI Agents SDK and Responses API; other providers go through LiteLLM
Requires Python 3.12 or newer

tools.name: auto-subs
tools.description: Offline subtitle generator with Resolve, Premiere Pro and After Effects integration
strengths: Runs fully offline; models downloaded on demand from an in-app Model Manager
Many engines: Whisper, Moonshine, Parakeet, Canary, SenseVoice, Cohere, GigaAM, Omni-ASR
Direct integration with DaVinci Resolve, Premiere Pro and After Effects
weaknesses: Optional MMS word-alignment weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, noncommercial only
Mac App Store build of DaVinci Resolve is not supported

tools.name: kagent
tools.description: Kubernetes-native framework for defining and running AI agents as custom resources
strengths: Agents, tools and model configs are YAML resources, fitting kubectl and GitOps workflows
Bundled MCP tools for Kubernetes, Istio, Helm, Argo, Prometheus, Grafana and Cilium
Sessions persist in PostgreSQL, with suspend, resume, checkpoint and fork
weaknesses: Requires a Kubernetes cluster and PostgreSQL; no standalone mode described
Model provider support depends on the chosen harness

tools.name: lmms-eval
tools.description: Evaluation harness for multimodal models across image, video and audio benchmarks
strengths: 100+ tasks across image, video and audio, with YAML task definitions for custom datasets
Runs models via vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible APIs or native wrappers
Reports confidence intervals, clustered standard errors and paired t-tests, not just accuracy
weaknesses: Eval server has no authentication; README says trusted networks only
Caption tasks (coco, refcoco, nocaps) need Java 1.8 installed

tools.name: pipelines
tools.description: ML pipeline orchestrator with a Python SDK, built on Argo Workflows
strengths: Pipelines defined in Python with the kfp SDK, published on PyPI
Components and pipelines are reusable across experiments and runs
Emissary executor is independent of the Kubernetes container runtime
weaknesses: Requires a Kubernetes cluster; no single-machine install described
KFP 3.0 branch drops Argo 3.x; Argo must be upgraded to 4.x first

tools.name: hyper-extract
tools.description: CLI that extracts knowledge graphs from documents using LLMs and YAML templates
strengths: 80+ YAML templates across finance, legal, medical and general domains need no code
Incremental feed with per-source provenance, rollback and re-feed of updated documents
Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Bailian or local vLLM endpoints
weaknesses: Requires a model with tool/function calling; extraction quality depends on that model
Anthropic, Gemini and DeepSeek have no embeddings path, so a second embedder is needed

tools.name: reme
tools.description: File-based Markdown memory store for AI agents with BM25 search
strengths: Memory is ordinary Markdown; indexes under metadata/ are rebuildable from the files
File operations, BM25 search and wikilink traversal work without LLM credentials
Integrations for Claude Code, Codex, Qoder, OpenClaw, Hermes, plus CLI, HTTP, MCP and Python
weaknesses: auto_memory, auto_resource, auto_dream and proactive refresh require an external LLM API key
Semantic search requires editing default.yaml to enable embedding components

tools.name: evalscope
tools.description: Evaluation and stress-testing framework for LLM, VLM and embedding models
strengths: Large built-in benchmark set covering text, multimodal, embedding, reranker, code and agent tasks
Evaluates any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with one command, no local GPU required
Includes perf stress testing with TTFT/TPOT and multi-turn trace replay
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.11 or newer
Agent and code benchmarks need Docker or an E2B sandbox

tools.name: transformerengine
tools.description: NVIDIA library for FP8 and FP4 Transformer training in PyTorch and JAX
strengths: Handles FP8 scaling factors and amax histories automatically via configurable recipes
Supports both PyTorch and JAX with autocast-style contexts
FP8 on Hopper, Ada, Blackwell, Rubin; MXFP8 and NVFP4 on Blackwell
weaknesses: NVIDIA GPUs only; low-precision modes depend on specific GPU generations
Training-focused; the README describes no inference or serving path

tools.name: ohmygame
tools.description: Desktop studio where an AI agent designs, builds and playtests games
strengths: Agent playtests the running game and retries fixes, including canvas and WebGL games
Bring your own keys: 40+ providers via Pi, or Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode
Plugins for Godot, Unity, Unreal, Cocos Creator, Blender, Aseprite and Tiled
weaknesses: Beta; README warns of rough edges
Installers only for macOS Apple silicon and Windows x64; Linux and Intel Mac planned

tools.name: ogam
tools.description: Offline mobile app for local LLM chat, image generation, vision and voice input
strengths: Runs any GGUF model on-device, with OpenCL GPU on Adreno and Metal on Apple Silicon
Covers text, Stable Diffusion images, vision, Whisper input and PDF knowledge base in one app
Can also use remote OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI), keys stored in system keychain
weaknesses: Text-to-speech, personas, MCP and calendar/email actions require the paid Pro tier
Hexagon NPU support is experimental and only accelerates Q4_0 and Q8_0 quants

tools.name: tgpt
tools.description: Terminal client for chatting with AI providers from the command line
strengths: Single Go binary for Linux, macOS, Windows and FreeBSD
Packaged in Homebrew, pacman, Scoop, Chocolatey and FreeBSD ports
Proxy support: HTTP, HTTP auth, SOCKS5 and SOCKS5 auth
weaknesses: Client for remote providers; README does not describe running local models
Prompts go to third-party providers, so queries leave your host

tools.name: seekdb
tools.description: MySQL-compatible database with hybrid vector and full-text search and forkable databases
strengths: Vector, full-text and scalar filters run in a single SQL execution plan
Runs embedded from Python, Node.js or Go, or as a MySQL-protocol server
FORK DATABASE and MERGE TABLE give copy-on-write branching with FAIL/THEIRS/OURS strategies
weaknesses: Benchmark claims against Milvus and Elasticsearch come from the project's own test
Embedded use needs Python 3.11+, Node.js 22+, or Go 1.24+ with CGO and a C compiler

tools.name: tract
tools.description: Rust inference engine for ONNX and NNEF models on embedded, GPU and WASM targets
strengths: Targets Cortex-A7 to x86, RISC-V, Metal, CUDA and WebAssembly, benchmarked nightly
Convert to NNEF once, then ship only tract-core and tract-nnef without protobuf
Pulsification turns sequence models into fixed-size streaming ones for real-time audio
weaknesses: Library and CLI only; no HTTP server or OpenAI-compatible API
ONNX is load-only; saving a converted model goes through NNEF

tools.name: chaterm
tools.description: AI-native SSH terminal that plans and runs ops tasks across servers and Kubernetes
strengths: Agent works across multiple hosts and Kubernetes clusters, with audit trail and rollback
Reusable agent skills package ops procedures for repeat use
Knowledge base uses hybrid vector and keyword retrieval with RRF fusion and reranking
weaknesses: License is not identified (NOASSERTION), so reuse terms need checking
Parts of the agent system are adapted from Cline

tools.name: memoh
tools.description: Multi-agent platform giving each agent its own persistent workspace and memory
strengths: Per-agent isolated workspace with filesystem, desktop and browser
Can host existing Claude Code and Codex agents in its workspaces
Multiple chat channels plus MCP tools and scheduled tasks
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license restricts use in closed-source network services
Split Server/Channel deployment needs a shared internal RPC secret and upgrade ordering

tools.name: mlx-serve
tools.description: Native Mac app and local server for open LLMs and media models
strengths: Single port serves OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama APIs with streaming, tool calls and vision
No Python needed at runtime or build time; works offline without an account
Runs MLX models and GGUF, plus image, video, music, speech and 3D models
weaknesses: App requires macOS 26.2 or later on Apple Silicon
Linux and Windows support is NVIDIA-only; Windows needs a build script

tools.name: sagemaker-python-sdk
tools.description: Python SDK for training, fine-tuning and deploying models on Amazon SageMaker
strengths: Unified ModelTrainer and ModelBuilder classes replace many framework-specific V2 classes
Fine-tuning trainers (SFT, DPO, RLAIF, RLVR) with LoRA or full tuning and MLflow metrics
Modular PyPI packages: sagemaker-core, sagemaker-train, sagemaker-serve, sagemaker-mlops
weaknesses: Tied to AWS: training and hosting run on SageMaker and need IAM roles and S3
V3 breaks V2 interfaces (Estimator, Model, Predictor); existing code needs migration

tools.name: Chroma
tools.description: Embedding database with a four-function API for Python and JavaScript
strengths: Four-function API: create collection, add, query, get
Handles tokenization, embedding and indexing; own vectors optional
Python and JavaScript clients; chroma run for client-server mode
weaknesses: README is thin: no port, resource or auth guidance
Hosted Chroma Cloud is the headline; self-hosting detail lives in docs

tools.name: pgvector
tools.description: Postgres extension for exact and approximate vector similarity search
strengths: Runs inside Postgres, so ACID, JOINs and point-in-time recovery apply to vectors
Offers both HNSW and IVFFlat indexes, plus half-precision, binary and sparse vector types
Iterative index scans (0.8.0+) address under-filled results when filtering with WHERE
weaknesses: HNSW and IVFFlat indexes on vector are limited to 2,000 dimensions
Approximate-index filtering is applied after the scan, which can reduce recall without tuning

tools.name: camel-ai/camel
tools.description: Python framework for multi-agent systems, role-playing and synthetic data generation
strengths: Covers agents, societies, memory, retrievers, interpreters and benchmarks in one package
Built-in synthetic data generation: CoT, Self-Instruct, Source2Synth, self-improving CoT
Cookbooks and Hugging Face datasets published (AI Society, Code, Math, Physics)
weaknesses: Research-oriented; production deployment guidance is not in the README
Quick start example uses OpenAI and needs an API key

tools.name: eino
tools.description: Go framework for building LLM agents and graph-based workflows
strengths: Typed graph and workflow composition, with graphs exposable as agent tools
Handles stream concatenation, merging and copying between nodes automatically
Interrupt/resume with checkpoints for human-in-the-loop agents
weaknesses: Go only; no Python or TypeScript bindings
Component implementations are in a separate eino-ext repository

tools.name: operit
tools.description: Android AI agent app that controls the phone, browser and a terminal
strengths: Runs on-device: MNN and GGUF via llama.cpp, plus Ollama and LM Studio endpoints
Per-tool permission control; default setting asks before each tool call
Extensible through ToolPkg, MCP (uvx/npx), Skills and a unified marketplace
weaknesses: Android 8.0+ and ARM64 devices only; no iOS or desktop in this repo
Building requires external subpack.zip, jniLibs.zip and libs.zip archives plus a submodule

tools.name: fractalworkspace
tools.description: Federated training and split-model inference across Android phones
strengths: Covers both on-device federated training and layer-sliced inference across phones
Raw datasets stay on devices; only checkpoint deltas go to the server
Explicit limits: 150MB partitions, 4,100-byte activation frames, single-use task_Id
weaknesses: Proprietary non-commercial license; commercial use needs written authorization
Requires a Firebase project with Firestore for the token and reward ledger

tools.name: slime
tools.description: RL post-training framework connecting Megatron training with SGLang rollout
strengths: Used for RL training of GLM-4.5 through GLM-5.3, per the README
Megatron args pass through directly; SGLang args use the --sglang- prefix
Custom generate and reward hooks cover multi-turn, tool-use and agentic rollouts
weaknesses: Requires Megatron, SGLang and Ray together; setup is involved
No Dockerfile or compose file detected in the repository

tools.name: go-stock
tools.description: Desktop stock analysis app with LLM agents for A-share, HK and US markets
strengths: Agent modes React, PlanExecute and DeepAgents, with 150+ built-in market data tools and MCP support
Works with local models (Ollama, LM Studio) and many OpenAI-compatible or Chinese cloud providers
Backtests prompt templates and AI recommendations against historical data and the CSI 300 benchmark
weaknesses: Developed mainly on Windows 10+; other platforms untested or have limited features
README and UI are Chinese-only; market data is focused on China-centric sources

tools.name: vision-agents
tools.description: Python framework for real-time voice and video agents with vision models
strengths: Pluggable processor pipeline for YOLO, Roboflow, or custom PyTorch/ONNX models alongside LLMs
Many integrations: OpenAI, Gemini, xAI, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Kokoro, Twilio, Telnyx
Guides for HTTP server, Prometheus metrics, horizontal scaling and Kubernetes deployment
weaknesses: Quickstart needs a Stream API key; free tier is 333,000 participant minutes per month
Video understanding struggles with small text and degrades after about 30 seconds

tools.name: ods
tools.description: Installer that sets up a local AI server stack on Linux, macOS and Windows
strengths: One command installs inference, chat UI, dashboard, voice, workflows, RAG and image generation
Detects GPU and picks a model; bootstrap mode lets you chat while the full model downloads
Supports NVIDIA, AMD Strix Halo and Apple Silicon Metal; cloud mode for hosts without a GPU
weaknesses: V3 pre-release: installers pull current main, not a signed release
Requires Docker on Linux and macOS; Windows needs WSL2 and Docker Desktop

tools.name: opencompass
tools.description: Evaluation harness for benchmarking LLMs and VLMs on 100+ datasets
strengths: Over 100 datasets plus VLMEvalKit integration in one config-driven workflow
Supports HuggingFace, LMDeploy and vLLM backends and hosted API models
Task partitioning, concurrent and distributed execution for large evaluation runs
weaknesses: Inference backends have conflicting dependencies; separate virtual environments recommended
Pyext-based code datasets (APPS, TACO, LiveCodeBench) need Python 3.10, not 3.12

tools.name: unstract
tools.description: Extracts structured JSON from PDFs and scans using LLM prompts
strengths: Prompt Studio defines extraction schemas in natural language instead of per-vendor templates
Deploys as a REST API or ETL pipeline from S3, GCS, Drive, SFTP to Snowflake, BigQuery, Postgres
Supports many LLMs, including local Ollama, and vector DBs such as Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus
weaknesses: Heavy stack: Django, Celery, FastAPI, Redis, RabbitMQ and PostgreSQL; 8 GB RAM minimum
LLMChallenge, SinglePass extraction, human review and SSO/RBAC are cloud or enterprise only

tools.name: data-juicer
tools.description: Operator-based pipelines for cleaning and deduplicating multimodal training data
strengths: 200+ operators across text, image, audio, video and multimodal data
Reproducible YAML recipes, plus a Python API for composing operators
Ray-based distributed execution with partitioning, checkpoints and OP fusion
weaknesses: Many operators need extra dependencies or GPUs; the install is split into extras
Large-scale performance figures come from big clusters (1280 to 6400 cores)

tools.name: opensquilla
tools.description: Personal AI agent that routes each turn to the cheapest capable model
strengths: Local model router picks a cheaper model per turn to cut token spend
Same turn loop for CLI, Web UI and chat channels
Supports 20+ providers, including Ollama for local models
weaknesses: Usage statistics reporting is enabled by default and must be turned off
Router needs native libraries (libomp, VC++ runtime) on terminal installs, or it falls back

tools.name: printfilm
tools.description: Step-by-step AI short video and serial drama maker, from script to final cut
strengths: Pipeline pauses after each stage so script and storyboard can be edited before continuing
Reusable character, scene and prop library keeps drama episodes consistent
Compose file pulls prebuilt public images; ARK_MOCK=true shows the UI without a key
weaknesses: Real generation depends on a TokenFree API key and credits; otherwise only mock mode works
Needs PostgreSQL and Redis alongside the API, web and admin services

tools.name: t3mp3st
tools.description: Multi-agent offensive-security framework driven by your coding agent or local model
strengths: Benchmark numbers re-derive from committed data with `npm run verify-claims`
Works keyless via a signed-in local coding agent or an offline model
Egress-scope containment is on by default and refuses off-target public hosts
weaknesses: Multi-operator swarm exploitation is unbenchmarked and described as unreliable
Cloud, mobile, AD and binary domains are scaffolding only

tools.name: litert-lm
tools.description: On-device LLM runtime with CLI and APIs for Android, iOS, web and desktop
