strengths: Python, Kotlin and C++ APIs marked stable; Swift, JavaScript and Flutter also available
Runs on Android, iOS, web, desktop and Raspberry Pi with GPU and NPU backends
CLI serve exposes an OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint for embedding models
weaknesses: Models use the .litertlm format, so other formats likely need conversion
Swift and JavaScript APIs are early preview; Flutter is community-maintained

tools.name: shimmy
tools.description: OpenAI-compatible inference server for GGUF models, written in Rust on WebGPU
strengths: Pure Rust with WebGPU shaders; no C++ toolchain, Python runtime or backend flags
Deterministic output for the same model, seed and params
Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Apple Silicon GPUs through one backend
weaknesses: v2 removed llama.cpp, MLX and HuggingFace backends; only Airframe remains
Only 26 certified model/quant combinations; mostly Q4_K_M quants

tools.name: dossier
tools.description: Self-hosted job search tracker that drafts tailored resumes and cover letters
strengths: Works with Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible APIs, Anthropic or Mistral
Storage is PostgreSQL or one SQLite file; export, import and nightly backups included
Drafts use only profile facts; unmatched requirements are shown as gaps
weaknesses: Single user with one password; no accounts
Desktop browsers only; English interface

tools.name: easel
tools.description: Social media content workbench for planning, creating and publishing posts
strengths: Covers discovery, planning, creation, publishing and metrics review in one workflow
Per-account profiles hold positioning, audience, preferences and long-term memory
Skills run real scripts and write artifacts to outputs/, organised per project
weaknesses: Needs OpenClaw, Node.js 24.22.1+ (25.x incompatible), FFmpeg and Playwright Chromium
Browser auto-publishing to Xiaohongshu risks verification, rate limits or account restrictions

tools.name: locally-uncensored
tools.description: Desktop app for local chat, image and video generation, and a coding agent
strengths: Installers for Windows, Linux and macOS, plus an Android APK; no Docker or config files
Installs and updates ComfyUI itself, with text-to-image, image-to-video and LoRA lanes
Coding agent shows diffs before applying; Local API is OpenAI-compatible behind a token
weaknesses: macOS build is Apple Silicon only, beta, and has run on one Mac so far
Windows installer is not yet code-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first run

tools.name: embabel-agent
tools.description: JVM framework for agents that plan actions toward goals, in Kotlin or Java
strengths: Non-LLM planner (GOAP, Utility AI option) picks action order and replans after each action
Typed domain model and Spring injection; unit and end-to-end agent testing supported
Per-action model selection, so cheaper or local models can handle point tasks
weaknesses: JVM and Spring only; no Python or TypeScript SDK
Natural-language actions, evolving mode and federation are described as future work

tools.name: audio.cpp
tools.description: C++ ggml runtime for local TTS, ASR, voice cloning and separation models
strengths: Covers TTS, ASR, VAD, diarization, separation and music models under one CLI and server API
Backends span CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU, SYCL and CPU, so no Python environments
Built-in WebUI with Studio, Arena, voice library and TTS narration editor
weaknesses: License is reported as NOASSERTION; model weights carry separate per-family licenses
Fast-moving 0.9.x releases; HIP gfx1151_v1 kernels, avatar voice chat and LatentSync are experimental

tools.name: mesh-llm
tools.description: Pools GPUs across machines behind one OpenAI-compatible API
strengths: Splits models too large for one machine into layer stages across peers
Same /v1 endpoint on every node, routed by model name
Prebuilt bundles for macOS Metal, plus Linux and Windows on CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, CPU
weaknesses: Mixture-of-Agents mode (model: mesh) is experimental and needs at least two models
Native Windows CUDA runtime does not cover RTX 50-series (Blackwell) yet

tools.name: Speakr
tools.description: Self-hosted transcription with speaker labels, summaries and chat over recordings
strengths: Many ASR connectors, auto-detected from config, including self-hosted WhisperX and VibeVoice
Speaker diarization, plus cross-recording voice profiles with the WhisperX backend
Multi-user with OIDC SSO, groups, sharing, per-user quotas and retention policies
weaknesses: Voice profiles and top-quality diarization need a separate WhisperX container with a GPU
Summaries and chat need an external LLM endpoint, cloud or local

tools.name: applio
tools.description: Voice conversion tool with a Gradio UI, training and plugin support
strengths: Install and run scripts for Windows, Linux and macOS, plus precompiled Windows releases
Windows updater keeps models, logs, audio, presets and settings across upgrades
Plugin repository, hosted playground and Colab notebooks with and without UI
weaknesses: Maintainers say updates will be infrequent: security patches, dependencies, occasional features
Official version requires accepting a separate Terms of Use in addition to MIT

tools.name: lichtfeld-studio
tools.description: Native desktop app for training and editing 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes
strengths: Training, live viewer, gaussian editing and export in one application
Exports PLY, SOG, SPZ and a standalone HTML viewer
Python plugin system plus MCP tools for scripting and agent control
weaknesses: Requires an NVIDIA GPU with compute capability 7.5+; AMD, Intel and older NVIDIA unsupported
Prebuilt Windows binaries need a paid donation via the Portal, not GitHub Releases

tools.name: letta-ai/letta-code
tools.description: Stateful CLI agent harness with self-editing memory, skills and chat integrations
strengths: Memory blocks and skills are tracked in git and can sync to your own GitHub repo
Reaches the same agent from CLI, browser, Telegram, Slack and Discord
Supports hooks, crons, heartbeats, subagents and configurable permission modes
weaknesses: Letta Cloud is the default backend; local mode must be chosen at setup
Remote computers and secrets require signing in with Letta

tools.name: goclaw
tools.description: Multi-tenant agent gateway in Go with team delegation, memory and chat channels
strengths: Per-user workspaces, RBAC and AES-256-GCM encrypted API keys for multi-tenant hosting
20+ providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Static ~25 MB Go binary; built-in tracing with optional OpenTelemetry export
weaknesses: CC BY-NC 4.0 license forbids commercial use
Server edition requires PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector

tools.name: sumy
tools.description: Extractive text summarizer for web pages and plain text, as library and CLI
strengths: Installs with pip or uv; usable as a library or via sumy and sumy_eval commands
Several extractive algorithms (LexRank, Luhn, LSA, Edmundson) with per-language tokenizers
Built-in evaluation commands compare summaries against a reference text
weaknesses: Extractive only: picks existing sentences, cannot rewrite or abstract
Language coverage depends on tokenizers; unsupported languages need manual additions

tools.name: natively-cluely-ai-assistant
tools.description: Desktop overlay that transcribes meetings and drafts live interview answers
strengths: Fully offline option: local Ollama models plus on-device ONNX STT (Whisper, Moonshine, Parakeet)
Bring-your-own-key support across several providers, with a model picker grouped by provider
Local SQLite vector search over past meetings, plus PDF, DOCX and TXT reference files
weaknesses: Custom personal/non-commercial license, not OSI open source (detected as NOASSERTION)
Built to hide from screen shares in interviews, which may breach employer or proctoring rules

tools.name: inspect_ai
tools.description: Python framework for running and scoring LLM evaluations
strengths: Over 200 pre-built evaluations ready to run on any model
Extensible through third-party Python packages for new elicitation and scoring techniques
Built-in support for tool use, multi-turn dialog and model-graded evaluation
weaknesses: README covers only development setup, not install or usage; users must go to external docs
Web UI frontend lives in a git submodule with separate TypeScript setup

tools.name: tensorflow/models
tools.description: Reference TensorFlow 2 model implementations, plus the Orbit training-loop library
strengths: Official directory is maintained by the TensorFlow team against current TF2 APIs
Orbit supports custom training loops with tf.distribute on CPU, GPU and TPU
Published on PyPI as tf-models-official, with a daily nightly build
weaknesses: Research directory is researcher-maintained and mixes TensorFlow 1 and 2 code
tf-models-official may lag master; nightly package needed for latest changes

tools.name: ml-engineering
tools.description: Open book of guides and scripts for training LLMs and VLMs at scale
strengths: Runnable tools: torch-dist-bench.py for network throughput, mamf-finder.py for real accelerator TFLOPS
Covers hardware, SLURM, debugging and inference, not only training
Links a collection of public LLM/VLM training logbooks
weaknesses: Reference text, not an installable framework or library
Described by the author as a personal brain dump; coverage may be uneven

tools.name: google-gemini/cookbook
tools.description: Jupyter notebook tutorials for the Gemini API, from basics to Live API and agents
strengths: Maintained by Google; notebooks track new Gemini models and API features
Each quickstart has an Open in Colab link, so no local setup is required
Covers many modalities: text, speech, Live API, image, video, music, transcription
weaknesses: Requires a Google account and a Google AI Studio API key
All examples call the hosted Gemini API; nothing runs locally

tools.name: mcp-for-beginners
tools.description: Hands-on curriculum for building Model Context Protocol servers and clients
strengths: Samples in six languages: C#, Java, JavaScript, Rust, Python, TypeScript
Covers stdio and HTTP streaming transports, testing, deployment, OAuth2 and Entra ID auth
Includes a 13-lab PostgreSQL-backed MCP server path as a capstone
weaknesses: Some examples remain pinned to spec 2025-11-25 while SDK support catches up
Several modules lean on Microsoft products such as Azure, Foundry and Entra ID

tools.name: comfyui-manager
tools.description: Manager menu for installing and updating ComfyUI custom nodes and models
strengths: Installs, updates, disables and removes custom nodes from a menu inside ComfyUI
Snapshots save the installed state and restore it on the next startup
Install Missing Custom Nodes finds extensions needed by the loaded workflow
weaknesses: Only works with ComfyUI; not usable standalone
Snapshot restore is incomplete for custom nodes not managed by Git

tools.name: horizon
tools.description: Daily AI-curated news briefings from RSS, Hacker News, Reddit and more
strengths: Profiles set per-source scoring rubrics, thresholds and output format, usually without code changes
Ten source types, including HN, Reddit, Telegram, GitHub, GDELT and Google News
Delivers via Markdown, GitHub Pages, email, webhooks (Feishu, Slack, Discord) and WeChat
weaknesses: Needs an LLM provider key or ChatGPT sign-in; Ollama appears only as a badge
Twitter/X source depends on Apify and a Playwright setup the Dockerfile lacks

tools.name: chandra
tools.description: OCR model that converts PDFs and images to Markdown, HTML or JSON with layout
strengths: Outputs Markdown, HTML and JSON with layout, extracted images and captions
Supports 90+ languages; README reports 77.8% average on its own 43-language benchmark
Two backends: local HuggingFace or vLLM server with parallel workers
weaknesses: Weights are OpenRAIL-M: free only for research, personal use and startups under $2M
Hosted Datalab API is stated to be more accurate than the open weights

tools.name: xformers
tools.description: PyTorch library of memory-efficient attention and fused transformer kernels
strengths: Exact (not approximate) memory-efficient attention via a single function call
Fused ops include softmax, layer norm, dropout(activation(x+bias)) and SwiGLU
Prebuilt pip wheels for CUDA 12.6, 12.8 and 13.0 on Linux and Windows
weaknesses: Tied to a specific PyTorch version (2.10.0 for the current stable wheels)
Source builds can take dozens of minutes and may run out of memory

tools.name: alphafold3
tools.description: Inference pipeline for AlphaFold 3 biomolecular structure prediction
strengths: Code is Apache-2.0 and covers the full inference path from JSON input to structure output
Data pipeline and inference can run separately via --run_data_pipeline and --run_inference
Alternative weights offered: SynthID Bio watermarked and Leaving Atom fine-tuned variants
weaknesses: Weights are not open: use only if received directly from Google, under terms of use
Requires separate genetic databases to be downloaded; sizes not stated in the README

tools.name: nullclaw
tools.description: Personal AI assistant runtime in a single 678 KB static Zig binary
strengths: README reports a 678 KB static binary, about 1 MB peak RSS, and under 8 ms startup
Gateway binds 127.0.0.1 by default, requires pairing, and encrypts API keys with ChaCha20-Poly1305
Sandbox backends: Landlock, Firejail, Bubblewrap and Docker, auto-detected
weaknesses: Source builds need exactly Zig 0.16.0; other versions are unsupported
Benchmark comparisons are the project's own, from a single macOS arm64 run

tools.name: prompt_engineering
tools.description: 22 Jupyter notebooks teaching prompt engineering with OpenAI and LangChain
strengths: 22 notebooks ordered from fundamentals to optimization, security and evaluation
Covers named techniques: zero-shot, few-shot, CoT, self-consistency, prompt chaining
Runnable code in notebooks rather than prose-only guides
weaknesses: Examples rely on OpenAI and LangChain; local model use is not described
README is heavy with promotion for a paid course, book and newsletter

tools.name: voiceink
tools.description: Native macOS dictation app using local speech-to-text models
strengths: Offline transcription; README states audio never leaves the device
Supports whisper.cpp, Parakeet and GGUF local models, plus SenseVoice Small
Per-app modes apply settings automatically by app or URL
weaknesses: macOS 15.0 or later only; no Windows or Linux builds
Not accepting pull requests; contributions limited to issues

tools.name: genkit
tools.description: Multi-language SDK for building LLM flows, tools and agents, with a local dev UI
strengths: Same API across TypeScript, Go, Python and Dart SDKs
Local Developer UI with playgrounds, execution traces and evaluation results
Provider plugins for Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama behind one interface
weaknesses: Python is Beta and Dart is Preview; only JS/TS and Go are production-ready
Production monitoring dashboard is described in the Firebase console, tying it to Google

tools.name: ai-coding-guide-zh
tools.description: Chinese tutorials for Claude Code, Codex, WorkBuddy and OpenClaw
strengths: Entry exercises ship with sample files and reference answers, including a 3/8 to 38 variant check
Covers four tools in one repo, with per-chapter version notes and a chapter-by-chapter audit list
Includes three offline scripts and a one-page cheat sheet for evaluating agent output
weaknesses: Chinese only; the English links point to the author's separate Meta_Kim project
Tracks fast-moving upstream tools, so version details can go stale

tools.name: digup
tools.description: Desktop app that searches local files by meaning across text, images, audio and video
strengths: One shared embedding space lets a text query match images, PDF pages, audio and video frames
Exact-string boost finds invoice numbers and error codes alongside semantic matches
Opens results at the PDF page, media timestamp or code line in your editor
weaknesses: Mac build needs Apple Silicon and macOS 14+; Windows and Linux builds are beta
Screenshot text recognition works only on macOS; legacy .doc, RAW and SVG are Mac-only

tools.name: nexent
tools.description: Generates agents from plain-language prompts, with memory, skills and MCP tools
strengths: Agents generated from a text prompt, no drag-and-drop orchestration needed
Multi-tenancy, RBAC and agent version history with rollback
Supports MCP tools and the A2A agent-to-agent protocol
weaknesses: Heavy stack: Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO; 8 GiB RAM minimum on Docker
Prompt-only agent creation gives less explicit control than a visual builder

tools.name: mlx-vlm
tools.description: Run and fine-tune vision, audio and text models on Apple Silicon with MLX
strengths: Covers many model families with per-model docs, including OCR, Gemma 4, MiniCPM-o and Qwen VL
Speculative decoding with DFlash, MTP and EAGLE-3 drafters; README reports up to 3.94x on Gemma 4 26B-A4B
Server adds continuous batching, automatic prefix caching and KV cache quantization
weaknesses: Targets macOS on Apple silicon; the only CUDA mention is activation quantization
Gradio chat UI needs the separate mlx-vlm[ui] extra

tools.name: weave-os/router
tools.description: Proxy that picks a model per request across Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini APIs
strengths: Accepts Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini request formats, with streaming, tool calls and vision
Installer configures Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, opencode and pi, with on/off switching
POST /v1/route shows a routing decision without calling a model
weaknesses: README recommends the Weave-managed router over self-hosting
Self-hosted HMM policy is frozen, without training, online learning or registry

tools.name: llm-d
tools.description: Kubernetes stack for distributed LLM inference on top of vLLM and SGLang
strengths: Prefix-cache-aware routing reported at 3x output throughput versus round-robin on Llama 3.1 70B
Supports NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs and Google TPUs, with vLLM and SGLang backends
Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV offload for large models like gpt-oss-120b
weaknesses: Requires a Kubernetes cluster; not a single-node or laptop server
Needs a separate model server (vLLM or SGLang) underneath

tools.name: kiln
tools.description: Desktop app and Python library for AI task evals, optimization and fine-tuning
strengths: Evals, RAG, synthetic data and fine-tuning share one dataset in a single tool
Non-engineers rate outputs in the app; engineers load the same projects via pip
Local-first: bring your own keys or run offline with Ollama; datasets are open JSON
weaknesses: Desktop app is source-available (fair-code); only the library and REST server are MIT
AI Assistant, Auto-Optimize and Eval Builder require the paid Kiln Pro service

tools.name: evoscientist
tools.description: Multi-agent research assistant with persistent memory, CLI, WebUI and chat channels
strengths: Six specialised sub-agents with a defined plan, execute, evaluate, write and verify flow
Memory is distilled each turn and AutoSkills proposes reusable skills for review
One agent session reachable from CLI, WebUI, Telegram, Slack, Feishu and WeChat
weaknesses: Listed providers are hosted APIs; local model support is not documented
Fast release cadence with behavior changes, e.g. v0.4.0 project .env scope change

tools.name: pilotdeck
tools.description: Workspace-based agent platform with editable memory, model routing and background tasks
strengths: Per-WorkSpace isolation of files, memory and skills limits cross-project context bleed
Memory entries can be viewed, edited, pinned and rolled back after Dream Mode consolidation
Smart Routing sends sub-tasks to lighter models; README reports $3.15 vs $18.36 on 7 tasks
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license constrains use in hosted or proprietary products
Requires Node.js 22.13+ but below 23; native modules can need build tools on Windows

tools.name: lossless-claw
tools.description: OpenClaw plugin that replaces sliding-window compaction with a summary DAG over SQLite
strengths: Keeps every raw message in SQLite; summaries link back to source messages
Agent tools (lcm_grep, lcm_describe, lcm_expand) recover details from compacted history
Summary and expansion models configurable separately, with per-session spend guard
weaknesses: Works only with OpenClaw 2026.9.2 or newer
Summarization consumes LLM calls, adding provider cost and quota use

tools.name: switch
tools.description: Puts coding agents and people in shared Slack, Teams, Discord channels
strengths: Connects to Slack, Teams, Discord, Telegram and Mattermost, so users stay in their chat app
Works with agents you already run: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, LangChain, ADK
Per-agent roles and connectors; agents only see rooms they belong to
weaknesses: Ships no agents or models; you must bring and run your own
License is Apache 2.0 plus Commons Clause, which restricts selling the software

tools.name: openagents
tools.description: Shared workspace where people and coding agents collaborate in threads
strengths: Connects 25+ existing agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Aider, Goose) to one workspace
Approval cards let agents ask before deploying, spending, emailing or deleting data
Agents and devices are private by default and shared per teammate
weaknesses: Aider, Goose and Cline integrations are Beta; DeepSeek Harness is a preview
Headless Goose runs in auto mode, so tools execute without prompting

tools.name: artificial-intelligence-deep-learning-machine-learning-tutorials
tools.description: Self-checking Jupyter lessons that build AI components from scratch
strengths: Exercises self-check when run, with hints on likely mistakes
Starter lesson runs on a laptop CPU with 8 GiB RAM, no GPU
Opens in Colab, Kaggle, Binder, Codespaces or local Jupyter
weaknesses: Two programmes are partly built: credit underwriting 4 of 8, proteomics 5 of 7
The 2017-2025 tutorials were retired and are no longer maintained here

tools.name: vulnclaw
tools.description: LLM agent CLI that runs penetration tests from natural-language prompts
strengths: Evidence gate rejects flags or conclusions that do not appear verbatim in tool output
13 LLM provider presets including local Ollama, plus any OpenAI-compatible base URL
Generates Markdown reports and runnable Python PoC scripts after a run
weaknesses: Full Web UI requires building the React frontend from source; the PyPI wheel lacks it
python_execute is described as high-risk and not a strong sandbox

tools.name: opendeepwiki
tools.description: Generates wiki-style docs and chat for Git repos, with per-repo MCP endpoints
strengths: Accepts Git URLs, ZIP uploads and approved local directories as sources
Per-repo MCP endpoints at /api/mcp/{owner}/{repo}
Separate model bindings for catalog, content and translation; translation falls back to content model
weaknesses: Needs an external LLM API key; local model setup is not documented beyond optional Graphify Ollama
Seeded default admin credentials must be changed manually before real use

tools.name: sdv
tools.description: Python library that generates synthetic tabular data from real datasets
strengths: Supports single-table, multi-table and sequential data, preserving primary and foreign key relationships
Built-in quality report scores column shapes and column pair trends from 0 to 100%
Offers classical (GaussianCopula) and deep learning (CTGAN) synthesizers behind one API
weaknesses: Business Source License, not an OSI-approved open-source license
Tabular data only; no text, image or other modalities mentioned

tools.name: sie
tools.description: Inference server for embeddings, reranking, extraction, OCR and LLM generation
strengths: One server covers embeddings, reranking, extraction, OCR, guard, translation, vision and Whisper
OpenAI-compatible endpoints allow drop-in migration for embeddings and generation
Helm, KEDA scale-to-zero, Grafana and Terraform modules for EKS, GKE, AKS and ACK
weaknesses: Separate Docker images per model bundle; the wrong image hides some models
Text generation needs the SGLang GPU image or MLX on Apple Silicon

tools.name: mxc
tools.description: Cross-platform sandbox SDK for running untrusted code from models and plugins
strengths: Native backends on Windows, Linux and macOS behind one JSON request format
Separate filesystem, network and UI policies; Node sample sets egress default to deny
SDKs for Rust, .NET and Node, published on crates.io, NuGet and npm
weaknesses: Windows Sandbox, MicroVM, Hyperlight and IsolationSession backends are marked experimental
Official Microsoft builds send required telemetry on the 1.1.0-alpha contract

tools.name: agentero
tools.description: Desktop reference manager and PDF reader that connects local agents over ACP and MCP
strengths: Connects local agents via ACP, including Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex
Exposes the paper library as an MCP server and through a headless CLI
Stores papers and notes as plain PDF and Markdown files in local folders
weaknesses: README is Chinese-first; English docs are in a separate README.en.md
Agent features need a separately installed ACP-compatible agent

tools.name: pagekin
tools.description: Desktop app for writing novels chapter by chapter with your own LLM
strengths: Works stored in a local folder plus SQLite database
Revisions shown as per-paragraph diffs instead of overwriting the draft
Each chapter prompt uses blueprint, characters, worldbuilding and summaries, not full chat history
weaknesses: No bundled model; needs your own API key or local Ollama
Only OpenAI-compatible and Gemini protocols; Anthropic and Azure need separate adapters

tools.name: oh-my-ppt
tools.description: Desktop app that generates editable HTML slide decks and exports to PPTX
strengths: Imports PPTX and exports editable PPTX, plus PDF, PNG, long PNG and MP4
Slides are HTML: drag, resize, per-element animation, and per-page chat edits
Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local Ollama
weaknesses: README is mainly in Chinese; the English version is a separate file
Release builds may be unsigned, so macOS and Windows show security warnings

tools.name: agentfield
tools.description: Control plane that serves agent functions as REST endpoints
strengths: Plain functions in Python, Go or TypeScript; no DSL or YAML graph wiring
Async runs, retries, backpressure (429/503 with Retry-After) and Prometheus /metrics built in
Per-agent DID identity, tag-based policies and offline-verifiable audit credentials
weaknesses: Routing adds roughly 100-200ms per cross-agent hop
Graceful shutdown terminates in-flight executions rather than draining them

tools.name: odysseus
tools.description: Self-hosted workspace for chat, agents, email, documents and calendar
strengths: Covers chat, agents, email, documents, notes, tasks and calendar in one app
Agents support MCP, shell, files, skills and memory
Includes blind side-by-side model comparison and a hardware-aware model cookbook
weaknesses: Agents have shell and local tool access, so auth must stay enabled
AGPL-3.0 license limits closed-source network deployments

tools.name: hello-agents
tools.description: Chinese-language course on building AI-native agents from scratch, with code
strengths: Covers paradigms, existing frameworks, and building your own framework in one sequence
Includes an Agentic-RL chapter from SFT to GRPO, plus evaluation and protocol chapters
Companion code and case projects: travel assistant, deep research agent, simulated town
weaknesses: Main text is Chinese; an English README exists but its chapter coverage is not stated
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license forbids commercial use

tools.name: smolagents
tools.description: Python library for agents that write their actions as code
strengths: Core agent logic is under 1,000 lines, so it is easy to read and modify
Works with transformers, llama.cpp, LiteLLM, OpenAI-compatible, Azure and Bedrock models
Imports tools from MCP servers, LangChain and Hub Spaces; agents can be pushed to the Hub
weaknesses: Built-in LocalPythonExecutor is not a security boundary; a sandbox is needed for untrusted code
Managed sandbox options (E2B, Blaxel, Modal) are third-party cloud services

tools.name: letta-ai/letta
tools.description: Stateful agents with persistent memory, run from a terminal UI or App Server
strengths: Installs from npm and runs as a terminal UI with `letta`
`letta server` runs the App Server for local or self-hosted agents
Reachable through Slack, Telegram, Discord and custom channels
weaknesses: This repo holds no active source; development moved to letta-code
Original V1 API server is retired and only on the archive branch

tools.name: skillopt
tools.description: Trains agent skill documents against a frozen model with validation-gated edits
strengths: Validation-gated edits with a textual learning-rate budget and rejected-edit buffer
Deployed skill is one markdown file, with no added inference-time model calls
Backends for OpenAI, Azure, Claude, Qwen, MiniMax, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
weaknesses: Training needs a separate optimizer model and scored rollouts, so API cost scales with epochs
Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and Devin integration files are in the repo, not the PyPI wheel

tools.name: lightgbm
tools.description: Gradient boosting library for tree-based models on tabular data
strengths: Parallel, distributed and GPU training are supported, with a guide for each
Official packages on PyPI, conda-forge, CRAN and NuGet, plus a CLI
Many listed integrations: Spark, Ray, Kubernetes, ONNX, PMML, AutoML tuners
weaknesses: Covers gradient boosted trees only, not neural networks or general tensor work
Most integrations and extra language bindings are unofficial, not team-maintained

tools.name: lm-evaluation-harness
tools.description: Benchmark harness that runs 60+ academic LLM evals across many model backends
strengths: Over 60 benchmarks with hundreds of subtasks, using public prompts for reproducible comparisons
Backends include HF transformers, vLLM, SGLang, NeMo, llama.cpp server and OpenAI-style APIs
YAML task configs with Jinja2 prompts; plugins register backends, filters and metrics without forking
weaknesses: No native multi-node evaluation for the hf backend; needs an external server or custom integration
Base install has no model backend; extras like hf, vllm and api must be added

tools.name: krita-ai-diffusion
tools.description: Krita plugin for inpainting, live painting and upscaling with diffusion models
strengths: Works on Krita selections and layers, with per-region prompts defined by layers
ControlNet and IP-Adapter support: scribble, line art, depth, pose, style and face reference
Can install a local ComfyUI server or connect to an existing or remote one
weaknesses: Requires Krita 5.2.0 or newer; unusable outside Krita
CPU generation is supported but described as very slow

tools.name: sana
tools.description: Efficient diffusion models and training code for high-resolution image and video
strengths: Full training and inference code, not only weights, including DDP/FSDP and RL post-training
Runs in diffusers, ComfyUI and SGLang (OpenAI-compatible serving)
4-bit and 8-bit variants; README says SANA runs within 8GB VRAM
weaknesses: Research repo with many sub-projects; no single UI or one-command install
Some newer pieces (Sol-Engine, H3) live on a separate branch

tools.name: langchaingo
tools.description: Go port of LangChain for building LLM applications
strengths: Native Go library that compiles into your service binary
MIT license with a docs site, API reference and examples directory
Common llms interface across providers, shown with OpenAI in the README
weaknesses: README says development is moving to a community effort and seeks maintainers
README shows only a basic completion example, no agents or RAG

tools.name: claude-trading-skills
tools.description: Claude Skills for market review, trade planning and journaling by individual investors
strengths: Workflow YAML manifests name exact skills, decision gates and artifacts in order
Five-skill starter path needs no paid market-data API
skills-index.yaml is a validator-enforced canonical index of every skill
weaknesses: Requires Claude (web or Code); not usable with other models
Many screeners require an FMP key; some workflows need FINVIZ Elite or Alpaca

tools.name: yao
tools.description: Self-hosted agent manager with isolated workspaces and a task board
strengths: Runs agents across multiple devices you add, managed from one place
Task board turns conversation requests into tracked tasks
Isolated workspaces keep work separate and build up documents
weaknesses: README gives no install steps, hardware needs or supported model list
License is not identified (NOASSERTION), so terms need manual checking

tools.name: sdnext
tools.description: Web UI for generating and editing images and video with diffusion models
strengths: Covers NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm/ZLUDA, Intel XPU, OpenVINO, Apple MPS and CPU-only
Handles image and video generation, plus captioning, tagging, upscaling and interpolation
SDNQ quantization and CPU/GPU offloading help fit models into limited memory
weaknesses: README gives no RAM or VRAM minimums
No tagged release; the quick start installs by cloning the repo

tools.name: Vespa
tools.description: Serving engine for vectors, tensors, text and ML ranking at scale
strengths: Vectors, tensors, text and structured data queried and ranked together
Machine-learned ranking models evaluated at serving time
Runs hundreds of thousands of queries per second on large internet services
weaknesses: README covers building, not running; install details live in docs
Heavy platform (Java and C++ engine) sized for multi-node clusters

tools.name: rivet-dev/rivet
tools.description: Stateful Actor runtime with SQLite and WebSockets for durable agents and realtime apps
strengths: Only external dependency is an S3-compatible bucket; no Postgres, NATS or FoundationDB
Runs on stock Node.js or Bun, not a custom runtime
Per-Actor SQLite, hibernation, cron scheduling and Actor-to-Actor calls built in
weaknesses: General actor platform; agent features come from optional libraries, not core
Headline latency and memory figures are vendor benchmarks against E2B and Durable Objects

tools.name: skorch
tools.description: scikit-learn compatible wrapper for training PyTorch models
strengths: Drop-in sklearn API: Pipeline and GridSearchCV work with PyTorch modules
Callbacks for early stopping, checkpointing, LR schedulers and sklearn scoring
Documented integrations with GPyTorch and Hugging Face
weaknesses: PyTorch is not a declared dependency; users must install a matching version
Requires Python 3.9 or higher

tools.name: flash-linear-attention
tools.description: Triton kernels and PyTorch layers for linear attention and hybrid sequence models
strengths: Covers about 40 architectures, from RetNet and GLA to Mamba3, KDA and Gated DeltaNet
Layers can replace standard attention in an existing model, with hybrid model support
Backend extras for CUDA, ROCm, XPU, NPU and CPU installs
weaknesses: Bare pip install does not pull torch or triton; a backend extra is required
Full training loop lives in a separate repo (flame), not here

tools.name: agentic-bug-hunter
tools.description: Bug bounty CLI that runs recon, hunting, validation and report writing with LLMs
strengths: Supports Ollama for fully local runs, plus about ten cloud providers and gateways
Covers recon, hunt, validate and report in one CLI, also as Claude Code slash commands
Persistent hunt memory with resume via /pickup and a 10 MB rotated JSONL cap
weaknesses: Full recon needs subfinder, httpx, nuclei, katana, ffuf and nmap installed separately
No Docker or compose setup; installs via pip, uv or install.sh

tools.name: dsh-infinite-gen-5
tools.description: Reverse-engineering plugin for DeepSeek Harness using Ghidra, x64dbg and Unicorn
strengths: Bundles Ghidra, JDK, Python and x64dbg in the Windows package; no commercial IDA needed
13 mutating or executing tools gated by host approval, with undo and audit log
Per-function dossier combines pseudocode, CFG, call graph and stack frame from one revision
weaknesses: Requires an existing DeepSeek Harness install, pinned to >=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0
Full support only on Windows x64; macOS is Ghidra static only and experimental

tools.name: harnessrouter
tools.description: One API that runs agent harnesses like Codex and Claude Code as backends
strengths: OpenAI Responses-compatible API; harness switched per request via metadata.harness_id
31 harness bases, with a support matrix per provider
Idempotency-Key retries, W3C traceparent propagation and generated OpenAPI spec
weaknesses: Harness is fixed once a setup is saved; switching needs a new setup
Container must run as root to manage per-session users; --user is unsupported

tools.name: swanlab
tools.description: Experiment tracking and dashboards for ML training runs
strengths: Two-call integration: swanlab.init and swanlab.log, installed with pip install swanlab
Hardware monitoring covers Nvidia, AMD, Ascend, Cambricon, Kunlunxin, Hygon, MetaX, Moore Threads and Iluvatar
Integrations for many training frameworks, including veRL, trl, LLaMA Factory, Ultralytics and TensorBoard
weaknesses: Main README and docs are Chinese-first; English README is a separate file
Default workflow needs a swanlab.cn account and API key for the cloud

tools.name: openless
tools.description: Push-to-talk dictation that inserts AI-polished text at the cursor
strengths: Many ASR and polish providers plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; no single vendor required
Four output modes, including a structured AI-prompt mode, and custom style packs switchable by hotkey
Streaming insertion to the cursor, with automatic one-shot paste fallback
weaknesses: Linux uses a separate native host and has no in-app updater
macOS build is ad-hoc signed; needs xattr -cr to bypass Gatekeeper

tools.name: nanomuse
tools.description: Personal agent for phone, desktop and web with a self-hostable relay
strengths: Apps for Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and web share one account
Cross-device tasks: '@Mac ...' from the phone runs on the PC, approvals return to you
Memory and persona are Markdown files you can read and edit
weaknesses: Screen-control 'Hands' are not available on iOS
Default setup uses the community relay; conversation text passes through it unless self-hosted

tools.name: lazypredict
tools.description: Python library that benchmarks dozens of scikit-learn-style models in one call
strengths: One fit() call returns a metrics table across classifiers, regressors or forecasters
Per-model timeout and cv options; slow models are logged as errors instead of blocking
Optional GPU path for XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, cuML, LSTM/GRU and TimesFM, with CPU fallback
weaknesses: Runs models with default parameters only, so rankings are a rough screen, not tuned results
Timeout interruption works on Linux and macOS only, per the README

tools.name: OpenLIT
tools.description: OpenTelemetry-based tracing, evals and guardrails for LLM apps and coding agents
strengths: Follows OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; OTLP on 4317 (gRPC) and 4318 (HTTP)
One-line openlit.init() instruments 70+ providers, frameworks and vector DBs
Covers evals, prompt versioning, guardrails, secrets and cost in one tool
weaknesses: Wide scope (Vault, OpenGround, Rule Engine) means more to deploy and learn than a tracer
Storage is ClickHouse, adding a database to operate

tools.name: Moltis
tools.description: Self-hosted personal agent server in Rust with chat channels and sandboxing
strengths: Single Rust binary with no Node.js or Python runtime; lightweight feature flag for Raspberry Pi
Commands run in per-session containers (Docker, Podman, Apple Container), not on the host
Many channels built in: Telegram, Signal, Discord, Slack, Teams, Matrix, Nostr, WhatsApp, web PWA
weaknesses: Large codebase (~270K lines, 59 crates) despite the auditability claim
Source build needs just and Node.js for Tailwind CSS

tools.name: translatebookswithllms
tools.description: Translates EPUB, SRT, DOCX, PDF, TXT and PGN files with local or cloud LLMs
strengths: Checkpointing lets interrupted translations resume where they stopped
Glossary and style presets, with an auto mode that derives both from the document
Nine provider options, including local Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible server
weaknesses: PDF output is reflowed, so the original page layout is lost
No OCR, so scanned PDFs are unsupported

tools.name: notte
tools.description: Python SDK for local and stealth cloud browser sessions used by agents
strengths: Local sessions need no API key and use the same observe/execute/scrape API as cloud
Cloud sessions expose a CDP endpoint usable from Playwright, Puppeteer or Selenium
Vault placeholders and act() variables keep credentials away from the LLM
weaknesses: SSPL-1.0 license is not OSI-approved open source
Stealth, CAPTCHA solving, Functions, vaults and personas need the hosted Notte API

tools.name: minimind
tools.description: Train a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch in plain PyTorch
strengths: Covers pretrain, SFT, LoRA, DPO, PPO/GRPO/CISPO and agentic RL in one repo
Core training code is native PyTorch, readable without trl or peft abstractions
Published datasets and checkpoints; mini data pair reproduces a chat model on one GPU
weaknesses: Models are 64M-198M parameters with a 6,400-token vocabulary, so output quality is limited
Full pretrain and SFT datasets are 10GB and 14GB, a heavy download

tools.name: qlib
tools.description: Python platform for ML-based quantitative investment research and backtesting
strengths: Covers data, modeling, backtesting, portfolio optimization and execution in one codebase
Includes many published quant models, with example configs run through qrun
Components are loosely coupled and can be used stand-alone
weaknesses: Official dataset is disabled for now; README points to a community data source
Bundled data comes from Yahoo Finance and the README says it may be imperfect

tools.name: a2a
tools.description: Open protocol for agent-to-agent communication over JSON-RPC and HTTP
strengths: SDKs in six languages: Python, Go, JS, Java, .NET, Rust
Agents collaborate without exposing internal memory, tools or logic
Supports sync requests, SSE streaming and async push notifications
weaknesses: Protocol spec only; this repo has no runnable agent or server
Roadmap still lists open items such as authorization schemes in AgentCard

tools.name: candle
tools.description: Minimalist Rust ML framework with PyTorch-like tensors and CPU, CUDA and WASM backends
strengths: Builds into small Rust binaries without Python, aimed at serverless inference
Many model examples: LLaMA 1-3, Mistral, Mixtral, Gemma, Phi, Whisper, Stable Diffusion, YOLO
Loads safetensors, npz, ggml and PyTorch files; supports llama.cpp quantized types
weaknesses: Library, not a server; OpenAI-compatible APIs come from external projects like candle-vllm
Requires writing Rust; no Python bindings or ready-made UI

tools.name: tensorrt
tools.description: Open-source plugins, ONNX parser and samples for NVIDIA TensorRT inference
strengths: Build targets cover Linux x86-64, aarch64, Jetson Thor, DriveOS, QNX and Windows
Import paths documented for ONNX, Torch-TensorRT, HuggingFace/Optimum and the network API
Per-model support matrix covers LLM, vision, audio, diffusion and multimodal models
weaknesses: Only a subset of TensorRT; the core engine is a separate GA download
Requires an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA 12.9 or 13.4

tools.name: AI Toolkit
tools.description: LoRA and LoKr training suite for image, video and audio diffusion models
strengths: Supports many recent models: FLUX.2, Qwen-Image, Wan 2.2, LTX-2, Ace Step
Same jobs run from the CLI with YAML configs or from the web UI
Layer targeting with only_if_contains and ignore_if_contains; LoKr supported
weaknesses: Manual install requires an Nvidia GPU; Apple Silicon support is marked experimental
AI Toolkit Manager installer is labelled experimental

tools.name: agentguide
tools.description: Chinese-language study guide and interview prep for AI agent engineering roles
strengths: Separate development and algorithm roadmaps, stated as 8-12 and 10-15 weeks
Covers agent harness, context engineering, MCP, RAG, eval and agentic RL topics
Includes an interview question bank (1500+ claimed) and resume guidance
weaknesses: Written in Chinese; English readers need translation
No license detected, so reuse terms are unclear

tools.name: rtranslator
tools.description: Offline real-time speech translator for Android using on-device Whisper and NLLB
strengths: Runs speech recognition and translation on the phone, usable offline with no server
Conversation mode supports more than two phones and Bluetooth headsets
WalkieTalkie mode works with one phone and detects which of two languages is spoken
weaknesses: Needs at least 6 GB RAM and a fast CPU; weaker phones may crash
First launch downloads 1.2 GB of models from GitHub, slow in some regions

tools.name: ufo
tools.description: GUI agent for Windows, plus a multi-device DAG orchestrator for agents
strengths: Hybrid UIA/Win32/COM control with GUI fallback for Windows automation
Galaxy decomposes tasks into DAGs and runs them in parallel across devices
Speculative multi-action batching reported to cut LLM calls by 51%
weaknesses: UFO² is Windows-only; Galaxy is marked active development with moderate setup
Needs a hosted LLM API key such as gpt-4o; local model setup not described

tools.name: gepa
tools.description: Python library that evolves prompts and other text artifacts using LLM reflection
strengths: Reads full execution traces, not just a scalar score, to guide each mutation
README reports 100-500 evaluations versus 5,000-25,000+ for GRPO
Built-in adapters for DSPy, MCP, generic RAG, LangChain and TerminalBench
weaknesses: Needs a measurable evaluator and a dataset or metric to optimize against
Reflection step depends on a strong LLM (examples use openai/gpt-5), adding API cost

tools.name: craft-agents-oss
tools.description: Electron desktop client for Claude and Pi agents with MCP and API sources
strengths: Connects to stdio and remote MCP servers, REST APIs and local files, configured by prompting the agent
Three permission modes (Explore, Ask to Edit, Auto) switchable with Shift+Tab
Headless server with token auth and optional TLS, plus a scriptable CLI client
weaknesses: Ollama and OpenRouter are reached through the Anthropic-style custom endpoint, not native connections
Slack and Microsoft OAuth need credentials baked into source builds

tools.name: sensenova-u1
tools.description: Open 8B multimodal model for image generation, editing and visual Q&A
strengths: One checkpoint covers text-to-image, editing, interleaved generation and VQA
Native 4K generation and bounding-box or reference-based visual control in U1.5
8-step LoRA and GGUF checkpoints reduce latency and VRAM use
weaknesses: README admits dense text, hands, small faces and multi-turn edits can still fail
Official GGUF weights for U1.5 are not out yet; current GGUFs are community-made

tools.name: deeplabcut
tools.description: Markerless animal pose estimation toolbox with GUI and Python API
strengths: Works on any animal or object you can label; multi-animal and 3D pose supported
Pretrained SuperAnimal models with published mAP tables on held-out datasets
Both GUI and Python API; pip install with optional [gui] and [tf] extras
weaknesses: SuperAnimal models are non-commercial, research use only
TensorFlow backend is planned for deprecation in version 3.2

tools.name: solace-agent-mesh
tools.description: Agent build-and-runtime platform coordinating agents over a Solace event broker
strengths: `sam config plan` and `apply` preview and apply manifest-based configuration changes
Installer verifies SHA-256 checksums plus Apple notarization or Authenticode signatures
Desktop app bundles the `sam` CLI and installs skills for Claude Code or Codex CLI
weaknesses: Source code is not yet in the repository; only desktop downloads and examples
Production use requires a Solace commercial license (BUSL-1.1 noted in header)

tools.name: ctranslate2
tools.description: C++ and Python inference engine for Transformer models on CPU and GPU
strengths: Supports FP16, BF16, INT16, INT8 and AWQ INT4 quantization
README benchmarks show lower memory than PyTorch and Marian on the same models
One binary selects CPU backend (MKL, oneDNN, OpenBLAS, Ruy, Accelerate) at runtime
weaknesses: Models must be converted first; no direct loading of original checkpoints
Library only; an HTTP API needs the separate ctranslate2-web-server project

tools.name: kungfu
tools.description: Durable Work layer that keeps tasks intact across coding agents and failures
strengths: Work state persists across agent switches, crashes and disconnects without copying chat context
Blocks a second live agent from writing to the same Work
Built-in deterministic Mock Agent needs no provider credentials to try recovery scenarios
weaknesses: Alpha prerelease; README says it is not stable or generally available
Regular onboarding still needs a supported real agent for independent review

tools.name: flaml
tools.description: Python AutoML and hyperparameter tuning library with a scikit-learn style API
strengths: Three-line scikit-learn style AutoML fit with time budget control
Generic tune.run for arbitrary functions, with cost-aware search and early stopping
Zero-shot LGBMRegressor drop-in picks hyperparameters from the data
weaknesses: The autogen module was removed; agent use now requires the separate AutoGen repo
Requires Python >= 3.10 and < 3.14; other versions not guaranteed

tools.name: behaviortree.cpp
tools.description: C++17 library for building behavior trees for robots and game AI
strengths: Asynchronous, non-blocking actions are first-class, with reactive concurrent execution
Tree structure lives in XML loaded at run time, not hard-coded in C++
Type-safe dataflow between nodes; custom nodes can be run-time plugins
weaknesses: No LLM, model or tool-calling integration; fits the agent category only loosely
Requires a C++17 compiler; Conan builds need CMake 3.23 or newer

tools.name: pysr
tools.description: Symbolic regression library that finds equations from data
strengths: scikit-learn-style fit/predict API with a table of equations by complexity and loss
Exports equations to SymPy, callable functions, and differentiable JAX and PyTorch
Custom operators, losses, constraints and per-operator complexity are configurable
weaknesses: Julia dependencies install on first import, which slows initial setup
Suited to low-dimensional data; high dimensions need symbolic distillation of a neural net

tools.name: gliner
tools.description: Small zero-shot named entity recognition models with training and serving code
strengths: Arbitrary entity labels at inference time, no labeled data needed
Runs on CPU; FP16, INT8, torch.compile and ONNX export available
Several architectures: uni-encoder, bi-encoder, relation extraction, decoder, streaming
weaknesses: Uni-encoder handles only about 50 entity types; more needs the bi-encoder
INT8 accuracy requires models trained with quantization-aware training

tools.name: nixtla
tools.description: Python client SDK for the hosted TimeGPT time series forecasting API
strengths: Forecast or detect anomalies in a few lines using pandas DataFrames
Zero-shot inference, plus fine-tuning, cross-validation and prediction intervals
Handles exogenous variables, multiple series and irregular timestamps
weaknesses: Model is closed source; the repo holds only the client SDK
Every call needs an API key; access starts with a free trial

tools.name: llm-compressor
tools.description: Python library that quantizes and prunes Hugging Face models for vLLM
strengths: Wide scheme coverage: W8A8, W4A16, NVFP4, MXFP4/6/8, plus KV cache and attention quantization
Multiple algorithms selectable via recipe: GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant, AutoRound, rotations, REAP pruning
Handles large models with DDP, sequential onloading and disk offloading
weaknesses: Output targets vLLM via compressed-tensors; other runtimes are not mentioned
Some features are labeled experimental, such as NVFP4 attention with SpinQuant

tools.name: fast-agent
tools.description: Python framework and CLI for building MCP-enabled agents and workflows
strengths: Covers MCP features: sampling, elicitations, OAuth with keyring storage, Streamable HTTP diagnostics
Agents defined with short decorators; prompts and config live in plain files for version control
Built-in workflows: chain, parallel, router, orchestrator, evaluator-optimizer, MAKER, agents-as-tools
weaknesses: CLI-first; no web UI or visual workflow builder
Python only; setup instructions assume the uv package manager

tools.name: lightly
tools.description: PyTorch library for self-supervised vision pretraining and latent world models
strengths: Covers MoCo (2019) through LeJEPA and Pixio (2025), each with docs and Colab notebooks
Modular losses and heads that can be mixed with custom backbones
PyTorch and PyTorch Lightning examples, including distributed, for every listed model
weaknesses: Computer vision only; no text or speech pretraining
Docker support and one-command pretraining are in the commercial edition

tools.name: java-sdk
tools.description: Official Java SDK for building MCP clients and servers
strengths: Reactive Streams API on Project Reactor, with a blocking synchronous facade
Modular artifacts: BOM, core, Jackson 2 and Jackson 3 bindings, bundled `mcp`
Server conformance suite passes 40/40 at conformance version 0.1.15
weaknesses: No built-in authorization; it must be supplied by the application or Spring
Client conformance 3/4 scenarios; Spring auth suite 12/14 scenarios fully passing

tools.name: dsha
tools.description: Android app that runs DeepSeek Harness in a bundled Ubuntu rootfs, no root
strengths: Offline Ubuntu rootfs in the APK: apt, PTY and native modules work without Termux
Accessibility-based screen control needs no ADB, Shizuku or root
Built-in wireless ADB pairing; one command whitelist shared by ADB, Shizuku and root
weaknesses: APK is about 302 MiB because the full Ubuntu environment is bundled
arm64-v8a only; Android 10 and below are unsupported

tools.name: trulens
tools.description: Tracing and LLM-judge evaluation for agents and RAG apps on OpenTelemetry
strengths: Traces are OTel spans, exportable to any OTLP backend such as Jaeger or Datadog
Seven agent evaluators, including plan adherence, tool selection and tool calling
Runs inline or as batch evals over a dataset via the Run API
weaknesses: Evaluation relies on LLM judges, so most setups need an external model provider
Python only; instrumentation is by decorator or framework package

tools.name: mljar-supervised
tools.description: Python AutoML for tabular data with automatic reports and explanations
strengths: Four modes (Explain, Perform, Compete, Optuna) set defaults for search depth and budget
Generates HTML leaderboard and model reports with SHAP, learning curves and confusion matrices
Includes golden features, feature discovery, fairness-aware training and custom metrics or folds
weaknesses: README install commands pin a 1.4.0 release candidate (rc6), not a stable release
Tabular data only; no text or image modeling described

tools.name: vllm-ascend
tools.description: Hardware plugin that runs vLLM inference on Huawei Ascend NPUs
strengths: Uses vLLM's hardware-pluggable interface, so the core vLLM code is not forked
Covers dense, MoE, embedding and multi-modal models on Ascend NPUs
Release branches per vLLM version, each with a stated CI commitment
weaknesses: Runs only on Huawei Ascend NPUs, not on NVIDIA or AMD GPUs
Pins exact versions: Python 3.12, CANN 9.2.1, PyTorch 2.10.0

tools.name: ax-llm/ax
tools.description: DSPy-style typed LLM signatures, agents and flows for TypeScript and ports
strengths: Typed signatures via string DSL, f() builder, or Zod/Valibot/ArkType with retry on constraint failure
Same provider-profile API across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Together, Fireworks, DeepSeek, Grok and others
Includes GEPA and few-shot optimizers plus typed flows with branches, loops and parallel nodes
weaknesses: Python, Java, C++, Go and Rust libraries are generated from the TypeScript source
C++ port is source build via CMake FetchContent only

tools.name: paperless-gpt
tools.description: LLM-based OCR, titles, tags and document linking for paperless-ngx
strengths: Supports OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic and Ollama, so it can run fully local
Four OCR backends: vision LLM, Google Document AI, Azure Document Intelligence, Docling
Links related documents via exact reference lookup and leaves ambiguous matches unlinked
weaknesses: No built-in authentication; needs a reverse proxy or VPN in front
Only works with paperless-ngx; tested against 2.20.x and a 3.0 beta

tools.name: yue2-studio
tools.description: Desktop app that generates full songs with an editable score from YuE2
strengths: Editable ABC score: change notes, tempo or key and re-render the same composition
Native C++/CUDA engine, no Python or Node.js in the runtime path
Built-in MCP server on port 8791 with a headless mode for agents
weaknesses: Prebuilt download is Windows x64 only
Needs an NVIDIA card with 6 GB VRAM or more; AMD and Intel via Vulkan are experimental

tools.name: birdnet-go
tools.description: Realtime bird, wildlife and bat sound classifier with a web dashboard
strengths: Multiple models run in parallel on separate audio sources, with cross-model agreement boosting confidence
Alerts to Discord, Slack, Telegram, ntfy, MQTT with Home Assistant discovery, webhooks and BirdWeather
Single static binary with BirdNET model embedded; runs on a Raspberry Pi 4
weaknesses: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license forbids commercial use
Perch, BattyBirdNET and Geomodel need a separate ONNX Runtime install

tools.name: llm-wiki-compiler
tools.description: CLI that compiles source documents into a cited, interlinked markdown wiki
strengths: Citations point to source files and line ranges, and lint validates them
Same wiki is usable from the CLI, an MCP server and a TypeScript SDK
Review queue can hold generated pages; OKF imports are staged for review by default
weaknesses: Compile step needs LLM calls, so cost and latency scale with source volume
Sources are top-level Markdown files by default; nested folders need config

tools.name: telegram-mcp
tools.description: MCP server exposing a Telegram account to AI clients via Telethon
strengths: 80+ tools spanning messages, chats, contacts, media, folders, drafts and admin operations
Chat allowlist and TELEGRAM_EXPOSED_TOOLS=read-only limit what an agent can touch
Four transcription engines, including local faster-whisper where audio stays on the machine
weaknesses: Acts as a full user account, not a bot, so mistakes can message real contacts
Rich message formatting requires Telegram Premium on the account

tools.name: meigen-ai-design-mcp
tools.description: MCP bridge to MeiGen's hosted image and video generation and inspiration search
strengths: Remote MCP URL with OAuth; no Node.js install or API key needed
Search and model lookups do not spend generation credits
Documented setup for ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex and OpenClaw
weaknesses: Generation runs on the hosted service and uses purchased credits only
Only the client bridge and guides are MIT; hosted service is separate

tools.name: heym
tools.description: Visual builder and runtime for multi-agent workflows with tracing and evals
strengths: Built-in traces, per-model cost tracking, alerts and OpenTelemetry span export
Agent review checkpoints pause execution and resume from a saved snapshot
Workflows can be served as REST/SSE endpoints or published as MCP tools
weaknesses: MIT license with Commons Clause restricts selling the software; not OSI open source
Requires PostgreSQL; local setup also needs Bun, Python 3.11+, UV and Docker

tools.name: mindshub
tools.description: Agent workspace for knowledge work, with swappable open agent harnesses
strengths: Swappable open-source agent harnesses (Anton, Hermes) selectable from a dropdown
Connectors for BigQuery, Postgres, Gmail, Drive, HubSpot, Notion and Linear with per-connection credentials
Cross-session memory, skill library and scheduled tasks included
weaknesses: Linux has no installer; requires building from source with make and submodules
Pro tier needed for all frontier models and private artifacts

tools.name: faster-whisper
tools.description: Python Whisper speech-to-text library built on CTranslate2
strengths: Benchmark: 1m03s vs 2m23s for openai/whisper; int8 uses 2926MB VRAM vs 4708MB
BatchedInferencePipeline cut large-v2 time to 17s at batch_size=8 in the README benchmark
Bundles FFmpeg libraries via PyAV, so no system FFmpeg install is needed
weaknesses: Library only: no server or UI; an OpenAI-compatible API needs a separate project like speaches
GPU use needs cuBLAS for CUDA 12 and cuDNN 9; older CUDA requires pinning ctranslate2

tools.name: pytorch_geometric
tools.description: Graph neural network library built on PyTorch
strengths: Unified MessagePassing API keeps custom GNN layers short, as the EdgeConv example shows
Large catalog of published GNN layers, each linked to its paper and often an example script
Covers heterogeneous graphs, dynamic graphs, and sampling for graphs with millions of nodes
weaknesses: Requires PyTorch; install steps and version matching are not in the visible README
Focused on graph learning only, not a general ML or LLM toolkit

tools.name: finrl
tools.description: Deep reinforcement learning pipeline for stock and crypto trading research
strengths: Example scripts cover data download, training five DRL agents and backtesting against MVO and DJIA
Data processors for Yahoo Finance, Alpaca, Binance, CCXT, WRDS, Tushare and others
Supports Stable Baselines3, ElegantRL and RLlib agent backends
weaknesses: README steers new users to FinRL-X; this repo is for education and research
Live trading support is basic, limited to Alpaca

tools.name: minicpm
tools.description: Small open-weight LLM family for on-device use, latest is MiniCPM5-2B
strengths: Standard LlamaForCausalLM architecture, so it loads in vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp and Transformers
Ships GGUF, MLX and GPTQ builds plus a DSpark draft model for speculative decoding
Pretraining, code, SFT, agent and RL datasets are released alongside the model
weaknesses: Benchmark claims come from the authors' own comparison set; no independent results cited
Repo is mostly docs and notebooks; weights are hosted on Hugging Face and ModelScope

tools.name: transformers-tutorials
tools.description: Colab notebooks for running and fine-tuning Hugging Face Transformers models
strengths: Every demo has an Open in Colab badge, so no local setup is needed
Covers document AI in depth: LayoutLM v1-v3, LayoutXLM, Donut, DiT, MarkupLM
Includes both inference and fine-tuning notebooks, some using HF Trainer or PyTorch Lightning
weaknesses: PyTorch only; no TensorFlow or JAX notebooks
Many notebooks use older APIs (e.g. DetrFeatureExtractor) and may need version pinning

tools.name: moonshine
tools.description: On-device speech-to-text and voice agent toolkit with streaming models
strengths: Runs fully on-device, no account or API keys required
One library across Python, WASM, mobile, desktop and Raspberry Pi
Streaming design does work while the user is still speaking
weaknesses: Legacy non-English non-streaming models use a non-commercial community license
Repo license detected as NOASSERTION although README states MIT

tools.name: yolov3
tools.description: PyTorch implementation of YOLOv3, YOLOv3-SPP and YOLOv3-tiny object detectors
strengths: Three variants (YOLOv3, SPP, tiny) with COCO-pretrained weights that download automatically
Export to ONNX, TensorRT, OpenVINO, CoreML, TorchScript and PaddlePaddle via export.py
detect.py accepts webcam, video, screenshot, glob and RTSP/RTMP/HTTP stream sources
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0; commercial use without AGPL obligations needs a paid Enterprise License
Last release was 2021-11-14, though commits continue

tools.name: speech_recognition
tools.description: Python library wrapping many speech-to-text engines and APIs behind one interface
strengths: One recognizer interface across offline engines and a dozen cloud APIs
Offline options: Sphinx, Vosk, Whisper, Faster Whisper
OpenAI-compatible self-hosted endpoints (vLLM, Ollama) work via OPENAI_BASE_URL
weaknesses: Microphone input needs PyAudio, which requires PortAudio setup on Linux and macOS
Google Cloud support is V1 only; V2 is not supported

tools.name: bayesianoptimization
tools.description: Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization of black-box functions in pure Python
strengths: Minimal API: a function plus parameter bounds, then maximize()
Pure Python, installs from PyPI or conda-forge
Supports inequality constraints and domain reduction via SequentialDomainTransformer
weaknesses: Bounds are required for every parameter
Only maximizes; minimizing means negating the target

tools.name: page-assist
tools.description: Browser extension with a sidebar and web UI for local models
strengths: Sidebar opens on any page via Ctrl+Shift+Y; web UI opens in a tab via Ctrl+Shift+L
Chat with the current webpage, toggled with Ctrl+E
Works with Ollama, Chrome AI (Gemini Nano) and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
weaknesses: Sidebar and chat-with-webpage unsupported on Opera and Arc; only the web UI works
Needs a separate model backend such as Ollama; it does not run models itself

tools.name: firecrawl-mcp-server
tools.description: MCP server giving agents Firecrawl web search, scraping, crawling and browser actions
strengths: Covers scrape, crawl, map, search, browser interact, monitoring and agent jobs in one server
Hosted keyless endpoint offers scrape, search and parse without signup
Runs via npx, Docker image or local Streamable HTTP; supports self-hosted Firecrawl
weaknesses: Cloud use needs a Firecrawl API key and consumes paid credits
Full profile registers 31 tools, which can strain clients with tool-slot limits

tools.name: dwzhu-pku/paperbanana
tools.description: Multi-agent pipeline that drafts academic paper diagrams and plots from method text
strengths: Five-agent pipeline with a Critic-Visualizer refinement loop and selectable pipeline modes
Gradio app, Streamlit demo with refine/upscale tab, and a CLI
Hosted Hugging Face Space for trying it without setup
weaknesses: Needs external API keys for both the main model and the image generation model
Output quality relies on PaperBananaBench references, which cover mainly computer science

tools.name: mergekit
tools.description: Merge pre-trained language models in weight space from YAML configs
strengths: Lazy tensor loading: merges run on CPU or with as little as 8 GB VRAM
Many methods: linear, SLERP, TIES, DARE, DELLA, SCE, Model Stock and others
Also covers MoE merging, LoRA extraction, evolutionary merging and tokenizer transplantation
weaknesses: Command-line only; no bundled UI
No Docker image or compose file provided

tools.name: infinigen
tools.description: Procedural 3D scene generator on Blender with ground-truth renders
strengths: Renders depth, surface normals and instance segmentation alongside RGB images
Covers nature, indoor scenes and articulated sim assets in one codebase
Exports to OBJ, OpenUSD and physics simulators
weaknesses: Install and usage steps are split across several version branches and docs pages
Not a diffusion-model tool; it needs a Blender-based setup and config tuning

tools.name: doctr
tools.description: Two-stage OCR library for PDFs and images, built on PyTorch
strengths: Swappable detection (DBNet, LinkNet, FAST) and recognition (CRNN, SAR, MASTER, ViTSTR, PARSeq, VIPTR) models
Handles rotated pages and returns nested page/block/line/word output exportable to JSON
Includes KIE predictor, layout detection and a FastAPI template with OCR and KIE routes
weaknesses: Python 3.11 or higher required; PyTorch is the only supported framework
API template is minimal; README example uses port 8080 while the server runs on 8002

tools.name: marvin
tools.description: Python framework for structured LLM outputs and task-based agent workflows
strengths: Typed, validated results via Pydantic types, e.g. result_type=int or custom models
Works with all Pydantic AI model providers; OpenAI is the default
Small API: run, Task, Agent, Thread, plus extract, cast, classify, generate
weaknesses: No database migrations yet; README says to expect resetting data on updates
README's tool example runs untrusted shell commands; no sandboxing described

tools.name: causalml
tools.description: Python library for uplift modeling and causal inference with ML estimators
strengths: Common interface across uplift trees, meta-learners, doubly robust and neural CATE estimators
Benchmark loaders (LaLonde, IHDP, Twins) with SHA256-verified downloads and ground-truth metrics
Docs include an estimator decision guide, tutorial, quickstart and example notebooks
weaknesses: README warns some experimental code has APIs subject to change
Tabular causal estimation only; no LLM or generative model features

tools.name: cuml
tools.description: GPU-accelerated scikit-learn-style machine learning library
strengths: cuml.accel runs unmodified scikit-learn, UMAP and HDBSCAN code via `python -m cuml.accel`
Falls back to the CPU implementation when an estimator cannot be accelerated
cuml.dask gives multi-GPU and multi-node execution for selected algorithms
weaknesses: Targets NVIDIA GPUs only; no AMD or other accelerator support mentioned
Speedups vary by algorithm and dataset; the 50x figure is an upper bound

tools.name: aibrix
tools.description: Kubernetes control plane for routing and scaling vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM
strengths: Routes by prefix-cache, load and prefill/decode placement, with session affinity
Autoscales on engine metrics: queue depth, KV cache usage, tokens
One gateway fronts vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM
weaknesses: Kubernetes only; no standalone or single-host install path described
Installs Envoy Gateway and KubeRay as dependencies, adding cluster footprint

tools.name: all-agentic-architectures
tools.description: Python library of 35 agentic patterns with executed notebooks and benchmarks
strengths: Uniform `.run(task)` interface lets you swap patterns without changing downstream code
All 35 notebooks are executed with real LLM outputs; 283 tests pass
Nine providers selected by one env var, including local Ollama
weaknesses: Benchmark covers one model (Llama-3.3-70B on Nebius) and mostly 1 to 3 attempts per task
Reference implementations for study, not a framework with deployment or serving

tools.name: koog
tools.description: Kotlin framework for building tool-calling AI agents on JVM and multiplatform
strengths: Idiomatic Kotlin DSL with Java API, plus Spring Boot and Ktor integrations
Multiplatform targets: JVM, JS, WasmJS and iOS from one codebase
Agent persistence, retries and history compression for long-running agents
weaknesses: Kotlin and Java only; no Python or TypeScript SDK
Requires JDK 17+ and Kotlin 2.3.10+ in existing projects

tools.name: usearch
tools.description: Proximity-graph nearest-neighbor index with bindings for 14 languages
strengths: Header-only C++20 core with no external dependencies; one C ABI under all bindings
RAM, VRAM and NVMe residencies exchange portable SafeGraphs checkpoint files
Embedded in ClickHouse, DuckDB, ScyllaDB and YugabyteDB for vector search
weaknesses: Library only: no server, REST API or built-in clustering
Sequence, shape and geospatial engines are experimental and exposed only via C/C++

tools.name: neuralforecast
tools.description: Python library of 30+ neural time-series forecasting models with sklearn-style API
strengths: Over 30 forecasting models behind one fit/predict API
Official NHITS and NBEATSx implementations from the papers' authors
Auto models tune hyperparameters with Ray or Optuna
weaknesses: Models saved before 3.3.0 need allow_pickle=True or a migration step
TimeLLM cannot be saved or loaded; train and predict in one process

tools.name: cumora
tools.description: Team chat where AI agents and humans share rooms, Kanban and calendar
strengths: BYOA mode runs agents on your own Claude Code, Codex and other CLIs; server never sees provider keys
Server-side coordination (stale-reply hold, atomic claims) keeps agents in a room from colliding
Clients for desktop, web PWA, iOS (TestFlight) and Android, with per-agent real email
weaknesses: Self-hosting needs Postgres and Redis; cloud agent pods also need Kubernetes
Cloud agents depend on the OpenAI API; OPENAI_API_KEY is required

tools.name: spark-nlp
tools.description: Distributed NLP library running pretrained transformer pipelines on Apache Spark
strengths: Runs NLP pipelines natively inside Spark, so jobs scale across a cluster
Imports models from TensorFlow, ONNX, OpenVINO and llama.cpp GGUF
Documented setup for Databricks, EMR, EMR Serverless and GCP Dataproc
weaknesses: Needs Java and Spark, which is heavy for single-machine use
Separate Maven artifacts per Spark and Scala version, including a Spark 4.0.0 build

tools.name: rust-sdk
tools.description: Official Rust SDK for building MCP servers and clients on tokio
strengths: Official SDK from the modelcontextprotocol org, tracking the 2026-07-28 spec and older versions
Proc macros derive tool and prompt schemas from typed Rust structs
Supports stdio, child-process and streamable HTTP transports, including stateless HTTP
weaknesses: 3.x release has breaking changes; upgrading from earlier versions requires the migration guide
Requires tokio; no other async runtime is mentioned

tools.name: knowhere
tools.description: Document parsing and retrieval backend that builds navigable memory for agents
strengths: Progressive ingestion makes documents searchable before background enrichment finishes
Citations keep source document, section path, page number and rendered page image
External agents can call the same corpus tools via MCP or POST /v2/retrieval/tools/invoke
weaknesses: Setup needs Postgres, Redis, S3-compatible storage and several external API keys
PDF and PowerPoint parsing depends on a vision-capable model provider

tools.name: anthropic-sdk-python
tools.description: Official Python client for the Claude API
strengths: Maintained by Anthropic; last release matches the latest commit date
Installs from PyPI with a short client setup
Apache-2.0 license, with a v1 migration guide for 0.x users
weaknesses: Only talks to Claude models through the hosted Anthropic API
Requires an Anthropic API key and network access

tools.name: litert
tools.description: Google's on-device ML runtime, successor to TensorFlow Lite
strengths: Compiled Model API picks accelerators automatically, no manual delegate setup
NPU support from several vendors: Qualcomm, MediaTek, Google Tensor, Intel, Broadcom, S.LSI
Covers Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows and web (WebGPU/WASM via LiteRT.js)
weaknesses: Embedded runtime library, not a server; no HTTP API for serving models
LLM inference lives in a separate repo, LiteRT-LM

tools.name: qwen-audio-agent
tools.description: Realtime voice front end that delegates tasks to backend coding agents
strengths: Voice frontend and backend agent are swappable; many cloud and local frontends listed
Backend agents over ACP reuse their own models, MCP, Skills and auth
Background tasks run in parallel; progress queries and cancellation work mid-conversation
weaknesses: Default setup needs a cloud Bailian/DashScope API key; fully local path is one option
Some frontends lack tool calling, e.g. MiniCPM-o 4.5

tools.name: sag
tools.description: Self-hosted knowledge base with event-entity retrieval and cited agent answers
strengths: Starts on SQLite and LanceDB; no external database needed
Every result and citation opens the original source chunk
Exposes REST/OpenAPI, OpenAI-compatible chat, MCP, and a CLI for Codex and Claude Code
weaknesses: Single-user by design; no multi-user support
Indexing needs an embedding model and an LLM endpoint for event extraction

tools.name: audiomuse-ai
tools.description: Self-hosted sonic analysis and playlist generation for Navidrome, Jellyfin and Plex
strengths: Supports Navidrome, Jellyfin, LMS, Lyrion, Emby and Plex, several servers in one deployment
Analysis runs locally without metadata or external APIs; no ads or paywalls
Native packages bundle embedded PostgreSQL, web UI and workers; no Docker needed
weaknesses: Requires PostgreSQL v15; other versions may cause errors
Needs AVX2 CPU; VMs must pass through host CPU, noavx2 images are experimental

tools.name: macpaw/openai
tools.description: Swift client library for the OpenAI API and compatible providers
strengths: Covers Responses, Chat Completions, audio, images, embeddings, Assistants and MCP tools in one package
Offers async/await, closure and Combine APIs, with request cancellation for each
Configurable host, port, base path and headers, with a relaxed parsing mode for other providers
weaknesses: Swift and Apple-platform oriented; no support for other languages
Needs a hosted API key; the README warns against embedding it in client apps

tools.name: tokenspeed
tools.description: LLM inference engine with a C++ scheduler and pluggable kernels for agentic workloads
strengths: Control plane in C++ enforces KV cache and request lifecycle safety at compile time
Kernel registry with plugin mechanism for heterogeneous accelerators
Day-0 model support posts for Kimi K3, Qwen3.8 and GLM 5.3 Flash on NVIDIA and AMD
weaknesses: Project dates from May 2026; the release history is short
README has no install steps, hardware requirements or API compatibility details

tools.name: everroom
tools.description: Electron desktop workspace that groups files, memory and agents into project Rooms
strengths: Data, indexes and documents stored locally in SQLite and content-addressed objects by default
Agents get Room-scoped tools only, with cancellation and reviewable document edits
Exposes a bearer-protected MCP documents endpoint and OpenAPI docs on the local gateway
weaknesses: macOS is the development target; Windows installer is unsigned and needs a Rust toolchain
APIs, storage schemas and agent contracts may change during development

tools.name: boxlite
tools.description: Embeddable micro-VM sandboxes that run OCI images for AI agents
strengths: Own kernel per box via KVM or Hypervisor.framework, plus seccomp/sandbox-exec layer
Daemonless library embed; also CLI, REST server and cloud deployment guides for AWS and GCP
Runs unmodified OCI images; boxes persist, can be cloned or exported as .boxlite archives
weaknesses: Needs KVM on Linux; macOS limited to Apple Silicon, macOS 12+
Windows support only through WSL2 with KVM access

tools.name: beeftv
tools.description: Desktop canvas for AI video production with a built-in agent and workflows
strengths: Node canvas links scripts, storyboards, images, video and audio in one project
Built-in agent plus MCP page to connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop
Model channels are configurable per modality, not tied to a single provider
weaknesses: Source-available license; resale, paid deployment and hosting need written authorization
Licensing is mixed: older history is MIT, newer original content is not

tools.name: deepdetect
tools.description: Torch-based training and inference runtime with a CLI and REST server
