strengths: One JSON API covers images, text, CSV, time series and sparse data
Model repositories stored on the filesystem, no database dependency
Python wheels for CPU and CUDA, plus a REST server for long-running services
weaknesses: Packaged CLI profiles cover only YOLOX, SegFormer and external PyTorch workers
Caffe is no longer an active backend

tools.name: whisperjav
tools.description: Local subtitle generator for Japanese video with scene, VAD and ASR pipelines
strengths: Two-pass ensemble with seven merge strategies and savable presets
Japanese post-processing: hallucination removal, sound-only line removal, timing repair
Scene detection, enhancement, VAD and ASR model are swappable per pass
weaknesses: Tuned for one domain; results vary with source audio quality
GGUF CrispASR pipelines are experimental and Japanese only

tools.name: roboflow/inference
tools.description: Inference server for running computer vision models and Workflows on cameras
strengths: Workflow blocks chain detection, OCR, tracking, time-in-zone and webhook or email notifications
Handles RTSP and webcam streams with GPU batching and multiprocessing
Documented install paths for Linux, Windows, Mac, Jetson and Raspberry Pi
weaknesses: Private workflows, fine-tuned models and Universe models need a Roboflow API key
Enterprise code is source-available only; production use requires a contract

tools.name: yovoice
tools.description: Desktop studio for local speech, voice cloning, song and score generation
strengths: Covers TTS, cloning, music, stem separation, transcription and MIDI scoring in one app
Native C++ engine with Metal and bundled CUDA 12.4/13.3 runtimes; no Python setup
Includes CLI, agent skill and authenticated HTTP API/MCP server
weaknesses: Several model weights (OmniVoice, YuE2, Breeze TTS 2, Voxtral) are non-commercial only
Linux build does not self-update and uses CPU unless a Vulkan runtime is downloaded

tools.name: transcribe.cpp
tools.description: C++ speech-to-text library running many ASR models from GGUF files
strengths: Covers 16 ASR families and 60+ variants through one C API and CLI
GPU backends for Metal, Vulkan, CUDA and ROCm, plus a CPU path
Published models are WER-tested against reference implementations, per the README
weaknesses: Input must be 16 kHz mono WAV; other formats need ffmpeg or sox first
Built from source with CMake; no Docker image or prebuilt binaries described

tools.name: ai4s-research/open-science
tools.description: Desktop AI research workbench with agents, notebooks, and provenance tracking
strengths: Provenance log links figures and reports to the exact code, inputs and run
Model-agnostic via OpenCode catalog, OAuth/API keys, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints
`osd server` runs headless with the same web UI; no-root Linux install script
weaknesses: Windows and Linux builds are not signed
Detected license is NOASSERTION, while the README badge says MIT

tools.name: nao
tools.description: Chat agent that answers warehouse questions from a data-team-maintained context layer
strengths: `nao test` compares agent SQL to expected queries, so context changes can be checked offline
Reachable from web UI, Slack, Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp, Mattermost or any MCP client
Shows the SQL and context files behind each answer; bring your own LLM key
weaknesses: Row-level security, Entra ID/OIDC SSO and LLM budgets need the paid Enterprise license
Open source edition caps user groups at 3 and has no multi-project support

tools.name: pomerado
tools.description: Generates MCP servers for websites from a plain-language task description
strengths: Needs only a text task description; no HAR file or recording required
Minted integrations run with no model request; only minting needs an API key
Works on sites behind login and two-factor authentication without saving credentials
weaknesses: Minting requires an OpenAI API key; no other provider is listed for building
Supports macOS and Linux only, and Node 24.21 up to below 25

tools.name: tooluniverse
tools.description: Catalog of 2,700+ scientific tools exposed to LLM agents via MCP and Python
strengths: Compact mode reduces 2,700+ tools to 4-5 discovery tools, saving context window
Runs via uvx as an MCP server, or as Python SDK and tu CLI
Two-tier cache (in-memory LRU plus SQLite) allows offline reruns and reproducibility
weaknesses: Tool coverage is biomedical and life-science oriented, not general-purpose
Many tools call third-party APIs and need separate API keys

tools.name: inno-agent
tools.description: Personal learning agent with layered memory, cron scheduler and Feishu/WeChat channels
strengths: Three separate memory layers: editable learner profile, wiki, and SQLite FTS5 session recall
Works with any openai-completions or anthropic-messages endpoint, including Ollama; models switch live
Desktop, web and CLI share the same runtime state
weaknesses: Single user only: no auth, no tenant isolation, one active agent session per process
Cross-session operations return 409 session_busy while another turn is running

tools.name: deeppapernote
tools.description: Agent skill that turns one paper into an illustrated Obsidian note
strengths: Ten paper-type templates, each with its own note structure and reading criteria
Crops figures and tables from the PDF and places them beside the discussion
Stops and asks for the paper when only the abstract is available
weaknesses: Needs a skill-capable agent such as Claude Code or Codex; not standalone
Scanned PDFs need Tesseract and pytesseract for OCR

tools.name: maverick-mcp
tools.description: MCP server for stock quotes, technical analysis, screening and portfolio tracking
strengths: Core tools need no API key; market data comes from yfinance
Portfolio, watchlists and trade journal persist locally in SQLite, with optional PostgreSQL
Supports STDIO and Streamable HTTP, with setup guides for several MCP clients
weaknesses: HTTP endpoint has no authentication; it binds to 127.0.0.1 by default
Daily history supports US symbols and only six exchange suffixes

tools.name: vibevoice
tools.description: Microsoft's open speech models for long-form ASR and streaming TTS
strengths: ASR handles 60 minutes in one pass, returning speaker, timestamps and text together
Streaming ASR, vLLM serving and ASR fine-tuning code are documented
BitNet CPU build shrinks ASR from 4.62 GB to 1.58 GB, RTF under 1 on 3+ threads
weaknesses: VibeVoice-TTS code was removed; the 1.5B TTS model is listed as Disabled
README says it is for research only, not recommended for commercial use

tools.name: voxcpm
tools.description: Tokenizer-free multilingual text-to-speech with voice design and cloning
strengths: Voice design from a text description, with no reference audio needed
Three cloning modes, including transcript-based continuation cloning
30 languages plus nine Chinese dialects, no language tag required
weaknesses: Documented requirements are CUDA 12.0+ and PyTorch 2.5+; CPU use only via GGUF port
GGUF on Apple M4 Pro runs at RTF ~1.76, slower than real time

tools.name: colossalai
tools.description: Distributed training library for large models with many parallelism strategies
strengths: Covers data, pipeline, tensor (1D to 3D), sequence parallelism and ZeRO in one library
Includes worked examples for LLaMA, GPT-2/3, BERT, ViT, MoE and Stable Diffusion
Publishes H200 and B200 benchmarks for 7B and 70B Llama-like training with parallel configs
weaknesses: README opens with HPC-AI Cloud and Model API promotions, mixed into the project docs
Last tagged release is 2025-06-04, well behind recent commits

tools.name: unlimited-ocr
tools.description: OCR model that parses multi-page PDFs and long documents in one request
strengths: Parses all pages of a document in one request, keeping cross-page context
SR-SWA keeps per-step decoding memory near constant regardless of document length
SGLang server exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint with streaming
weaknesses: Serving needs a customized SGLang wheel pinned to one dev build
Many SGLang memory settings need manual tuning to avoid OOM

tools.name: agent-s
tools.description: Computer-use agent that operates desktop GUIs via screenshots, mouse and keyboard
strengths: Works on any GUI without per-app API integration or scripting
Runs on macOS, Windows and Linux; pip install gui-agents plus a CLI
Reports 72.60% on OSWorld using multi-rollout selection; papers are published
weaknesses: Requires a separately hosted grounding model such as UI-TARS-1.5-7B
Executes generated Python on your machine; no built-in sandbox

tools.name: cloudflare-os
tools.description: Agent chat workspace where AI builds sandboxed per-user apps with approval-gated access
strengths: Gadgets run in Dynamic Worker sandboxes with internet disabled and iframe-isolated clients
Gatekeepers simulate side effects; users approve or reject queued actions in bulk later
Capability-based access: agents and gadgets get no resources until explicitly introduced
weaknesses: README calls it early access with many rough edges; this is a version 2 rewrite
Self-hosting on plain workerd is marked COMING SOON; local mode is not for production

tools.name: holaos
tools.description: Electron desktop workspace that runs agents beside live apps, with local memory
strengths: Runs Claude Code, Codex and its own agent over shared memory, skills and tools
Memory, embeddings and session history stored locally as readable, editable files
Supports MCP servers, 50+ OAuth integrations and bring-your-own-key providers
weaknesses: Modified Apache 2.0 license with commercial-distribution and branding conditions
Built-in models and marketplace tie into a holaOS account; sign-in required for those

tools.name: agent-squad
tools.description: Routes queries to specialized agents in Python, TypeScript and Swift
strengths: Same orchestration model in Python 3.11+, TypeScript and on-device Swift
Classifier routing, streaming and non-streaming responses, pluggable storage and retrievers
SupervisorAgent queries sub-agents in parallel; GroundedAgent limits replies to fetched tool output
weaknesses: Pre-built agents and examples lean toward AWS (Bedrock, Lex, Lambda)
JevClassifier needs a TypeSafe AI API key and a paid external service

tools.name: sandbox-runtime
tools.description: OS-level filesystem and network sandbox for agents and arbitrary processes, no container
strengths: No container needed; uses native OS primitives on macOS, Linux and Windows
Deny-by-default network and write access, configured in ~/.srt-settings.json
Usable as CLI or library, with per-command allow lists and an ask callback
weaknesses: Beta research preview; APIs and config formats may change
Reads are allowed everywhere by default unless denyRead is configured

tools.name: amagine3d
tools.description: LLM agent that writes editable build123d CAD for printable enclosures
strengths: Outputs editable build123d source plus real STEP, STL and 3MF with color regions
Agent checks measured wall thickness, interference and motion clearance on generated BRep geometry
Candidates are committed only after checks pass, so the last accepted version is kept
weaknesses: Scope is limited to printable hardware enclosures and related structures
Requires an OpenAI Responses-compatible API key or gateway; no local model path described

tools.name: olares
tools.description: Kubernetes-based personal cloud OS for running local LLMs and AI agents
strengths: Pools GPUs across nodes with time-slicing, memory-slicing and exclusive modes
Bundles files, VPN, reverse proxy, Vault and app market in one system
Multiple install paths: shell script, ISO image, Docker Compose
weaknesses: Needs 4 CPU cores, 8 GB RAM and 150 GB SSD; installation fails on HDD
Script install supports only Ubuntu 22.04 to 25.04 and Debian 12 or 13

tools.name: tradingview-mcp
tools.description: MCP server for market data, technical analysis and backtesting across stocks and crypto
strengths: 39 tools covering screeners, indicators, multi-timeframe analysis and news in one server
Backtesting with 9 strategies, walk-forward split and overfitting verdict
No TradingView account or API key needed; installs via pip or uvx
weaknesses: Depends on unofficial public endpoints, so data can be delayed, incomplete or break
News and sentiment need a Marketaux key; free tier is 100 requests/day

tools.name: fastvideo
tools.description: Post-training and inference framework for accelerated video diffusion models
strengths: Covers training and inference: LoRA, full finetune, DMD2, Self-Forcing, FSDP2, sequence parallelism
Runs on NVIDIA CUDA 12/13, DGX Spark, Apple Silicon via MLX, and AMD ROCm
Publishes distilled checkpoints (FastWan, FastH3) on Hugging Face with cookbook recipes
weaknesses: Sparse-attention speedups depend on VSA kernels, which need a separate install step
Multi-GPU use on low-RAM hosts like Colab risks OOM; README advises num_gpus=1

tools.name: WhisperLive
tools.description: Near-real-time Whisper transcription server with WebSocket and REST clients
strengths: Three backends: faster_whisper, TensorRT and OpenVINO, with an AMD ROCm guide
Accepts mic, files, RTSP, HLS and raw PCM streams over WebSocket
Optional batch inference groups multiple client sessions into single GPU calls
weaknesses: TensorRT backend needs separate TensorRT-LLM setup and manual engine builds
Diarization needs optional pyannote.audio and is unsupported on TensorRT

tools.name: onednn
tools.description: Optimized CPU and GPU deep learning primitives library used inside PyTorch and TensorFlow
strengths: Runtime ISA detection with JIT kernels for Intel 64/AMD64, AArch64 and RV64 CPUs
Data types from f32 down to f4 and s4, including OCP microscaling formats
Graph API fuses larger patterns such as SDPA and GQA; post-ops fuse into matmul and convolution
weaknesses: Low-level C/C++ API; README advises most users to go through a framework instead
NVIDIA and AMD GPU backends are experimental; PPC64 and s390x have limited validation

tools.name: raptor
tools.description: Security research framework chaining scanners, LLM triage, PoC and patch generation
strengths: Covers source, dependencies, binaries, fuzzing and crashes in one workflow
Custom sandbox: Linux namespaces, Landlock, seccomp, or Seatbelt on macOS
Mechanical scans and SCA run without an LLM (/scan, --no-llm)
weaknesses: Authors call it not polished software; most of the code is AI-generated
Interactive shell needs Claude Code with a subscription or Anthropic API key

tools.name: flashrag
tools.description: Python toolkit for reproducing and building RAG pipelines on benchmarks
strengths: 36 pre-processed RAG benchmark datasets and 23 algorithms with reported results
Dense (Faiss), BM25 (bm25s or Pyserini) and SPLADE retrieval via Seismic
Custom pipelines by subclassing BasicPipeline, configured through YAML or dict
weaknesses: Research-oriented; not a ready-made document Q&A app for end users
Faiss has to be installed through conda because the pip package is incompatible

tools.name: ailearning-theory-applying
tools.description: Chinese course notes and notebooks on ML math, deep learning, Transformer and BERT
strengths: Covers math basics through Transformer and BERT in one repository
Competition solution notebooks, many bundled with datasets, so they can be rerun
Transformer explained in eight short chapters, from embeddings to final output
weaknesses: Written in Chinese only; the README has no English version
Little on current LLM tooling beyond one 2024 competition write-up

tools.name: py-xiaozhi
tools.description: Python voice client for Xiaozhi AI servers with MCP tools and GPIO
strengths: Three front ends: PySide6/QML GUI, Textual TUI, and GPIO for headless boards
Offline wake word via Sherpa-ONNX with custom keywords
Runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, and ARM boards (Raspberry Pi, RDK, Jetson Nano)
weaknesses: Needs a Xiaozhi-compatible backend and internet; no local LLM is run
Python 3.10 to 3.12 only; GUI and TUI need separate extras

tools.name: neuralnote
tools.description: Audio plugin that transcribes audio to multi-instrument MIDI locally in a DAW
strengths: Multi-instrument transcription of full mixes, with per-instrument gain, mute and solo in a built-in synth
Runs locally on Metal, Vulkan or CPU; audio never leaves the machine
Transcription can be paused and resumed, even after reopening the DAW session
weaknesses: MuScriptor weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, so non-commercial use only
Large model runs about 0.5x real time on an M1 Pro GPU; CPU not recommended

tools.name: physicsnemo
tools.description: PyTorch framework for training physics and scientific ML models
strengths: Models are ordinary torch.nn.Module objects, usable inside existing PyTorch code
ShardTensor domain parallelism shards one large sample across GPUs, with DDP or FSDP2
Wide model coverage: FNO, MeshGraphNet, Transolver, DoMINO, GraphCast, Pangu, FengWu, TopoDiff
weaknesses: Install extras target CUDA 12 or 13, so it is built around NVIDIA GPUs
Narrow domain focus; not meant for LLM or general deep learning work

tools.name: beeai-framework
tools.description: Python and TypeScript library for building multi-agent systems
strengths: Same toolkit in Python and TypeScript, installable from pip and npm
RequirementAgent enforces rules such as forced tool calls at a given step
Can serve agents over A2A and MCP, and use MCP tools
weaknesses: RequirementAgent is described as experimental in the README
IBM states it will not maintain or support the code as a product

tools.name: project-maya
tools.description: Runs very large MoE LLMs locally by streaming experts between GPU, RAM and SSD
strengths: Tiered expert placement across VRAM, RAM and SSD lets 200-750B models run on one GPU
Publishes user benchmarks with hardware and version, e.g. 81 tokens/s on one RTX PRO 6000
OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API with tool calls; up to 8 concurrent requests on three models
weaknesses: Needs roughly 56 GB to 192 GB of RAM plus VRAM, depending on the model
Each model needs its own engine; support is limited to the five listed families

tools.name: fastembed
tools.description: Python library that generates text and image embeddings with ONNX Runtime
strengths: No PyTorch dependency; ONNX Runtime keeps installs small and suits serverless runtimes like AWS Lambda
Covers dense, sparse, ColBERT, ColPali, image embeddings and cross-encoder rerankers in one API
add_custom_model registers unlisted Hugging Face ONNX models for embeddings and reranking
weaknesses: Only models with ONNX exports are supported; custom models need pooling and file settings
GPU use needs the separate fastembed-gpu package and a matching CUDA setup

tools.name: ai-knowledge-graph
tools.description: Turns documents into an interactive knowledge graph using an LLM
strengths: Every extracted edge keeps its source sentence; inferred edges record their method and are capped
Exports to JSON, CSV, GraphML (Gephi, yEd, Cytoscape) and a Neo4j Cypher script
Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenAI and Gemini
weaknesses: graph-serve has no authentication; it binds to 127.0.0.1 by default
Graph quality depends on the chosen LLM; reasoning models need a large max_tokens

tools.name: lightx2v
tools.description: Inference framework for video and image diffusion models
strengths: Wide model coverage: Wan, HunyuanVideo-1.5, LTX-2, Qwen-Image, MiniMax-H3, Self-Forcing
Ships FP8/NVFP4 quantized and 4-8 step distilled weights on HuggingFace
CFG and Ulysses parallelism plus offload; HunyuanVideo-1.5 runs on 24GB RTX 4090
weaknesses: Setup is script-driven per model; weights and caches are prepared manually
Attention and quantization kernels need separate installation steps

tools.name: datachain
tools.description: Python library that indexes cloud files into versioned, typed datasets
strengths: Checkpoint recovery resumes a failed UDF from the last uncommitted batch
delta=True reprocesses only new or changed files and drops results for deleted ones
Pydantic return types become queryable columns; vectors stored in the same rows for similarity search
weaknesses: Distributed compute, shared registry, MCP endpoint and Knowledge Base require Studio
Agent skill targets only Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot and Pi

tools.name: leptonai
tools.description: Python SDK and lep CLI for managing NVIDIA DGX Cloud Lepton workloads
strengths: Single CLI covers endpoints, jobs, dev pods, Ray clusters, Dynamo deployments and Slurm inspection
Dynamo commands support multi-node and disaggregated prefill/decode with vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM
Shell access through workspace API over HTTPS, no SSH keys needed; Teleport SSH also supported
weaknesses: Only works against NVIDIA DGX Cloud Lepton; it is not a self-hostable serving stack
Requires a Lepton workspace account and login to do anything useful

tools.name: maxtext
tools.description: JAX library for pre-training and post-training LLMs on TPUs and GPUs
strengths: Large model library: Gemma, Llama, DeepSeek V4, Qwen 3.x, Kimi K2.x, GPT-OSS, Mixtral
Pre-training and post-training (SFT, GRPO, GSPO) in one codebase
Scales from a single host to tens of thousands of chips
weaknesses: Primarily targets Google Cloud TPUs; GPU support is secondary
README says the main branch is not production-ready; use PyPI releases

tools.name: webclaw
tools.description: Rust CLI and MCP server that turns web pages into clean markdown or JSON
strengths: Many output modes: markdown, llm text, tables JSON, selectors, query filtering, and RAG chunks
Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows, plus Homebrew, Cargo and Docker installs
npx create-webclaw configures MCP for Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex CLI and others
weaknesses: JavaScript rendering needs a build with the browser feature and local Chrome
AGPL-3.0 license restricts use in closed-source network services

tools.name: fairchem
tools.description: Pretrained UMA atomistic models and ASE calculator for materials and chemistry
strengths: One UMA model covers catalysts, materials, molecules, MOFs and molecular crystals via task names
Drop-in ASE calculator; install with pip install fairchem-core
Multi-GPU and multi-node inference with LAMMPS integration, set with workers=N
weaknesses: UMA checkpoints are gated on Hugging Face; access request and login required
Model and checkpoint licenses vary by application area, separate from the MIT code

tools.name: contextgem
tools.description: Python library for extracting typed, source-referenced data from documents
strengths: Items carry references to source paragraphs or sentences, with optional justifications
Works with any LLM supported by LiteLLM, including Ollama and LM Studio
Decision models return per-answer probabilities with configurable thresholds
weaknesses: Tested with hosted LLMs; smaller local models may not follow extraction instructions
Decision models need an external provider such as TypeSafe Jev or OpenAI Decisions API

tools.name: biomcp
tools.description: CLI and MCP server for querying biomedical databases like PubMed and ClinVar
strengths: Single binary with stdio MCP and HTTP serve modes, plus Claude Code plugin and embedded skills
Cross-entity pivots (variant to trials, drug to adverse events) without rebuilding filters
Most commands need no API key; optional keys raise rate limits or enable OncoKB, DisGeNET
weaknesses: Depends on live upstream APIs; some sources restrict commercial or clinical use
Rate limiting is process-local, so many workers need one shared HTTP endpoint

tools.name: mcpproxy-go
tools.description: MCP proxy that federates many MCP servers behind one quarantined endpoint
strengths: Single binary for macOS, Linux and Windows with the web UI embedded
New servers are quarantined and tool definition changes held for review by default
Pluggable Docker scanners (Snyk, Semgrep, Trivy, Cisco) with SARIF output and risk score
weaknesses: On the 45-tool benchmark the initial menu is larger than listing all tools (2625 vs 1730 tokens)
Quarantine has documented gaps: schema-only edits, and auto mode does not hold changes

tools.name: blockrun-mcp
tools.description: MCP server for market data, search, media and Polymarket trades, paid per call
strengths: Two payment modes: self-custody USDC wallet (Solana, Base, Arc) or API key with card-funded credit
Optional spend confirmation and BLOCKRUN_BUDGET_LIMIT cap paid calls
Tool profiles (trading, media, research, chat) cut schema context from 14.3K to as low as 2.2K tokens
weaknesses: Full profile costs about 14.3K tokens of context on every turn
Polymarket trading needs a wallet keypair; API key mode cannot trade

tools.name: hanlp
tools.description: Multilingual NLP toolkit for tokenization, tagging, parsing and NER, mainly Chinese
strengths: Covers many classic NLP tasks with pretrained models: tok, POS, NER, dep, con, SRL, SDP, AMR
Native and RESTful APIs share the same semantics, so code ports between them
Custom trie dictionaries with force, merge and correct rules feed into downstream models
weaknesses: Native API requires Python 3.6 to 3.10, which is dated
Last release is 2025-01-13; the README is Chinese-first

tools.name: fish-speech
tools.description: Expressive multi-speaker text-to-speech models with voice cloning
strengths: Voice cloning from 10-30 seconds of reference audio (S2-Pro)
Inline tags like [whisper], [excited], [laughing] control emotion and prosody
Drama 3 can replace single words in audio and revise earlier takes
weaknesses: Custom Fish Audio community license; S2-Pro weights under a separate research license
Drama 3 is 35B total parameters; hardware requirements are not stated in the README

tools.name: dexter
tools.description: Terminal agent that plans and runs financial research using live market data
strengths: Logs every tool call and agent step to JSONL scratchpad files for inspection
Includes loop detection and step limits against runaway execution
Eval suite with LangSmith tracking and LLM-as-judge scoring
weaknesses: Needs a Financial Datasets API key, a third-party data service
Setup lists an OpenAI key as a prerequisite; fully local use is not documented

tools.name: whisperx
tools.description: Batched Whisper transcription with word timestamps and speaker diarization
strengths: Word-level timestamps via wav2vec2 forced alignment, not just utterance-level timing
Batched faster-whisper inference; README claims 70x realtime with large-v2
Runs on CPU with int8 or on GPU; memory tunable via batch size and compute type
weaknesses: Diarization needs a Hugging Face token and accepting the pyannote model agreement
Words like "2014." or "£13.60" get no timing because the aligner cannot place them

tools.name: ds4
tools.description: Native C inference engine for a few large open models on Mac, CUDA and ROCm
strengths: Multi-GPU CUDA including Ada Lovelace; reports ~126 t/s aggregate on eight L40S with 16 sessions
SSD streaming runs models larger than RAM; two-Mac RDMA tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism
Includes CLI, HTTP server, native coding agent with saved KV sessions, and ds4-eval
weaknesses: Not a general GGUF runner; only the project's own GGUF files for a few models
README calls it beta quality and fast-changing, with possible regressions

tools.name: googlecloudplatform/generative-ai
tools.description: Notebooks and sample apps for Gemini, Imagen, Veo and Chirp on Google Cloud
strengths: Organized by topic: Gemini, Agent Search, RAG and grounding, vision, audio, setup
Links to related Google repos such as ADK Samples and Agent Starter Pack
Setup guide covers the Gen AI Python SDK, Colab and Workbench
weaknesses: Tied to Google Cloud services and Google models; no local or open-weight models
README states code is demonstrative and not officially supported

tools.name: turbovec
tools.description: In-process quantized vector index for Python and Rust using TurboQuant
strengths: README reports 4.4× faster than FAISS FastScan at 4-bit, at matching recall
7.8× smaller than float32 at 4-bit, 15.5× at 2-bit
No training or rebuild; add and remove cost microseconds per vector
weaknesses: Scans every vector, so query cost grows linearly with corpus size
Lossy: top-1 matches float ground truth 96–98% at 4-bit on OpenAI embeddings

tools.name: rd-agent
tools.description: LLM agent that proposes and implements ML experiments for quant and data science
strengths: Reports MLE-bench results: 30.22% overall with o3 research and GPT-4.1 development agents
Ready-made CLI scenarios: fin_quant, fin_factor, fin_model, general_model, data_science
LiteLLM backend works with OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and DeepSeek, among others
weaknesses: Linux only; most scenarios need Docker usable without sudo
Needs a chat model with json_mode plus an embedding model, so API costs apply

tools.name: stable-baselines3
tools.description: PyTorch implementations of reinforcement learning algorithms with a scikit-learn-like API
strengths: Consistent sklearn-like API across algorithms; a PPO run is a one-line call
Supports Gymnasium envs, Dict observations, custom policies, callbacks and TensorBoard
Type hints, high test coverage, and benchmark results documented per algorithm
weaknesses: Assumes prior RL knowledge; README says not to use it without practice
Maintenance mode only; no major new features planned for the core

tools.name: litgpt
tools.description: PyTorch LLM implementations with recipes to pretrain, finetune, evaluate and serve
strengths: Single CLI covers download, finetune, pretrain, evaluate, chat and serve
Readable single-file model implementations, easy to debug and modify
Supports LoRA, QLoRA, adapter finetuning and full pretraining from scratch
weaknesses: Only the listed model families are supported; new architectures need code added
No Docker or compose files in the repo

tools.name: corenlp
tools.description: Java NLP toolkit for tagging, parsing, named entities and coreference
strengths: One pipeline runs tokenizing, tagging, NER, parsing and coreference from two lines of code
Published on Maven Central; builds with Ant or Maven, and Gradle dependency snippets are given
Model jars for nine languages, also hosted on Hugging Face Hub
weaknesses: GPL license rules out use in proprietary software you distribute
Models ship as separate jars; the shift-reduce parser and WikiDict need extra English downloads

tools.name: babeldoc
tools.description: PDF paper translator that keeps layout and outputs bilingual PDFs
strengths: Outputs monolingual and bilingual PDFs, side by side or on alternating pages
Glossary CSV support plus automatic term extraction for consistent terminology
Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local servers such as Ollama
weaknesses: Only OpenAI-compatible LLMs supported; not optimized for Bing or Google engines
Mainly tested on English-to-Chinese; other language pairs untested

tools.name: so-vits-svc-fork
tools.description: Singing voice conversion with realtime mic input, GUI and CLI training
strengths: Realtime conversion from microphone via `svc vc`, plus file inference with `svc infer`
Installs with pip; pretrained models download automatically, no fairseq needed
Full CLI pipeline for preprocessing, splitting, diarization and training
weaknesses: README declares the project no longer maintained, since Spring 2023
Only 4.0v1 models are compatible; 4.1 and other models are unsupported

tools.name: Steel Browser
tools.description: Self-hostable browser API that runs Chrome sessions for agents and scrapers
strengths: Connects with Puppeteer, Playwright or Selenium, plus Node and Python SDKs
Session state, proxy chains, extensions and stealth plugins are built in
/scrape, /screenshot and /pdf endpoints return page content, images or PDFs
weaknesses: README labels it public beta, so APIs may change
Commands API for agents is experimental and off by default

tools.name: funclip
tools.description: Clip videos by selecting text or speakers from an ASR transcript
strengths: Paraformer gives token-level timestamps, so clips cut precisely on selected text
CAM++ speaker recognition allows clipping all segments from one speaker
Gradio UI plus a two-stage CLI (recognize, then clip) for scripting
weaknesses: Default models are tuned for Chinese; English uses a separate Paraformer model via -l en
MOSS backend has only segment-level timestamps and needs a separate vLLM service

tools.name: agent-governance-toolkit
tools.description: Policy enforcement, identity and audit for AI agent tool calls
strengths: Deterministic deny at tool-call level, not prompt-level; two-line `govern()` wrapper to start
SDKs in Python, TypeScript, .NET, Rust and Go, plus Claude Code and Copilot CLI plugins
Adapters for Semantic Kernel, LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, LlamaIndex, Haystack and others
weaknesses: Public preview; README warns of breaking changes before GA
Python has the full stack; other language SDKs cover only core governance

tools.name: sandstorm
tools.description: Sandbox host that pauses and snapshots idle gVisor or Firecracker sandboxes
strengths: Four-tier lifecycle: frozen wake about 0.1 s, snapshot restore about 0.2 s
Two backends in one fleet; gVisor needs no KVM
Single binary serves master, node and web console
weaknesses: Wakes that cannot start within 2 s are refused with a 503
Must be built from source with Rust and Node 22.12+

tools.name: skill-recorder
tools.description: Electron app that turns a screen recording into an agent skill
strengths: Generates SKILL.md files or scheduled automations from a single recorded demonstration
Narration is transcribed on-device with Whisper, covering 99 languages
Imports MP4/WebM recordings, so no live capture or screen permission is needed
weaknesses: Analysis requires a GitHub account with Copilot access; no other model provider is documented
Analyze uploads frames, URLs, clipboard previews and terminal output to GitHub's cloud

tools.name: hands-on-modern-rl
tools.description: Open course teaching RL from CartPole and DQN to RLHF, GRPO and agents
strengths: Covers classic RL through RLHF, DPO, GRPO and agentic RL in one sequence
Runnable examples: CartPole, Atari Pong, LunarLander, BipedalWalker, DPO, code RLVR, GeoQA
Online ModelScope Studios and companion notebooks allow training without local setup
weaknesses: README says content is AI-assisted and not fully reviewed; code may not run as expected
Some chapters are still under construction and may contain mistakes

tools.name: djl
tools.description: Engine-agnostic Java framework for training and running deep learning models
strengths: Native Java API that works like any regular library in an IDE and build
Engine-agnostic: switch deep learning engines without rewriting application code
Model zoo with Criteria-based loading, plus built-in training and datasets such as MNIST
weaknesses: Java-centric, while most ML tooling and examples are in Python
README shows only classic deep learning examples, no LLM serving or agent features

tools.name: jupyter-ai
tools.description: JupyterLab chat extension that connects ACP coding agents to notebooks
strengths: Supports many agents via ACP, auto-detected once their dependencies are installed
Agents must request approval before writing files or running commands
Drag and drop files or notebook cells into chat as context
weaknesses: Does not run models itself; requires installing a separate agent
Tied to JupyterLab, not usable outside it

tools.name: mcpo
tools.description: Exposes any MCP server as an OpenAPI HTTP endpoint
strengths: One command turns any MCP server into an OpenAPI server with /docs
stdio, SSE and Streamable HTTP upstreams; OAuth 2.1 with dynamic registration
Config file in Claude Desktop format with hot reload
weaknesses: Last commit 2026-02-27
Single shared API key; no users or RBAC

tools.name: realtimetts
tools.description: Python library that streams LLM text into low-latency speech across many TTS engines
strengths: One TextToAudioStream API over about 30 engines, local and cloud, with fallback engines
feed() accepts generators, so speech starts while an LLM is still streaming
Qwen server exposes /v1/audio/speech with voice cloning and a browser studio page
weaknesses: Each engine has its own license and terms; users must verify them separately
Local playback needs PyAudio and PortAudio; Linux and macOS require a manual install

tools.name: iree
tools.description: MLIR-based compiler and runtime for deploying ML models from datacenter to edge
strengths: One compiler and runtime path covering datacenter through mobile and edge targets
Installable from PyPI as iree-base-compiler and iree-base-runtime
Nightly CI on Linux arm64 and macOS arm64
weaknesses: Compiler toolchain, not a ready-to-use model server or chat app
Extending or debugging it requires MLIR and compiler knowledge

tools.name: viseron
tools.description: Local-only NVR with object, motion and face detection for IP cameras
strengths: Runs locally only, so camera footage stays on your own host
Configuration file is editable from the built-in web interface
Modular components, with a searchable Component Explorer in the docs
weaknesses: README gives no hardware, RAM or GPU guidance
README lists no supported detection models or camera protocols

tools.name: chat-ollama
tools.description: Self-hosted chat app with knowledge bases and MCP tools on SQLite
strengths: No separate database or vector service; SQLite and local files hold all data
Chat and embedding endpoints are configured independently, including Ollama via its OpenAI-compatible API
Active runs survive browser close and app restart on an intact data volume
weaknesses: No application login; anyone with network access can use the app and its tools
MCP tools run without per-call approval

tools.name: mteb
tools.description: Python toolkit for benchmarking embedding models on retrieval and other tasks
strengths: Installs with pip or uv and runs from Python or the `mteb run` CLI
Named benchmarks carry citations and can export task tables as LaTeX
Feeds the public Hugging Face MTEB leaderboard, with documented steps to add models
weaknesses: Evaluation only; it does not train, fine-tune or serve embedding models
Task and model catalogs live in external docs, not the README

tools.name: Laminar
tools.description: Observability platform for AI agents with tracing, evals and SQL-queryable traces
strengths: SDKs for TypeScript and Python start tracing with one initialize call
Query traces, spans, metrics and events with SQL, including via MCP and CLI
Signals describe agent behavior in plain English and notify in Slack
weaknesses: README recommends the managed platform or the full compose file for production
Chat-with-trace and SQL-with-AI need a separately configured LLM provider

tools.name: geoai
tools.description: Python package for training and running deep learning models on satellite imagery
strengths: Covers the full pipeline: data download, chip generation, training, inference and export
Reads and writes GeoTIFF, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage and GeoParquet
Catalog of 20 remote sensing foundation models, with TerraTorch backbone loading
weaknesses: Narrow domain: geospatial raster and vector data only, not a general ML library
Builds on PyTorch and other packages, so installs carry heavy dependencies

tools.name: miles
tools.description: RL post-training framework pairing SGLang rollout with Megatron-LM training
strengths: Fully async rollout and training workers, with configurable on- and off-policy schedules
Recovers a dead SGLang engine in place and resumes the run without a restart
Supports MXFP8, NVFP4, FP8, INT4 QAT, BF16, FP16, plus LoRA and multi-LoRA
weaknesses: Aimed at multi-GPU clusters; the README gives no single-GPU or small-scale path
Requires SGLang and Megatron-LM stacks, which adds setup work

tools.name: uzu
tools.description: Rust on-device inference engine with Python, Swift and TypeScript bindings
strengths: Same chat API across Rust, Python, Swift and TypeScript
Embeds in the app process, so no separate server to run
Examples cover streaming, tool calls and structured output
weaknesses: Each loaded model can use significant RAM; README advises one session at a time
Example model IDs use Mirai-format quantization; other formats are unclear

tools.name: aimet
tools.description: Quantization and compression toolkit for PyTorch and ONNX models
strengths: Broad PTQ set: AdaRound, SeqMSE, CLE, AdaScale, SpinQuant, BatchNorm folding
Separate aimet-onnx and aimet-torch packages installable from PyPI
Also covers QAT and compression (spatial SVD, channel pruning, per-layer ratios)
weaknesses: Supports only PyTorch and ONNX models
QAT is available only through aimet-torch, not ONNX

tools.name: category_encoders
tools.description: scikit-learn transformers that encode categorical columns as numeric features
strengths: About 23 encoding methods behind one sklearn transformer API
Works with numpy arrays and pandas DataFrames, and drops into sklearn pipelines
NestedCVWrapper and PolynomialWrapper add overfitting control and polynomial target support
weaknesses: Supervised encoders need fit_transform on training data; fit().transform() can give different results
GLMMEncoder needs the optional statsmodels dependency via the glmm extra

tools.name: tensorfold
tools.description: Zig inference server for Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs, no Python needed
strengths: Serving needs no Python or MLX installation; the engine is a Zig binary
One server exposes OpenAI chat/completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages APIs
Runs on both Apple Silicon (Metal) and NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA)
weaknesses: Linux needs NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0) and glibc 2.28 or newer
No CPU-only serving path is described; needs Apple Silicon or NVIDIA GPU

tools.name: edgequake
tools.description: Rust implementation of LightRAG that builds a knowledge graph from documents
strengths: Postgres is the only datastore; no separate vector or graph database
Per-workspace model roles across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, Ollama, llama.cpp and others
Multi-tenant isolation, built-in auth, OIDC SSO and audit logging
weaknesses: Evidence recall trails Python LightRAG (0.932 vs 0.949) in its own benchmark
Graph extraction needs LLM calls per chunk, adding ingestion cost and time

tools.name: dstack
tools.description: Control plane for provisioning GPUs and running workloads across clouds and on-prem
strengths: One YAML and CLI workflow across GPU clouds, Kubernetes and on-prem SSH fleets
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU and Tenstorrent accelerators
Covers dev environments, training tasks, scaled inference services and volumes
weaknesses: Backends must be configured per cloud or Kubernetes cluster before use
Server requires Git and OpenSSH; Windows only via WSL 2

tools.name: veomni
tools.description: PyTorch distributed training framework for text, vision-language and omni models
strengths: Combines FSDP2, Ulysses sequence parallelism and expert parallelism for large MoE training
Example configs for Qwen3, Qwen3-VL, DeepSeek, Llama3, GPT-OSS, Wan and LTX-2.3
Runs on NVIDIA GPU, AMD ROCm, Ascend NPU and Cambricon MLU
weaknesses: RL post-training for omni models with VeRL is listed as upcoming
Some model support is marked experimental, such as HunyuanVideo 1.5

tools.name: trainer
tools.description: Kubernetes operator for distributed training and LLM fine-tuning jobs
strengths: Covers PyTorch, JAX, XGBoost, DeepSpeed, MLX and Megatron-LM runtimes under one TrainJob API
MPI runtime for multi-node, multi-GPU jobs on Kubernetes
Integrates with Kueue, Slurm Bridge and KAI Scheduler for scheduling
weaknesses: Project is alpha status; the README warns APIs may change
Requires a Kubernetes cluster; not usable on a single workstation

tools.name: ai-chatbot-framework
tools.description: Self-hosted multi-user agent with a per-user Docker sandbox, memory and skills
strengths: One sandbox per user with persistent /workspace, resource limits and gVisor in the production stack
Stateless app processes scale with docker compose --scale, using Redis and PostgreSQL
Any LangChain chat provider, per-user API keys, and per-task model choice including local llama.cpp
weaknesses: Production setup needs host prep: gVisor, user-namespace remapping and a sandbox egress firewall
Version 2 drops the old NLU intent/entity builder; it survives only in git history

tools.name: inferencex
tools.description: Continuous inference benchmarks across GPUs and serving frameworks, with public dashboard
strengths: Covers many SKUs: H100/H200, B200/B300, GB200/GB300 NVL72, MI300X to MI355X, TPUv7x
Benchmarks rerun continuously, with new models added on release day per the news log
Apache-2.0, with an open-source dashboard in a separate repo
weaknesses: Not a tool for serving models; it measures other engines
Official results need the SemiAnalysis repo and their hardware; forks are labelled unofficial

tools.name: adk-java
tools.description: Java library for building and orchestrating LLM agents in code
strengths: Agents, tools and orchestration defined in plain Java, so they can be unit tested and versioned
Composes specialized agents into hierarchies for multi-agent applications
Optional google-adk-dev artifact adds a UI for testing and debugging agents
weaknesses: Agent evaluation is listed as 'Coming soon', so no built-in eval yet
Tool ecosystem is oriented toward Google services, such as GoogleSearchTool and Gemini

tools.name: smart-second-brain
tools.description: Obsidian plugin adding hybrid search, a topic graph and an AI agent
strengths: Search and Smart Graph work immediately with no AI provider configured
No telemetry; notes only go to providers you configure
Runs on both Obsidian desktop and mobile
weaknesses: Requires Obsidian; not usable on plain Markdown folders without it
Daily update check contacts GitHub unless disabled in settings

tools.name: mcp-server-excel
tools.description: MCP server and CLI that drive the real Microsoft Excel app via COM
strengths: Uses real Excel, so PivotTables, macros, Data Model and formatting are preserved
Covers Power Query, DAX, VBA, Python =PY(), Goal Seek and charts
Same commands available as MCP server or CLI for token-lean agents
weaknesses: Windows only; not intended for Linux, macOS or server-side batch use
Requires Microsoft Excel 2016 or later, a paid dependency

tools.name: vestige
tools.description: Append-only, hash-chained memory store for agents, exposed over MCP
strengths: No embeddings, LLM, GPU or API keys needed; benchmarked on an i5-2520M with 8 GB RAM
Append-only signed log keeps superseded facts and returns receipts for admitted writes
Reproducible retrieval benchmarks on LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, BEAM and MemoryAgentBench
weaknesses: Benchmarks measure top-k retrieval only, not answer accuracy
LoCoMo turn-level exact R@1 is 47.92%, so top-slot misses are common

tools.name: paddleocr
tools.description: OCR and document parsing toolkit that outputs Markdown and JSON from PDFs and images
strengths: Three PP-OCRv6 tiers (1.5M, 7.7M, 34.5M params) cover edge to server
One PP-OCRv6 model handles 50 languages; PaddleOCR-VL covers 111
Outputs Markdown, JSON and DOCX; PP-StructureV3 returns table cell and text coordinates
weaknesses: Depends on the PaddlePaddle framework; GPU installs need matching CUDA builds
Benchmark claims such as 96.3% on OmniDocBench are the authors' own

tools.name: annotated_deep_learning_paper_implementations
tools.description: Annotated PyTorch implementations of deep learning papers with side-by-side notes
strengths: Broad coverage: transformers, diffusion, GANs, RL, optimizers, normalization, LoRA, GNNs, CFR
Each implementation has side-by-side code and explanation on a hosted website
Compact PyTorch code that is readable for studying the original papers
weaknesses: Written for study, not as an optimized production library
No release tags; versioning is only via the pip package

tools.name: self-llm
tools.description: Chinese-language tutorials for deploying and fine-tuning open LLMs on Linux
strengths: Covers 50+ models, each with its own deployment and fine-tuning walkthrough
Hardware sections for AMD ROCm, Ascend NPU, Moore Threads MUSA and Apple M
Worked examples such as a LoRA chat model and a math-tuned InternLM2 model
weaknesses: Main README is in Chinese; the English version is a separate file
Core tutorials target Linux; other platforms get sections for only some models

tools.name: insightface
tools.description: Face detection, recognition and alignment toolbox with ArcFace and RetinaFace models
strengths: Covers recognition, detection and alignment with training code, datasets and IJB/Megaface evaluation scripts
Python package runs inference with automatic CoreML, CUDA or CPU provider selection
InsightFace Server offers a Web UI, REST API and SQLite storage in one Linux x86_64 container
weaknesses: Models and training data are non-commercial research only; commercial use needs separate licensing
Inswapper and buffalo_l models require contacting the maintainers for a license

tools.name: mlc-llm
tools.description: ML compiler and inference engine for running LLMs on GPUs, phones and browsers
strengths: One engine covers AMD, NVIDIA, Apple and Intel GPUs on Linux, Windows and macOS
Also targets browsers (WebGPU/WASM), iOS/iPadOS and Android (Adreno, Mali via OpenCL)
OpenAI-compatible API over REST, Python, JavaScript, iOS and Android
weaknesses: README gives no install steps, model list or memory requirements; docs are external
No Docker or compose files detected

tools.name: F5-TTS
tools.description: Flow-matching TTS and voice cloning with Gradio and CLI
strengths: pip install f5-tts; Gradio UI, CLI and a ghcr.io Docker image
Triton plus TensorRT-LLM runtime: 253 ms average latency at concurrency 2 on L20
Training and fine-tuning via Accelerate or a Gradio finetune app
weaknesses: Pretrained weights are CC-BY-NC (Emilia data); code is MIT, models are non-commercial
Reference audio needs a transcript, or an ASR model runs and uses more GPU memory

tools.name: amazon-sagemaker-examples
tools.description: Official notebooks for training, tuning, deploying and operating models on SageMaker
strengths: Maintained by the SageMaker team, covering training, customization, evaluation, inference and MLOps
Each notebook is self-contained with its own scripts, data and relative paths
Covers fine-tuning methods: SFT, DPO, RLVR, RLAIF, MTRL and CPT
weaknesses: Requires an AWS account, IAM role setup and an S3 bucket
Tied to AWS services; running elsewhere needs modification

tools.name: pinchtab
tools.description: HTTP server and CLI that lets AI agents drive Chrome with compact snapshots
strengths: Text extraction at about 800 tokens per page, versus roughly 10,000 for raw output
Persistent named profiles keep logins across restarts; multiple isolated instances run in parallel
Binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, with sensitive endpoints off and a local-only site allowlist
weaknesses: Needs a locally installed Chrome or Chromium; none is bundled in the binary
Not designed for multi-tenant or public-internet exposure; remote setups must be secured manually

tools.name: sensevoice
tools.description: Multilingual speech recognition model with emotion and audio-event tags
strengths: One model outputs transcript, language ID, emotion tag and audio-event tag
README reports over 5x faster than Whisper-Small in its benchmark setup
Multiple runtimes: FunASR Python, ONNX, Libtorch, FastAPI, and a GGUF binary without Python
weaknesses: Released checkpoint supports only 5 languages, not the 50+ cited for the research work
Speaker diarization needs separate FSMN-VAD and CAM++ models; accuracy not validated

tools.name: bitsandbytes
tools.description: 8-bit and 4-bit quantization and 8-bit optimizers for PyTorch models
strengths: Drop-in Linear8bitLt and Linear4bit layers plus 8-bit optimizers in bitsandbytes.optim
Documented integrations with Hugging Face Transformers, Diffusers and PEFT
Wide hardware matrix: x86-64 and aarch64 CPU, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel XPU, Windows, macOS
weaknesses: Library only, no model server, UI or CLI; requires writing PyTorch code
Gaudi has partial 4-bit support and no 8-bit optimizers

tools.name: h2o-3
tools.description: Distributed in-memory machine learning platform with AutoML and R/Python clients
strengths: Broad classic algorithm set plus AutoML, accessed from R, Python, Scala, Java and REST
Exports models as POJO or MOJO for fast scoring in production
Runs as a cluster across nodes, with Hadoop and Sparkling Water (Spark) integration
weaknesses: Not an LLM or generative AI toolkit; focused on classic tabular ML
Building from source needs JDK, Node.js, Gradle, Python and R

tools.name: clearml
tools.description: Experiment tracking, pipelines and dataset versioning for ML jobs
strengths: Two-line Task.init() captures git state, packages, parameters, console output and GPU/CPU metrics
Auto-logs PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras, XGBoost, LightGBM, scikit-learn, Matplotlib and TensorBoard
Dataset versioning on S3, GS, Azure or NAS, with a clearml-data CLI
weaknesses: Full use needs a ClearML server, hosted or self-deployed
Serving, agent, session and fractional GPU modules live in separate repositories

tools.name: freevideo
tools.description: Local MiniMax H3 video generation on consumer GPUs, run as a ComfyUI plugin
strengths: Runs MiniMax H3 with as little as 8 GB VRAM and 16 GB RAM
Picks int8 or FP8 weights per GPU and probes available attention kernels
Launchers for Windows, macOS and Linux install ComfyUI and models, with offline install
weaknesses: Model weights use the MiniMax H3 Community License with territorial and acceptable-use limits
macOS support is an Apple silicon preview, tested only on an M5 with 24 GB

tools.name: textract
tools.description: Python library and CLI that extracts text from many document formats
strengths: Published on PyPI, so installation is a standard pip install
MIT license
Full documentation hosted on Read the Docs
weaknesses: README has no usage example or install instructions
README badges point to Travis CI, which suggests dated CI config

tools.name: csharp-sdk
tools.description: Official C# SDK for building MCP clients and servers on .NET
strengths: Maintained under the modelcontextprotocol organization as the official C# SDK
Modular packages: Core has minimal dependencies, separate hosting and ASP.NET Core packages
Extension packages for MCP Apps, Skills and long-running Tasks
weaknesses: Choosing among six NuGet packages requires reading the docs first
Limited to .NET; no other language bindings

tools.name: mujoco_menagerie
tools.description: Curated MuJoCo robot models for arms, quadrupeds, humanoids and drones
strengths: Every model follows the same layout: model XML, scene.xml, meshes, LICENSE and build README
Python package loads a model with mm.load('unitree_go2') and exposes an editable MjSpec
Some models ship MJX variants for JAX-based simulation
weaknesses: Quality grades (A+ to C) are defined but not yet applied to models
Licenses differ per model (BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, MIT), so check each LICENSE file

tools.name: codex-desktop-linux
tools.description: Community repackaging of OpenAI's Linux ChatGPT desktop app with optional add-ons
strengths: Verifies the upstream package through a signed chain: pinned key, InRelease, Packages, SHA-256
Builds deb, RPM, pacman, AppImage, Nix and a local Gentoo ebuild
Official ELF runtime and bundled tools are preserved byte-for-byte
weaknesses: Unofficial; supports only the latest signed stable OpenAI package, on amd64 and arm64
Builds locally and needs Node.js 20+, Python 3, a C/C++ toolchain and Rust

tools.name: llm-for-zotero
tools.description: Zotero plugin for chatting with papers and running an agent over your library
strengths: Citations in answers jump to the matching passage in the Zotero PDF reader
Agent write actions use confirmation cards and can be undone from the conversation
Saves notes to Zotero or local Markdown folders such as Obsidian and Logseq
weaknesses: Agent Mode is labelled beta and is disabled by default
Web search requires a separate Tavily key

tools.name: vieneu-tts
tools.description: Vietnamese text-to-speech with voice cloning and an OpenAI-compatible streaming API
strengths: Torch-free CPU install via ONNX Runtime; RTF about 0.5 on a 12th-gen Core i5
OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech with streaming; first audio about 115 ms on RTX 3060
Voice cloning from a 3–8 s clip with automatic denoising, plus 25 preset voices
weaknesses: Focused on Vietnamese; the README describes no other languages beyond English
Newer v4 with closer cloning fidelity is proprietary and API-only

tools.name: whisper-asr-webservice
tools.description: REST API server for Whisper speech-to-text with three selectable engines
strengths: Switch between openai_whisper, faster_whisper and whisperx with one environment variable
Outputs text, JSON, VTT, SRT and TSV, with word-level timestamps
Speaker diarization available through the WhisperX engine
weaknesses: Speaker diarization works only with the WhisperX engine
README documents no authentication or access control for the API

tools.name: pentest-swarm-ai
tools.description: Autonomous API and web-app pentester using concurrent agents on a shared blackboard
strengths: Non-LLM verification oracles (OOB, differential, timing) mark confirmed findings as VERIFIED
Runs on Claude, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible APIs or fully local Ollama and LM Studio
Scope enforced fail-closed at tool layer and executor, with an audit trail
weaknesses: Marked alpha in the README badges
AGPL-3.0 license may restrict use inside proprietary services

tools.name: ramalama
tools.description: CLI that runs and serves AI models in rootless Podman or Docker containers
strengths: Auto-selects an accelerator image for CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Intel, Ascend, MUSA, or Asahi
Runs rootless with read-only model mount, no network, dropped capabilities, and --rm cleanup
Pulls from Hugging Face, ModelScope, Ollama, and OCI registries; can convert models to OCI images
weaknesses: Container mode needs Podman or Docker; Windows requires WSL2 with Docker or Podman Desktop
MLX runtime on macOS works only with --nocontainer and a host-installed mlx-lm

tools.name: openlake
tools.description: Rust storage engine with S3 API and KV cache offload for vLLM
strengths: vLLM KV connector installs via pip, no vLLM code changes
S3-compatible API works with the standard aws CLI
RDMA, GPUDirect Storage and SIMD Reed-Solomon erasure coding for durability
weaknesses: No Docker image or compose file; the object store is built from source
Full performance relies on Linux io_uring; macOS supports TCP mode only

tools.name: mtplx
tools.description: MTP speculative-decoding inference server and Mac app for Apple Silicon
strengths: Uses the model's own MTP heads, so no second draft model uses RAM
Serves OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, plus embeddings and rerank endpoints
Auto-tunes draft depth per Mac and keeps plain decoding as baseline
weaknesses: Apple Silicon and macOS 14+ only; no Linux or Windows support
Works only with MTPLX-prepared model packs, not arbitrary MLX models or MTP sidecars

tools.name: brightdata-mcp
tools.description: MCP server for web search, page scraping and remote browser control
strengths: Hosted URL or local npx; documented for Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Zed, Warp and others
1,200+ pre-built scrapers return JSON for Amazon, LinkedIn, TikTok, npm, PyPI
GROUPS and TOOLS options cut the 30 tools down to what an agent needs
weaknesses: Requires a Bright Data account and API token; usage beyond the free tier is paid
Backed by Bright Data's hosted scraping service, so not self-contained or offline

tools.name: agency-orchestrator
tools.description: YAML DAG runner that chains 276 role-based LLM agents
strengths: Detects parallel steps from depends_on and runs them concurrently
Reuses logged-in coding CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot), so no API key is needed
Per-step acceptance criteria and assertions trigger one targeted rework before a step fails
weaknesses: Docker image has no login auth; token protection is opt-in via AO_WEB_TOKEN
README says 8B-class local models make multi-role output worse than one prompt

tools.name: langalpha
tools.description: AI agents that research markets and trade your brokerage account
strengths: Order limits and approvals are enforced on the host, not by prompts
Persistent workspaces keep files, chats and notes across sessions
Produces Excel models with live formulas, PDF reports and interactive dashboards
weaknesses: Self-host has delayed quotes only; no options chains or short interest data
Self-host is single-user with no sign-in and listens on all interfaces

tools.name: prime-rl
tools.description: Asynchronous RL trainer for large LLMs, built on FSDP2 and vLLM
strengths: Async RL with FSDP2 training and vLLM inference, including FP8 inference and PD disaggregation
Expert and context parallelism for MoE families such as GLM-5, Qwen3 MoE, GPT-OSS
Examples scale from one consumer GPU to Slurm clusters of 32-2048 GPUs
weaknesses: Requires at least one NVIDIA GPU; no CPU-only training path
Trainer supports only listed model architectures; others fail at setup

tools.name: liveagent
tools.description: Tauri desktop agent with local file and shell tools, MCP and a browser gateway
strengths: Desktop app works standalone; the gateway is only needed for browser access
Bridges stdio and http MCP servers and loads Skills packages on demand
Sub-agents run in parallel with worktree isolation and automatic merging
weaknesses: Models are reached via Claude, Codex and Gemini protocols; local model runtimes are not mentioned
LLM layer is a bundled K-brain executable; the README does not describe it

tools.name: openclaw-windows-node
tools.description: Windows tray app that connects a PC to an OpenClaw gateway as an agent node
strengths: Per-capability opt-in for shell, camera, screen, location, TTS and STT
system.run sandbox with Strict, Balanced, Open and Custom presets; no host fallback on failures
Setup wizard installs a local WSL gateway or connects to an existing one
weaknesses: Useless without an OpenClaw gateway; it is only a companion client
Windows 10 20H2+ or Windows 11 only; no macOS or Linux build

tools.name: typewhisper-mac
tools.description: macOS menu bar dictation with local or cloud speech-to-text and workflows
strengths: Many local ASR engines, so audio can stay on the Mac
Workflows trigger per app, per website or from a hotkey
Local REST API and CLI for scripting transcription
weaknesses: macOS only, 14.0 or later; Apple Silicon recommended
Speaker detection, iCloud sync and meeting automation are Premium features

tools.name: local-studio
tools.description: Desktop coding-agent UI, forked from T3 Code, with a local model gateway
strengths: Controller serves /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages and /v1/responses across machines
Installs a controller on Linux or macOS tailnet machines over ssh as a user service
Can launch pinned registry recipes on free NVIDIA GPUs
weaknesses: Needs at least one agent CLI (pi, omp, or another provider) installed and logged in first
Windows installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen warns

tools.name: opengui
tools.description: Android GUI agent framework that operates real phones via screenshots
strengths: Plugin install for WorkBuddy or DeepSeek Harness avoids deploying the full backend
Full stack adds CLI, REST API, and Feishu, Telegram and Discord task dispatch
Works on real devices over USB debugging, or on a local Android emulator
weaknesses: BUSL-1.1 license: production and commercial use require a paid license; not OSI open source
WorkBuddy plugin is macOS only and is a public-testing prerelease

tools.name: mcpvault
tools.description: Local MCP server to read, search and edit Obsidian vault notes
strengths: Works on vault files directly; no Obsidian plugin or running Obsidian needed
Path checks block traversal, symlink escapes, dotfiles, .obsidian and .git
Optional --read-only flag removes all mutating tools from discovery
weaknesses: Stdio only; no remote or HTTP transport is documented
Requires Node.js v22.12.0 or later

tools.name: PicoClaw
tools.description: Go assistant agent that runs in under 20 MB on $10 boards
strengths: Single static binary for RISC-V, ARM, MIPS and x86; runs on $10 Linux boards
10 to 20 MB resident memory; boots in under 1 s on 0.6 GHz
30+ providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, vLLM, Bedrock and Copilot
weaknesses: README warns of unresolved security issues; not for production before v1.0
Gateway binds 127.0.0.1 by default; Docker needs PICOCLAW_GATEWAY_HOST=0.0.0.0

tools.name: deepinfer
tools.description: Offline inference engine for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 and Ascend 950
strengths: Batch-invariant inference and deterministic sampling with a fixed seq_seed (NVIDIA only)
Structured outputs constrained by regex, JSON schema or EBNF grammar
Supports both NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs
weaknesses: Supports only one model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
Offline inference only; no HTTP server or API in this release

tools.name: vit-pytorch
tools.description: PyTorch implementations of Vision Transformer and many of its variants
strengths: Covers about 30 ViT variants behind similar constructor-style APIs
Includes a distillation wrapper and self-supervised options (MAE, Dino, EsViT, masked patch prediction)
Single pip package; models are plain PyTorch modules
weaknesses: No pretrained weights; README points to timm for pretrained ViTs
Examples use random tensors; no training scripts or benchmarks in the README

tools.name: learnopencv
tools.description: Code for LearnOpenCV blog tutorials on computer vision and deep learning
strengths: Covers classic OpenCV topics in Python and C++ with a matching blog post each
Recent entries track current models such as YOLO26, SAM 3, RF-DETR and Qwen3-VL
Each tutorial lives in its own folder, so examples run independently
weaknesses: No license detected, so reuse terms are unclear
Several listed posts have no code link

tools.name: lingbot-map
tools.description: Feed-forward streaming 3D reconstruction and camera pose model for video
strengths: Streaming inference reported at ~20 FPS on 518×378 over sequences above 10,000 frames
Windowed mode and keyframe interval handle very long videos, e.g. a ~25,000-frame demo
Includes evaluation scripts for KITTI and Oxford Spires, plus an interactive viser viewer
weaknesses: Quality degrades when the KV cache holds more than 320 views, so long videos need tuning
Offline renderer needs Kaolin, ffmpeg and a manually built CUDA extension

tools.name: DeepWiki-Open
tools.description: Generates browsable wikis with diagrams from Git repositories
strengths: Accepts GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repositories as input
Produces diagrams and a codemap, not only text documentation
Helm chart and published container image for Kubernetes
weaknesses: README gives no local setup steps beyond the Helm chart
Helm example needs external provider API keys (Google, OpenAI)

tools.name: llmware
tools.description: Python framework for RAG pipelines with a catalog of 300+ local models
strengths: One ModelCatalog interface across GGUF, OpenVINO, ONNXRuntime, PyTorch and cloud APIs
Ingests pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, csv, html, wav and images through one add_files call
Mix and match embedding models and vector DBs per library, such as Milvus or ChromaDB
weaknesses: Library only; no web UI or server is described in the README
Needs a text-collection database and vector DB; setup details are not in the excerpt

tools.name: nofx
tools.description: AI-assisted crypto trading system with reviewed orders and an autonomous trader mode
strengths: Frontier requires explicit approval per trade and shows stop, targets, leverage and margin first
Supports Binance, Hyperliquid, OKX and Bitget in Frontier; Bybit, Gate, KuCoin, Aster, Lighter in runtime
One-line installer pulls published Docker images; no Go or Node setup needed
weaknesses: Autopilot can place real trades while running; README warns AI strategies can lose money
Default model and paid-data access go through Claw402, funded with USDC on Base

tools.name: spring-ai-alibaba
tools.description: Java framework for building agents and multi-agent workflows on Spring AI
strengths: Built-in Sequential, Parallel, Routing and Loop agent patterns plus a lower-level Graph API
Context engineering hooks: human-in-the-loop, context compaction, tool retry, call limits
A2A support through Nacos integration for distributed agents
weaknesses: Java and Spring only; requires JDK 17+
Quick start and examples default to a DashScope (Aliyun Bailian) API key

tools.name: HuggingChat UI
tools.description: SvelteKit chat front-end for any OpenAI-compatible API, behind HuggingChat
strengths: Works with llama.cpp, Ollama, OpenRouter, Poe and HF Inference Providers via one base URL
Embedded MongoDB persisted to ./db when MONGODB_URL is unset, so dev setup needs no database
MCP server support with per-user servers, health checks and tool call display
weaknesses: OpenAI-compatible APIs only; legacy provider integrations, GGUF discovery and embeddings were removed
Requires MongoDB 6/7 for real deployments

tools.name: open-seo-mcp-skills
tools.description: Claude skills for SEO and AI-visibility work via the hosted Ryze MCP
strengths: Rankings and traffic come from your own Search Console and GA4, not scraped estimates
Skills are plain Markdown under MIT, so they can be edited or pasted into other clients
Covers audits, rank movers, competitor gaps, backlinks and GA4 AI-referral reports
weaknesses: Every skill depends on the hosted Ryze connector, which is not part of this repo
Competitor and backlink data goes through DataForSEO via Ryze; pricing terms are not documented here

tools.name: nnunet
tools.description: Self-configuring U-Net framework for biomedical image segmentation
strengths: Derives preprocessing and network configuration from a dataset fingerprint, with little manual tuning
Covers the full workflow: preprocessing, training, model selection and inference
Supports 2D and 3D data, arbitrary channel definitions and multiple image formats
weaknesses: Supervised semantic segmentation only; not a general vision or LLM toolkit
Requires setting up nnUNet_raw, nnUNet_preprocessed and nnUNet_results paths

tools.name: ai-agents-from-zero
tools.description: Chinese tutorial with runnable code for building LLM agents in LangChain and LangGraph
strengths: Covers LangChain, LangGraph, MCP, A2A, RAG and fine-tuning in one ordered curriculum
Two full projects with separate source repos: NL2SQL (Qdrant, Elasticsearch) and DeepAgents research
Examples run from the repo root with a requirements.txt and .env-example
weaknesses: Main text is in Chinese; English version exists only under translations/en
Most examples need paid or free-tier cloud API keys unless Ollama is used

tools.name: cost-xray
tools.description: Per-source token and cost breakdown of Claude Code and Codex API requests
strengths: Reads raw requests, so system prompt and tool schemas are visible, unlike log-based usage tools
Prices individual tool calls with cache read/write/fresh split and flags unused MCP servers
Local only: binds to 127.0.0.1, no telemetry, secrets redacted before writing to disk
weaknesses: Only Claude Code and Codex supported; other agents need a new adapter module
Claude per-source split is estimated via tiktoken calibration; only the total is exact

tools.name: Text Embeddings Inference
tools.description: Rust server for embedding, re-ranking and sequence classification models
strengths: No model graph compilation step; small images and fast boot
Token-based dynamic batching with tunable --max-batch-tokens
Built-in OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and optional API key auth
weaknesses: Only embedding, re-ranking and classification models; no text generation
Volta GPUs not supported; Turing and Blackwell images are experimental

tools.name: local-dream
tools.description: Android app that runs Stable Diffusion on-device, with Snapdragon NPU acceleration
strengths: NPU inference on Snapdragon: SD1.5 on Hexagon V68 or newer, SDXL on 8 Gen 3+
CPU/GPU fallback through MNN for devices without a supported NPU
Built-in upscaling with Real-ESRGAN and UltraSharpV2
weaknesses: NPU path limited to Snapdragon; other SoCs only get CPU/GPU
SDXL needs substantially more memory than SD1.5

tools.name: safetensors
tools.description: Tensor file format and library that avoids pickle, with zero-copy lazy loading
strengths: Loading a file cannot run arbitrary code, unlike pickle-based PyTorch checkpoints
Lazy loading of single tensors; README reports BLOOM on 8 GPUs dropping from 10 min to 45 s
Native bfloat16 and fp8 dtypes, and no file size limit
weaknesses: Stores only tensors and string metadata, no custom code or arbitrary structures
No strided tensors; everything must be packed before serialization

tools.name: tutti
tools.description: Desktop workspace where Claude Code, Codex and Hermes share context and files
strengths: Agents from different providers share context via @ references to past chats, files and tasks
Runs on your existing Claude Code, Codex and Hermes subscriptions
Built-in apps (image canvas, docs, slides, prototype design) usable by you or by agents
weaknesses: Group chat, multi-user rooms and cross-device sync are only in Tutti VM, which needs an invite code
Supported agents are limited to Claude Code, Codex and Hermes; OpenClaw is still in development

tools.name: esm
tools.description: Protein language model and structure predictor with SAE interpretability tools
strengths: Local inference of ESMC 6B and ESMFold2 from Hugging Face weights via pip install esm
ESMFold2 takes protein, DNA, modified residues and ligands; single-sequence mode is faster
Includes ESMC sparse autoencoders across layers and a binder design notebook
weaknesses: pip install is about 5.6 GB, mostly the CUDA build of torch
flash-attn and transformer-engine are not on PyPI; separate wheels are needed

tools.name: michaelfeil/infinity
tools.description: Rust server for embeddings, reranking and classification over a REST API
strengths: Embeddings, rerank, classify, token classification and SPLADE endpoints in one server
Uses all visible CUDA GPUs by default, one full replica per GPU
Pooling is chosen automatically from checkpoint metadata
weaknesses: v3 license is custom source-available (Infinity Restricted MIT), not plain MIT
Documented setup needs an NVIDIA GPU with SM80 (Ampere) or newer

tools.name: octopus
tools.description: LLM API gateway that aggregates provider channels behind one endpoint
strengths: Converts between OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic formats; README shows Claude Code and Codex setup
Single binary with embedded frontend; SQLite by default, MySQL or PostgreSQL optional
Groups map several provider channels to one model name, with automatic failover
weaknesses: Statistics are batched in memory; kill -9 can lose them
Default login is admin/admin and must be changed manually

tools.name: nemo-agent-toolkit
tools.description: Python toolkit for profiling, evaluating and tuning agents built on any framework
strengths: Works alongside LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel and Google ADK instead of replacing them
Built-in profiler, offline evaluation system and hyper-parameter and prompt optimizer
MCP client and server support, plus A2A protocol for distributed agents
weaknesses: Deprecated as of October 2026; end of life by end of 2026
Running the examples requires cloning the repo and installing from source

tools.name: data-analysis-agent
tools.description: Flask app that turns plain-language questions into SQL, charts and reports
strengths: Supports Excel/CSV uploads plus SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server connections
41 chart types and export to Excel, Word and PowerPoint
Built-in statistics commands: K-Means, decision tree, winsorizing, trimming
weaknesses: License is CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial, so not usable for commercial deployments
Windows installer v1.5.0 still depends on a retired cloud login service

tools.name: torchrec
tools.description: PyTorch library for training recommender models with sharded embedding tables
strengths: Sharding strategies: data-parallel, table-wise, row-wise, column-wise, and combined variants
Automatic planner generates sharding plans for a given model
Pipelined training overlaps data transfer, communication and compute
weaknesses: Focused on recommender systems; not meant for LLMs or general model work
Source install needs PyTorch nightly builds and a separate FBGEMM install

tools.name: bitterbot-desktop
tools.description: Self-hosted personal agent with persistent memory and self-tested skills
strengths: Memory, identity and skills stored as inspectable files and SQLite on local disk
Generated skills must pass held-out task checks and a canary before promotion
Reachable from Control UI, WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Signal, Slack and email
weaknesses: Windows is supported only through WSL2
Marketplace and USDC payment layer are experimental and unaudited

tools.name: vcptoolbox
tools.description: Agent server with associative long-term memory and 300+ plugins
strengths: Text-marker tool protocol works with any model that outputs text, no native function calling needed
300+ official plugins across six plugin types, deployable on distributed nodes
Retrieval hot path runs in a Rust native kernel (RiverMemo topology V3)
weaknesses: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license forbids commercial use
README warns the agent has low-level permissions; unofficial relay APIs risk leaking data

tools.name: oterm
tools.description: Terminal chat client for Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic and pydantic-ai providers
strengths: Runs in the terminal, no web server or browser needed
Covers Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic and any pydantic-ai provider
One-command start with uvx oterm
weaknesses: Terminal-only interface, no web UI or multi-user accounts
README has no feature list; details are only in external docs

tools.name: isair/jarvis
tools.description: Voice-first desktop assistant that listens to room conversation and answers by name
strengths: Uses recent room conversation as context when addressed by name
Local Whisper STT, Piper TTS and local LLMs; no cloud AI required
Memory stored locally, with a Memory Viewer and redaction of sensitive data
weaknesses: License is non-standard; free for personal use only, commercial use needs contact
Developed mainly on macOS; Windows and Linux behavior may differ

tools.name: bionic-gpt
tools.description: Rust agent runtime with chat workspace, RAG and sandboxed bash for internal teams
strengths: Virtual filesystem exposes datasets, skills and memory without copying them into the sandbox
SSO/OIDC, team permissions, audit trails and usage controls are listed as built in
Works with hosted, private or local models; Apache-2.0 licensed
weaknesses: Requires Postgres and object storage, so heavier than a single-binary chat UI
Enterprise support, SLAs and supported releases are commercial only

tools.name: open-ai
tools.description: PHP client for the OpenAI REST API with streaming support
strengths: No third-party runtime dependencies; only PHP cURL and JSON extensions
Generic request() reaches Containers, Evals and admin endpoints without dedicated methods
setBaseURL() and setApiVersion() allow OpenAI-compatible providers such as ByteDance Ark
weaknesses: Methods return raw JSON strings by default; callers must json_decode themselves
HTTP 4xx/5xx errors do not throw unless setThrowOnError(true) is enabled

tools.name: easy-stock
