tools.description: A-share research desktop app with AI stock analysis and portfolio checks
strengths: Four research depths, including a quantitative overview that needs no model call
Portfolio score uses fixed weights of 35/25/25/15 across four dimensions
Long tasks save checkpoints and resume; inspections reuse stock reports under 24 hours old
weaknesses: PolyForm Noncommercial license: source-available, not OSI open source, no commercial use
Covers China A-shares only, with Chinese-language UI and data sources

tools.name: sglang-omni
tools.description: Multi-stage serving runtime for omni, speech, TTS and ASR models
strengths: Covers many models: Qwen3-Omni, MiniCPM-o 4.5, Fish Audio, Higgs Audio, Qwen3-ASR, MiniMax Music 3
OpenAI-style endpoints: /v1/audio/speech, /v1/audio/transcriptions, /v1/realtime
Pluggable inter-stage transport: shared memory, NCCL, NIXL, Mooncake
weaknesses: Apple Silicon support is experimental and limited to Qwen3-ASR
Batch, streaming and voice features vary by model

tools.name: behavior-1k
tools.description: Simulation benchmark of 1,000 household activities for embodied AI agents
strengths: Covers 1,000 household activities drawn from time-use surveys and preference studies
Single monorepo with a modular install script for choosing components
MIT license, with a paper (arXiv:2403.09227) and project website for reference
weaknesses: README gives no hardware, simulator or dependency details; these are only in the external guide
No Docker or compose files in the repository

tools.name: baocut
tools.description: Desktop video editor that coding agents drive through a CLI and MCP
strengths: Agent and human edit the same timeline with shared undo, not a flat MP4
Local Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, HTDemucs, Real-ESRGAN and RIFE, plus many API providers
CLI, MCP server and skill expose one documented tool catalog
weaknesses: Agent features need a signed-in engine such as Codex CLI or Claude Code
ffmpeg and ffprobe are not bundled and must be installed separately

tools.name: bkn-foundry
tools.description: Backend for ontology-based business knowledge networks that agents query and act on
strengths: Per-object and per-action permissions with pre-execution checks and audit logging
Traces calls from intent to knowledge node, data source and tool
BKN Lang defines the model in Markdown, so definitions diff and review like documents
weaknesses: No web console; BKN Studio is a separate repo and not part of this release
Install needs a Kubernetes cluster and three scripts; Linux is the supported target

tools.name: minutes
tools.description: Local meeting recorder that stores Markdown transcripts and exposes them to MCP clients
strengths: Transcription and speaker processing run on-device; audio stays local
Plain Markdown with YAML frontmatter works with Obsidian, grep and Logseq
MCP server with 34 tools, plus CLI, TypeScript SDK and Claude Code plugin
weaknesses: Cloud summarizers or agents receive meeting text once you authorize them
Linux support is a prebuilt CLI for x86-64 Ubuntu 24.04; older distros build from source

tools.name: sokuji
tools.description: Live two-way speech translation for meetings, with cloud or on-device models
strengths: Local mode runs ASR, translation and TTS offline with no API key or GPU
Ships 44 ASR, 75 translation and 137 TTS models, with one-click download
Virtual microphone and live subtitles work with any meeting app
weaknesses: Two-way auto language detection depends on the Soniox cloud provider
OpenAI-compatible provider is Electron only, not in the extension

tools.name: GoModel
tools.description: Go LLM gateway with OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible APIs, caching and budgets
strengths: Accepts OpenAI and Anthropic SDK requests unchanged by only changing the base URL
Covers caching, budgets, rate limits, failover, key rotation and guardrails in one gateway
Exports Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces, with a built-in dashboard and playground
weaknesses: Prompt compression, intelligent routing and OIDC SSO require the paid GoModel Pro
Speed and efficiency claims come from the project's own benchmarks

tools.name: image-to-3dlab
tools.description: Local pipeline from text or image to rigged, animated 3D game characters
strengths: Full local pipeline: image, 3D model, rig, animation and GLB export in one studio
Pixel Match restores source-image pixels on low-poly models, keeping text and logos sharp
Runs on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA and AMD ROCm (Pixal3D only on AMD)
weaknesses: Weights run roughly 8 to 20 GB per backend and are downloaded separately
TRELLIS.2 and Hunyuan3D-2.1 CUDA routes are Linux-only and untested on real hardware

tools.name: scopeweaver
tools.description: Multi-agent LLM penetration-testing system with Go backend and Next.js UI
strengths: Supports keyless native Ollama, with an optional local-only network mode
Interception rules and approval records gate agent tool calls, with built-in destructive-command rules
Single Go binary with embedded frontend, plus Docker Compose and in-app updates
weaknesses: Scope is prompt-level guidance, not a network boundary; egress control must be external
Requires PostgreSQL, and only one server per database is supported

tools.name: ms-365-mcp-server
tools.description: MCP server exposing 300+ Microsoft Graph endpoints for Outlook, Teams and OneDrive
strengths: 300+ tools defined declaratively in src/endpoints.json, one per Graph endpoint
Read-only mode, tool presets, regex filters and --allowed-scopes limit access and token use
Supports Global, China 21Vianet and GCC High clouds
weaknesses: Teams, SharePoint and shared mailboxes need --org-mode set from the start
GCC High needs your own Azure app registration and client ID

tools.name: oracle3-prediction-market-agent
tools.description: MCP server and Python engine for prediction-market research on Kalshi and Polymarket
strengths: Public Kalshi and Polymarket reads need no exchange credentials
Constraint checks return baskets, per-leg fees and net edge, and work offline
Includes six Skills and a Python strategy interface with paper and live adapters
weaknesses: Quickstart is an editable install from a git checkout; no Docker image
Live order execution is outside MCP and needs the separate CLI/Python engine

tools.name: clawmetry
tools.description: Dashboard for agent session timelines, tool calls and cost
strengths: Reads existing session files; no SDK or instrumentation, and no added overhead in the agent process
Covers 32 agent runtimes in one dashboard with a per-runtime switcher
Context-window usage is sized per provider, and /api/context-coverage reports where it cannot see compaction
weaknesses: Free package reads only OpenClaw, NemoClaw, Goose and Qwen Code; the other 28 need a paid plan
Support for the other 28 runtimes lives in a closed-source `clawmetry-pro` companion

tools.name: ai-engineering-hub
tools.description: Collection of 93 runnable AI tutorials on RAG, agents, MCP and fine-tuning
strengths: Roughly 93 self-contained projects, each in its own folder
Wide coverage: RAG, agents, MCP, voice, OCR, fine-tuning, evaluation
Projects sorted into beginner, intermediate and advanced tiers
weaknesses: No single install; each project has its own dependencies and setup
Many examples need third-party API keys such as Firecrawl or AssemblyAI

tools.name: agents-course
tools.description: Free Hugging Face course on building agents with smolagents, LlamaIndex, LangGraph
strengths: Covers three frameworks: smolagents, LlamaIndex and LangGraph
Final project has automated evaluation and a student leaderboard
Bonus units on function-calling fine-tuning and agent tracing and evaluation
weaknesses: Repository holds course source; lessons are read on the Hugging Face site
Requires basic Python and basic LLM knowledge

tools.name: IndexTTS
tools.description: Zero-shot TTS with emotion, speed and pronunciation control
strengths: Emotion control via reference audio, an 8-value vector or a text description
Inline pronunciation overrides: Pinyin, CMU phonemes and Japanese Kana
BF16 inference with optional DeepSpeed and compiled CUDA kernels
weaknesses: No Dockerfile or compose file; install is uv plus CUDA Toolkit 12.8 or newer
Model weights (IndexTTS-2.5, IndexTTS-2) are separate multi-GB downloads

tools.name: jev-ultrafast
tools.description: Browser agent that picks an operation and numbered page element per request
strengths: One network round trip per decision, with operation and target heads sharing state
Default loop uses structured DOM state, not screenshots
Executor rechecks page freshness and click occlusion; model output never becomes selectors or JS
weaknesses: Superseded by ultrafast mode in Browser Use; this repo is kept as an experiment
Needs TypeSafe and text-model API keys; live examples make paid calls

tools.name: 100-days-of-ml-code
tools.description: Chinese-language machine learning course with daily scikit-learn and Keras exercises
strengths: Code updated for current scikit-learn and Keras 3, with Python 3.11/3.12 setup docs
Each lesson ships as script, Markdown and notebook, generated by tools/sync_lessons.py
Basic lessons need no GPU; deep learning dependencies are installed separately
weaknesses: Only Day 1 to 54 of 100 are written
Chinese only; the README shows no English lessons

tools.name: ludwig
tools.description: YAML-configured training and fine-tuning for LLMs, multimodal and tabular models
strengths: Whole experiment defined in one YAML file; ludwig train, predict and serve cover the workflow
Wide LLM tuning coverage: SFT, DPO, KTO, ORPO, GRPO, many PEFT adapters, QLoRA
Mixes text, image, audio, number and timeseries inputs in one config
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.12+ and recent PyTorch, Transformers and Ray versions
Config schema is large; advanced options need reading the docs

tools.name: inkos
tools.description: AI agent for writing novels, short stories, scripts and interactive fiction
strengths: Per-book state validated with Zod; chapter text and state are committed atomically
Models can be routed per agent role, such as writer and auditor
Same harness behind Studio, TUI, CLI and a JSON interact mode for external agents
weaknesses: README is mainly in Chinese; English writing is enabled with --lang en
Needs an external LLM API or a local endpoint such as Ollama or LM Studio

tools.name: glm-5
tools.description: Open-weight GLM-5 series LLMs for coding and long-horizon agent tasks
strengths: Apache-2.0 repo; weights offered in both FP8 and BF16 for each release
Serving guides for SGLang, vLLM, Transformers, KTransformers, Unsloth and Ascend NPU
GLM-5.2 documented with a 1M-token context
weaknesses: 744B-parameter models need multi-GPU servers; README gives no hardware requirements
Repo holds docs and links only; weights live on Hugging Face and ModelScope

tools.name: interpret
tools.description: Python library for training interpretable models and explaining blackbox ML models
strengths: EBM AUROC is on par with XGBoost on the README's five benchmark datasets, with exact explanations
One API covers glassbox models plus SHAP, LIME, Morris and partial dependence explainers
Includes differentially private EBMs with epsilon and delta parameters
weaknesses: Aimed at tabular classification and regression; no LLM or deep network interpretability in the README
EBMs use pairwise interactions by default; 3-way and higher need a custom notebook

tools.name: ed-donner/agents
tools.description: Six-week course with notebooks for building and deploying AI agents
strengths: Covers six frameworks in one course: OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, LangGraph, Google ADK, Pydantic AI, MCP
Separate setup guides for Windows, Mac and Linux
Guide on running with cheaper APIs like DeepSeek or free local Ollama
weaknesses: Videos and course resources are hosted outside the repo
Default path needs an OpenAI API key and some paid usage

tools.name: torchgeo
tools.description: PyTorch library of geospatial datasets, samplers and pretrained models
strengths: Union (|) and intersection (&) operators combine datasets with differing CRS and resolution
Pretrained weights for multispectral sensors, using torchvision's multi-weight API
Lightning datamodules with fixed splits and a YAML-driven `torchgeo` CLI
weaknesses: Geospatial imagery such as Landsat must be downloaded by the user; only some datasets auto-download
Tied to PyTorch and Lightning; no support for other tensor frameworks

tools.name: lazyllm
tools.description: Python framework for building multi-agent and RAG apps with local or hosted models
strengths: Same code path for local models and online providers such as OpenAI, Kimi, Zhipu, Qwen
Flow primitives (pipeline, parallel, diverter, loop, switch) compose RAG and agent graphs briefly
Fine-tuning and inference frameworks share one API, with automatic framework selection
weaknesses: Local inference limited to lightllm and vllm; fine-tuning limited to collie and peft
Online fine-tuning only for GPT, SenseNova and Tongyi Qianwen

tools.name: nod
tools.description: Personal agent with its own browser and Linux workspace that asks before acting
strengths: Server-side trust check; actions it does not cover wait for user approval
Vault enters passwords and cards on sites without exposing them to the model
Memory notes are visible and editable, each linked to its source message
weaknesses: Labeled research preview; Windows and Linux builds are previews
Safety check is a model's judgement; Claude Haiku 5.5 let 8 unsafe actions through in tests

tools.name: comfyui-impact-pack
tools.description: ComfyUI nodes for detecting and re-detailing regions of generated images
strengths: FaceDetailer and Detailer (SEGS) re-sample detected regions and paste them back
Large SEGS toolkit: filters, merge, pixelwise mask ops, tile SEGS, element decomposition
Supports SAM and SAM2, including SAM2 video tracking for per-frame masks
weaknesses: UltralyticsDetectorProvider (YOLO) needs the separate ComfyUI-Impact-Subpack
Frequent breaking changes across versions, with minimum ComfyUI versions and changed parameters

tools.name: claude-tap
tools.description: Local proxy and trace viewer for inspecting AI coding agent API traffic
strengths: Covers about 15 clients, including Claude Code, Codex CLI and App, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode
Structured diff between adjacent requests shows which prompt, tool or parameter changed
Traces stay on the local machine; common auth headers are redacted before recording
weaknesses: Codex App capture needs a local CA trusted in the macOS login keychain
Native AWS Bedrock and Vertex require forward proxy mode; reverse mode breaks SigV4

tools.name: tts-webui
tools.description: Web UI that runs many open text-to-speech and audio models
strengths: Covers TTS, music generation, voice conversion and transcription models in one interface
Extension system with in-app marketplace; most models install on demand
OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint works with Silly Tavern and OpenWebUI
weaknesses: Base install is about 10.7 GB, plus 2-8 GB per model
Combined dependencies trigger pip conflict warnings; README calls them normal

tools.name: paper-search-mcp
tools.description: MCP server for searching and downloading academic papers from 20+ sources
strengths: Concurrent multi-source search with deduplication and a single standardized Paper format
Works without API keys; optional keys for Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, CORE, DOAJ raise limits
Open-access-first download fallback chain, with Sci-Hub off by default
weaknesses: Google Scholar search is often blocked by upstream bot detection and rate limits
Several sources are metadata-only or unreliable: PubMed, Crossref, OpenAIRE, BASE, CiteSeerX

tools.name: cloddsbot
tools.description: Chat-driven trading assistant for prediction markets, crypto and perp futures
strengths: Trades on Polymarket, Kalshi, Betfair and others, plus Binance, Bybit and Hyperliquid perps
Risk controls include circuit breaker, daily loss limits and kill switch; arbitrage defaults to dry-run
`clodds mcp` exposes its skills as MCP tools for Claude Desktop and Claude Code
weaknesses: Claude is the primary model; the other seven providers are secondary
Live trading with leverage up to 200x puts real funds at risk

tools.name: clearcam
tools.description: Self-hosted NVR adding object detection and phone alerts to RTSP cameras
strengths: Notification URL is configurable, so alerts can go to Home Assistant, Pushover or n8n
Web UI on localhost:8080 for live view, events and recording playback
Runs from source with pip install and one command; AMD and NVIDIA selectable via DEV
weaknesses: Windows is not supported; the README says an ffmpeg fix is needed
Remote streams and app push notifications require a paid premium account

tools.name: splash
tools.description: Apple silicon inference server with speculative decoding and OpenAI/Anthropic APIs
strengths: README reports 74 tok/s on Qwen3.8-27B, 4.5–5.3× llama.cpp decode on the same GGUF weights
Serves both OpenAI and Anthropic API formats, with tool calls, JSON Schema output, images and PDFs
Prefix caching, request batching and an optional SSD cache for long contexts
weaknesses: Requires Apple M3 or newer on macOS 26.4+; no Linux, Windows or NVIDIA support
Only five listed model families, each needing a matching DFlash2 draft

tools.name: cv-cuda
tools.description: GPU-accelerated image processing operators for vision pipelines
strengths: Wheels for CUDA 12 and 13 on x86_64 and aarch64 SBSA, Python 3.10 to 3.14
C/C++ and Python APIs; tensors can come from GPU decoders like nvImageCodec
Jetson Orin and Thor builds are available alongside server GPUs
weaknesses: Requires an NVIDIA GPU with compute capability 7.5 or higher
No native Windows support, only WSL2

tools.name: beav
tools.description: Desktop workspace for social-media creators: research, drafting, image and video editing
strengths: Covers collection, drafting, image generation and video editing in one app
Per-account spaces keep positioning, style and published posts as long-term memory
Connects Codex, Claude Code and Cursor via MCP config that Beav writes for you
weaknesses: Open-source code is stuck at 2.5.0 and differs from the current release
MIT Non-Commercial license; commercial use needs written permission from the author

tools.name: ml
tools.description: Machine learning and deep learning library for PHP
strengths: Brings ML training and inference into PHP codebases without a separate Python service
40+ supervised and unsupervised algorithms plus preprocessing and cross-validation
Optional extensions: Tensor for fast math, Swoole for multiprocessing, GD for images
weaknesses: Fast matrix math needs compiling the Tensor extension with a C toolchain and BLAS libraries
Requires PHP 8.3 or newer

tools.name: spectrum-ts
tools.description: TypeScript SDK for connecting agents to iMessage, Slack, Telegram and WhatsApp
strengths: One message-loop API across iMessage, WhatsApp Business, Telegram, Slack and Terminal
Scoped provider packages allow a smaller install than the batteries-included spectrum-ts
Custom platforms can be added via definePlatform
weaknesses: Fastest path depends on hosted Spectrum Cloud and a Photon account for project ID and secret
Local iMessage requires a separate explicit package install

tools.name: pypots
tools.description: Python library for imputation and forecasting on time series with missing values
strengths: Five task types behind one unified API
Runnable example script for each algorithm and task in the model table
Optuna-based hyperparameter tuning; companion TSDB supports 172 datasets
weaknesses: Many models (Transformer, iTransformer) are adapted to missing data, not built for it
Task coverage is uneven; many models support only imputation

tools.name: pyts
tools.description: Python library for time series classification with scikit-learn-style transformers
strengths: Scikit-learn-style estimators that fit into existing pipelines and cross-validation
Wide algorithm coverage: BOSSVS, SAXVSM, shapelets, TimeSeriesForest, ROCKET, WEASEL+MUSE
Includes DTW variants and time-series-to-image transforms (GAF, MTF, recurrence plot)
weaknesses: No deep learning classifiers listed; algorithms are classical ML and feature-based
README says main-branch features may be missing from the latest release

tools.name: observer
tools.description: Screen, camera and audio watcher that runs micro-agents on local models
strengths: Desktop app bundles llama.cpp and runs GGUF+mmproj models with no separate server
Agents are a prompt plus JavaScript, with sensors for screen, camera, clipboard and audio
Decision models return typed probabilities (yes/no, choice, score) instead of free text
weaknesses: Call, WhatsApp and SMS need whitelisting; SMS is blocked for US and Canada
sendEmail only goes to your signed-in account email

tools.name: react-native-executorch
tools.description: On-device model inference library for React Native apps, built on ExecuTorch
strengths: Hardware backends: XNNPACK (CPU), Core ML and MLX (Apple), Vulkan (Android GPU)
Task hooks like useLLMChatSession handle model download, caching and lifecycle
Inference runs offline on the device; no user data leaves the phone
weaknesses: Requires New Architecture, React Native 0.83+ or Expo SDK 55+ dev builds; Expo Go unsupported
Needs iOS 17+ or Android 8+ (minSdkVersion 26) and react-native-worklets 0.10 to below 0.14

tools.name: kitops
tools.description: CLI that packages AI/ML models and datasets as versioned OCI artifacts
strengths: Stores models in existing OCI registries, so no new artifact server is required
SHA-256 digests per layer plus Cosign signing for tamper detection and provenance
Pull only needed layers, such as model weights without the dataset
weaknesses: Packages and distributes artifacts only; it does not train or serve models itself
Policy administration, multi-layer scanning and audit logs are in Jozu Hub, a separate product

tools.name: mlops-python-package
tools.description: Python MLOps project template with MLflow, Pydantic configs and CI
strengths: Jobs are YAML-configured and selected via Pydantic discriminated unions; `--schema` prints the config schema
Pipeline moves the `Champion` alias only after the candidate passes heldout thresholds
CI and git hooks share the same mise tasks; pytest enforces a 100% coverage gate
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.14 or newer, uv 0.13 or newer, and mise
Example is one bike-sharing regression dataset; other model types need rewriting

tools.name: agentmesh
tools.description: Private network for agents to publish, discover and call tools and models
strengths: Deny-by-default: nodes expose nothing and calls need a policy grant on service names
Short-lived, offline-verifiable credentials issued from your OIDC identity provider
Direct connections with relay fallback, so nodes behind NAT can join
weaknesses: Pre-1.0; sandboxed agents and the mobile app are still in preview
Not an officially supported Google product and excluded from its vulnerability rewards program

tools.name: cybermes
tools.description: Bug bounty automation with a Go MCP server and 200+ security playbooks
strengths: Two modes: autonomous CLI agent, or MCP server for existing AI editors
Offline knowledge base of 200+ playbooks plus PayloadsAllTheThings and HackTricks data
smart_pipe filter archives raw tool output and passes only high-signal lines to the model
weaknesses: Depends on external tools (subfinder, httpx, katana, ffuf, nuclei, sqlmap) installed separately
'Zero-false-positive' claim rests on a PoC gate; no benchmark is given

tools.name: csghub-server
tools.description: Go REST API server for hosting and managing models and datasets
strengths: Git LFS support, including downloads of individual LFS files
LFS storage can be local or any S3-compatible service
Git server is pluggable; Gitea is supported, GitLab is a stated target
weaknesses: Backend only; the web UI lives in the separate CSGHub repository
Model format conversion is still unchecked on the roadmap

tools.name: dodaios
tools.description: Desktop chat that briefs, launches and monitors multiple coding agents
strengths: One chat supervises many coding agents; README cites 30 at once
Chats, memory and documents are stored as local files on your machine
Works with existing Claude/ChatGPT plans, API keys or local Ollama models
weaknesses: New chats default to Bypass permissions, where nothing asks before acting
Desktop installers are unsigned; Windows and macOS show warnings
